title: Good quality, effective product but may not be thick enough for some.
text:
These bunion correctors are well-made and consist of a squishy type gel that has a very high tack to keep them in place. This is a unique product, and the first time that I’ve seen things like this (domestically anyway). I decided to give them a try and for the most part, am pretty pleased with them.

Comfort-wise, they’re pretty decent but you may need to get used to them as they may feel out of place initially. You also will need to get used to and walk/move around in way that keeps the corrector in place as it has a tendency to slip out if you move your toes a lot while walking. Also, if you have somewhat of a more extreme case of bunions, it may actually be a bit painful with all that pressure on your toes at the beginning. You may want to ease into it based on the level of discomfort that you experience.

Depending on the severity of your bunions, this actually may be a bit too small (in terms of displacement) for you. I am a moderate case and even then, I kind of wish that they were a bit thicker as it really doesn’t push far enough for me. Being thicker would also help keep them in place better in my opinion.

Once you get used to these, they seem to work well. Obviously, the results won’t be immediately apparent, but I can feel them beginning to apply outward pressure when moving around (and bending my toes).

THE GOOD:
• High quality gel material
• Comfortable for the most part
• Tacky surface keeps them in place
• Unique product, not many others like it

THE BAD:
• May be uncomfortable while adjusting to it
• May be too small (thin) for some depending on your severity
• Until you learn how to walk with them, they may pop out or shift around

In all, a good purchase. Every case will be different, but it worked well-enough for me.

Full disclosure, I received this product for a discount for my unbiased review. These opinions are my own and were not affected by the promotion offered by the seller.

text: I bought this toe stretcher in order to reverse the damage done by years of wearing shoes that were too narrow for my wide feet. These toe stretchers are ridiculously small for anyone with a women's size wide foot. The holes have to stretch in order to get past the widest part of my toes (the ends). Once I get them over the ends and push towards the heel, the spacing between the toes is way too small. It has the same distance divider between the smallest toe and 4th toe as it does between the big toe and 2nd toe. When I compare my feet, one with a stretcher and one without, the small toes might have a little extra space between them, but the big toe is actually held in a pulled in position. Since I bought this to add extra space between the bigger toes, this makes the product useless and even counterproductive. I did experiment with taking the big toe out of its hole and moving the big toe ring between the 1st and 2nd toe to provide more stretch, but not sure how that would work in the long run.

title: A pefometer I'd walk a mile with. Well maybe a few steps more or less than a mile anyway.
text:
This pedometer does not have all the bells and whistles of its more expensivej brethren but it cerainly serves the purpose I wanted it for. In keeping with my diet and exercise goals, i simply wanted something to track the number of steps I take each day. This does so adequately for me. It may not have my steps down to an exact number, it seems to be off a little bit sometimes, but it is close enough for my needs. It is constrcted of a sturdy plastic. I doubt it would break easily if dropped or knocked into something, but i likewise would not go trying to prove me wrong. It has a small lanyard attached to it. The important numbers are of a size that makes them easily readable. Some text is pretty small and might prove bothersome to some that have bad eyesight.

My only dislike is the pedometer's push buttons. It requires a lot of pressure to push the buttons in. After setting the pedometer up, my fingers were sore for a day. I understand why - the makers obviously do not want the buttons to be triggered during the pedometers use by the activities the wearer undertakes. Still, couldn't a snap slide or switch mechanism be employed that disables or enables the buttons at which point people don't have to press those buttons so hard? O.K., perhaps i am just a cranky old fart with hands not as versatile or tough as they once were.

I am pretty satisfied with my purchase. I recommend it if you want a fairly simple pedometer and not one that has a lot of functions you don't really need or plan on using.

title: Sharp, beautifully crafted nail nippers
text:
[[ASIN:B01HRS3CAC Tobete Stainless Steel Nail Nipper Toenail Scissor Clipper Cutter Pedicure Manicure Tool]]

This toenail nipper is made of surgical grade stainless steel and has a brushed finish. It comes with a plastic cap that fits over the blades to protect them and hold them closed when stored. There is a flip up wire spring hinge that allows the blades to open after they've been used to cut and then flips down again when you want to close the blades and store the nipper. The handles are 5.0 inches long and have angled, parallel knurling grooves for a non-slip effect. The overall length of the nipper is 5.9 inches and the jaws open more than an inch. It is easy to clean: simply wipe down with alcohol and allow to dry. It comes with a satisfaction guarantee or your money back.

I really like these nippers. They are very sharp and work well. My hands don't slide forward on the handles as with my old nippers. The knurling on the handles really works. This nipper is large enough to be comfortable in my grip. The workmanship is high quality, no metal flash, just a smooth brushed finish. The joints work well. The only thing that is not up to snuff is the alignment of the wire spring hinge. It is centered on the handle when in the down position, but is way off center when you flip it up, so it probably just needs to have the bent portion where it fits in the handle adjusted (not that I know how to do that), but it means that it doesn't spring open as reliably as it would if it engaged the handle completely. (See the last six photos)

title: It really does work!
text:
I ordered this 2/28 and it arrived 3/2. Shipping was quick and sufficiently packaged for shipping. The product packaging arrived with no dents or damage. I was surprised that the packaging did not include any seal to show it had not been opened or used previously. The carton holding the unit slides right out of either end of the outer box sleeve. It included the unit and a simple instruction booklet. It's more like a quick start guide, which is nice because no one likes paging through a detailed booklet and searching for your appropriate language. No CD, no inserts, no ads, no user manual tome. Awesome. A note about the directions: they read a little funny because obviously English is not their first language. They are Swedish...I did my research. :)

I plugged it and hit the power button...where is the digital display screen?? It took me a few seconds but it illuminates on the backside through the handle. I easily switched to Fahrenheit by pressing the "+" and "-" at the same time. While it warmed up, I took the before photo (my hair was wavy, warped, frizzy and had an impression from a headband I wore all day). The straightener was ready to go by time I finished that.

So, I'm a "lazy" hair styler. I do not like taking a lot of time to straighten or curl my hair. In addition, I have limited dexterity with my right hand. So the easier, the better. I have a habit of buying these styling tools, hoping that I would get the quick and easy results they promise, such as the InStyler Original Rotating Hot Iron and the Conair Infiniti Pro Curl Secret Curling Iron (both great, too). But when I started seeing these brush straighteners, I thought, "I could do that!" So, I literally started to just brush my hair with it, not even holding it taut like they say in the directions. If this works even in my lazy way, then we have a winner. Sure enough, 10 minutes later, my hair was straight and tamed. Normally, if I want to straighten my hair after the air dry wave and headband, I'd have to wet it, use the hair dryer and my Instyler to get it to look like it does with this one tool. It felt like a rubbery brush going through, which felt good on the scalp and was warm (not hot) to the touch on the surface. I was able to brush through my hair without any burns, even when I hit my ears and neck. I'd say it's more of a 2 in 1 styler...how can they say it's a detangler when they say to have your hair "neatly brushed before using the straightener"?

I'm really happy with this product and it will become part of my daily routine. It gives me the results I expect for my fine, but thick, hair. Bonus: the long cord comes with a velcro wrap for easy storage. I received this product at a discount for my honest and unbiased review.

text:
Relative to the t:clip and t:slider cases, this is lower-profile and more robust. I accidentally sheared off several of the clips on the old models, but that's impossible with the solid metal, though it does slide more (so be careful when wearing it, say, on the waistband of yoga pants). However, the orientation can only be switched when the case is off, and to either vertical (tubing exits at the top), or horizontal (tubing exits on the right). This is a bit annoying to me, as I wear my pump on my hip pockets, alternating sides depending upon where my infusion set is, and I like to check my CGM reading or occasionally deliver a correction bolus without taking it off my pocket--the vertical orientation works fine on my right hip, but "upside down" is the best option for the left hip (so the button points downward, and the tubing exits toward my front), which worked with the t-slider but is not possible with this case.

text: I purchased this newstyle 700ml humidifier and the smaller 500ml version. I can say I was skeptical at first purchasing something like this online. I had to watch the instruction video on online to figure out how to operate it (I'm not a manual person) but once I did that it was a snap. It was very simple to use even the little ones can refill and change the settings on their own to their liking with out me having to start it for them (which I constantly had to do with the other store bought humidifiers).The first thing I noticed was the packaging for each humidifier was wrapped up well and very protected.The humidifiers each came with a measuring cup (which I really liked), a power cord, and a english manual. I liked the setting options they had like the heavy light or mist flow, using the timer or the on option (which automatically shuts off once empty), but the main reason why I purchased these two was because of the multi light settings. That's the best feature for me (and the little ones) because it has multiple color choices which can rotate through on it's own or you can just leave it on one color of your choosing on dim or the brighter light option. The other features is the timer or on option (with auto shut off), easily refillable, and it's so quiet (no loud water making sounds). If it came with spa type noise options it would be the perfect humidifier but that would probably lead to a higher price, all in all a very good purchase.

text:

I do have two cons which is why I am only giving this brush 4 stars: 1. title: Motivating!
text:
First, out of the box, this scale is solid. It's rather simple to setup as well, something I was curious how it would work, but the instructions were easy and I had it online in no time. Now I never really paid too much attention to the accuracy of the scale, because I'm not particularly concerned with that. What I'm really looking for in a scale is it's consistency to measure. As long as I can see progress of my weight and body fat %, that's the most important.

Since having this scale it motivates me more and more to get off my butt and do something! I love having 2 numbers measured, weight and body fat %. Since muscle weighs more than fat, my weight may never change, but my body fat % could go down, which is a good thing. This scale has done a great job of keeping me informed.

Being a wifi scale records every time you step on this thing. So there is no more lying to yourself anymore (as many of us probably do). Looking at my weight and body fat % changes over the last couple months has really been enlightening. Overall, I love this thing (along with my Fitbit Ultra). These products are great for recording your health and gives you goals to hit new potentials!

title: Bugfree
text: Last year I went along with my husband on a fly-fishing trip to Wisconsin. This is a heavily wooded area with clear flowing streams and many, many, insects. Including tiny, biting gnats which practically ate me alive, and made me completely miserable. It all ended when a guy who ownes a summer home there couldn't help but notice me in all my frustrations and misery. He came to me like an angel, who let me try what he uses himself. I never tried the stuff before, and as soon as I put it on there was absoutely no gnat, or any other insect near me. They went away completely and ended my suffering! It was an instant relief! I was completely bug free for about 2-4 hours. Then you need to re-apply it. I wonder if it can be purchased in a larger size bottle. Like an 8 oz or more? On amazon, it seems to only come in a 4 oz bottle. Maybe because it's more convenient to travel with? That I can understand. I ordered two bottles. One from two different sellers thinking one was a smaller bottle, but no, both are 4 oz. I wanted an 8 oz or larger bottle of it, but this is actually better. I can easily travel lighter with a smaller amount when I go back to Wisconsin again. Then when I run out, I have another. Or I can use it at home too, to chase away those pesky mosquitos in the evening who come out to party on people! Or I might give one to my sister who has 3 kids...she may need it on them. I love this product also since it is a sunscreen too. Who wants skin cancer, right? Also, it is a lotion...keeps your skin-so-soft! I love this great product by Avon, and highly recommend it. My first time trying it and I was very pleased! Everyone should keep a bottle of this stuff on hand in the trunk of your car, in your fishing bag, at home, the beach, anywhere it may be needed. Hope this helps!

title: Bugs go Away!
text: Last year I had gone on a fishing trip with my husband to Wisconsin. Around the rivers there are thick woods. In these areas they are full of insects. We went in the summertime, and there were millions of these tiny gnat like bugs that bit me all over. I was practically eaten alive and miserable. I was sitting next to the river and a guy who owned a summer home nearby couldn't help but see me in all my frustrations and misery, came to my rescue with Avon's SSS Bug Guard. I had never tried it before and he came like an angel and let me put some on. I couldn't believe that as soon as I had it on, not a single insect came near me! Not just the biting gnats but no other insect either! I was completely in peace and bug free for about 2-4 hours. You have to re-apply it. It is great stuff, and that's why now if I go back to those woods in Wisconsin I never will go without this product. It is very necessary for me. That's why I ordered this on Amazon, but I ordered two bottles because it is a smaller bottle than I expected. It only comes in a 4 oz. bottle, so 2 bottles would add up to 8 oz. Maybe they make them small, so you can travel easily with it. Then I understand. For travel the size is perfect. Anyway, this product is guarenteed to work. Even I would use it at my own home in the summer evenings when the mosquitoes come out to party on people! I strongly recommend it!

title: READ THIS FIRST...
text:
I own the first two products they put out, Journey to Wild Divine and the Passage, with the original lightstone. If you own either of these you should recognize that this product is not really NEW. It contains much of what you already have. Also note that I can't use either of them anymore becaue they didn't upgrade the lightstone software. I also had an issue after I lost my disks. They told me they had no record of my purchase. Luckily I keep paperwork and was able to send them the original purchase order that came with the product...but it took a good deal of time to get through to them.

The problem here is that they don't appear to be a real hardware/software company, just product promoters who subcontract as needed. They purchased services to create these products which they have now re-assymbled by adding new dialog and an enhanced interface. There does not appear to be a full time programer on staff who sends out updates to registered users. As one viewer remarked, you have to purchase upgrades to Windows 7. That is not something a registered user should have to do, especially on a "new" product. This also suggests that there is no programmer on staff, so they pass the cost of subcontracting one to make changes on to you. They design and sell updates when they get complaints about things not working or when a new operating system forces them to. Unlike Heartmath, the company that makes EMWAVE they are just three men with reputations that can sell and a product that can be rehashed every so often for resale. Companies like Emwave produce new products periodically because they intend to stay in business. This should be another concern here. If they are rehashing old stuff, do they really intend to be around next year when you lose your disk or need a new driver for Windows 8?

My 8 month old son got bitten by mosquitos in his sleep- 6 huge bites on his face and 4 on his legs. Needless to say I have gone on an all out warpath against all blood sucking mosquitos. Crib net? Check. Bug zapper machine? Check. Citronella stuff? Yup (although now our house smells like a campground). I then remembered that skin-so-soft worked well against mosquitos. When I looked for that item, I discovered Avon makes this Bug Guard PLUS sunscreen! yay! One application of lotion to protect him in two different ways! The scent is pleasant. The product is a winner in my book.

Now, at night, I don't apply this on him as I feel the sunscreen isn't necessary. Instead I spray around his crib with OffFamily Clean Scent- virtually no scent at all. Man, I can't wait for mosquito season to be over!!!

title: Delivery system not the best for me.
text: I take magnesium regularly for leg cramp prevention. I try to take it at night before bed to try and head cramps off at the pass, but unfortunately this is not always possible to do. Well, unfortunately I do not find that the liquid easily comes out of the tube when opened, and I have to squeeze and roll it several times to get every drop out. Also it is only about 1/2 of the dose as my other under the tongue formula, so I do not think it packs enough of a punch for my needs. We are all different, so your requirements may be different. I still get leg cramps the nights I use this... but that is me. Sometimes nothing helps me, no matter what or how much. You need to be the judge on things like this based on your experience taking it.

title: There are things I like and things I don't care for.
text:
What I like is that the ease of the roller ball, and the hardness of it, allows you to roll right over your clothing... so if you do not feel like getting undressed (other than after a shower, or any other reason why you are not clothed), it seems like it is still effective even thru "average" wight clothing. I am sitting here with sweatpants and a thermal shirt on, and the rolling motion is still felt thru my garbs. The instructions on the box do not say anything about "skin," and just mentions "affected areas."

Now I will go the opposite direction with this... let's now assume I am now in only my birthday suit, and I want to rub in a lymphatic massage oil, or any other herbal oil or body butter... can I use this roller to roll over or to apply something to my skin that also helps my lymphatic fluids to move? The directions on the box that this ships in do not mention anything about using this product with oils or creams. THEN i did just look at the sales/info order page here on Amazon and it does mention using it with these products. I only checked here to double check it's usage. Good to know, but I with this was printed on the box or came as an inserted instruction. But, now I know and will proceed to try that!

The only other negative that I noticed, and this is probably just me, but I felt my soft tissue on my upper outer arm kind of hurt, like light bruising, after rolling this over that area a few times. That sore feeling did go away after a couple minutes. I got this becasue I have lymphedema swelling and liquid retention mostly in my left leg, becasue I had uterine cancer and 50+ lymph nodes removed 16 years ago. My arms are fine, but I do have fibromyalgia sensitivities, so that is probably why this would have felt like it hurt. (Kinda dumb observation on my part I admit, being that I am the one who controls the pressure! Not the fault to the product! But I guess it doen't take much pressure to use this ball, and that can be a good thing.) THis said, compared to other lymph massagers, like wooden U shaped sticks and wands, they tend to massage up a larger and flatter swath, involving more skin area with each stroke. This one is more like a rolling acupressure point. I an not tell which method moves the lymph better... I am going to guess this is personal preference.

title: My Favorite BJJ Finger Tape
text:
I have tried lots of brands, and certain performance aspects of this tape makes it my favorite finger/toe tape.

Pros:
- It doesn't bond too harshly to the skin, which I prefer, as it makes taking off a painless event.
- However, it bonds VERY well to itself. I make sure to make a couple of passes over itself to ensure it stays.
- Comes with a container. This is a nice convenience.

Cons:
- It can be difficult to take off, so I make sure to always leave the end of the taping on the skin only, so I have something to pull when class is over. I usually leave this "tag" in between my fingers.
- It can be difficult to tear, or cut with scissors. I usually use scissors, as it is less frustrating. Tearing is frustrating due to the thin width, as the adhesive side will fold on itself and make it nearly impossible to set it flat again.

title: Lightweight but works great.
text:
I had another hair straightener that I used and liked. I went to visit family out of state and my beautiful niece borrowed and kept it. (Along with a few other items I brought with me, that’s what aunts are for) That meant I had to replace it since I loved using it on my hair.
This one is smaller than the other one I had and it is MUCH lighter. I opened the box and saw the brush, instructions, and 2 clips to hold up your hair. It is a very pretty purple, white, and silver color combo. It also has a nice loop so you can hang it up on the wall.
This has 2 heat settings, 140 degrees, 160 degrees, and 180 degrees in Celsius or 284 degrees, 320 degrees, or 356 degrees in Fahrenheit. They list both which I really like since I am much more used to Fahrenheit than Celsius. There is only one button to select your heat setting. You just cycle through until the light is where whatever temperature you want is.
My hair is thin, when shorter it has a tendency to curl just enough to be annoying but not enough to be a real curl. It flies away (frizzes) and I usually wind up putting it up in a ponytail just to get it out of the way.
I waited for this to heat up (super quick, almost no time at all) and I started brushing my hair with it. I did a simple underbrush and completely finished my entire head in about 15 minutes or a bit less.
My frizzes/fly away hairs were mostly gone. I still had a few but I had no product in my hair to help. I just wanted to see what this thing could do by itself. I actually don’t mind my niece keeping my other one (I did give it to her, she didn’t just take it). This one pulled less of my hair out with it and I didn’t burn myself. I’m prone to burning myself on hot things.
This one doesn’t have the regular brush bristles but has open slots to brush your hair with. It doesn’t matter, it worked and did so quickly.
I got lucky and was able to receive this at for free or a discounted rate for review but all opinions are my own. I am not required to give a good review, just an honest one. I shop a LOT on Amazon and depend upon reviews to help me shop so I hope my reviews can help others. If you think my review is helpful, please click yes.
Overall I really like this straightener. It is lightweight and worked quickly. My niece is not allowed to keep or even use this one.

title: Helped with my bone spurs
text:
I actually ordered this for my husband but they didn’t fit him. He has a size 12 foot and there was no way these were going on his feet. So I decided to try them out. I don’t have Plantar Fasciitis but I do have bone spurs that hurt. I wear an eight and a half shoe usually. They fit my feet but I wouldn’t order them if your foot was any bigger.
I have to admit when I opened the package the smell was bad, really bad. I hand washed them in some Dawn and most of the smell went away. This did not include any directions for washing or use. That was disappointing.
I saw that on quite a few of these the bottom had an open pocket on it. Mine did not, they may have redesigned these. The stitching on my mine was really good actually and I was surprised after seeing some other reviews.
I wore these to a theme park and walked most of the day in them. My bone spurs didn’t bother me as much so they did help, a lot. They picked up quite a bit of dirt and so I threw them in the washing machine this time. They made it through it. The rest of the smell was finally gone.
While I really liked these for me, they did smell and they didn’t fit the hubby’s feet. I wish you could pick sizes like small/medium or large/extra-large.
I received this at a discounted rate for review but all opinions are my own. I shop a lot on Amazon and depend upon reviews for my purchases and hope my reviews help others. If you think my review is helpful, please click yes.
Overall am I satisfied with my purchase? Yes, but they were supposed to be for the hubby and he couldn’t wear them even though they did help with my bone spurs.

title: DON'T DO IT -- IT'S DAMAGING SYNTHETIC GARBAGE
text:
The Background:

I typically don't use shampoos at all because they strip my hair unnecessarily; I have been a devoted co-washer for the longest time. Because I have natural hair (3c-4a, medium density, and slightly porous) that's prone to dryness and the summers are hot and dry where I live, I've been trying to up my protective treatment game. I typically prefer natural sources for moisturizing and strengthening (stuff I can get from my pantry or refrigerator) but I've been trying out Dr. Miracle's Daily Anti Breakage Strength Créme for my edges and ends and thought the Miracle Repair kit would be good to try on my next wash day. Well yesterday was that day.

The Experience:

The shampoo is non-lathering which indicated to me that it did not contain harmful sudsing agents. Even still, I diluted it in water using less than half of the amount provided. My scalp felt immediately clean and then soon after my hair felt noticeably stripped (by wash day I have significant buildup of Jamaican Black Castor Oil and other emollients on my hair). I tried to ignore my nagging doubts, knowing I still had two condition treatments to go.
The conditioning treatments were both very cheap in feel (as opposed to other luxurious oil-rich more natural products -- you know the feel I'm talking about) yet I foolishly proceeded, hoping to be proven wrong. Neither of the conditioners left my hair feeling softer, more manageable, or moisturized. After the final rinse and absorbing the excess water with a t-shirt, my hair was frizzy as all get out, dry-feeling, and tangled in all the frizz. Basically this "repair kit" had me playing catch up with all my other regular products just to reverse the damage and I was unable to detangle without breakage. Unacceptable.

I typically wear a twist out, but this morning I have yet to see the dried results because I went with a head wrap this morning, not wanting to take my twists out (they were still a little damp because of all the Komaza coconut leave-in and Jamaican black castor oil I had to slather on to compensate).

Never. Again. ALWAYS go with your gut instincts, people. And just like with processed food, if you can't pronounce or identify most of the ingredients in something -- DON'T USE IT.

Next wash day I will be returning to my regularly scheduled programming of co-washing and detangling (with something luxurious like Komaza's Moja conditioner), and then moisturizing and sealing with Komaza's coconut leave-in, Dr. Miracle's Strengthening Creme (jury is still out) and plenty of JBCO. I may have to throw in a deep conditioning treatment of ripe mashed avocado, coconut oil, honey, and vitamin e as well. Lesson learned.

title: Misleading Labeling....
text: Ok, so I rarely leave feedback that is so negative, but I feel like there are a few things I should mention here. First of all this product is listed as "120 COUNT - 4 MONTH SUPPLY - Do not get tricked by small bottles. You will not have to reorder for four entire months!" Sure, it is a four month supply.... if you only take 1 pill a day. However, the bottle label itself states that adults are to take 3 tablets daily. Uhhh...hello.... 120 count/3 pills a day = 40 days of supply, not 4 months. I am not sure why the seller would label their product this way, it is deliberately misleading. I purchased the supplement thinking what a great deal it was, 4 months worth of vitamins for 30 bucks. Think again, I guess. Additionally, this multivitamin contains milk and wheat ingredients. I didn't see this fact listed on the product page, it is in small print on the bottle label. My wife has celiac disease, and she almost took this supplement. That would have been terrible! If I had known it contained wheat ingredients I would not have purchased it. I'm not sure how well this supplement has been working, as I do take several other supplements such as gingko biloba and ginseng. title: Great even though I'm not completely blind......
text:
I have recently reached the metallic age, silver in my hair, gold in my teeth, and lead in my pants. My vision is still ok, I can usually read a decently sized watch without my reading glasses. My biggest problem is trying to read the date. Always a fan of digital watches, but not a fan of huge watches, I tended to use watches like the Timex or Casio digitals with stainless steel bands. After exhaustive searches I had to resign myself to the fact that I couldn't use a digital anymore. I did find one digital with a standard size face but large numbers, but the backlight was dismal. That was a surprise since they made others with standard size numbers with super bright backlights. Anyway, I switched to a white faced analog with big numbers, and that was okay, but impossible to read the date. Then I found this watch. Fantastic! The face is about 1-1/4" (case size is 1-1/2"), what I would call standard size. It is about twice as thick as a standard analog watch, but that hasn't given me any problems. I replaced the leather band with my favorite stainless without issues. There is no backlight, but I can easily read the time in just about any light level except black, I can even read it in the movie theater. One push of the button and it speaks the time clearly, loudly enough for me to hear if there isn't a lot of background noise, but not so loud as to disturb others around me. Push the button twice and it speaks the date. Brilliant! No more digging for my glasses so I can read the date off my cell phone. The battery should last me for awhile, since I don't use the speech every day. The automatic time setting wasn't necessary for me, but was a nice feature and will certainly help someone who can't set the watch themselves. There are instructions about leaving the watch on your windowsill, on a certain side of the house, in a certain position, etc. for best reception for the automatic setting feature. I did an experiment. The first night I did nothing, and slept with the watch on my wrist as I am accustomed to (it arrived at my house with the correct time). It didn't update. The next night I set it in the window sill, and it did update. Since then I have slept with it on my wrist every night, and it still updates 90% of the time. I live on the east coast of South Florida, and have a stainless steel band on the watch. I'd call that excellent reception.
THIS IS IMPORTANT: Do not take this watch to the drugstore and have the person there replace the battery. They probably won't do it correctly, and will likely break your watch. ABSOLUTELY take the instructions with you and preferably go to a jeweler to have it changed. It isn't that difficult to change (if you have decent eyesight), it is a standard battery, but you have to follow specific instructions or you can damage the watch. I am very happy with this watch, and the slight bit of trouble needed to change the battery is far better than all the frustration I had with not being able to read my other watches.

title: Cushiony, but made my feet slide forward in my shoes
text: I purchased these for walking around Disneyworld to prevent plantar fasciitis. I have had this condition on separate occasions in both feet, and the last time, despite cortisone injections, wrapping, and TENS therapy, it lasted two years. Before my trip, I purchased new Brooks running shoes which help prevent over-pronation, and in addition, I got these gel inserts for additional cushioning. When I first put these cushions on, they slipped on easily due to a powdery film they were coated in. The smell was not unpleasant, kind of lemony. I was able to fit my socks over them with no problem by carefully rolling the socks on so as not to shift the cushion. Walking around the first hour, it felt like I had a springy cushion under my heels, and I was hopeful that I would be able to walk an entire day without pain. However, after that first hour I began to feel my feet sliding forward a bit at every step, and my toes were uncomfortably pushing against the front of my shoes. The more I walked, the worse it got. I ended up taking the cushions off. I believe my shoes just didn't have enough room for any extra cushions as they fit my feet exactly, with no extra space at all. I could have removed the insole, but then I would lose the firm support that they provided, which is necessary to prevent feet from rolling inward. I was disappointed, during the short time I wore the cushions, they did feel nice. Maybe they would work in a different pair of shoes.

title: Smooth Energy with Serious Focus
text:
I just got my order of Reloaded Advanced Gaming Formula in the mail. Let me give you some thoughts about the other products I’ve tried and give you some insight about my experience with Reloaded. I’ve been taking other “energy and focus” supplements for a long time. G-Fuel, Sneak, Proven4, Valis - you name it and I’ve tried it. First off, I’m not very sensitive to caffeine because I take so much. So when I take a product I really don’t notice any sort of effect. There’s no energy, just a crash. With G Fuel and the others it’s like I’m just drinking expensive and foul flavored water. With G fuel, I don’t notice any focus or enhanced reaction time and I could care less about anti-oxidants. Same with the other gamer supps. It’s like they’re all the same, crappy formula, use the same ingredients, and all taste equally bad. So I was skeptical about Reloaded but since it used different ingredients I thought I’d give it a shot.

I ordered 2 packages of Reloaded. The Voodoo berry, which is like a grape/cherry blend and the Tropical Daiquiri. Both of these tasted AMAZING. Better than any energy drink or pre-workout I’ve tried. I’ve been on a big VPX Bang kick and Reloaded, to me, tasted way better. I’m a pounder. I don’t nurse my energy drinks. I drink them pretty fast (mainly because they taste terrible). I really enjoyed drinking Reloaded and I wanted the flavor to last. So I compromised. I chugged one serving then I drank my second serving a bit slower. It was amazing!

I wasn’t expecting to really “feel” anything with reloaded, but I was wrong. You know how you kind of get desensitized to caffeine supplements and they just kind of lose their effect after a while? That’s why I was so surprised that I actually felt something different. I actually felt energy. No, not that jittery nervous energy that you feel with drinks like Monster and Bang. It was like a smooth energy. So smooth that I didn’t even notice it tapering off. My friends said I was more talkative. I noticed that I was extremely focused as well. They all thought I was taking adderall or something. That’s really what I can compare it to. You feel that same kind of focus and energy. It’s pretty crazy!

Some of the other things I noticed was that I wasn’t hungry, so I wasn’t snacking a lot. I didn’t crash or get tired. I was just in the zone. I enjoy working out, gaming and I’m in college so I study quite a bit. Reloaded has helped me perform better in all 3 of these areas and I haven’t noticed any sort of decline in how well it works. I did some research into the main ingredients and they are legit “cutting edge”. Developed by DARPA for elite warfighters?? It doesn’t get more legit then that. Also, it isn’t loaded with caffeine. It contains Teacrine and Dynamine. These ingredients are what give you the energy. They don’t effect your central nervous system or your adrenal glands, and they are considered premium and safe ingredients. Way safer than caffeine and you don’t build a tolerance to them.

Overall, this is a great product. It isn’t cheap, but it works. It works better than anything out there. I’ve got friends that are on the football team that take it religiously. I’ve got friends that are like elite Twitch streamers and gamers that swear by this stuff even though they are sponsored by G-Fuel. I can’t say enough about this.

If anyone has any questions, please feel free to ask!

The fact that there are more than four legs does improve the stability, and it does fold down nicely into about the same space as a collapsible camping chair once you manage to get the mechanism to cooperate.

I literally came to Amazon today looking for an alternative, so unless the foldability is essential to you and this is the only one in your price range, consider other options. I figured it had to be the weather, work, stress etc. But I realized that each time I quit taking BTT the migrains would stop. You can turn it off by unplugging it, but I have right electrical sockets and I'd much rather just flip a switch when I want to then it off, rather than have to unplug it and lay it on the dresser. Insuppose the manufacturer assumes that one should let it run 24/7. I have had not reason to be concerned, but if I am going to be away from home for many hours, or the weekend, I just feel better turning it off.

title: Premium price, shoddy quality
text: I have bought and used Verilux products for years, but have now turned against them. First I bought a desk lamp that failed within a year. When I asked for a repair or a refund, I was quoted something like $30 for the service, which together with shipping costs would have just about equaled the purchase price. Then I bought this floor lamp to replace an old one from the same company, and it proved to be absolute rubbish. I simply could not attach the base to the upright because the screw holes were misaligned, so that every time someone picked up the lamp, the base parted company with the rest of it. Then a couple months ago, a bulb failed. The replacement lasted one month, and when I replaced THAT, it too failed just a few weeks later. At $20 a bulb, that's not acceptable. Perhaps the ballast failed, as another unhappy shopper commented. In any event, I took this one to the dump -- just two years after I purchased it -- and replaced it with a plain wrought iron lamp from L L Bean that takes incandescent bulbs. So much for energy efficiency! I still have two Verilux desk lamps, but I won't be replacing them when and if they die. I suspect that what has happened is that Verilux shifted its production to China several years ago, with the predictable results.

title: Compared to Dr. Sholls
text:
I like to wrap a couple toes before long hikes, and had found and purchased Dr. Sholl's moleskin rolls. They were excellent. When I had used the whole role, I found these off brand replacements.

Compared to Dr. Sholl's, they are slightly less adhesive, and just a bit spongier. I found neither difference to be a negative. In fact, the less adhesion was a plus. These are much easier to strip the backing off before applying. And once done, they pull off easier. With Dr. Sholl's, at times it almost felt like I might pull a toenail off during removal. These have enough adhesion that they stay in place for me while in use, but then remove without trouble. If you have used this type of product before, and found that they come off during use, then I would recommend Dr. Sholl's.

Otherwise, I found these to be just as comfortable, just as effective, slightly easier to apply and remove, and less expensive.

title: Well worth the small cost
text:
Used this for the first time today to give my 8 cats worm pills. I got better at using it with each cat. It definitely made the job easier, but a few tips based on my short experience...

- If you have a round, disc-shaped pill, put it in the tip flat and not sideways, otherwise the plunger may not push it out.
- Getting the pill situated properly in the tip took a few tries, but not a big deal.
- The plunger worked quite well on the half pill I had to give a few of my cats.
- Make sure you put the plunger far enough into the cat's mouth so the pill lands where they can't spit it back up. I follow the pill with a 1 cc plunger of water to encourage the cat to swallow (using a different syringe, not the pill gun).
- Someone else mentioned in a review that the pill gun takes a little longer than typical items to arrive. That was true in my case, too.
- The best thing is I didn't risk sharp teeth baring down on my fingers as I tried to stick a pill into an unhappy cat's mouth.

title: Good, with small Modifications
text:
A nice reminder for better posture, although the back likes to ride up to the neck, as another reviewer noted. It ends up pinching the back of the neck if it's not corrected.

I modded this by sewing a durable strap that hangs down the center of the back. That way, when the brace starts to ride up, I just tug at the strap until it adjusts back to where it should be.

The velcro and straps are very strong. After adjusting them to your preferences, they won't be loosening anytime soon.

The pads are comfortable, but a bit bulky.. so unless you're wearing a jacket over it, it'll be obvious when wearing outdoors. I personally find it better just wearing around the house.

By the way, when doing small tasks while wearing the support, it is almost disabling for the arms. It'll start to cut off circulation to the arms, making it uncomfortable. I can't even type on the computer while having a problem, and the straps are barely tight enough to keep the shoulders pulled back to a healthy posture. It can be remedied by loosening the shoulder straps, but by doing that ruins the shoulder support. In other words, it's only good to wear when walking or when not moving around the arms in front of you--such as watching TV.

Overall, I'm glad I bought it. It's already helped with my posture, and after a couple of months of wearing on-and-off, I can now see my shoulders having a more correct posture without wearing the support.

title: These are nice bags, but one star off because they are ...
text: These are nice bags, but one star off because they are a bit fragile, and they do not work well for what I wanted to use them for. In terms of the bags, they are a nice size (bigger than normal 13 gallon bags, so they'll definitely fit a 13 gallon trash container) and the material seems to be of high quality, and the seams all seem tight and well sealed and all of that. For collecting normal recyclables or compostable foodstuffs, I think these would work fine. But I wanted to use these to collect used kitty litter, and for that purpose, these didn't work as well as I expected. First of all, although they're fine when you pull them off the roll, as soon as I put them on the litter box, they tear with even just a little scraping, so you have to be super careful. It's a little weird...they're "stretchy", but yet not really tear-proof. Hard to describe, but it's not what I would have expected. The other thing is that the smell of used kitty litter floats right through these bags. Maybe that's because it's made of compostable material...I don't know, but because of that, it doesn't really do the job, for me. So if you want a nice compostable bag to hold recyclables or kitchen scraps--these are good, get them. But if you want something that's a little stronger and will hold odors in, then I would look for something else.

title: Good value but I foresee issues
text:
After working as a paramedic and after carrying a personal fully stocked BLS jump bag in my vehicle for nearly 30 years, I have become particular with the bag I use. Recently, the metal zipper on my original bag broke. That one lasted me for decades.
After buying several other smaller bags, I finally broke down and bought this one.
There is plenty of room for all of my BLS supplies and the dividers provided do give you a nearly endless variety of layouts
While I have confidence in the fabric and straps of the bag holding up to wear and tear, I have to admit the zippers give me a lot of concern. Unlike the metal zippers of my old bag, this one comes with plastic ones with fairly large teeth. They were given me a problem right out of the packaging. EMS bags should have easy access, In an emergency, every second could count. Someone should not have to take precious time fooling around with a zipper trying to access their supplies.
Hopefully future designs will include YKK zippers for more reliable access.
While I am not sending this bag back and I'm sure to get a lot of use out of it, I can't not justify anything more than a fair rating on this product.

title: Great for shielding eczema on elbows from irritating fabrics.
text: I suffer from itchy eczema on my elbows which is exacerbated by clothing made of synthetic fabric like polyester.  Consequently, this is a bigger problem in the winter when I wear long sleeves to keep warm.  I bought this product to make myself 100% cotton "under sleeves" to protect my elbows from my synthetic shirts and blouses, and to also protect my clothing from the greasy ointments I still need to use on my elbows to keep the skin soft. I have found that my "under sleeves" also cut down on my unconscious scratching.  To make a sleeve, I just cut a length of this cotton "tubing" twice the size I need, then I fold it over so I have a double thickness of tubing.  Once it's positioned over my elbow, I wrap a piece of "self-adherent bandage tape" around my under sleeve to hold it in place. Once the sleeves get yucky from the ointments I just throw them away and start again, but I guess I could wash them, too.  Since I have started using my "under sleeves" the eczema on my elbows has improved immensely!

title: A quality product at a premium price.
text:
This Carlyle Plant-Based Protein Powder comes in a 2.3-pound container that yields about 15 servings. Although each service of this Carlyle Plant-Based Protein Powder is completely Vegan and Gluten-Free it delivers 30 grams of protein and 15 grams of fiber per serving.

What I liked most about this Carlyle Plant-Based Protein Powder was:
- Rich in superfoods
- A good source of plant-based protein and fiber
- Can taste some of the real food that went into the manufacturing of this product.

What I liked least about this Carlyle Plant-Based Protein Powder was:
- Pricy. This product is almost 40 bucks and only yields 15 servings which means you're paying 2.67 dollars per serving. That's higher than most of the most popular protein powders.
- Doesn't blend smoothly. I suspect the 15 grams of fiber per serving are at play here but this powder retains lumps and grittiness even after a minute in a powerful blender.

Overall, if you are in the market for a high-quality, plant-based protein powder that offers both protein and fiber this offering from Carlyle deserves a good bit of consideration. I took this product for over a month and enjoyed getting superfoods like Kale, Spinach, and Sprouts in this mix. The biggest barrier to me purchasing this product again is the price. It's almost cost-prohibitive especially in comparison to other protein powders that deliver similar macros at half the cost. Still, the cost of clean, quality foods is far less than prescription medications so there's merit in making this investment. 4.0 out of 5.0.

title: The potion for GAINS!!!
text:
This Aggressive Labz Behemoth Creatine Power Plexx comes in a colorful 6.85" x 3.5" x 3.35" container that contains a pound and a quarter or 60 servings of creatine.

This Aggressive Labz Behemoth Creatine Power Plexx formula is actually composed of two elements. The first is a 5000mg, 7-blend creatine mix. The second is a 7-ingredient absorption blend that is designed to catalyze the body's uptake of creatine. Combined they deliver high-quality creatine that is fast-absorbing and flows well into a muscle-building routine.

I started strength training again at the end of February following the principle of 15-20 reps per body part per week to bolster my strength and build muscle. I started my journey with resistance bands and no creatine. This month I kicked things off with iron weights and a creatine regime and the difference in two weeks is noticeable. I have increased my bench and leg press weight by 10 and 25 pounds respectively and my clothes fit differently as my sleeves are more snug around the shoulders. Meanwhile, I had to tighten my belt a notch.

While it's hard to say quantify much credit I can give to two weeks of a creatine regimen I am absolutely certain it has played a significant role in the gains I have earned so far. This Aggressive Labz Behemoth Creatine Power Plexx is a fixture in my daily routine now. 4.5 out of 5.0.

I can only assume that the brilliant bean counters at Abbot decided that the almond ratio was getting a bit to spendy in this slow economy and decided to make a change...for the worst. I USED to be able to expect at least one Almond per bite. And because it takes me about eight bites to eat a bar...you can do the math.

Several orders ago I noticed a severe decline in the Almond to bar ratio. Sometimes as few as one or two Almonds per bar, and sometimes ( not infrequently mind you). NO almonds per bar. So tried a second batch and even a third, all spread out over several months in the failing hope that I had simply gotten a bad batch. No such luck.

I vote with my wallet and so Abbott, when you start adding enough Almonds to your zone bars for me to get at least a couple in every bar, give me a call. Until then, you will have to bilk someone else out the premium you charge for an experience you no longer deliver.

Adieu.

title: Better than 1% accurate, but limited display angle; 3xAA batteries NOT included
text: The LCD display reads OK when the scale is at or above eye level, but it is nearly impossible to read if you are looking down at it. The Amazon description says 2x AAA batteries are included. What I received (blue color model) takes 3x AA batteries and they were NOT included, so I took off one star for that. Apart from that, it seems to work fine. It includes one more tiny thing not shown in the photo, a U-shaped cotter pin that goes through the threaded end of the shackle bolt after assembly, to stop it from working loose.  I made a webbing sling and weighed myself with it. It says 176.3 pounds (repeatably) and my Tanita HD-317 bathroom scale says 175.8 pounds. Tanita claims theirs is accurate to 0.2 pounds. I don't have an calibrated proof mass, but at least they agree within 0.3%.  It seems to have kg as "native" units with 0.1 kg resolution. The pounds and newtons are converted from that reading, so the readout changes in steps of about 0.2 pounds and 0.9 newtons.  When you turn it on it auto-zeros, so if it's turned on with a load and then unloaded, the reading goes negative.

title: Bad Eye strain. Great idea though!
text:
The glasses, first of all, came bent. I fixed that by heating the frames, bending them to the correct position, and cooling under running water. No biggie.

Next came the issue of headaches/eyestrain.

While lying in bed reading my kindle (e-ink screen, so no eye strain normally) i felt this tugging sensation in my eye, near my retina. I took the glasses off, and the tugging was gone. After putting them back on, within seconds I again noticed the sensation. I decided to try leaving the glasses on. Reading for 20 minutes resulted in a VERY painful headache and nausea--so much so that I quickly walked to the sink.

The glasses do rotate the angle of viewing in a clear, optical-quality fashion, so they'd be really good for a periscope or something of that nature.

The problem is that your eye wants to focus on something that's way too far away. This causes over correction in the eye, resulting in eyestrain.

title: Good lumbar support, fixed my lower back pain
text:
I started using this back cushion about 4 months ago, and although there may be other factors, I haven't had lower back pain since. I was having pretty much continuous trouble for the six months before that. I ordered this second one for use in the car.

What I especially like about the Back Pillo is that unlike foam rubber cushions it self-adjusts to the chair back. I have used it on 3 different chairs with various lower back curvatures, and the Back Pillo works fine on all of them. The foam rubber ones are more finicky to set up, and what works on one chair might not work on another.

The important thing to remember when setting up the Back Pillo is DO NOT OVER INFLATE IT, or you will lose the lumbar support. When properly inflated it will be very floppy, and you may even wonder how it could give you any back support at all. This instruction is printed on the back of the Pillo near the filler spout, but all the pictures you see (including the one on the package) show it puffed up full of air. Go figure. I try to put in just enough air that I can feel the Pillo pushing against the small of my back when I lean back in the seat. It may take some experimenting to get it just right.

text: I bought this for my mom for Christmas 2011.  My mom is an avid sewer and loves to do various crafts but it's so much easier for her to sew and craft with natural light so I thought this would be a great aid in her being able to craft at her favorite time...night. Yes, it is difficult to put together at first and took 3 of us holding various parts, but once it's together it's been great for her.  Please remember that this is not a whole room light.  This light has a fixed purpose and that is for reading, sewing, or crafting where the light is directly over the object.  My mom also reads under it too if the print is to small in what she's reading and she says the difference between regular light and this is literally like night and day.  This light will not light a whole room nor is it designed to.  When I bought this for her I got her a replacement light since I figured the bulb would be hard to find in stores.  Well 2 years later and hours upon hours of use and she still hasn't had to replace the light.  To be honest I'm not even sure any of us know where the replacement bulb is anymore.  This lamp has also survived two moves like a champ without so much as a scratch.  In the name of full disclosure it should be noted that I personally don't use this lamp, but from the way my mom praises it and constantly thanks me for getting it for her I'd say it's a winner for anyone who does crafts or someone buying this for someone who does a lot of crafting or reading.

title: No steam feature - False advertising on current model they're selling in Aug 2019
text:
I bought this iron specifically because of the steam feature that is touted in both the title as well as in several of the reviews. However the iron that I received has no steam feature whatsoever.

The one I received does match the product photos where it looks like there's a little receptacle for water but there isn't oh, that's just the temperature gauge, but the description about providing Steam and all the reviews about steam are obviously for a previous model that used to provide steam and had a steam on/off switch which this one also doesnt. There is no steam feature whatsoever in this iron that they sent me.

False advertising. I didn't need another flat iron because I already have one that works perfectly well, I specifically wanted this as an addition to the one that I already have because of the steam feature.

Make sure when you read reviews that you're checking the most recent ones if you're looking for a particular feature. I did miss but I couldn't find any recent reviews that had mentioned the steam feature so I figured that if they had removed the steam feature they wouldn't be stating that in the title still. So I took a chance and ordered it anyway, however this is a different model than the reviews match with. you will see that the most recent reviews don't mention the steam feature at all because there is none anymore. Somebody else also in the questions above received the same model that I got and sent it back because it didn't have the steam feature.

Its not worth the hassle to send it back.

But if you're looking for a steam flat iron, save your money and look elsewhere because this one doesn't provide it.

According to him the house smelled like a urinal,the dog was a 'dud', and we needed to take her back to the pound.. I begged for a 30 day trial period where I could work with Lolly and her anxiety and also work on the carpet. I did lots of research on Amazon and decided to try Emmy's Best in conjunction with a blacklight. It took several days and several applications and lots and lots and lots of white towels, but I managed to pull up the majority of the stains and smell, replacing them with Emmy's Best nice lavender fragrance. I also doubled my efforts with Lolly and her housetraining, and 2 weeks into our 30 day trial I think we can call it a success. So Emmy's Best saved my dog and also my husband's sanity. Thanks!

title: Comfortable and well designed.
text: I broke the coronoid process of my ulna in a fall, and the splint I received was not very comfortable. I came to Amazon looking for something better, and ordered two different splints. This one is by far the best one out of everything I have tried, for comfort as well as protecting my elbow and keeping it in position. It is sleek and not bulky, while being very adjustable. The top and bottom straps can be swiveled on their rivets so you can have them connect in whatever direction you choose. They also have a movable velcro piece so you can directly choose where the velcro connects, and this means there's no flapping end of a strap. The inner padding also connects in with velcro, meaning you can reposition it as desired. I can even type more comfortably while wearing this splint, which means so much right now for my productivity! I much prefer the black color over the medical white/beige combo that some splints come in, and I can also more easily fit a sweater over this splint. I am very happy to have found something that makes having a broken arm easier.

title: a great product, IF you make some DIY upgrades
text:
I bought a couple of these for my aunt - for $30 each - and put one under her fav armchair and another under her loveseat. She's found them very helpful and so will you if this product is used with care.

First off, as it's held together with screws, which will, of course, loosen with repeated use, use metal "lock" washers when assembling it (you'll need 8, which have to be bought separately). Second, as the tubing is quite thin (maybe an inch in diameter), it can only be used under an armchair, loveseat, or sofa that has a FLAT bottom (if the chair has legs that are over an inch high, you'll have to get a couple of 2x4's - or however high the bottom of the chair is off the ground - and cut some grooves into them to slide the Riser legs under and then slide the 2x4's and the Riser under the chair). Third, as the Riser has two cross braces in the front, this product obviously cannot be used with a recliner. And, lastly, since this product is made of hollow metal tubing, the vertical supports will likely "wobble" - if not get damaged i.e. bent - if used by someone over, say, 200 lbs who has weak legs and, therefore, has to mainly use their arms to egress from a chair.

BTW, for added assistance in getting in and out of chairs (esp for individuals who have weaker knees/legs), I recommend the UPEASY POWER SEAT or SEAT ASSIST the former of which I've paired with the Riser for added stability/security (and which MUST be used on top of a flat, level, relatively hard surface for it to work properly [I simply discarded the seat cushion from my aunt's chair, put a piece of plywood on the chair, put the Power Seat on top of the wood, and then covered the seat of the Power Seat, which is a bit on the hard side, with a slip-on cushion for greater comfort]).

title: Great product for my dislocated lumbar discs!  Works better than the two prescribed braces I've had!
text: I'm 45, and I've had a issues with my back since I was 19.  I slouch often due to the pain in my lumbar spine from dislocated discs and because of the counterweight from my size DD chest.  I'm on pain management, so I've been prescribed a couple of types of braces.  Once, I was prescribed a clavicle brace, which was awkwardly uncomfortable.  It was 100% unbeneficial and did not work at all.  Not to mention, the design was not very intuitive, and I could not even put it on by myself.  A few years later, I was prescribed a $1500 back brace, which also did not work.  I could put it on myself and it was more comfortable than the clavicle brace, but no matter where I positioned it or how tight I made it, it provided absolutely no support.  The other day, I began reading a lot of Amazon reviews, looking for some sort of back brace to help my posture which would help elevate some of the pain in my back.  I'm on enough pain pills and pain patches to kill a horse, yet I still have pain.  Instead of increasing my doses, I was hoping there was something else I could try - a last ditch effort before asking my doctor to increase my pain meds.  This back brace is great!  It is not as constricting or as uncomfortable as the two prescribed braces I've owned.  It holds my posture upright and is easy to put on and easy to adjust.  The material is soft and smooth, which helps tremendously with the comfort.  I am so thankful for this back brace!  It does hurt a little bit (more like 'sore' than 'hurt', I suppose) around the front of the underarm area (the area where the brace goes underneath your arm), but it helps if you wear a shirt with sleeves underneath the brace.  With any device that is pulling on your body, it is going to 'dig' into your skin a little and cause soreness, so I'm not surprised by the 'digging' sensation.  It's not enough to bother me or to make me want to return it, especially with a shirt on underneath the brace.  A shirt makes the soreness almost nonexistent.  In the end, the brace definitely does its job, and it does it well - a lot better than the expensive, prescription braces I've owned.  Overall, I am very satisfied and very pleased with this brace.  If something were to happen to it, like if I left it on vacation or something, I'd buy another one in a heartbeat!

title: So far, so eh.
text:
As far as face cleaners go, this is okay.
First off, it comes with a body attachment and a lot of different heads, which is very nice. It also comes with a pink carrying bag. This was a great thought and is very appreciated even though it isn't the most attractive bag I've ever seen.
At first I was immediately disappointed with the product. The battery cover is difficult to open, and the head really isn't that strong. It seems like with any pressure at all it will stop rotating. I can't use this on my body with the wider body-brush attachment because of this. It just doesn't seem like it does much. The 'makeup' pad I tried out and just felt very weird, lol. I'm not a fan but maybe someone else would enjoy putting on/taking off makeup that way. The exfoliating head will MESS YOU UP. It doesn't play around and you don't need much pressure to get that to work on your skin. It feels like sandpaper being rubbed all over. Using it lightly is really recommended, especially on areas with thinner skin. The massage head with the rollers is the most 100% useless one. Like I said before, pretty much any pressure makes the head stop rotating. So if you try to use the massage head, it just will sit there. You might as well just take it in your had and rub it on yourself. The main head (for me), the actual facial cleaning one, is overall decent. I feel it does alright and, after a bit of trial and error, have found a balanced routine and end up enjoying the product.
Overall, I'm sure there are better ones out there but this is a pretty good starter kit.

EDIT: I was contacted by the company and they were extremely nice. They said they would make it so that the next 'batch' will have more of a resistance and won't stop working under so little pressure. They also are sending me a set of replacement heads, which is very sweet. Really great company!

text:
I like many others have been looking for COVID clippers. I have cheap Wahl corded clippers but they're loud and bog down. My kids hated getting their hair cut and I didn't enjoy it either. I was going to buy cordless Wahl Senior clippers until I found these. I figured if they don't perform, I'll just send them back. These aren't going anywhere.

Just as advertised they're incredibly quiet. The come perfectly setup and ready to go. The arm is a little tight but functions fine. Turn them on with a solid feeling switch and no clattering at all, just a nice buzz. The motor never bogged down even when removing bulk (though our hair isn't too thick) and had great results skin fading. The case is slightly bulky but feels good in the hand and materials all feel of a good quality. I cut both my kid's hair and my own and only ran down the battery 7%.

I only have two complaints. 1.) A bag would be very useful to keep it all together. The box can be used for that function but it would be much nicer to have a bag. 2.) The blade guards are limited on size (biggest 1/2") and fit a little loose. They're just basic plastic. The guards are Wahl compatible though so replacements are easy to come by.

Overall, for $50 I'm very happy with my purchase. As long as they hold up (which I'll update if I have problems) five stars.

title: A wonder device that put a stop to my elbow pain
text:
I didn't really know what to expect from an elbow brace. I didn't have any diagnosis either - just pain - so I wasn't even sure if what I was feeling would be addressed by this device. When I received it and put it on, I have to say that I was still skeptical. The inside of the brace is very soft, and I felt like I couldn't get the thing tight enough to even notice it being there. Feeling stupid for having purchased, I made a motion to start to remove the brace, and that's when it hit me. The motion that I just did with my wrist (supinate - turn my hand palm-up) would normally send a mild shock of pain up my arm.

That didn't happen this time. I checked it again. Same pain-free result.

I don't know how this thing does what it does, but it absolutely *DOES* work. I suppose I could Google it for you, but at the moment it's magic.

So, of course, I made it my goal to find the limits of the effectiveness of the pain-relief. Let's go lift weights! Well, it has its limits.

Since I received two of them in the package, I had my wife try one also. She actually plays tennis, so she's more familiar with people wearing these contraptions. The only complaint she had was about the Velcro closures... The Velcro extends out from under the fabric of the brace. That's not a problem in and of itself, but she kept trying to remove the brace by pulling on the end of the fabric, which seems the obvious place to lift but winds up damaging the device by separating the fabric cover from the Velcro underneath. That's a minor thing when you're talking about pain relief, so I decided to keep the five-star rating because I did not experience this confusion.

I received these elbow braces at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. I have tried to deliver facts to you that would assist you in your purchasing decision, and I hope you find this review helpful. If you have questions about the product or about my review of it, don't hesitate to add a comment and ask your question. I'm always happy to answer.

title: Color Me A Happy Camper
text:
In the late eighties I had access to very high quality food grade guar gum. The cleanest and purest and for all practical purposes extremely neutral in flavor. Eventually my Rolls Royce guar source dried up, and everything I purchased after that was decidedly NOT neutral in flavor. Here we are many years later with a new bag of guar gum up on the counter, and very little hope it will be any better than all the others.

Let's give it a shot: A favorite recipe (really a recipe concept) was to create a very stiff whipped cream from nothing more than dry nonfat milk powder, frozen fruit, guar gum, flavor extracts & some sweetener. There were a lot of different variations on this theme, which was always a major hit at many ladies' luncheons.

The mouth feel and textures generated by this concept could be anything from a soft serve ice cream to an unbelievable mountain of whipped cream just as light or as stiff as desired. All from the exact same quantity of starter ingredients. The more it's whipped, the greater the volume achieved. The only difference between two cups of soft serve ice cream or six cups of fluffy whipped cream was the addition of 2 tablespoons COLD water and simply continue whipping for a few minutes longer.

For today's test:
I tossed 1/3 cup dry NONFAT milk powder into the food processor along with a teaspoon of guar, 6 ounces FROZEN peach slices, half a teaspoon each of vanilla & almond extract, and some artificial sweetener. That's all. Flipped on the processor and let her run around 3 minutes This was long enough to dissolve the dry ingredients and allow my guar /frozen fruit/NONFAT milk powder combo -> to do its magic. AND IT DID. :) Color me a happy camper.

The textures achievable are just great. I give it five stars. Flavor-wise: The guar taste itself is very mild and completely acceptable. Four and half stars.

text: I got this pump for my second child (who is now 4 months old)and I LOVE it! It has made breast feeding SO much easier. This pump does not have as high of a suction because it isn't needed. Everyone commenting on the lack of power on here is what freaked me out about buying this. It using the whole suckling motion so you get the soft cups actually squeezing down and the suction together. It is totally comfortable and does just as good of a job if not better. When I switched over I did experience a lack of milk in pumping (it didn't decrease my milk supply though) but it only lasted about 2 days. I can pump 6oz with this pump in one sitting in about 15-20 minutes (and Im not an over-producer or anything). My parts wore out in about 3 months but I called customer service and they over-nighted (so I wouldn't be without a pump) new parts to me free of charge. Then called a few days later to make sure that fixed the problem and everything was working ok. I was a little nervous to go with this pump when I was looking for one but I am VERY glad I did. I tried carnuba wax, compound, and a clay bar. They all worked, just not very fast. I saw YouTube videos on how to remove paint overspray and a lot of pros recommended Rapid Remover.

Very Happy!!!

It's my first time using an electric toothbrush and I'm glad this is the brand that I tried!

The shape of the brush can reach the inner sides of my teeth, which I prefer over a small round brush. There's a lot of replacement heads and I picked the light purple. There are 6 different modes to choose from and I personally like the whitening, polish and sensitive. I love the design and idea of a silicon handle much better than plastic because of the grip and it doesn't slip of your hand even if it gets wet, unlike with a plastic handle. The battery life is unbelievably long! I only charged it once and I've been using it for almost a month now.

The device shuts off after 3-5 minutes, so you'll know you already did enough time for brushing. Such a great product! I didn't know the price of electric toothbrushes, so I thought it's a bit steep, but it's definitely cheaper than most brands and works just as well.

title: Best massager I have ever purchased!
text:
The Koo-Care Massager is the best massager i have ever purchased.  It feels close to real hands doing a kneading massage. 
Here is what I love about this massager:
• Excellent build quality - really nice leather.  I have been using the massager for about 3 months now (since May 2017) and no signs of it breaking or any wear and tear of the materials.
• The heating does not get hot; just a little warm and that is ok for me.  I don't really use the heat function I use a heat pad for that.
• The massage heads are strong.  The massager will stop if you put too much weight on it!; for example when using it on my lower back by laying on it.
• I love that it has a battery so I can use freely without being limited by a wall plug.
• I can take it with me in my car to get a quick massage.  Great for loosing up my back after morning traffic, during lunch time at work and before driving home after work.
• Finally a massager I can use between going to the spa that really digs deep into my lower back muscles.
• I use it on other parts of my body like hands, legs (feels really good on the upper legs)

Finally, I must say that the customer service at Koo-Care is excellent (the best I have ever experienced on Amazon).  The first unit I purchased from them had a defect and they sent me another Koo-Care massager free of charge!  I highly recommend them.

title: Impressed and happy. Passed 9 panel on short notice.
text: Backstory: Just under 6’ roughly 215lbs. Veteran. PTSD, depression, anxiety, back pain. Self medicating because other medicine is not enough, yet live in a state where it is not legal. Working at a company as a temp for quite awhile. They finally decided to higher me. Thought I would have two weeks to get clean so I bought a pack of 10 tests from Amazon figuring I would test every few days to track progress...but after four days, found out 9 panel test was just another two days away. Shocked, I bought this from my local head shop as an Amazon purchase wouldn’t have been delivered soon enough. I diluted with nearly a gallon of water the day before test. Next day, got up at 5:30 and drank 32oz of water. Then at 7:30 drank this. Followed directions and waited 10 minutes. Filled bottle up with water and drank it. Peed a couple times and started testing. After 4 or 5 pees, started to see a faint negative on tests. After four of those in a row, it was roughly 9:30 and I felt comfortable about testing negative. Had to be at test site before 10:59 so I planned to leave at 10:15 for a 15 minute drive.  Thought I was in the clear but I figured I’d test one more time before leaving. Popped positive. Thought I missed my window so I drank another 32oz of water and left in a hurry. Big mistake. Got to the facility and realized two people were ahead of me. After the second went in, someone with an apt. showed up and was placed ahead of me. I had to pee so bad, though, that I begged the woman to take me next. The other person was polite and willing seeing as I was now dancing like a three year old with crossed legs after having paced the floor. Took test. After a night of mental anguish and a morning of utter torture, my results came back negative. I got hired in full time with amazing benefits. No more night terrors for awhile as I can have my medicine again. Vale 4X saved my skin, but you really need to dilute. It will turn your urine bright yellow. If you smell the drink in your pee, it’s working. It masks the dilution by adding to the urine what would have normally been there minus the toxin. Overall, I’m really happy and impressed, but drink it quick. Once you start, DO NOT STOP because it is not delicious at all. I imagine it tastes as if it was real pee itself but wouldn’t know for sure as I’ve never drank urine, but drink Gatorade, too, to help wash it down. 10/10 would recommend, but I wouldn’t trust the 1 hr part. Took me longer than that to start peeing clean and that was after diluting with water.
