title: Finally getting my self-esteem back!!
text:
First of all, everyone understands how one's facial appearance is directly tied to one's self-esteem. For me, my self-esteem is directly tied to Cellbone's Prep Skin Refresher!!!! I won't ever stop using this product.

A little about me/my skin: I am a 42-yr old Asian-Pacific Islander and have medium-tone skin, which essentially translates into severe post-acne hyperpigmentation anytime I break out. I never broke out as a teenager so it was so strange to me that I started breaking out badly the last 2 years. (I attribute most of it to job-stress so I really figured there was nothing I could do about my poor complexion). I recently saw a photo of myself from 2009 where I had no makeup on, and I pratically cried. I had forgotten that I had GREAT skin up until recently. I had gotten into this vicious cycle as of late: wearing concealer & makeup to hide the dark hyperpigmentation, which I'm certain resulted in more breakouts = more hyperpigmentation. It was just awful!! I was at my wit's end. I couldn't get my skin under control even with prescription drugs.

In January, I began both salycylic & glycolic acid treatments, and those helped the hyperpigmentation somewhat. I continued to breakout a bit and was willing to suffer through the breakouts in hopes that things were merely getting worse before they would get better. In March, I took a nearly 3-week long trip to hot, dusty Tanzania (climbed Mount Kilimanjaro, went on safari, & then chilled out on Zanzibar). Well, I was without the comforts of home for the majority of that trip so I used pre-moistened face wipes & hot water (when it was available) to cleanse my face & always followed up with the Prep Skin Refresher. Translation: I was hot,sweaty, & dusty/dirty the majority of the time. My breakouts stopped "dead in their tracks," and my hyperpigmentation appeared to improve. Upon my return from my trip, I continued with the Prep Skin Refresher post-face wash and have only had 2 glycolic treatments since I returned.

I can't believe how my complexion is improving!! I'm actually not scared to look in the mirror now, and I'm no longer morbidly depressed about how I look without makeup. I know it's definitely this Cellbone product that has attributed to my vast improvement. (While the glycolic acid treatment does help, I'm only doing that every other week). I'm using the Prep Skin Refresher daily, usually in the a.m. & in the p.m. I haven't changed any other face, body, or hair products--so I know it wasn't an allergy. Again, I was using this product religiously when I was camping on Mount Kilimanjaro (hey, I didn't shower for 6 nights, but I still didn't break out!!!!)

I also have before & "so far" pictures, so I have an objective gauge as to my improvement. I would like my skin to get a bit better before I'm brave enough to post the pictures for you all, but stay tuned. I'll update this review when I get up enough nerve to add the pictures. I don't know what's in this stuff, but I SWEAR it's worth trying if you have acne/hyperpigmentation. I've been using this since the beginning of March, and I still have half the bottle left.

I hope others who are "suffering in silence" will give this a shot. I think it's a small price to pay to help your self-esteem! Also, Cellbone threw in 2 other free samples that I haven't tried yet (I didn't want to "waste" the product on my poor skin, but I'll try them this weekend). Cellbone: you have a customer for life. Please please please don't get rid of this Prep!!!

title: Works well but there are a few tradeoffs to consider
text:
I have previously purchased the black plastic (no spring) version of this button pant extender. The one thing that bothered me about the plastic version was that on about half of the pants that I tried it on, the whole thing came off when unbuttoned. You couldn't just leave it on a pair of pants. Here are the pros and cons of this "spring" version:

Pros:

Stays on when unbuttoned (unlike plastic version)
Stretches more than fixed plastic version - more adjustable
More comfortable than plastic version

Cons:

I personally prefer a less noticeable black button but other folks may like this silver color
The extra stretch unfortunately also means it is more likely to show your zipper - I recommend "shirt tail out" to hide it
They are somewhat more difficult to fasten and unfasten than the non-spring plastic ones.

Update:

For lounging around the house, these work fine. However, for walking somewhere outside, I find that I prefer linking two of the no-spring plastic ones together. It just feels a bit more secure and not quite so loose.

title: Rapidly and completely dissolves; tastes good enough to drink every day, for months.
text:
Don't expect this to taste like a bowl of fresh peaches. Think canned, maybe? It works well enough, definitely not sweet like candy, and doesn't taste like the dirt flavor I get from many stevia-sweetened products. Granted I don't care too much about the taste of protein supplements: I certainly don't hate this flavor with the fury of some others who reviewed it. I don't mind it, although I like the peach flavor from the other (i.e. not "Naturals") line better. I have been drinking this every day for just about 3 months, and I'm not tired of the flavor, which is saying quite alot actually. The powder itself dissolved rapidly and fairly completely with just a bit of spoon-stirring.

TIP: stir the powder into water for a bit to get most of the powder into solution, and then let it sit for a minute or so. I've found that most of the small clumps actually break up on their own this way. Then you can stir it just a few more times, and it's perfect. If you shake this up in a shaker, be prepared for massive foaming- it is a protein mix, with no surfactants, so that's what is going to happen. Don't do it, unless you want to waste protein by making into foam, and then drying to drink the mess without coating your beard or face in foamy whey protein and smelling like peaches.

text: We have a Sonic care toothbrush, and these replacement heads fit it. I did notice that the toothbrush heads are shorter than the originals. title: Great - After a Small Tweak
text:
When I first used this, the tip would stop spinning as soon as it touched my tooth. I could not polish at all. It's not that the motor is too weak or that the parts are too flimsy, it's that the motor shaft was slipping as it turned inside the tip holder.

I removed the holder and placed a tiny bit of the polishing paste inside it. I then pressed the holder back onto the motor shaft. This totally solved the problem. The motor has plenty of torque and does not stall. I was quite impressed at how easily stains were removed.

I'd give the device five stars except that not everyone will figure out how to fix the slipping problem and would have an essentially nonfunctional item. Also, the head of the unit is way to big to allow polishing the back teeth unless one has a very big mouth (literally).

title: Great for dribblers
text:
Okay, well, I got the Oscars yesterday from Amazon, which means I think they shipped 'em before I actually placed the order. Unbelievable.

The first thing any manufacturer of any cloth diaper will tell you is that you have to wash it first or they won't be absorbent. Apparently there is "sizing" still on the fabric, and that acts as a water-resistant barrier till it's washed off. Let me be clear that I have NOT yet washed these, and today I didn't ask much of them. I don't feel like I can really say much about their absorbency, but that won't stop me. ;-)

First is the fit, which is tight. These run small, so be aware. I know they need to be snug in order to not have gaps wetness can get through, but these are really tight.

That aside, they fit well, coming up high enough in front and back. Also, the material in front--what your "tender bits" rub against all day, is very, very soft. The pad, just as advertized, goes up all the way in front and back, and--hazzah!--is full-width in front. Conni says there is an opening, and there is, but I have no idea how it could be a functional fly. I'm guessing it's there for those using a catheter or something. Honestly, I can't imagine being able to twist and wind your dude through that. But the point is that, unlike nearly every other brief I've tried, the "fly" in no way compromises or reduces the size of the pad.

I don't expect these to be very capacious, and press-out might be a serious issue when sitting, but these aren't a replacement for disposable absorbent underwear or diapers. If you need discreet protection that fits well and holds a few bursts, get the Depend Real Fit (it pains me to say that Depend has finally done something right, but they did). But if you have some dribbling and need something that will keep your fly dry, after a few washings I'm willing to bet these will be great. I'll wash them a couple times and let you know.

title: Good for safety, but not ideal for sound quality.
text: I have used these ear plugs at a couple of concerts and I do find that they help in protecting my ears from getting damaged. title: WOW!
text:
I really wish I'd taken some "before" pictures but, to be honest, I did NOT think this stuff would work half as well as it did! My Jeep has full aluminum fenders from GenRight Offroad and they were looking pretty oxidized and stained by different types of dirt and mud.

READ AND FOLLOW THE DIRECTIONS.

I originally started with a 15:1 mix like it says on the bottle and watched it bubble up like hydrogen peroxide as soon as I started it on the metal. The first round, I only let it set on the metal for maybe 10-15 seconds before I wiped it with a microfiber towel. Still, the results were instant and obvious. After two cycles of spraying 15:1, letting it sit for 20 seconds or so and wiping it, I upped to a 12:1 mixture and let it sit for about 30 seconds. I could not believe it was that easy. Mix, spray, wipe evenly, rinse with water. The aluminum came out looking better than it did when I first got it! After I got everything shined up nicely, I hit it all with some aluminum sealant to protect it and keep it looking as good as it does.

I only used about 6 ounces out of the gallon. With 120 ounces remaining, I'm not going to run out for a long time! Very happy overall, definitely recommend if you've got some aluminum you want to look like new.

text:
[[VIDEOID:6858992263dbac023a6a6e2eb9aa9f53]] I purchased two of these cushions to use with my dining room chairs. The cover that comes with this cushion is slippery and dangerous.

When I unpacked the boxes (which were identical), I quickly noticed that they came with two separate covers. One was a black cover with slippery beads on the bottom, and the other is gray with honeycomb grips. I initially reached out to Customer Service shortly after getting them, and they told me that "yes, indeed the box is unmarked, and no I can not get another cover unless I purchase it."

I shrugged it off as poor customer service and decided to live with two mis-matched covers - not the worst thing in the world. I've owned them for about 8 months now, and the black cover has become more and more slippery. Several times people have slipped off the chair with it, and I've since banned my kids from using the one with the black cover.

But we paid $80 for each of these and the cushions themselves are very comfortable. So I decided I would reach out to sales and purchase the gray cover, which doesn't slip. After talking with sales, they're not even aware that there IS a second cover, and I could "gamble" and buy another black cover. What kind of customer service is that? Do they not even care if people get hurt? This company obviously cares little about safety and even less about customer satisfaction, so I won't be purchasing anything from them again.

My recommendation: Buy this if you are using this without the cover or like to live life on the edge (literally).

title: Design flaws limit use, may create risks
text: I am a post-polio survivor, and have used crutches for over 60 years. While the general quality of the Medline units was similar to others, I have (after several attempts) noticed design flaws, relative to my 20+ year old forearm crutches. The distance between the handhold and the crutch body is too short, forcing one's hands against that shaft. My old ones are at least 1/2" further away. When the Medlines arrived, one cuff was almost 1/2" wider at its mouth than the other, too wide to hold a male's arm, unless he's a longshoreman or body builder. I ordered a pair of replacement cuffs, which took 3 weeks to arrive. I then noticed that they (and the originals) had too much rotational play, i.e., the cuffs rotated slightly with each step I took. The holes that held the cuff to the shaft are slightly too large, allowing the rotation. This was sufficient to create both balance issues and wear on the forearms of my shirt sleeves. I will donate these units, which are OK for short term use by a recovering person, but not acceptable for someone who will use them on a continuous basis.

title: Not quite what I hoped for
text:
I was hoping that this device would actually wake me up at a good point but before I was already awake. What I've found is that just as I wake up (am consciously aware of it anyway), the watch alarm then goes off. I can't recall a single time in 2.5 months that it actually woke me out of a light sleep (at a possible waking moment). That said, I have been getting up earlier since I started using the watch, possibly because it reminds me that I should not go back to sleep after a light wakeup. If I were just basing my review on the above, I'd only give it one or two stars.

But I gave it three because I'm finding that it does help me to assess my sleep and cross reference that with different things like if I had a late dinner the night before, if I exercised the day before, if I drank alcohol, etc. This information combined with the Data A value (average duration of full sleep intervals) are useful information.

All that said, I don't think this watch is for everyone. And the software that comes with it is pretty basic and could be "A LOT" better which suggests that it was the minimal effort needed. Makes me wonder about how serious a device it really is (as opposed to a gimmick).

As others had noted, the vibration and audible alarms are not sufficient to wake people out of a deep sleep.

If I knew then what I know now, I'm not sure I would purchase this again, considering it's price.

title: templet not correct and screw heads too large.
text: Templet for the bulbs was correct as were the top holes but the bottom holes were an inch off. Note, do not remove the back cover sheet and expose the sticky back. You will have a lot of trouble getting the templet off. Instead tape the templet  to the duct. Also get some real sheet metal screws say #6 x 1/2". Measure the head of the screw and get a drill bit the same size and drill open the key slots on the unit so the screw head will go thru. Cut out the two large bulb holes on the duct first making sure they match location with the actual bulb sockets before you cut. Put unit without bulbs on the duct making sure you are centered and mark the top of the key slots. My top slots were very close to the templet. Remove unit and drill the top two screw holes and put screws in and hang the unit making sure you slide to the end of the screw slots. Now mark the top of the bottom screw slots, remove unit, drill bottom holes and put in screws. Rehang unit to make sure all screw holes fit. Remove unit and install bulbs making sure they are tight. DO NOT TOUCH THE GLASS ON THE BULBS, if you do get some alcohol and clean the glass. Carefully insert the bulbs and unit into duct over the screws and slide down. Tighten screws snugly but not over tighten or you might strip the threads. Hope this helps.

title: Stop spending so much on name brand razors!
text:
Update June 2021

My original review is below. I can't believe Ive been shaving with this for a year already! I was prepared for it to be disposable since the whole thing cost less than genuine Norelco Replacement blades. But I'm still on my original set and they still cut good.

Some things I've seen in the last year I don't like:

A piece fell off the back of the shaver head. It is cosmetic only as it doesn't affect the hair collection. It's just annoying that it did. But replacement heads that are only about $15 will fix that issue.

Another thing I don't like is how little hair can be stored before it needs to be emptied. I have to empty it after everu shave or it doesn't collect any more and it just gets all over me. Sometimes if it's been a day or two I have to empty it during the shave.

Those are minor issues and since it has worked so good and still cuts well a year later, I wish I could give it another star. Seriously don't worry about if it's a decent product. It is!

Original Review June 2020
Ever since I started shaving around 35 years ago, I've been using Norelco Shavers. The last several I've bought were Waterproof and came with systems to automatically charge and clean my razor. I didn't think I could get any better than that. The reality is they didn't work so well. My first auto clean razor didn't last even a year. The mechinism part that does the cleaning broke. So I bought a different one here on Amazon. While it does still clean and charge my razor, the price of the replacement heads have been getting more and more expensive. Currently their replacement heads are nearly $60. I tried some sold here in Amazon thay are obviously after market heads. While they are sharp they don't hold the heads in place right so they end up snagging your hair. That is the state I found myself in. Pay $60 for genuine Norelco heads for my razor that's now 5 years old or try something else. I found this razor for just over $40. I was skeptical as I've been conditioned to belive that one has to spend $200+ on a razor if you want it to work. But at only $40 it's about the price of the cheap replacement blades and I figured it couldnt be worse than those.

So here's what I think of this new razor!

I love the shape. At first glance it seemed weird. But I had already been holding my Norelco this way instead of using the handle which isn't very ergonomic.

The shave is awesome! I haven't had a shave this close in years. And since the heads are actually smaller in diameter they even reach right up to my nose which the Norelco really struggled to do.

I like it that this one is also Waterproof so I can wash it under the faucet.

Some concerns I have:

The charging cable is a very tight fit. And since the razor is so light compared to my Norelco, I was genuinely afraid I was going to break it when I plugged it in to shave. It did finally go in and on the plus side, I can charge it anywhere since it uses a standard USB plug.

As I mentioned it is very light. Much lighter than a Norelco. Does that mean it's cheap and will break soon? I don't know. So far it's a champ. If it breaks soon, I'll be back here to post an update.

This model has a built in led light. It's supposed to make it where you can shave in the dark. First, I don't generally shave in the dark. Second, I don't think they give enough light to make a difference. It would be better if that energy was saved so the shaver could go longer in between charges.

This shaver comes with more attachments than any I've ever seen. Honestly I won't be using most of them.

Some of these are advertised as head Shavers for those who prefer to go bald. While I'm sure it would work great for that, don't worry if you want to only shave your face. It works great as a face shaver.

In sum up, I can't believe I was able to be shaved so well by a razor that is so inexpensive. Even if it only lasts 6 months, and I have to buy a new one, it's less expensive than Norelco. I think I'm done with the big name brand. I know their razors don't cost so much to make. So I'm tired of making them rich and having to shave with dull blades too long since I cannot afford to drop $60 every 6 months.

I'd buy this again and I'll reccomend it to friends!

I TOTALLY recommend giving this a shot if you need something to block out noisy neighbors, roommates, partners snoring or just general background noise.

title: Too mired by issues to be an effective sleep aid...
text:
I really liked this thing at first, but after about two nights of using it I quickly realized a lot of stuff I don't like about it.

-Half of the sounds are four second loops. And when something loops for four seconds, and you have trouble falling asleep, you'll start to quickly be irritated by hearing the exact same sound every four seconds. For the rain sound, for instance, would it have been so hard to capture more than four seconds of rain?
-The volume buttons are on the bottom, so when you want to adjust the volume, you have to pick it up and fumble with them. This wouldn't be so much of a problem if every sound didn't have vastly different dynamic levels. If you have the volume mid level, some of them are quiet as a mouse, but some of them are loud enough to make your ears ring.
-For a device that's supposed to help you sleep, they neglected one MAJOR no-no for sleep aid devices--if there's any light which most negatively affects your sleep, it's bright white light. There's a reason alarm clocks pretty much all come in a muted red color--red doesn't do much to keep you awake. The darker you can make your room, the better you'll sleep. This thing has a VERY bright white light that can't be turned off, and unless you cover it with a shirt or something, it will keep you awake.
-Each of the sounds has some kind of weird overtone within the loop that you will quickly notice. If you, like me, have trouble sleeping because of an overactive mind that dwells on fine details, these will drive you wild. The stream noise, for instance, is a short loop that ends in some kind of noise that sounds like a trampoline spring being compressed. Hard to notice unless your listening for it, but when the loop is four seconds, it becomes all you notice. And it's very annoying. All of these loops have weird little parts like that. I ended up keeping it on ocean because its weird overtone is the least perceptible of them all.

Besides that, it's an attractive little device and the dial is smooth and easy to use.

title: Cool case, plugs not great for helmets.
text:
These arrived on time, packaged well. The container with screw top is cool, and the little clip attaches to my motorcycle's tank bag zipper, so ear the plugs are really accessible, even when I'm ready to ride. I was hoping to find reduction in white noise inside my helmet, that didn't interfere with hearing my gps directions in my helmet comms. I was interested in this product because of the promise of moderate noise attenuation -- old school foam plugs reduce by 30bB, whereas these were more like 15ish.

The ear plugs themselves are awkward to put into my ears, particularly with medium-long nails. The shape of these is like a teeny tiny umbrella. You hold the little post between your fingers and insert the cup portion into your ear.

I bought them to combat the mostly white noise that comes with long distance motorcycling, as I'm close to heading out to ride parts of Route 66.

What was the biggest disappointment is with my helmet on, the wind noise actually transfers from the helmet, to the ear-plug "post", magnifying the wind noise with an odd thumping sensation, much like when someone opens the back windows of the car on the freeway. I literally pulled over on the freeway shoulder, took off my helmet, and yanked out the ear plugs -- threw them into the garbage when I got home! I've gone back to the old school foam plugs to cut white noise, but keep them in the container that came with this purchase. I wasn't happy, but my use was specifically for motorcycling. They may work for you if you're not planning on utilizing them with a helmet.

title: 'Nerd' is not a bad word!
text:
Assuming that your glasses are properly fitted for your face, but you still have problems keeping your glasses from sliding off due to oily skin, or sweat, Nerdwax can help. It's formulated to be just tacky enough to stick, but not too sticky as to mess up your glasses.

I couldn't find a comprehensive ingredient list, but Nerdwax is a beeswax-based blend of natural and organic, cosmetic-grade ingredients. It looks like a tube of lip balm, but it's tackier. Apply it by rubbing some on the nose pads or the part of the frame that touches your nose (you can even apply it to the earpieces, if you don't have hair back there to get in the way.)

I mostly sit in the A/C, so I just apply a thin layer. It lasts a couple of hours on my oily skin. If I were in sweatier conditions, or moving around more, I could definitely apply a thicker layer, or build layers up throughout the day. It's easy to apply, and removes with a paper towel.

I didn't experience any breakouts or allergic reactions using Nerdwax. I didn't even really find that it left a residue behind. It's a great short-term solution for keeping my glasses where they're supposed to be. I do wish it lasted a little longer on my oily skin... and I wish it didn't look so much like my lipbalms, because I don't want to mix them up!
(I received this product for review purposes. My opinions are my own. For more information and pictures, please see my blog, Lit From Within.)

text:
Shipping took 3 weeks to get to the US west coast.
Battery leads (just like most LiPo packs I've ordered from China) had the polarity swapped. Easy to fix, just carefully pop out one lead with a jeweler's screwdriver, wrap the metal pin with electrical (insulative tape), then remove the other lead, then swap the connector positions. Took all of 2 minutes while being extra careful to not short out the pack.

Used this battery in a GameBoy RetroPi build and it fits with ease in the standard location (with double sided tape). This pack powers a Kite Circuit Sword CM3 board for a solid 5 to 6 hours playing PSX games.

This product is great for boosting your energy during a workout. I typically use it on those days I feel sluggish, sore, or unmotivated. It really helps me to get through those last 15 seconds of a hard set. I would definitely use it and buy it again but I HAVE to give it 4 stars for the following reasons:
1. The taste. It tastes like lemon peel and stevia mixed together, with a faint chemical/vitamin flavor. I hork it down and shudder a little, and I think the reason some people love it and some hate it is the stevia - if you don't mind the flavor of stevia, you will probably love it.

You have to hold the power button down for a while for it to turn on- longer than 1 second.
Brush one: had the strongest vibration, but hardly heated up, and didn’t chill that much. I sent this one back.
Brush two: good vibration and chill functions. Heat function gets very hot, slowly cools to warmish, then super hot again. I kept this one. Over time the heating and chilling functions have become less strong, but the vibrating function still works well.
Bottom line is they tried to pack too many functions into one small inexpensive devise. I think to make a devise that was truly good hearing, cooling and vibration that it would cost quite a bit more. I would not buy it again.
I did appreciate that it came in minimal packaging (no plastic), but the plastic base it comes with is unnecessary, ugly, and the brush doesn’t even sit well in it.

title: Beautiful, smells great, regulates humidity well
text:
Update: Since writing the review I have determined using other hygrometers that the digital hygrometer included with this humidor is reading low. The humidor was actually holding dead on 70%.

Original review:
I've used a tiny little humidor for years, and it's always just been a little too small. So I picked this one up.

The appearance is beautiful, and the cedar smells wonderful. There is plenty of room, including for longer cigars that would not fit at all into my smaller humidor. I like the acrylic window. This humidor comes with a digital hygrometer and a humidor-bead-based humidifier. For the moment I have my both under the window where I can watch them as I tweak things, but eventually they'll go on the underside of the lid once I'm satisfied I have things set up the way I want them. There was a set of instructions that came with the humidor. I certainly appreciate instructions, but they were slightly lacking. Seasoning instructions as well as instructions on the use of the humidor beads would have been appreciated.

After seasoning the humidor, I've let it sit for a good long while to see how well it regulates humidity. I've never used humidor beads before, and, as suggested by the instructions, I'm also using humidor fluid (propylene glycol / distilled water 50-50 mix) for my first time so I'm still in the learning curve. As such it's regulating a little lower than I'd like it to so I still have things to tweak. But, and this is the major point, it's regulating solidly- meaning the humidor is doing its job. Through strong external humidity swings, both above and below the internal humidity, the internal humidity might as well have been on a rail. In fact, I had to take the hygrometer out of the humidor for a while to make sure it was even still working, and of course it was.

Very pleased!

title: Is this really SAM-E?
text:
Not convinced that this is SAM-E. It's cheaper, in capsules, and 500 mg. However, instructions are to take it with a meal. Anyone who takes SAM-e knows you have to take it one hour before or two hours after a meal. There are inspiring certifications on the bottle, but one is FDA. I have never seen any mention of FDA on a nonpharmaceutical supplement. Label declares that contents have been assayed. Seems like the label already says some pretty questionable things.
So... After taking one capsules pre-breakfast and one pre-dinner, for over 3 weeks, I was seriously questioning the efficacy. Today I took two capsules before breakfast, and felt nothing. If I had taken two 400mg tabs of Jarrow, Nature Made, or Doctor's Best, at one time, I would have been crawling up the walls. I learned early on that 1200 mg was too much for me in a day. 800 is excellent. But clearly 1000 mg of WELOVEVITAMINS SAM-E was not doing what I expected.
Granted, it's a new company. Perhaps the Sam-e isn't stored at a low temperature? Is it even possible to deliver Sam-e in a gel-cap?

Regardless, I'd ordered two bottles, and I'll be returning the second one. This may be less expensive, but if it's not SAM-E, then it's not much of a savings!

To the manufacturer...the guy with the good intentions: show us the assays and quality Certification that the ingredients in your pills are what they purport to be. Could be this brand just doesn't work for me.

title: Bright White = 3000K, Soft White = 2700K
text:
I generally think this is an AMAZING price for this product. I would preface it by saying that the color temperature of these lights are 3000K! This looks (in my unprofessional opinion) like 5000K or "daylight" CFLs. I enjoy the 2850K GE Reveal light bulbs and I really like the L Prize 2700K from Philips compared to these 3000K ones, but they are half the price. Be very aware that this is 3000K, I believe 3000K looks really nice in the bathroom / tiled room, but somewhat off putting on its own. I use a combination of the L Prize 2700K and 3000K in my apartment (12 bulbs = 10_3000K 2_2700K) and it really works for me. If you are used to "daylight" CFLs, go for these ASAP as they use a lot less energy and are suitable for rapid on/off.

//Not sure if Amazon will delete this, but I paid ~$27 for a 2-pack at HomeDepot [if you delete, please just change to "Other Retailer"] for these, which is by far the cheapest I have seen LED lightbulbs so far. These are NOT rated for closed light fixtures, but I put them in there anyway just to see how fast they would degrade (Hoping to upgrade to newer LEDs as the tech evolves).

Economics:
$14 per bulb @ 10.5 Watt vs 60 Watt. ~ 83% lighting energy savings.
Long rated life and rapid on/off makes this a no-brainer for bathroom application.

Style:
Color Temperature of 3000K much worse than 2850K or 2700K.
Beautiful Spherical Incandescent Style (vs. buglight LED design or nasty coil CFLs)

Performance:
Enclosed Fixture (TBD) - So far, glass is barely warm to the touch, seems fine to me. Even if it loses its life in 3 years vs its ridiculous 18 year rated life, I will be perfectly happy. Plus I want the new color changing LED tech from Philips Hue and LIFX in the future anyway.
Cheap ceiling facing IKEA lamps - seems to run as cool as my L Prize 2700K bulb, although I have no fears for the L Prize since it is torture test rated by the US Department of Energy.

Brightness:
800 Lumens means nothing to me, I think you need at least 4 of these lights to really brighten up a room (~300 sqft).

Tips for Philips:
Please explain the difference in manufacturing process vs. the L Prize bulbs. Is the only difference color temp & these are made in China (vs. L Prize made in USA)?

4 stars for being the cheapest LEDs around.

title: Extremely Inaccurate
text:
At first I was extremely excited about my new aria. I've owned a fitbit for a few months and was excited to add this to my exercise gadget arsenal. My wife and I both use the product and noticed during our first week that the scale's readings seemed extremely off. We re-calibrated and tested it again which gave us a slightly more accurate reading.

We've kept a very consistent pattern for measuring our weight: Always on a Friday, always first thing in the morning prior to food or drink (in a fasted state) and always in the exact same location. Each week our readings have been extremely spiky in an impossible way.

The thing that seems to be most off is the body fat% reading (honestly, the most important measurement). I somehow went from 16% body fat one week to 46 the next, back down to 20 something and then spiked up to 60. If I had been eating or drinking a lot prior to the weigh ins, I'd expect this, but with keeping our same fasted state each time this just seems too wildly inconsistent (especially for the price).

The actual weight measurements are off by about 2 pounds each time as well and vary by as much as 6 pounds just by stepping off of the scale and back on.

I was concerned about these measurements so went to my local gym to have my bf% professionally measured and found that the scale hasn't been anywhere accurate at any point in time. I also tested several other body weight scales and found that I was consistently two pounds heavier than the scale reported to me (while still in a fasted state).

Overall, for the price paid, I was expecting a lot more from this scale. I'll definitely be returning it this weekend .

title: Lots of Steam
text: I have never owned a steamer before, and had to go online to look up what this could even do for me after I purchased it.  (It came "free" with my purchase of a Soniclean vacuum cleaner.)  Since I could find not a single review anywhere on the web of this particular device, I thought I would share my experience.  I found the size and shape of it to be quite comfortable.  My 8-year-old daughter was able to use it easily (with me watching closely!)  The biggest thing about it is that when it is left on the highest setting, it produces remarkable amounts of steam!  I ran it at full blast for probably 30 minutes before it ran out of water.  That was enough to clean both sides of my queen-size mattress on one occasion, and enough to clean all the grout in a full sized shower on another occasion.  The steam button is conveniently placed on the handle, and the lock feature is wonderful (I have four small children in the house!)  The attachments are the cheap part of this steamer.  The squeegee head was slightly warped and left streaks on my window, the furniture cleaning pad has elastic that is starting to come off right out of the box, and the bristles on the scrubbing head were all permanently melted and bent after a single shower scrubbing session.  I would rather have cheap accessories that I can replace on a solidly built body that will last a long time, than the other way around, so I can live with that.  Also, the instructions are barely there, basically just a picture of the device and all the attachments, so be prepared to look things up online if you have never used a handheld steamer before.  There is a mistake on the instructions, and that is when it says it take 30 seconds for steam to form.  I timed it at 2:52.  Just under 3 minutes is a fine time frame for me, just not what they claim it is.  After trying it out all over the house, I found that my favorite use for it is washing windows.  It takes 10 seconds to squeegee the window, another 30 seconds to wipe up the puddles along the bottom, and voila, clean windows!  It was worth $50 just for that!  Just find a 50-foot extension cord before you start, so you can do the whole house in one grand rush.  I am giving this steamer three out of five stars, and adding an extra star for the Soniclean company, because they were very communicative and helpful with a service issue I had with the vacuum cleaner that I bought at the same time.

title: Perfect clutch for my waver
text:
[[VIDEOID:7f58e72415c0d371f50e843539ba1cd2]] I do not have the 32 mm waver from Mermaid; in fact, this the first item that I own from this brand. But I was in need for a carrying bag just like this one for my 32 mm triple barrel waver from another manufacturer.
It is not easy to find a proper bag or case for such a big hair tool. That's when I found this wonderful clutch that is not only big but also comes attached to a heat resistant mat that ads an extra layer of cushioning to the equipment inside. This combo makes it perfect for traveling, just keep in mind that this is not shock-proof or water resistant as a hard case.
I consider this bag a universal size for storage. If you see in the attached video and pictures, I tried to ilustrate how roomy the bag is, not only for the waver, but also for other large hair tools like my big Revlon 1Step volumizer, the Revlon 1Step Plus (which is longer than the original), even my extra long flat iron and my curling wand fit together!
About the design, it is not very trendy, the pink color is probably too bright for me. The velcro in the middle of the heat resistant mat is somewhat annoying, you have to be careful not to put a hot tool right on top of it or else it will ruin it. Once everything is wrapped up, the safety buckle will secure everything in place. So, in the end, what is really important to me is the functionality of the product, and this one truly honors the purpose for what it was intended.
I think this combination of a heat mat and carrying clutch is a great resource to keep my hair tools protected.
I highly recommend it.

I was no longer able to ride my bike as I could not hold the handlebars without pain. Like many others I was willing to try anything for relief although with skepticism. I can now report that Flexcin did improve my situation. I can now ride my bike and the swelling and pain has diminished considerably while my flexibility has improved a lot. I followed instructions exactly . I was thinking of quitting the trial after 6 weeks as I had not seen any benefit. I decided to go a full two months and one day after about 7 weeks I woke up with an almost unbelievable improvement in the pain and swelling. I wondered if I was fooling myself but it continued to improve each day and it has sustained the improvement as long as I stay on the maintenance dose. To be clear my wrist is not recovered to its full strength or flexibility  and I do some swelling but I can say the benefit I get is well worth the cost.

title: Waited about 2 months to write a review
text:
I live in a 1 bedroom apartment that has a silverfish problem and sometime an issue with cockroaches during the warmer months. I installed these ultrasonic pest repellers while the weather was still cool, one in my bedroom and one in between the kitchen and living area. During the first couple of weeks, I noticed the spiders that like to sleep in the corners of my living room eventually leave. I always assumed they were dead but after installing these repellers, I realized that they were alive and well after all. I've noticed only one cockroach since installation and a handful of silver fish. I used to see at least 2 silverfish a day slithering along my walls but now, it's seldom. It took me a while to write the review because I figured as soon as I wrote the review, I would begin seeing the little pests more frequently.

I also love that they don't seem to bother my dog. However, the repeller in my bedroom makes a clicking sound while the one in my living area/kitchen does not.

Overall, I'm satisfied with the product because the exterminator coming by to spray was unhelpful.

title: Absolutely Outstanding Product
text:
[[ASIN:B002AI6DVA O' Berry 3137 Linoleum/Hardwood Squeeeeek No More At Joist Screws 50 ct]][[ASIN:B0006IK8YE [[ASIN:B0006IK8YE O Berry Enterprises 3233 Squeek No More Kit]]]][[ASIN:B000H5WV1Y O Berry Enterprises 325[[ASIN:B001L1FRW8 O'Berry Squeak No More Kit With Additional 250 bonus Screws]]1 Replacement screws]][[ASIN:B004LY9CF0 Counter-Snap Kit Replacement Screws - 500 pack]][[ASIN:B002AI6DVA O' Berry 3137 Linoleum/Hardwood Squeeeeek No More At Joist Screws 50 ct]]

This is an outstanding product that solves an otherwise insoluble problem--squeaky hardwood floors. The white oak hardwood floors upstairs in my 1936 house were so squeaky that we could not go anywhere upstairs unaccompanied by the sound of groaning and squeaking floors. Several contractors told me there was nothing that could be done to correct the condition--which turned out to be wrong, thanks to this product.

To use this system successfully, however, you have to know exactly what you are doing. The descriptions in Amazon.com about which products to buy and how to use them is confusing and incomplete. On my first try I got it wrong and placed more than 40 screws with very disappointing results. I then watched the process as demonstrated by Patrick O'Berry on YouTube ([...]) and I saw right away what I was doing wrong. I then proceeded to drive about 400 screws into 1500 square feet of hardwood floors using O'Berry's method and solved my squeaking floor problems completely. I could barely believe it: I went from having a major problem to having no squeaking problem at all.

One essential step is to place the screws where the hardwood grain will conceal the screw holes. Oak grain has plenty of places where the screw holes will not be visible. Other essential practices--all demonstrated in the O'Berry You Tube clip--include the step of drilling test holes to make sure you are hitting the joists before you start trying to screw the hardwood down. The test hole is necessary because a stud finder, even a very sophisticated one, won't reliably locate a joist through 1-1/2 inches of hardwood and subfloor and the random pattern of nails that pin the hardwood to the subfloor. Also notice carefully the differences between the at-the-joist and between-the-joist screws and the respective stand-off tools (O'Berry calls these tools "jigs" or "fixtures") used for each type of screw--they are superficially similar but each tool is designed to snap the screws at different locations. These differences are mentioned in the O'Berry You Tube demonstration. Unfortunately, Amazon at present supplies only a carpet kit and one of the two necessary types of standoff fixtures for hardwood floors (for the at-the-joist screws), so you will need to purchase the between-the-joist standoff jig from a specialty online supplier of squeaky floor tools.

I got equally good results eliminating squeaks in carpeted floors laid over 3/4 inch plywood subflooring. Again, Patrick O'Berry's You Tube demonstration makes the process very clear. ([...]). The carpet standoff jig looks like a three-legged crab, but it uses the same kind between-the-joist screws as are used for hardwood floors. Also, in this case, a stud finder should be able to locate the joists because there is only one nailing pattern and one layer of wood, if that's what you have. Carpeting over hardwoods, however, would need to be screwed down using the hardwood method.

While getting the hang of the process I also called O'Berry Enterprises with some questions, and Patrick O'Berry answered the phone. So good help is available if you need it.

title: Item description is misleading but otherwise it is pretty awesome.
text:
This is my first foray into trying an air purifier. I was looking for something to aid the dehumidifier in my 700 square foot basement. Not knowing much about what to look for, I wanted something that could help with the litter box smells, possibility limit any mold spores and keep the air quality in the basement a bit better.

I was immediately met with disappointment when I looked at the box the item came in and it said 500 sq ft right on the front. Reading more, I did find that it will circulate air for 1000, but at a much lower rate and not be quite as effective. The effect is that the litter box is still noticeable for quite a while after the cat uses it, making me uncertain about how it is doing for the rest of the air quality.

I did test that in our bathroom after repainting in there. It worked great at keeping the air nice and fresh smelling in there, but that is only a 100 square foot space. It was quite remarkable. You could smell the paint as you walked to the bathroom, but when you opened the door, you could not tell there was wet paint in there. So the thing works awesome for smaller spaces. We are going to move this one to our bedroom, and look for something larger for the basement, or possibly get a second one of these for the basement and run two down there.

title: Does Not work on Android. The Android sleep app is not the one you need.
text:
I bought this product in 2018 and enjoyed it for a few months before I stopped using it. I recently wanted to use it again and I don't have the same phone or the original log-in information. They emailed me log-in info but I couldn't get the app to work. After 2 messages with the seller I finally figured out what the problem is.

The app you need to use is called Sweetsleep, with no space between the words and is only found on the Apple App store for iPhone and iPad. So it worked on my old iPhone.

In the android Play store, there is an app called Sweet Sleep with a space between the words. It's not the same app and does not track your sleep patterns. It only plays music. So I can't use this with my Samsung S10.

I hope this helps people having the same issue.

title: For Tendinitis Aid: Great Value and Worthwhile Bands
text:
I have tendinitis in both arms...golf elbow in one arm and tennis elbow in the other. My physical therapist recommended that I buy arm braces so that I could resume my daily activities faster. The more you inflame your tendons the longer it will take to heal. The arm braces help to prevent further aggravating the tendinitis. ***They will not heal you.*** It seems odd that simply pressing on the tendons prevents inflammation, but I must say that the arm braces really are helping me. Find the place in your elbow that hurts when you touch or press on it and then place the bump in the band about an inch below your elbow in that same spot. I wear the braces when I know that I will be lifting items or doing activities that aggravate my arms. I do not wear them to sleep.

I bought these bands because they were priced low and had great reviews. It was cheaper to buy 4 bands than 2 at the time I purchased them, so now I have two extras that I will probably never use! I am happy with the quality of these bands. They seem like they will outlast my need for them. I recommend them highly for golf or tennis elbow tendinitis.

I ordered the professional scale because I intended to use it outside most of the time. The case is metal, the numbers easy to read, the controls easy to use and the setup is straightforward with clear instructions.

To test the scale accuracy I hung it in my basement, rigged a sling and weighed 6 10lb bags of sugar. The scale recorded 60.1 lbs. I weighed each bag of sugar individually and the weights added up to 60.1.

I next rigged up a device that I could use to weigh myself, zeroed out the weight of the device using the Tare button and recorded my weight. I then compared that number to the weight displayed when stepping on my bathroom scale. The weight totals differed by 1.5 lbs at approx 185lbs.

I am totally satisfied with this scale. If that feeling ever changes I will modify this review.

text:
First this product is made specifically for MEN. I have seen reviews from women on here and while I'm sure it's safe for them to use, it's good to note this is MADE FOR MEN! It should be noted that DAA has been studied to have great benefits for men, especially those over 40.

D-Aspartic acid is a natural compound that is synthesized within the human body
D-Aspartic acid has a distinct biological role separate from l-aspartic acid
There is evidence that D-Aspartic acid may be more effect for males over 40, who have naturally reduced testosterone levels relative to their youthful counterparts
The general recommended dose of D-Aspartic acid is 3g per day

D-Aspartic Acid - The Edge on Testosterone:
Testosterone is the single most important hormone responsible for the varying masculine characteristics expressed in humans. In bodybuilding, considerable focus is constantly directed to increasing testosterone levels to encourage muscle growth and achieve increased muscle mass and strength. In males, specialized Leydig cells produce testosterone. Androgen receptors expressed by satellite cells in muscle tissue and muscle nuclei allow testosterone to produce the much sought after anabolic effects.

title: Avoid these - cheap and unreliable.
text:
This is the worst possible implementation of an amazing idea. I felt so much relief after getting these and getting my medications set up - no more anxiety about "did I already take this today?"

But after just a few days, it's become clear that this product is not going to work out. The lids do not stay on - it's not that they aren't child proof, it's that they literally fit so loosely on the bottles that if you pick the bottle up by the lid, it pops right off. If you squeeze the bottle even slightly, the lid pops off. I've lost about 40+ expensive prescription pills into the sink so far due to lids coming off unexpectedly.

But then you figure "ok, this guy is just rough with his bottles" - that isn't where the issues end.

The biggest problem is that the lids just stop working unexpectedly (and permanently) without warning. I've had 3 lids stop working - the timers are blank and no amount of opening and closing brings them back to life - in just 2 weeks. I assume the batteries are dying, but they cannot be replaced so the bottles just become trash.

Plus, the bottle sizes are strange - the small ones are too small (slightly smaller than your normal bottle from a pharmacy), and the big ones are too big - why?

Considering how expensive these are, they are very poorly made, and I really had high hopes for them. Wish they made a more durable version.

title: Fantastic White Noise Machine
text:
This is a great white noise machine, packed with a lot of little features that make a big difference. I love that it has a built-in rechargeable battery and can be charged over usb type-c. This makes it incredibly portable, allowing it to be charged with the included wall adapter, a portable battery bank, or even a laptop computer. And with more and more devices using type-c cables, it just makes it very easy to only have to carry along one cable to use across all of my electronics.

It comes with 7 white noises, 7 fan noises and 15 natural sounds, bringing it to a total of 29 sounds to choose from. I honestly only use about 5 of the included sounds myself, but still great to have the variety. It also has a built-in RGB night light where you can not only control the color, but also set a lighting mode. I particularly like using the pulsing mode, however you can choose a mode to cycle through all the colors, you can set the brightness, and can simply turn it off entirely. Best of all, it will remember your selected options even after powering down, so you don't have to re-select them every single time you use this. Lastly, you have the option to run it indefinitely or you can set an auto-shutoff timer of either 30, 60 or 90 minutes.

The build quality is quite good. Buttons have a nice tactile click, the volume dial spins just fine and it has a nice rubber ring at the bottom to keep it from sliding around your table. It's relatively small, measuring about 4.7 inches across and about 2.7 inches tall (up to the button which is the tallest point). The instructions claim that it has a 7 hour battery life, and can be charged up in approximately 2.5 hours. I've never had the battery fully drain on me so I cannot confirm those numbers, but I can say that the battery life has been more than long enough for my usage.

So far I haven't had any issues with this device. If after some time I spot an issue, I'll be sure to update this review with my findings. Also, with Amazon prices fluctuating often, it may be useful to know that I purchased this at a price of $24.99 in June 2020.

Pros
- Rechargeable Battery allows portable usage
- Uses USB Type-C which is great!
- 29 different sounds (though I typically only use about 5 of them)
- RGB nightlight w/ customizable color and lighting mode
- Built in memory allows it to remember settings after shutdown
- Good build quality and reputable brand

Cons
- None yet, will update

title: Easy use & heats quickly but curl is modest. 👀
text:
Okay, I love the idea of a heated lash curler as an alternative to the old clamp and curl I’ve used for my entire make up wearing life. In theory, this sounded great, but the results were not quite as impressive for me as I hoped.

PROS:
☑️ Simple to use (after you’ve applied your mascara) and takes about 10 seconds to heat up. The display goes from a purplish-pink to white when ready.
☑️ 4 different heat settings from 55-85—displayed in celsius only—to choose from based on coarseness of lash hair. Also, the display is very clear and easy to read for temp and battery charge.
☑️ Extremely lightweight and similar dimensions to a tube of mascara.
☑️ Rechargeable, so no need to mess with batteries. And since the amount of time it gets used is so brief, the charge really does last.

NOTABLES:
🔘 I tried each of the settings on various occasions, and it took the highest (85C) to see much of any curl. As you can see from the before and after pics, the curl I got was so minimal, I’m not sure it made much of a difference for the effort? title: Low power == low connection range
text:
This product advertises 30 meters (about 90 feet) of bluetooth connectivity range. That number is typically given on many products as a theoretical max range, given ideal conditions, and a direct line of sight to the device.

It doesn't come close.

First, it's a small device with low power requirements. Second, it's designed to be worn underneath clothing, and is positioned between the legs, putting a lot of signal-blocking human in the way.

I'm lucky if it stays connected when I take my phone out of my pocket. I can't imagine how a caretaker could stay connected.

Other than that, it's a little finicky, but seems to work. I'd prefer a sensor that could attach to higher capacity plastic backed diapers. It's also not waterproof, so be careful not to get moisture inside during a change. If you do, remove the battery, then use some isopropyl alcohol to evaporate the water away, and it'll work again.

I was not happy that these didn't come with any instructions such as whether to apply the patch vertically or horizontally to your foot, or how many days in a row you should wear these, etc. I found that they stayed on my feet better if I applied them horizontally. They came off my feet any time I tried the vertical method - in the morning I would find them bundled up & attached to my blankets down at the foot of the bed.

When they did stay on for most of the night, I found myself a bit nauseous and with a headache and irritability the next day. I didn't correlate these symptoms to the Foot Patches until my friend explained to me that these symptoms are common of detoxing. I do not drink alcohol or do any drugs, but assume the patches are helping my body to purge other natural toxins and maybe emotional baggage. So, I will continue to use and hope I start feeling better soon.

title: Functions but poor engineering
text:
First of all let me say that I have purchased and used another competing product that's only slightly more expensive than this one so I had a good base for comparison.

The handle is essentially a solid piece with no adjustable angles and so it's critical you have to be at the right angle or the effectiveness goes down very quickly. In fact if you're consistently at a suboptimal angle then it will be almost nothing more than a convenient back scratcher.

Essentially the housing unit snaps in and is a solid piece that you can push to pull out so it's really a fancy plastic tool that you connect into. The housing unit houses what amounts to two side by side three blade heads so that it's an extra wide shaving surface with an extra thin lubrication strip.

While it does get the job done if you've ever used another brand that has large blades engineered for its use along with a bendable adjustable arm and a lot more reuse from what I can imagine then you'll probably be disappointed in this.

Overall in comparison I would expect this to retail for about half this price or less so I don't really think it's a very good value for the money in my opinion.

title: AMAZING RESULTS!
text:
I have suffered from break out on my skin for 15 years now. I've tried practically everything else there was to try, from doctor's prescription creams and antibiotics, to various homemade concoctions. Trying to avoid products such as Proactiv, which have very aggressive chemicals in them that permeate the skin and go directly to the liver, I thought I'd try the last resort - tea. Honestly, I did not expect much. Both because of my dismal experience in trying to find a "cure" for my lasting condition, and because, well let's be honest, who really believes a tea could cure you of anything?? But I was desperate, so I tried. The tea, to my great surprise, also did not taste bad at all. I could not believe it when a few weeks after drinking a cup of tea every night I actually started to see my skin clearing up! For the first time in over a decade, I am not able to wear shirts I was never able to wear before because they exposed too much skin in areas I was ashamed to let show.

This tea was a wonderful surprise! I continue drinking one cup every day and continue to enjoy the great results!
I recommend this with all my heart!

title: I wanted to like it. :-(
text:
The whole idea of selling concentrated pouches and using the same big spray bottle over and over again is a potentially great, money-saving idea.

However, this product smells almost like a scented play-dough, or just very artificially gross cleaning product. Just imagine the most artificial “outdoor” smell, and that’s what you have here. It’s not overpowering, and not horribly weak. I really wanted to like it! But in the meantime, I’m giving it to one of my teenage boys to use for his room. Because no matter how unappealing this smell is, I’ll take this scent over the smell of a teenage boy any day. He can spray it over the mounds of dirty clothes on the floor, and as long as the blue dye doesn’t stain the clothing, it might make a little bit of a difference in there.

That’s another thing! Who adds dark blue dye to air freshener???!!!!!! Dye is ok for cleaning products, but not air freshener! Especially when it’s coming out in large quantities from a giant spray bottle! Go with clear or even ultra light pink so that I don’t turn my furniture colors while attempting to make it smell better! Please. :-)

title: So delicious!
text:
I started my Keto journey last October. I went through a season of experimenting with low carb desserts and found many of them to be either artificially or overly sweet, bitter, lacking flavor or horrible texture. When you do find something that tastes good, you often have to limit the quantity to the size of a quakurge.
I am thrilled to have discovered Keto Indulgence! It is so delicious. It has a smooth chocolate hazelnut flavor, great texture and no aftertaste. Mind you, if you've just started Keto, it's not going to taste like a Snickers or Hersheys bar, but if you've been on the Keto journey and have conquered your carb addiction, this is an immensely satisfying treat. When I want to feel like I'm indulging in a decadent dessert,, I crumble it up in my 5% Greek yogurt, add a few macademia nuts and a few raspberries and voila! you have a Keto Blizzard- LOL! I've also added it to a cup of coffee...mocha-licious!
I do think it's a bit pricey, but I am willing to make the occasional splurge. One final note, the exterior packaging is flimsy and looks like it has been previously opened, but the chocolates themselves are individually wrapped and have not been compromised.

Bottom line, does not seem to be the product for easily scrubbing in tight spaces. With wand, the device is almost four feet long. Without wand, almost two feet. Wonder why such a long battery. Who knows?
5. Purpose of each brush? Who knows?
6. Red light in the battery (the long pvc piece) probably indicates the battery is charging. Will it turn green when fully charged? Who knows? How long to charge or tell if full charge? Who knows?
7. During assembly, it was necessary to force connection between wand and engine. Connection between battery and wand was smooth.
8. Connection between brush and engine does not seem to be complete (not a tight fit). Will see how well brushes stay connected when I operate the scrubber.
9. As mentioned by other reviewers, speed (torque) seems to be minimal but that may improve upon full charge.
10. The box describes this as a "multifunction power scrubber." What is the "multi" feature? Who knows? Perhaps fact there is more than one brush. As to the "power" part, see comment 9.

May be a great product but I am keeping all contents and watching the 30 day clock.

title: Excellent Product With Great Results
text:
First thing is first, for full disclosure sake, I am an employee of Beachbody. That, in addition to my extensive marital arts training and fitness lifestyle, makes me hyper critical of all workout and performance supplements. Aside from my sensitivity to caffeine, I generally dismiss a product if it does not have a direct usefulness in the many martial arts practices and competitions (Wrestling, Jiu Jitsu, Judo, Pankration, MMA) I take part in.

I've tried Gatorade, PowerAde, Body Shield, Vitamin Water and a slew of other "Sports Drinks" designed to help rehydrate a body after an intense workout, but I generally have the exact same experience each time. I step onto the mat for my match, fight furiously (I promise that no workout is as intense as 1 on 1 combat) and come off the mat with muscles that are generally blown out and cramped from intense exertion. This wouldn't be a problem if I had loads of time between each match, but I don't and having a constant and flowing use of all my muscles is incredibly important.

Beachbody's Performance line has lots of interesting supplements in it but Hydrate is the one for me and the one product whose effects I notice immediately. Most rehydration liquids do nothing for the cramping that I experience right after trying to choke someone to sleep or rip a limb off, but Hydrate is something special. You don't need to drink a ton in my experience, as a little seems to go a long way. A double serving gets me through a solid 2 hour Jiu Jitsu training situation, and I can't rave about it quite enough during my tournament settings. So far it is the only hydration liquid I have ever noticed to severely cut down or eliminate cramping due to intense exercise, and has generally kept me in the stronger in the game for longer. It is a product I have no desire to train or compete with out.

title: Review of buffer only
text: I did not purchase this product but did purchase the buffer alone.  It came with a two-pack of buffer bonnets.  The original bonnets worked okay but replacements I have purchased have been near to worthless.  Much too big and floppy.  The buffer itself is pretty lightweight and easy to handle with one hand, several holding positions are comfortable, give some relief over long use.  I used mine to polish and wax a sailboat and then recently my car.  My experience would suggest that the boat was a good use, the car not so.  Instructions clearly state that buffer should not be run unless in contact with a surface and this is so.  Lifting it from a surface before turning it off can result in the bonnet flying off.  The first time I did this with the boat I watched the bonnet quickly sink into the murky depths.  My reticence with the car, so I would not recommend this package just because of the buffer, is that less than pretty much full surface contact is similar to no contact.  The surface of my car has many concave sections and small or thin sections so the buffer was not in complete contact.  It does not do well using just the edge for a small or thin section.  Several times the bonnet actually wound itself further into the holding space and jammed the buffer, then came out pretty oily/greasy so I am concerned I have removed some of the "permanent" lubrication.  The boat, picture a long hull, was a much flatter surface so less likely to do this.  Because it is so light I was able to use it for long periods of time, trading hands for relief, but with relatively little fatigue.  Another review elsewhere suggested that complaints of others about the buffer were really more related to the over-sized and floppy bonnets.  I would agree.  That reviewer suggested buying Turtle wax bonnets at Wal-Mart.  I did that, less expensive than the Ryobi bonnets, fit better, and worked much better.  I have been completely unable to find a replacement pad for the buffer which is now showing some wear.  Actually I came across this produce searching for a source for replacement pads.  Right now it looks like the only way to get a replacement pad is to buy a new buffer...and it is apparently discontinued at Home Depot.  I would go 4-5 stars for use with a boat, but only 3 for the car...unless maybe you have a big old behemoth with massive large flat sections.

title: Fake Science
text: It is not my job to save people from fake science, but this is for the handful of people who are discerning enough to look at reviews before buying. While the placebo effect is well known to work and walking in the dirt is good for your mental health as it helps you slow down, breath, and disengage from the stress of the rat race, I would encourage you not to spend any money on earthing products. The author's "science" is 180 degrees off- the earth is positively charged and is not conductive as the majority of it is silicon based, not metallic as claimed. This is a snake oil salesman preying on the desperate; it would be one thing if he was citing anecdotal evidence and saying "I don't know how this works but I have seen that it does." It is totally something different to misrepresent what is happening with false science trying to dupe a public who have forgotten their 7th grade Earth Science education.

title: Refinements needed: The light is too bright, and it needs an on-off switch...
text:
A couple of blue lights glow BRIGHTLY to indicate, I guess, that the UV-C light is not burnt out. I assume the the blue light is harmless, but, given the warnings about how deadly UV-C is to living things, you can't help but wonder if dangerous UV-C "leakage" will burn your retinas or something. My wife wondered this, too. "If that light is so powerful, is the light coming from it safe?"

Worse, it's WAY too bright to keep on in a bedroom. I immediately put black tape on it so I could sleep...then hid it in a box! The fan sound is gentle white noise, not a problem. Some people like a little white to to help with sleep. But blue light - the color of sunlight - is not good for sleep at all. And finally, if you want to save the 10 watts or so that I measured this unit at with a watt meter, you must pull it out of the outlet. No on-off switch. Stupid.

Does it work? Well, it's a matter of proving a negative. My bedroom smells clean and fresh with it, but then, it didn't smell bad without it. I haven't gotten sick since I started using it, but then...would I be sick now if I DIDN'T use it? Probably not. I guess the test will come if I get a cold or the flu and use this to fight germs in my sickroom. Again, if I recover fast, can I thank this device? There's really no way for a non-scientist to prove if it's doing anything at all...no way for a lay person to measure germs in the air with or without. I'm not saying it doesn't perform as advertised...I'm just saying that it's hard to determine what it accomplishes, if anything. Just be aware that it's NOT a filter, and it removes no particles from the air. Doesn't claim to. So, my next purchase may involve a HEPA filter device (for allergy relief) with a built-in UV-C light (just for that extra degree of feeling like I'm doing something beneficial, even if I can't prove it).

title: Wholly inaccurate
text:
I bought this hoping to have some better information and tracking capabilities. I have foudn the measurements to be so far off as to be wholly innaccurate and fitbit support to not respond to their own forums in over one week.
So, here are 3 readings, each a day apart.
Today (9/26) at 9:19AM
249.7 lbs 35.8% fat

Tuesday, Sep 25 at 9:15AM
249.9 lbs 33.8% fat

Monday, Sep 24 at 2:38PM
251.7 lbs 32.6% fat

This would indicate I'm getting fatter, as a 3.2% increase is about 7.5 pounds of fat. In 3 days, when I'm being active and eating ~ 1,000 calories under daily goal each day. I thought there might be an adjsutment I could make, so I asked if there was something I could do to get better results. I was ignored. Then I had this following result.

This was Tuesday, 9/25.
Today at 12:12PM
248.6 lbs 23.5% fat

Today at 9:19AM
249.7 lbs 35.8% fat
I walked a golf course, and in 3 hours and 3 minutes, lost 12.3% bodyfat. 12.3% of 248.6 pounds is 30.5778 pounds.

I spent entirely too much for a scale that is less reliable than Miss Cleo. I recommend no one purchase this item!

title: Stopped sucking her fingers after 2 weeks and has never gone back.
text: My daughter sucked her pointer and middle fingers of her left hand upside down.  She did it for a long time and I was getting worried about her soft palate and her teeth.  So at 3.5 years old, I bought this item.  I was extremely hesitant because it was so expensive.  I had tried bandaids, fingernail polish, gloves, but nothing was working!  So when I put this on her, she had no problem wearing it.  She tried sucking on it a few times but it was very awkward for her so she stopped.  Anytime she washed her hands, I cut the band off and put a new one on.  She could not get it off on her own at all and I was impressed at how unnoticeable it was to her.  People would ask me about it and sometimes it took me a minute to even figure out what they were talking about because it was so routine.  After 2 weeks of having it on her, I took it off and she never sucked her fingers again.  I know it seems like a lot of money, but in the long run I feel I prevented costly dental work.  It has been over 2 years now, by the way, and still no sucking her fingers.

title: Traction *and* Stabilization - Highly portable, and at a good price!  I'm going to keep a spare around...
text:
Value - This traction device can be had for under $20 - less than the cost of 4 coffees from a cafe! I absolutely adore coffee, but would gladly give up half a dozen cups of good coffee to get this device. I love coffee, so that's saying a lot!

Quality - As expected, the item is constructed out of inflatable plastic. The photo matches what I was sent (no bait and switch). Unlike regular inflatable plastic devices that you inflate by blowing with your mouth, this one includes a rubber bulb for pumping, similar to a manual blood pressure cuff. There is also a roller clamp, like the ones on an IV, to lock the device when it is inflated to your satisfaction.

Fit - I was concerned when I unboxed it that it would FEEL cheap and uncomfortable (it was cheaper than all the similar products, and looked easy to use). That turned out not to be the case, to my surprise. There is comfortable velveteen on all the surfaces that come in contact with your head/neck and shoulders. I have a very slender, long neck, and the velcro straps had a wide enough range of adjustment that I could fit the device properly (yet, my 6ft tall husband can also fit the device just fine).

Use – The bulb pump allows for easy inflation, even if you have weak and arthritic hands like I do. I had no issues putting the device on myself, and inflating it to perform traction without any assistance. I have a genetic disorder which causes me to produce weak collagen, called Ehlers Danlos Syndrome. I find this device to be highly useful for any time I may fall asleep sitting up. Due to my hypermobility, when I nod off in an airplane, a chair, or in the car, my neck bends in unnatural angles and I wake up in a lot of pain. If I wear this device, it prevents any possibility of bending of my neck into an unnatural position.

General - If you need traction, this works pretty well. If you need neck stabilization due to craniocervical instability, hypermobility, or another issue, this device does the trick cheaply. I was concerned that it would give me a choking sensation, but it didn't, even when fully inflated. Because of the way the velcro closures work to secure the device, there really isn't any pressure on your throat – and that is important to me. So far, I haven’t had any sensation of choking, which I’m already prone to just by leaning my head back when it isn’t braced. This device is easy to toss in a bag, so I take it with me when I’ll be gone overnight for any reason!

PROS: Works well for traction, or to stabilize the neck while sleeping upright. The unit has durable parts connected to the inflatable part. Easy to deflate, and compact enough to be portable.

CONS: People who are rough with their stuff might puncture the plastic early. The item did not include any instructions, anyone not familiar with the ball pump setup may need a few minutes to figure out how to deflate the unit without pulling the bulb off. There is a mechanism at the top of the bulb that you can screw/unscrew to lock in or release the air. Deflating it is simple, just not necessarily intuitive for people who haven't used a blood pressure cuff or other similar device.

text:
[[VIDEOID:5680804e8ee68b37423d8c4a2bbb1aed]] I had a funeral for the pad, since it died just around 9mos. I didn't have insurance, since it is not provided... so I was unable to provide a casket for it.

I bought a plastic one from Walmart that's last me over 7yrs!!! I like this one bevause it's comfortable, soft & can be washed. Too bad it's "dead" now! I know engineers who work for companies to intentionally make products go out after a certain time - mainly after the warranty is up on the item, pretty messed up huh! The warranty on this heating pad is only 90 days.
It gets one star, for keeping my back warm for the months it did last. If your cold, put a heating pad against your lower back & I find it warms the entire body up. It's very comfortable, underneath my lower back. I washed it & it continued working for a bit after that. The lowest setting is sometimes just enough warmth for me... heated up pretty well - WHEN IT *WAS* WORKING!
Does anyone else find it odd that back in 80s an early 90s these types of products lasted SO long... MOST electronics did! And now it's 2019, and you know we've advanced technology wise, so why in the he11 are things not lasting as long as they used to?! BECAUSE THEY'RE USING THAT TECHNOLOGY TO MAKE PRODUCTS GO OUT SOONER, ESPECIALLY AFTER WARRANTY IS UP!!
What a wonderful world we live in... with loving, compassionate & unselfish people.

title: It's ok except for a very dangerous ingredient.  Please be careful...
text:
I was recently diagnosed with hypothyroidism and I have been tweaking the dosage of Synthroid with my physician to find the right dose. It's been grueling, as I'm sure others with thyroid disorders can agree. When I saw I could review this at a discount for my opinion, I jumped on it. Anything to help me get out of this crazy funk that I'm in. Once I started taking it, I felt an immediate boost of energy (thank God..I needed that) BUT I decided to do some research on some of the ingredients. All are great for what it says it does, except for one - Bladderwrack. Reading the MedlinePlus page on it scared me enough to stop taking it.

According to them, "Bladderwrack is POSSIBLY UNSAFE when taken by mouth. It may contain high concentrations of iodine, which could cause or worsen some thyroid problems. Prolonged, high intake of dietary iodine is linked with goiter and increased risk of thyroid cancer." It goes on to say "Thyroid problems known as hyperthyroidism (too much thyroid hormone), or hypothyroidism (too little thyroid hormone): Bladderwrack contains significant amounts of iodine, which might make hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism worse. Don’t use it."

This was all I needed to stop. I would rather stay in this funk until I find the right Synthroid dose than end up way worse than what I am now. It's a shame because the ingredients are perfect...except for this one. You can read the article here: https://www.nlm.nih.gov/medlineplus/druginfo/natural/726.html
