title: Downbeats Initial Impressions
text:
They do the job, but should double-flange silicone eartips with a plastic tube insert cost this much? Also, they do not go into the ear far enough to minimize occlusion effect. A useful product, and they come with a nice pill vial for storage (equipped with an o-ring, because silicone eartips need weatherproof housing), but for $14 this is not a very good value--I feel like I could make a pair on my own using leftover double-/triple-flange eartips from previously purchased headphones and some narrow inner-diameter tubing from a hardware store for about $0.25.

Update: Less than two weeks after purchasing these, the metal ring connecting the pill vial to my keychain broke; also, the o-ring is absent, and the paint is chipping off of the pill vial. I have a peanut lighter that has been on my keychain for about a year and a safety whistle that has been on my keychain for nine years, that have fared just fine, so I am concluding that the pill vial is not well-made. And I am lowering my rating to one star.

Recommendation for Downbeats: redesign the product to reduce occlusion, outfit them with a quality case, then sell this improved version for a more reasonable price.

I got a massive stye on my eye and I wasnt going to take chances. It was really painful (first one I got ever) and it quickly kept getting worse day by day. I ordered this immediately based on reviews and it was worth it.

On day 1 and day 2, I was taking topical antibiotic (erythromycin) and it was not making it better. I have a high pain tolerance and had to take an advil so I could do work. I applied castor oil that evening.

On day 3, I started taking oral antibiotics and the situation was stable but no real improvements. Pain level was still high. Extreme swelling despite hot compresses.

On day 4+, this arrived and I put it it on my eye roughly 2x a day. I put a lot on right before bed.

Basically each day, my stye completely resolved & healed. I lessened my antibiotic dosage as well.

I definitely went all in with antibiotics AND this but it was worth it! :) Thanks yall!

title: Perfect for (that time of the month)
text:
As much as I was using Salonpas for a while (back some years ago), these Coralite pain patches are massively more affordable given the amount you get, vs. Salonpas. These Coralite pain patches work exactly the same as those, except for one caveat... if you have sensitive skin and/ or suffer from eczema, you may want to really think on using these before you do. I suffer eczema, but I use these still for years, regardless. My eczema flares up in the one spot I use these patches on (after the 2 to 3 days in a row, a month) that I use these. The lower left of my stomach area is where I suffer great, unbearable pain, due to monthly cramps. If you have sensitive skin (eczema-related, or not), these will leave a mark when you pull off the patch. Using these long-term, as like how I do, that "mark" will eventually turn into a mildly-dark scar over time. At 50 years of age, this really doesn't bother me in the slightest.

These patches, once in place, after about 10 minutes of application, these patches do last 8 hours. And, there is a faint, cool menthol smell. The pain, as painful as my cramps are, completely disappear for 8 hours, the power of the medicine in the patches never waiver. I want to also add, that same with the previously used Salonpas patches, these Coralite patches do in fact make me tired, and I will knock out for a few hours... so, if wearing during the day, I make sure I will be at home.

I do want to mention that you get one packet of 20 patches per box, once opened, and after you get one, you need to either wrap up the opened package and put in a ziplock bag... or, you need to wrap it up pretty tightly with Saran wrap/ or, other plastic wrap. I say this, cause I learned first-hand with the very first box of these I used, the medicinal effects of these patches will weaken over time, if not stored wrapped up.

title: Great jolt of energy
text:
I've used the peppermint flavor of this spray for over a year now. There are almost no bad things to say about it.

A quick word about me: I'm a caffeine junkie. But I have to avoid coffee itself as well as carbonated sodas. So I look for other caffeine delivery methods and have tried most of them.

Each spray is about a third of a cup of coffee. To get the most out of it, I tend to take two sprays at a time: one under the tongue, one on the tongue. I let the spray sit in my mouth for a bit before swallowing. Mostly that's to increase the caffeine absorption, but it also helps my breath. I don't usually have halitosis (I hope!) but having nice tasting breath can't hurt.

The effects are pretty quick, usually within just a couple of minutes. It isn't an instant rush, and doesn't come on all at once. But the effect is noticeable and lasting. I don't recommend more than three sprays at a time before you get used to the effects or you might be bouncing off walls and arranging carpet fringe.

The only drawback to this is that the bottles are a bit flimsy and don't stand up to travel or pocket use. I keep one in my backpack for air travel and it will occasionally develop a very slow leak. The good part is that the spray doesn't seem to stain and it smells nice. The bad part is that everything in my backpack would smell like fresh peppermint. So I keep the bottle in a small plastic baggie when traveling (the "snack size" fits just fine). But this is well worth keeping in your pack - take a couple of sprays just before you land and you're ready for your destination!

Overall this is a great product, well worth buying. At the moment Amazon is selling these through Chemical Evolution and I LOVE this supplier. They often send me free samples of other products at no charge, and in a recent order actually included a hand-written note thanking me for my order!

title: Be careful, once contaminated will ruin other coins
text:
I'm not sure which coin I cleaned that contaminated by jar (probably a really dirty penny - actual dirt rather than tone) but after that the silver coins I cleaned started getting brown spots after several days. Its also important to thoroughly rinse the coin in running water after dipping (don't just dip it in water) then dip it in deionized water and let it dry. I want to find some kind of holder I can snap a coin into then dip so that when drying neither side is actually touching anything. Paper towels are rough and can scratch proof coins' mirrored fields. If you have a lot of coins to clean or even just a few very valuable coins I suggest getting the gallon sized container so that you can use new cleaner for each coin and aren't risking contamination. Use gloves and be sure to tightly close the jar. When left in my hot car it leaked even though the jar remained upright and crystals formed all around the lid (maybe that's what ruined my jar rather than contamination?).

When in doubt, don't clean your coin, let the pros at PCGS/ANACS/NGC/IGC do the conservation work.

title: Rip-Off. Price is 5x the Worth
text:
I needed to replenish the water supply for my humidifier. I was attracted to this product for the convenience of the multiple smaller bottles. Unfortunately, at the $50 price, I assumed to receive multiple 24-bottle cases. This product is only one 24-bottle case.

24 count of 20fl oz bottles = 480fl oz total = 3.75 gallons total. So, that's $50 for LESS THAN 4 gallons of water. They are essentially charging 5x the amount this water is worth. I can buy 5 gallons of distilled water locally for under $10. I do not recommend buying this water, as it is grossly overpriced.

In addition to their outlandish pricing, they held no accountability and gave me a short answer when I asked for a refund. I asked for additional details and answers, and they never responded. I do not recommend purchasing water from them.

After this experience, I worry that CPAP users may fall victim to the representation of this product as well. "CPAP Water" is just a glamorized way of saying "distilled water". Please don't think this water is any different than what you can get at Walmart for a fraction of the price.

title: Absolute Back Saver:  Please Read!
text:
I Even Use This For Side Sleeping..a BACK SAVER!

I have a bad back. I'm a guy, 38, about 5'8", 195lbs and I sleep on a futon on nights my wife tosses and turns in bed (which is most evenings. But hey, I snore too, so the banishment is mutual.)
After a night of sleeping on the futon, I always awake with such severe lower back pain that it literally takes me hours to just work the kinks out before I can expect to do anything productive whatsoever. It's gotten to the point where I expect the pain.
I try everything to alleviate the problem before I fall asleep: I support myself with a bed wedge, I elevate my legs, I use a pillow between my knees and I support my neck properly. I've looked into how to do all of that, trust me. My legs and neck feel okay the next day, but nothing seemed to be able to help the lower back pain.
Keep all this in mind.

I gifted this Purple brand "Simply" seat cushion to my mom last Christmas 2017. I purchased it on the maker's website as I wasn't aware it was here on Amazon at the time.
My mom has unfortunately passed away since due to a heart attack, so the cushion is here with me now, and I've personally been using it since. I'm a graphic illustrator (I work on digital artwork at a desk.) I sit most of my day. The Simply Cushion saves my rear during the day as advertised; I wasn't surprised at that.

What I WAS surprised at is, while I sleep on the futon on my side, this Purple "Simply" cushion ENTIRELY removes my lower back pains as I sleep.
Entirely. I'm not kidding. It's as if I went from a 85 year-old's back to that of a 20-something again. No kidding.
I sleep on my side and position the Simply cushion at my hip or a little lower. That's all! No more back pain!
I was so astonished at the results that I've recently also purchased the back cushion as well. I plan to use it as intended in the car and as a travel pillow.

I'm a jaded guy. I don't have high expectations for movies, video games, music, anything these days. I expect to be let down or at best, I go into things not expecting much so I'm not disappointed. TRUST ME: you should get hyped for this purchase. It'll last, it'll work, and it's reliable.

As for the scent, mine never had any whatsoever. As for any white residue I'm reading about, mine also never had any. I promise you it was brand new when purchased.
The gel insert (the main pillow itself) is a little wider without the zippered pillowcase than with with it. The case is easily washed in the laundry if need be, and if I want to, I can rinse off the gel pillow part with water and leave it to air dry.

text: The belt for Delta/Rockwall table saws with a different number has been identified as not fitting where this belt fits - and  it doesn't. It is so close, but you just cannot get it on. This one fits and it goes on without the removal of the motor or such - just slide it on. The motor has two main bolts that hold it onto the casting. Besides holding things together, these two bolts affect the alignment of the drive shaft relative to the arbor shaft pulley. They should be tightened so that the shaft and the pulley are parallel. If they are not parallel, the belt will either work its way off the drive or will pull the belt back against the saw's casting. Either situation will cause early death of the belt.

title: Metal is so much better than plastic!
text:
I had been using a plastic tongue scraper for years, but I had heard that metal ones were more effective, so I thought I'd try this one. After one try, it was obvious that metal ones are so much better. The plastic one I had looked like a toothbrush with a little plastic rake on the end. I could work on my tongue for a minute and feel like I was getting nowhere. With this metal one, I was amazed after just one pass over my tongue. It is like a squeegee for all the white crap on my tongue! It only takes a half dozen passes and your done in like 10 seconds! Afterwards, my mouth is noticeably fresher feeling for hours.

The two handed, bow style makes it incredibly easy to use, and unlike my old plastic one, it doesn't hurt at all. Additionally, the silver and gold styling is very nice looking and feels very sterile and durable while being very easy to clean.

I was fortunate enough to receive a discount on this tongue scraper so that I could try it out and provide an informed review.

title: Ok Nightlite, But Sound Is Too Loud
text:
I like the item as a nightlight - it projects a moon and stars onto the wall/ceiling with various color LED lights. I believe there are five colors to choose from. It will only stay one color at a time - it does not cycle through them, as some other products do.
I did not feel that the light was too bright, in fact I thought it could've stood to be a little brighter... but this is more of a "cute" item than functional - the stars look great on the wall, but it doesn't really illuminate the room itself like a standard nightlight would. Also, depending on which color you choose, the light is varying degrees of brightness... I normally leave it on green/yellow, which are the brighter ones; red is a very dim color.
The product also has "soothing" nighttime sounds you can listen to: rain, bubbling brook, crickets/owls, the ocean, a heartbeat, and chirping birds (not a night noise? but ok). The major problem with the product, however, is that the sounds are FAR too loud, even when the volume is turned all the way down. It's like the volume that you'd listen to on a radio or something during the day.
I'm certain I could never fall asleep with any of the noises on. Muffling it with a blanket or something doesn't seem to do much good, and then the sound is distorted. Putting it in the room next door might solve the noise problem, but then the light isn't useful.
I wish the volume had a knob, so you could turn it up/down, because then you could set the volume at an appropriate level for sleeping (i.e. just barely audible). The problem is that it only has buttons to go up/down, and the range just isn't suitable.
I would recommend the product just as a fun toy for a child's room for the star projection, but if you need a regular nightlight, this isn't the best option. And I definitely don't recommend it as a "white noise" or sound machine if you want it to fall asleep to.

title: It does work but don't believe the hype
text:
I've successfully recharged about 80% of my alkalines, including ones that dipped below 1.0V. The weakest battery that I was able to recharge had a baseline of 0.86V. All got "renewed" to about 1.5V or a little more. The other 20% refused to work. The only leakages I've experienced came from Rayovac AAA's, even though they had never been charged before. I have never charged any battery more than twice so I can't say if I can go beyond 5-10x, much less 100x. But the "renewed" batteries did perform like new alkalines.

As for NiMH's, it does charge them but I wouldn't recommend using this charger for them since it only automatically shuts down for alkalines.

It's hard to compare this to other alkaline chargers because it seems to use a different method. Most other alkaline chargers finish in about 16-18 hrs but this takes about 3 days. And while others recommend charging way before the battery is depleted (> 1.0V), this one doesn't. You can still charge if the battery is on its last breath.

So while I agree that the hype is misleading, it does work -- at least to the extent that I've tested it. Aside from functionality, I should point out that the door is flimsy. I need to keep it shut with tape.

title: Great idea, flawed execution
text:
These were a gift for my wife who always has cold feet! There are only 2 sizes, and the ranges are pretty liberal, so it should have come as no surprise when they were too big for her feet. She is around 7.5, and these list the max for small as Women's 8.5, so that extra room does make a difference for her when she's wearing them. I can only imagine someone with a size 5 or 6 foot, they would be swimming in these.

That being said, she can wear them and it's noticeable but not a deal-breaker that they are a little too big. The main issue with these warming slippers is that the warming is not consistent throughout the foot. It seems like them heat is mainly concentrated in certain areas like the back heel area. Charging is easy and convenient with an included USB-C "Y" adapter so you can charge both batteries at once. You have to unzip a pocket on the top of the slippers, pull out the adapter and unplug it. Then reverse after charging. Pretty simple, but it does mean that as you are walking you are bearing the burden of a battery pack on top of each foot. Again, not a deal-breaker, but not ideal. And, as I think others have mentioned, it's real easy to push the buttons on the side of the slippers when you brush up against stuff, it happens all the time to my wife while wearing these.

Ultimately, these foot warming slippers do the job, if not perfectly. I've not comparison shopped, but I'm going to opine that the current retail of $80 is high for these. I'd rather pay around $40 now that we have them and have tried them, but again, I don't know what the market is like for these. Recommended, but with some reservations as stated.

As an additional note, I think the fact that they broke so similarly (see attached pic) probably indicates that there is a problem with molding, meaning that all/most will be likely to break this way. For this reason I would strongly recommend avoid this product unless you are alright with this issue.

For example, this issue doesn't actually both me much because I do design work and have a 3D printer at home, and thus can print out some beefier handles no problem, although I can't imagine most potential customers are in a similar situation.

As for how well silicone works compared to other options, in my opinion it's fine but nothing special. You won't get as much per pass as the standard disposable ones, but washing it isn't too bad so I don't mind. It still works alot better than those brush solutions, so I plan to continue using it after replacing the handle.

title: Maybe useful to keep good posture good but that's it
text:
I'm at a computer most of the day so I hunch over a bit this was the first product in what now seems to be a very long process of finding a useful brace. Immediately after putting it on and tightening it my skin was pinching (see picture) through a shirt no less. There was no correction to my hunching/slouch the only thing it did was pull my shoulders back (in the pictures it rests between shoulder blades in practice i can't get it to stop bunching on my neck) causing more pain to my neck and upper back. To feel the correct posture position you'll have to do the heavy lifting as letting your muscles relax this will make you hunch over even more, if I wanted to do all the work I wouldn't need a brace in the first place. This product is NOT what you want to use to correct your posture moreso for after a real brace and keeping your good posture. Not saying it's a bad product just advertised as a "corrector" when it's more of a stabilizer.

Will re-review after I use a real correction apparatus then this one to keep it corrected (or attempt to) and the sellers admit this is a stabilizer not a corrector.

Over the last 2 years I try to use this daily. Now THIS I know works better than any other MV ever taken because:

Feel: more energized than if I didn't. When I took these regularly, the afternoon tiredness didn't exist anymore.

I don't like the taste of coffee and don't really do soda/coke, so it was pretty challenging for me to get things done after 2pm. Within about 3 days of using these I could definitely tell a difference in how I felt overall. It may have been a placebo effect but it sure was worth it to just feel over-all more energized and a better sense of well being. Afternoon sleepiness is now a thing of the past. Your pee will be bright yellow for 6 to 8 hours after taking this, with the intense colour tapering off as the hours wear on.

Contents: Have you looked at the contents of these? The daily values are one of (if not the) best I've seen while comparing many other brands of MV's. It even has 100% recommended DV of iron for women, plus so many other things in higher value than other MV. This explains why the dosage is 2 (kinda big pills :)) But it has a sweet vanilla-like coating so that helps with swallowing them.

Verdict: This formula really works. Even when doing workouts like T25/P90x3 or any other consistent workout program, I try to make sure I take this daily as I feel it helps with recovery and helps lessen that burnout feeling you can get with consistent HIIT workouts. Overall, A difference is quickly noticed within a few days of not keeping up with these. I try not to be dependent on any supplements for long term, but these I depend on.

Suggestion: take no later than early afternoon. I felt as if it messed with my sleep on an occasion where I took it after 4pm. title: Noticeable reduction of smell from biological sources
text:
Works great in smaller spaces to help contain smells from a biological source (e.g. a litter box). Given the reviews here, I was expecting a 120 db freight train roaring through the cat room, but it really isn’t noisy at all. Does it make noise? Yes, things with moving parts tend to. Is it really noticeable? No, it is not.

It’s also important to understand the theory of operations of different types of air purification systems: UV isn’t a mechanism to remove smells from non-bacterial sources or removing particulate from the air, for that you need either a traditional HEPA, electrostatic, or even a catalyst (PCO) type filtration system. What UV does is interfere with the DNA/RNA of pathogens causing them to not to be able to replicate. No/less bacteria = smell reduction.

The usual Amazon review armchair Sc.Ds will go on about ozone and UV nanometers and whatnot to flex their interweb muscles based on some random Wikipedia article of why this won’t work and why you need ozone, but the reality is that once you’re in the UV part of the electromagnet spectrum, you’re going to have some sort of impact on DNA regardless of wavelength. Do some nanometer lengths have greater impact than others? Sure, but it doesn’t mean that it’s ineffective, it’s just slower. UV isn’t something you want to play around with, which is why we all wear some sort of sunscreen to prevent skin cancer.

Speaking of cancer, that’s exactly why you DO NOT want ozone generation in your house, and I wish people would stop going on about needing it in these reviews. Ground level ozone is damaging to the mucus membranes in your lungs, and more so to the young, elderly, pets, and people with breathing conditions such as asthma, COPD, etc. Don’t take my word (another random Amazon reviewer) on this, think critically and do your own research here on the mechanisms of the how and why by googling the EPA’s report on this topic.

Anyway, to condense: this seems to work in a small space where I have a litter box, and I’m pleased with the purchase.

It also has a surge protector. The one I use is this: [[ASIN:B002Z7EDCC 360 Electrical 36083 1-Outlet Compact Rotating Surge Protector]]

---------------------------

Update 07/2020

So I've had these since November 16, 2014 and they're still working! A lot of people mention the fan dying but none of mine have died; I have 3 of them! It says on here to replace the UV-C bulb every 6-9 months and many people say their bulbs burned out either sooner or later. But even after all these years, not one of the UV-C bulbs I have has burned out. I ended up replacing one after 2 years because it seemed a bit dimmer than the other two but I probably could have just let it do it's job until it actually did die. I've had all 3 running 24/7 for years. I really think the reason I haven't had problems is because of the surge protector I've used and also the fact they're pretty secure in the socket. Without the surge protector (3 prong) holding them, they tend to lean out of the socket because of their weight. I bought them because I have 2 cats in a small apartment. I honestly can't say if they're actually effective or not. I think at this point I'm just so used to them being there that mentally I just keep them. I clean them periodically (easy to unscrew); I clean out the dust film on the inside walls and the vents. I'm writing because I want people to know that they can indeed work and last a long time. An issue for why they don't might be the power quality in the home/apartment/sockets.

text: I have been waiting for months to order multiple GermGuardian GG1000 Pluggable Units, since the majority of the reviews are very good, and I am wanting a product like this in my home. I purposely did not order the other (square-type) pluggable unit with a usb charger, as the reviews stated that product was heavier and tended to pull away from the wall and the socket.  Well- I have to say I am VERY disappointed that all three of the units that I received from Amazon today are doing what the square-type product apparently does- they are all three pulling away from the wall and falling out of the socket.  I read many reviews and do not recall reading this as a problem for anyone.  The only way that I can get the unit to stay in the socket is to literally duct tape it to the wall.  The units are bottom heavy, and it doesn't make a difference if you turn the unit sideways- it still pulls out from the wall and socket.  I did give three stars because the product is actually working well/ removing odors.  However, I think GermGuardian needs to implement a fix here because of the heaviness of the unit and the pull tendency.  If I can't figure out a better way to anchor these units, they are all being returned.  I can't exactly give these as gifts and say, "Oh, btw, you'll need duct tape to make it work."

title: Humidity affects performance in a major way--needs water vapor to work properly
text:
Try to understand its limitations. Any device using UVC will produce some ozone. PCO devices require water vapor to produce hydroxyls instead. If you have humidity of about 60% it will probably work well. If humidity is low you won't get much hydroxyl action and its fresh feel, and will have irritating incomplete chemical byproducts. Some expensive PCO devices like Air Oasis place a gel inside to keep a supply of water vapor available for the process. I am considering one. Professional remediator units such as Titan hydroxyl generators specify 60% humidity. I bought this small Germ Guardian and put it in my basement and was very happy with it. Yay, i'll get more I thought. I bought some for other parts of my house and there was a very irritating smell. Put them in the garage to run and "off gas" and it was more horrible still. I sent all back but one in my basement which is still performing.

Well now I know that it was probably the humidity levels that were the issue. I'm in a very dry climate. My basement is cooler and has higher relative humidity than the rest of my house. So elsewhere in the house, I was getting ozone but little to no hydroxyl. Ozone is prone to leave breakdown products from VOCs. Here is a study of an industrial-level-remediation hydroxyl generator, which indicated it took about five days to completely break down house-fire type smoke odors in a testing room. http://envair.ca/wp-content/uploads/2016/06/Mike_Pinto_Hydroxyl_Radicals_for_Fire_Restoration_Part_2_Study_Final.pdf. They don't discuss humidity but this one does http://hydroxyltruths.com/Comparison-UVSystems%20Total%204-15-13.pdf.

Just found some mold on my pantry floor from a leaky container of fruit. Pulled out several cardboard containers with visible mold. Sprayed this https://www.amazon.com/EnviroKlenz-Fragrance-Free-Non-Toxic-Treatment-Upholstery/dp/B01I00V9II all over the floor and put my Germ Guardian in the pantry with a jar of water and a fabric pad sticking out to help diffuse it into the air. So get busy lil hydroxyls and decontaminate my pantry! I will leave it for several days and re-evaluate. Seems weird to be adding humidity to the air where mold is found, but we'll see. So far no nasty odors from the Germ Guardian like before.

title: Understanding how UVc works....
text:
***SEE UPDATE BELOW***
Original review - 9/13/14 - I've just ordered (3) of these units from Amazon for my own home so can't speak for the build quality of these units (yet), but work with UVc enough in large-scale commercial applications to know how the process works.

UVc works by converting some Oxygen (O2) molecules into Ozone (O3). Ozone has a very short life span, quickly reverting back to O2 when it comes into contact with a contaminant, but yet is also nature's most effective sanitizer. The process to create ozone is the same as you experience in lightning storms with the crisp smell when electricity is applied to the surrounding air.

Ozone removes odors very effectively but neutralizing the containment through oxidation. In addition, oxidation also kills many bacterias and some viruses not just in the air but any surfaces the treated air comes in contact with. It's like bleach but without the chemical smells and dangerous spills. This is why hospitals like this technology so much. The point to remember is ozone does NOT remove particles in the air, but those particles certainly are clean ones.

The low fan speed being reported is due the fact that applying an electrical charge to oxygen atoms takes some time, relatively speaking. You can't do this with a high volume of air across a single bulb thus the need for a slower speed of air movement. But the low speed air that does come out, will surely cleanse the air and surfaces it comes in contact with. This is also why this likely will only work in a small room or area (less than 500sqft I would guess). You would need more/larger bulbs with larger surfaces areas exposed in the air chamber to do larger volumes of air.

The UV-C light works in the 185nm and/or 254nm wavelength and is harmful if exposed, which is why the bulbs are sealed from direct view. Seriously, don't open the unit up and try to get it to work "better". There likely are safeguards to prevent this.

I'll follow up this review once I've had a chance to use the units myself.

**UPDATE - 10/2/2014**
I bought (3) and returned (2) after trying these units out (I never opened the other 2). I've also downgraded to 3 stars from 5 for the following reasons:
- Yes, this unit is loud. I tried it in kitchen and the hard surfaces (granite) just seemed to project the fan noise throughout the house. I've since demoted this to bathroom and it's still very loud even with door closed.
- Having tried it in kitchen and bath, it doesn't seem very effective. I found no discernible difference in letting this unit work versus time taken through natural dissipation of cooking/odors
- As mentioned in my original review, ozone is what removes odors through the use of UVc light. I see the product description and the packaging mention this unit produces no ozone. A quick visit to the manufacturer's website says the UVc light penetrates thin-walled viruses and bacteria altering the DNA. I can't speak for this method, so I have to assume the time exposed and the power generating the UVc light isn't sufficient enough to create the ozone. I see this as a reduction in effectiveness compared to my experiences with commercial applications of UVc. Granted, you don't want accumulated quantities of ozone confined in an indoor space and this product prevents that.

I tried many professional cleaniners specifically made for washer but none worked. The odor (and the germs, I presume) just wouldn't go away for at least 6 months. text:
I've used this product for a little under a year now.

I purchased it for the bathroom and tested it for cat litter. I haven't noticed anything different at all with the smells. It does move the air, but I have no idea (like everyone else) if the light is actually doing anything.

It may be killing germs, but the smells are still there.
You have to leave this plugged in to work. It is loud for me. Sounds like a blow dryer on low. Some people like it as white noise, I don't.

The only thing I found that effectively eliminates odors is the fresh wave crystal gels.
The replacement bulbs are pretty expensive as well.

This $40 purchase, plus electricity, plus replacement bulb after one year will run you around $100 every year.

I bought this based on some highly rated reviews, but many of the reviewers seem very suspicious after a closer look. They have only one or two reviews and rate the different models of germ guardian really high. Then another product they rate low. I wonder if they are paid reviewers.

Knowing the total cost, questionable reviews and uncertain effectiveness, I would not buy again and would not recommend it to anyone.

title: defective design
text:
I had an alarm clock many years ago that had a receptacle that I used to plug in a lamp. When the alarm set time was reached, the lamp lit. That's is basically what I wanted in this product. The problems started with the lighting of the panel. It is so bright, I could easily read by it. It keeps me awake. I've read that melatonin production is inhibited by any light source in the room. I went to a guy who installs window tinting and got some scraps of dark tint material and put several layers on the face of the clock. That helped, but then the clock face light quit altogether. For me, that was a good thing, even though I could no longer read the clock at night. I used a separate timepiece with a push-button light for that purpose. The supposed sunrise simulation is bogus. The designer has it step up in brightness, rather than a smooth gradient.

Interestingly, the guy who gave me the tinting material told me that people like me come in routinely for the same reason.

I'm an electronics engineer and have been programming lots of devices for most of my life. I found this thing to be very complicated to program and the icons are very hard to see, even after I removed the tinting material. When I'm sleepy and want to be sawing logs in a few minutes, the last thing I want to do is to start studying a new device, or try and remember the steps to follow to do something that should be really simple. I haven't quite thrown it in the trash, but it's getting close.

So, as a message to alarm clock manufacturers, consider building a device that does not unintentionally disturb your customer's sleep (what a concept!!!) by making it emit no light unless a button is pressed. Make it a simple and cheap device that simply activates an external receptacle (15A) in a gradual way by using a D/A converter with more than 4 bits. That's it: forget the radio, the CD player, the tweety bird, the lamp. I already have a lamp next to my bed. If I could turn it on and off with a button on the alarm clock and have the lamp SLOWLY and GRADUALLY come up to full brightness in the morning with an option for an aural alarm (just in case), I'd buy it. I want it so much that I'm considering building it.

title: Long Lasting gel pack
text: Many years ago now, when I went to a chiropractor, he gave these exact gel packs away for free, with his business printed on them. I have squished them, had them in the car, sat on them and they held together. So after many years, it was time for new ones, the old ones still can be used but they are not as plump an more, these are 5 years old. The gel is no longer clear and over time some as seeped out. I have looked and looked for gel packs but never thought to look on Amazon for this brand until the other day when I was using the old one, the light bulb kicked on and I found this 5 pack for a very reasonable price compared to others out there. And they were the product I have been used to. I have Osteoarthritis an am in lots of pain so I have these all over the house, one at the computer, one at my favorite chair, one in my bedroom, one in the refrigerator for a bad pain day. Now, these are very cool just at room temperature, I might add and sometimes they make your lower back sweat. SO what I came up with is a cover for them. I bought 13x13 washcloths here on Amazon, it was a pack of 4. Now you could use 12x12 but the 13x13 is the color and thickness I wanted. SO how do you make the cover? open the washcloth now fold it in half, making sure the fancy edge is up at the top ( if you look at image you can see it) . Now using straight pins pin along the bottom and up the side making sure all is even. I do not have a sewing machine so I sewed these by hand and all on the outside not turning them inside right ,and with needle and thread. I plan to put a button on them with just a thread loop to hold it closed ( good thing I saved old buttons, now if you do this, make sure your button is flat or your back will feel it). When all is said and done, your gel pack will stay in place, and not be sweaty against your back and even if you freeze the pack, the little pouch will protect your skin from the frozen object. This is where you can pick out one or more of those fancy thick facecloths with your favorite theme or color on it. the 13x13 one, you could fit two packs in one if you wanted extra padding. Any way, I hope you have a pain free day and hope you can use my idea with your new gel packs.

I was previously using and double headed toothbrush made by Enzydent for dogs teeth. It was time to replace the Enzydent toothbrush due to age (every 4 months). The bristles were becoming loose and it was becoming harder to clean my dogs teeth with the bristles becoming softer.

Well, I thou ghb t these were good at first, but I started noticing my dog develop tart and plaque build up on her teeth. I began to notice that the bristles on this double headed toothbrush are way way to soft for my dogs teeth. The bristles literally collapse around the teeth when brushing, when they need to stay semi firm to help polish and remove any food debris, ting plaque or tartar. I ended up taking my dog to the vet and showing him my dogs teeth and he even said the toothbrush is way way to soft to do anything. So I threw these in the trash and began my search for a better toothbrush. I finding a better toothbrush with semi stiff bristles. After two brushing sessions with a newer toothbrush I can see it removing some plaque and tartar that the ones I originally bought weren't doing at all.

Its really sad, as I had John Hope's for these when I bought them off Amazon. Unfortunately I cannot recommend these I would instead search around for great dog toothbrushes and find one with semi stiff bristles m.

title: Lots of pure menthol crystals!
text:
This is as basic as it gets: Just as close to 100% pure for menthol crystals. Just not that when you do decide to use these you won't need much.

I created a liquid by dissolving 1gm of menthol crystals in 10mL of propylene glycol (PG) to make a simple oil-like extract (100mg/ml). I microwaved the PG for FIVE SECONDS to make it warm enough to easily dissolve the crystals. This extract can be bottled up and dripped into or onto anything that needs some mintiness. The resulting extract can be mixed with isopropyl alcohol for a very basic and cool liniment.

You don't need much menthol since this is very pure stuff. One pound of this will last a VERY long time! There's no sugar or anything else. It's all icy-cool menthol.

title: Difficult to get out of crevices/messy
text:
This is most likely being used by children that need some work on their brushing habits. It can be a great tool for that, but some things to consider first:

1) It can be messy. Once inserted into the mouth, you chew it up like a Flintstones vitamin--tastes similar. Everything in your mouth turns dark purple. You will need to spit the excess into the sink once entire mouth is coated (this can be a challenge depending on age). Depending on your child's motor skills, purple splatter can end up on the counter, walls, floor, and on them (it will obviously be in the sink). So keep that in mind.

2) An entire tablet may not be needed depending upon age of person using it--my son is 8 and I could probably get away with using only half at a time.

3) If the person using it has deep crevices in their teeth, they may not be able to get it all out in one brushing. This results in in dissolving slowly and keeping a light pinkish/purple hue in your mouth. My husband and I both tried brushing out bits that were stuck in the crevices of our son's teeth, as well as in between his teeth, and were unable to do so completely. For this reason, I recommend only using at night.

For these reasons, I don't recommend using frequently unless you feel absolutely necessary, and recommend monitoring children using these tablets.

text:
Bought this to use on my favorite belt - a custom-made three-braid saddle leather belt that's over 10 years old that I wear almost everyday, doing everything from casual wear to mowing the lawn in summer and running the snow blower in the winter. In other words, it has seen more than its fair share of wear over those years.

title: The 4 Stars isn't the Aria's Fault...
text:
Okay, there are some flaws that all of these scales. They use inductance to measure body fat %%. I'm not going to get too deep into the electrical definition of inductance - but for the sake of argument - it's measuring the electrical resistance between one foot and the other. It does some pretty fancy calculations based on your height (that you tell the software) - your weight, which it measures pretty accurately... and it tries to figure out your body fat percentage. Then, it does some more math and will figure your lean body mass.

Overall, it's a pretty neat technology... but it's not 100% accurate. Now - just to be clear - it's not a flaw with the Fitbit Aria specifically, just in all inductance scales. There's no way for the scale to know how hydrated you are... if you're retaining water or excessively dehydrated - it throws off the calculations between fat mass and lean mass. I've had it jump 3-4% body fat in the space of a day. It's best to watch trends in the readings... it's not a medical grade device, but if you weigh yourself at the same time every day, get into a routine... then you can watch trends in your body weight and what it says is your body fat %%.

Knowing that - I'd still recommend this scale.

It's fairly simple and straight forward to set this up - get it connected to your wireless network and associated with your Fitbit account. Just follow the instructions closely. It will connect up to your wireless network - it'll sync with your Fitbit account almost instantaneously.

Fitbit has a very very nice ecosystem of health monitoring products. For me, it's not just the bands and it's not just the scales... but you can use their app to view how you sleep, how active you are, resting HR... and with this scale, your weight and (relative) body fat %%, lean body %%... and you're able to have some objective numbers to watch.

I'm giving this 4 stars because as neat as the technology is, it's not perfect, but just to be clear, it's not a problem specific to the Aria

title: Finally, A Natural Way to Wake Up!
text:
I bought this Good Morning Sunrise Wake-Up Alarm Clock for myself for Christmas because my bedroom does not have any windows and I wanted to walk up with the light again. Since I started working nights, my internal time clock is chaotic and I over sleep or undersleep almost every day. I need the light to wake up.

This clock was alittle difficult to get set up, with so many options. The light can be adjusted, the sounds can be adjusted, the radio can be set, the time needs to be adjusted. I haven't gone through all the options yet, but the gradual lighting of my room has been fantastic. I only wish the light would come on more slowly, as it goes from dark to light in 15 minutes.

The nature sounds are nice too and there are several options, some more annoying than pleasant. But everyone will have different favorites because this is a personal thing.

Overall, I would highly recommend this product as it does everything it claims. I have been better rested since I set up this product in my windowless room.

title: Miles better than alcohol for cleaning up TIM.
text:
I've been building PCs for over 20 years now and I've always used either rubbing alcohol or denatured alcohol to clean thermal paste from my heatsinks and CPUs. Arctic Clean works much better than any alcohol solvents I've tried.

You just put a few drops of the solvent on the grease and let it sit for a minute. It completely dissovles the grease and lets you easily wipe it up. No smearing at all.

Once you've removed the existing paste just put a couple drops of the purifier on and wipe it clean. The purifier is almost like a thicker version of rubbing alchol. It dries quickly and doesn't run all over the place after being applied.

I'm disappointed I waited this long to try this stuff, it's defintely worth the money if you're going to be cleaning up thermal paste.

Be aware though that it is rather large (11" x 3 1/4"), and the motor's noise can be distracting. Also, I don't recommend it for men who are on the small side or overly large. title: Room for improvement
text:
This thing is $9, so expectations should be somewhat tempered, I realize. I was traveling and wanted something that would fit in my pocket to hold a couple of each of my pills for easy access throughout the day without having to carry around multiple pill bottles. This is attractive enough, compact but with adequate capacity for my daily needs, easy to open, and has three separate compartments. I am not at all convinced the shell is actually metal, feeling and sounding much more like plastic, but again, for the price, whatever.

The real problem is that when closed, there is too much space between the lid and the top of the divider, so when it’s in your pocket or bag, all the contents are jostling around, colliding into one another and the container itself. Not only had the pills not stayed in their own compartments, several of them had been broken into shards, some nearly disintegrated altogether and the remainder coated in their dust.

If this is going to sit somewhere, stationary, it may work for you. If you intend to make any movements with this in your possession AND you actually want to be able to take the medicine you put inside of it, it will almost assuredly not work for you.

title: Ear plugs perfected
text:
For those following, I have tried several sets of ear plugs, in the quest for the most comfortable one, with ease of insertion, and a high amount of noise reduction. After going through several models, from different manufacturers, these Howard Leight Max 1's have emerged as my current favorites.

For starters, they claim to be the best selling polyurethane ear plug, and are used throughout industrial applications. I figure if they are good enough for a construction site or factory floor, where workers use them day after day, that is a good start that they are more than adequate for my needs at home.

They are smoother than other plugs, and this enhances the ease of insertion. While, at least for me, it takes a few attempts to get the ear plug fully in, these Max 1's go right into the ear canal fully on the first shot. They are also airy, and roll down easily despite their larger size. This makes them fast to put in, so the work can begin without the frequent delays I had while inserting other ear plugs.

Once in place, it is important to hold them in place for 30 secs to let them fully expand. Once that happens, they are the most comfortable I have used, and they feel like a "mini marshmallow," exerting just enough pressure to stay in place and stop the noise, but nothing more. They are totally comfortable, whether for an overnight sleep, or working a long day while in place.

They have a 33 NRR, which puts them at the top of any ear plug for sale that I have found. When I compare them to other ear plugs with the same high NRR, I fnd them the quietest of any ear plug that I have used. After all, this is what you use an ear plug for anyway!

The selling point of these Max 1's is that they are a little larger than some other products. This is a selling feature to those with larger ear canals (typically males and Caucasians) that do not get an effective seal with standard size, or slim fit ear plugs.

As an added feature, I like the bright orange color. I find it a safety feature to let folks know that I will not hear them if they start talking while I am working.

They come prewrapped in a clear plastic pack, that is even perforated for easy removal.

In short, this 10 pair makes a perfect fitting trial, before committing to purchasing the larger box to confirm if it serves your needs.

title: Didn't work correctly and overpriced for it's lack of features
text:
I work in EMS and I decided to get this to use both for family, as well as use it while on a BLS truck without a monitor.
Initial impressions seemed fairly positive. The unit itself moderately sized- about the length/width of a Nintendo 3DS when opened up, but obviously much thicker. When I first opened the box I saw a universal power adapter which I thought was a bit weird. When I opened the actual pouch the unit came in (which was a nice touch!) I saw that the power adapter has a European Type-C plug. I guess they must've given me the European Model, but it did come in English so.... It did let our a rather unsettling large spark of electricity when I plugged it the wall.

I first tried the hand-held mode which.. did not work at all. It kept saying no contact. Well whatever, so next I moved onto using the limb leads (making sure to set the mode to limb) and yeah, it worked, albeit with some artifacting. It unfortunately only shows 3 leads, despite having 4 electrodes which could easily offer up the augmented vector leads... Even more bizarre is the firmware actually has options to view leads V1-6, not sure how they manage that without a 12-lead.... I also noticed it also does pulse-oximetry. I thought great, I've got a USB probe so I can try it in this unit since it has a USP port. Well, No. What the images don't show is that the pulse-ox only works using their proprietary six-pin adapter, which is clearly marked on the actual unit itself, just not on the images. Oh you can buy one from their site, it's $125 or so.... Yeah Uh after shelling out almost $250, I'm not about to drop more.... I mean I probably would have kept it if the hand-held EKG mode worked but, yeah no, it's not worth it with that busted.

tl;dr:

PROS:
Color display
Large display
4-limb connectors
Audible alerts
Carry case
SpO2 monitoring
PC Software has nice features

CONS:
No augmented vectors for EKG
Pulse-ox not included
EU model(?)
Artifacts on EKG waveform
Low Gain

title: Life Changing!
text:
These are fantastic, I don’t write reviews but I wanted to make sure that if you were looking for a TRULY life changing insole you spent the money on these. I want to preface this by saying I have tried the Dr. Sholes machine for specific orthotics, plantar fasciitis insoles (many different brands) and about every “sport” insole out there. These by far are the best and do the most for my feet, back and legs in general. I have had lower back surgery to remove a sever hernia, have had plantar fasciitis for 10 years and also ligament damage to my foot (thank you special forces) so needless to say at 31 my lower half is pretty beat up.

Its hard for me to stand in one place for more than 10 minutes and it always feel like my left foot is going to explode, I’m a triathlete so I still puts lots of “soft” miles on my body, these really do allow me to run more. Don’t be fooled, there is no one product that can really take all the pain away but these do a great job of mitigating the pain not only when I run but mainly allow me to get back out there day after day. With other products I could mentally muscle through a workout but I would be smoked for a few days after, even with lots of icing and therapy. These do a great job and are very comfortable once you get used to the air moving around, they actually feel like they capitulate you forward slightly with the air moving back to from and vice versa with every step.

Even at 215 pounds these really do stand up to punishment, I played 6 hours of tennis my third day wearing them. You can simply throw them in the washer and they clean right up with no issues as stated in their directions. I will say that my first pair had a malfunction and one of them flattened out, I immediately ordered a second pair from amazon to get them the next day because I didn’t want to go without them. The return policy was great, I sent back the bad pare and then immediately sent me another, no hassle and no issues.

I will wear these for the rest of my life and don’t go without them when wearing shoes (u can wear them with flip flops but I choose not to). I literally take them out of my dress shoes of all shapes (square toes, wingtips, ect) and throw them in my running shoes then into my cleats for softball. They literally feel great in any shoe.

Thank you AirFeet and if you haven’t realized it yet I highly recommend this product and wrote this detailed review in hopes that another runner/triathlete or soccer mom who has feet issues can help relieve some pain.

title: Not for the Slue-Footed
text:
As the care giver, I was excited to get my cousin this upright rollator. Reluctantly, I had to return it for his use.

PROS: It's pretty and is easy to assemble and disassemble with its instructions. It weighs less than our current comodita roller. It is way more affordable and was on sale for even less at the time. Encourages user to walk in upright position.

CONS: Not enough foot room for someone slue-footed. Was unable to completely rest forearms down in armrests. While can adjust horizontally, cant adjust vertically or diagonally. As a result, could not walk continuously and comfortably.
Too bulky to fit in my large car trunk (Chysler 300) without lowering arms and totally emptying truck. Too bulky to easily fit in back seat. Once I did, no one else can sit in back seat.

Side note:. Non Slue-Footed caregiver can use upright with no problem with foot room or armrest. Good for daily walk and back arthritis. Still has car storage issues. Don't have home storage for 2 rollators.

title: Portable, Stylish, Sideway Fold Rollator
text:
Just received my second order of the same rollator. Amazon refunded me $50 for I didn't receive storage or transport bags. Luckily I already have these from another earlier order. Only 3 colors available. First order I was able to choose among more colors. First order was red. Handles are different from first order (no thumb rest) but cushioned which is nice. Expandable height and rear width seems a tad less than the first order when comparing side by side and pulling out tape measure. First one taller than the box of the second one when storing first one for spare parts. Now wondering if box was mislabeled like for the petite model. Sure hope not. Not sure which order is the latest model. User says the new one is still comfortable and he likes it even the new handles and color. I don't think he notices that it may be like 1 inch shorter in height and back width when walking with it. Sitting and handling are the same for him he says. Rollator gets a lot of attention at the adult day care center (ADCC).

First rollator I ordered about 1 year ago. User uses it on average 5 days a week at the ADCC. Shuttle driver, user and caregiver (me) love it for it folds sideways and is not heavy. Its flexible for fitting in tight places like small doorways. User is slew footed so the extra foot room near the back wheels keep him from tripping and falling. This feature and side folding are what sold me on this rollator which cost more than others. The downside is it broke which I chalk up to the daily storing on the shuttle bus. I think the drivers are a little heave handed so I asked current driver to treat the new rollator with better care. There are two plastic tubings that hold the seat and removable bag in place. One of them broke off so I couldn't use the portable storage bag if I wanted. Also one of the screw/nuts came out so couldn't use anymore as a seat. A trip to Home Depot could have remedied this had I found the problem before I had to place the second emergency order which came on a Sunday! Thanks Amazon Prime. The brakes do need adjusting I found out when I tested so I will do doing it for the second rollator. I ordered it again so its pretty good. I love that I can fold it up compactly for travel (e.g., cruise cant wait). It fits in the back seat laying sideways or in my truck for my outings with its user.

Recommendation for Comodita: Place brake line inside or clipped to frame so it looks even more stylish. User didn't have problem with this as is.

title: Ingeniously simple design but effective to relieve neck pain.
text: I have experienced chronic neck pain for many years with multiple causes. The first time I was prescribed neck traction it consisted of a contraption that was hooked over a door. You would fill a gallon milk container with water to use as a weight for the traction. Truthfully that type was not effective for me only to give my family members a reason to laugh at me strapped to the door. The next device was  purchased at a medical supply company. You would lie on the floor on your back placing/strapping your head on it. Slowly pumping a bulb to the desired pressure. Both options were stationary. This neck traction device is not stationary. You can move around to be comfortable. Able to read a book or watch TV to pass the time. The body of the device is made up of 3 inflatable neck pillows. The fabric is soft and comfortable. You pump air into it by a bulb that is like the bulb you use to take a blood pressure. There is an additional mechanism to lock so the air will not escape/leak. You have control of how much air is pumped in/the amount of traction. As with any medical device besides receiving your doctors approval you proceed cautiously and gradually. One of my diagnosis that contributes to my chronic neck pain is degenerative disc disease. I benefit from the gentle stretch and release of pressure that neck traction achieves. This is a quality product which I recommend. One last tip is to release air slowly before removing device. Best wishes for relief of your pain.

title: Helps a lot
text:
The prenatal cradle has helped my back pain significantly, and I am happy with it. It gets 4 stars because it doesn't relieve my back pain completely. In addition, the sizing is hard to get right. Most reviews said even if you rate as a size small according to the prenatal cradle's weight recommendations, to get a size medium. Therefore, that's what I did. I use it on the smallest of the three settings, and it works pretty well. However, I was just beginning my 3rd trimester when I started wearing it. I am quite large (this is my second pregnancy, and at 32 weeks now I've already exceeded the amount of weight I gained during my entire pregnancy the first time around, which ended just before 36 weeks), but I'm also only 5 feet tall. Yet, even now, I am 40 lbs below the minimum suggested weight for the size medium. Had I ordered the cradle sooner, and I needed it sooner because my back started hurting during my second trimester, it might have been too large to use at first even on the smallest setting. Whether or not the prenatal cradle size small would have worked throughout my second and third trimesters, I will never know, but I'm thinking it would have. So my suggestion would be if you are short, to get the size that does match your weight, and if you are an average or tall height, to get one size larger than your weight.

I'd also like to mention that I tried a couple of the supporters that go around the hips and lower back. One of them relieved my back pain completely, but it squeezed my hips so much that it hurt my hips to walk, and it folded over and was uncomfortable when I sat down. The other one I tried made my back hurt even more than without wearing it. The prenatal cradle is very comfortable while sitting or standing, and as I mentioned earlier, helps reduce my back pain a ton. I do wear a thin, stretchy, seamless, short-sleeved shirt underneath it. Good luck!

title: but I am nursing and it was recommended to me by my OB that I continue to ...
text:
I am no longer pregnant, but I am nursing and it was recommended to me by my OB that I continue to take prenatal vitamins while doing so. I have had some issues on and off since pregnancy with yeast infections, so I thought the probiotics would also be a good idea.

I have taken some other brands of probiotics that just really tore up my stomach for days. I'm glad to say this one, so far, hasn't been too harsh. It is a bit annoying having to take this supplement in two pills, but if that is the way I have to do it then it is convenient to only have to buy one item instead of two.

I was hoping by continuing to take prenatals, that the typical postpartum hair loss wouldn't occur, but that has not been the case unfortunately. I can't say anything negative about the vitamin part of this package, it's perfect as far as a vitamin goes. It isn't too hard to swallow although it is on the larger side, typical of a prenatal vitamin pill. I also didn't get any foul aftertaste.

The biggest issue I had with this product is the packaging. I found the packs pretty hard to separate even though there were perforated lines. I ended up having to cut them apart and then stick a pen or knife tip into the pill section to get them out. Pretty bad if you accidentally puncture the probiotic capsule, so watch out for that.

I received this product at a discount in exchange for my unbiased review. My opinions are my own and were not influenced by this fact.

title: So.. um.. Ya... This happened...
text:
For Valentines Day, my wife got me a couple of these FBombs.. because, ya know.. I'm on a Keto/Adkins high fat - no carb diet. Wait - no I'm not.
Pour this into your coffee! It'll give you energy!! Ok... I pour it into my coffee.
10:00am: I drink the oil-coffee and enjoy the twist of pure coconut oil and palm oil in my bullet proof Folgers original. Not bad.
10:30.. I get down to the last ounce or so and notice.. something is not feeling quite right in the ole tummy.. gurgle-pop-groaaan.. Hmm...
11 o'clock.. I'm beginning to hear sounds that remind me of one of those soundboard downloads from the late 90's of struggling bowels. Nothing like what my body had produced before.
Noon.. time for lunch. I go the safe route and get a burger from my local pub and have a tea. Nothing crazy, cuz I have no idea whats going on. I get 3/4 done with my burger and it hits me... I'm about to crap my pants.
(I am not a public pooper, so I'm in a real pinch here). I flag down the waitress like I'm trying to get the attention of the traffic helicopter.. pay my bill.. and hightail it back to work. It's still public, but it's WAY better than erupting at the bar.
12:53pm.. it begins.. I'll skip the details, but lets just say it was like a slip n' slide party back there for the next 6 hours.
7:00pm.. It's still not over.
11:00pm.. party's still raging.
5:00am.. the majority of party goers have left the building, but we're still making some crazy sounds.
4:00PM the NEXT DAY.. the aftershocks are still prevalent. I'm sure I'll survive... but @#$%&$# #$&&!!!
Be careful folks... this stuff is.... EFFECTIVE....
This is NOT for casual use.
This IS a great gift idea for someone you hate.
I'm positive it serves the purpose for folks that are on lo-carb / high fat diets.. but for the rest of us... Don't do it, man!
As for my wife... I'm sure she (wait there's another grumble below!) I'm sure she feels bad, but I'm also sure shes been laughing her @$$ at all this.

title: The front part is excellent for necklaces that tend to get tangled
text:
Since this was only around $17, I wasn't expecting much; however, I was pleasantly surprised. The front part is excellent for necklaces that tend to get tangled, and I like that it snaps for those necklaces that don't have clasps. It has two small pockets for the rest of the necklace to go in, and even if I shake it a little, they tend to stay in those pockets.
The middle part is roomy enough for several pairs of earrings, and it's a good thick material so they won't slide around. The holes are also spaced fairly far apart so you can put several dangling earrings in there and have room for studs as well. And also I use safety pin to hold my charms in the ear holes. which it is great.
The next flap was just a zipper pouch, and I had enough room for one pearl necklace and the matching pearl bracelet, so it's not super roomy...
The thing about the ring holder is that it was kind of hard to get my rings on it...it's wide at the top of the thick ribbon, and the snap is kind of bulky. I wear a size 6 1/2 ring, so if you wear a 6 or smaller, I doubt your rings would slide down it.
In the outer flap I could fit 3 long necklaces and a few thin bracelets. I could fit one big giant chunky bangle just inside the whole organizer since it's kind of wide. I usually take two middle out of the case to give more room which make very slim case. which I like it about.
I'd say this was a very good purchase. It held much more jewelry than a roll, and it wasn't as expensive as several others I saw. Also, it kind of looks like a makeup case when closed, so I don't think you'll have to worry about leaving it in the bathroom at a hotel...love it.

title: HELPS PREVENT Sensory Overload Anxiety
text:
I looked into this product to combat my anxiety from sensory overload. I can't function well in loud environments, whether I'm in a loud lobby, or I am in a lecture with a loud professor, these earplugs have helped make these environments quieter for me. I love how much these earplugs allow me to comfortably hear those directly around me while making everything/one else almost mute. I also can't stand loud sound effects in scary movies, but this product has helped me enjoy all types of movies again.

If you're concerned about this product getting lost in your ears, DON'T. I would say I have average ear canals and I have had no issues applying/removing these earplugs. Also, the fact that they're transparent helps give me more peace of mind because the last thing I want is to have people easily notice that I have earplugs on in class, or in public settings. Honestly, my only complaint is the little container these plugs come in. The threading on the screw cap feels a bit cheap. Pros:

Cons:

1. Quality. Bristles fall out after a few days of use. However, to be fair, the quality seems to have improved somewhat in the last year that I've used these replacement heads, and bristles don't fall as often as they used to.

2. Still, due to sub-par quality, these replacement heads do not last nearly as long as genuine ones.

Overall, the number one reason to use these replacement heads is the price. Genuine Oral-B heads are expensive and if you use your Oral-B toothbrush 2-3 times a day than buying cheap substitute leads to substantial savings over time.

title: Miracle Cure for Infected Wounds!
text:
I am originally from Germany and we have used Kernseife since I was a little girl. In my family it was often used when we developed an infection from stepping on something and bacteria entered the wound. Instead of going to the doctor and getting antibiotics, my dad just had has soak the affected body part and the infection resolved itself even in cases like lymphangitis. It can be used on humans and animals.

Here is how to use it: clean the wound with running, warm water, drop the soap in the water and either allow it to sit or prepare by making a very soapy water (like washing your already washed hands over and over in the water), take out soap to dry to store for later, and then soak the affected body part. Dry off and either apply Neosporin or just a band-aid. We did not have Neosporin and a band-aid did the job. It may take a couple of days of soaking but even with the worst case of lymphangitis when I was 11 years old, it disappeared after just one soak.

Good luck and I hope it works for you as good as it works for me. :)

Rob's wife

title: They work very well!
text:
I was very impressed with this set of Pet Hair Removers. We have a fabric sofa and a Blue Heeler mix who sheds gobs of dog hair. It's so gross. we like to keep fleece blankets on the sofa to cover with when we watch movies on Friday nights but they always get so full of dog hair. Then I throw them in the wash and they come out with less dog hair, but still quite a bit. so....I bought these...hoping they will minimize some of the dog hair in the wash and help me get dog hair off the sofa.
I was skeptical at first because I have tried lint rollers, those paddles/brushes have have the one directional fibers that are supposed to magically sweep the dog hair away and those things hardly work at all. BUT, I first tried one of these things on the sofa. It quickly gathered up a decent gob of fur that I was able to grab and throw away. Those fleece blankets I love so much.....threw those in the wash with these sticky hair removers and WOW!!!!The had quite a bit of fur on both of them and less fur in the lint catcher. Then all I did was rinse them outside(I don't want all that fur going down the drains) with a dab of Dawn dish soap. They are both sticky again and ready for the next wash.
The shape of this set of Pet Hair Removers works well for my hands too. They are easy to grip and I don't get any cramping in my hands at all from swiping them over the couch fabric. They were worth it and worked much better than I thought they would. I would buy them again.

title: DownBeats are the best soft sound attenuators I've used.
text:
I need ear plugs of some kind for a number of reasons. I have extremely sensitive hearing and tend to get uncomfortable adrenalin surges when loud and sudden noises occur. I also like to attend concerts from music types from orchestral traditional music to jazz/fusion to all-out metal rock music.

In the work I do (IT, office-based business), I am called to conference rooms for meetings several times a day. Inevitably, someone on the conference speaks mouse-quiet and someone has the microphone permanently embedded in their teeth so that not only are they louder than anyone, we get treated to breathing and mouth noises for an hour at a time. Also, inevitably, the person running the call has the speaker/speakerphone turned up to its maximum volume. With some folks, this isn’t a bad thing. With most, however, it’s really grueling to have remote callers screaming at you at 125 or more decibels for long periods of time. This is the PERFECT time for the DownBeats ear plugs. They fit my small-medium ear channels, and they aren’t grossly obvious to my colleagues. This is a life saver for me: it really is excruciating when a caller is screaming at me through low-fi speakers in the room for what seems like a lifetime.

Some have asked about the color of the stems. My family has four sets of DownBeats, and all of them have clear stems. It might be a manufacturing batch or maybe a supply difference that causes some to have white stems. None of ours have white stems and hide very nicely in our ear channels.

When I go to concerts, the DownBeats aren’t quite as attenuating as I would like. They work great and are very unobtrusive to my ears (as in, how they feel in my ears) and are unobtrusive to the sound quality, save a little shaving off of the high trebles and a bit of the mids. For me (this is a personal thing), I would like for them to attenuate a little more when I am at a loud concert. When the sound technician is attempting to produce the current show as if she/he was engineering The Who in the 70s, I find the DownBeats lacking a bit. At a recent Pat Metheny concert, I couldn’t have been happier: the Carolina Theater in Durham had the balance, EQ, and volume just right (and besides, Path Metheny and his folks understand a little –used thing called dynamics).

To give you an idea of the flexibility of the fit of DownBeats, I can use an Apple ear phone reference to help you: my ears channels are small to medium. Apple EarPods and ear buds don’t fit in my ear. I’ve never been able to use them because they don’t even slightly fit in my ear channels. My wife, on the other hand, has much larger ear channels and comfortably wears both Apple EarPods and the older ear buds. Here’s the punchline: The DownBeats fit both our ear channels just fine. They are flexible and soft enough to really do the trick.

One more thing about comfort… They’re very shallow. I have deep ear pockets and my wife has shallow ear pockets. In my case, I have learned how to grip the DownBeats by their stems and push them in my ear channels in just the right way. It takes a moment to get them settled in or get them out, but in neither case is it hard to do. In addition, I can wear them for a few hours at a time without having ear-compression issues or ear-contact sounds that are irritating. With my wife, the DownBeats are really easy to pop in or out, as her smaller fingers and larger ear pockets give her more room to get the DownBeats just right.

Overall, I’m very happy with them. We have a couple of pairs in her purse and one on my keychain. I also have a set at work I keep on my badge for ready use for those lovely multi-continent dial-in meetings.

The DownBeats beat the pink foam ear inserts for me at concerts because DownBeats don't kill the best parts of the sound spectrum - although pink foam inserts to make loud concerts quieter.

This is a really good product, I ordered these because I have a job which requires A LOT of walking and running around all day long which causes pain in my ball of foot. I tried some the best ranking amazon products but none of them worked for me. I ordered these because after my experience with some of the silicone metatarsal pads I ordered on amazon, they felt great on my feet taking away almost 60% of my pain. So I knew that silicone will be much comfortable and cushiony than gel.

The only reason I'm giving a 4 star rating for this product is because A.) I really wish they were long enough to cover the toes because in order to use these, you have to remove the old insoles from your shoes. These are not long enough to cover the toes so when you wear your shoes with these insoles, your toes are not on the same level as the rest of your foot, they drop a bit so it does cause pain in the toes which is weird but it's true. (I actually cut my old insoles around the toe area and placed that in the shoe before putting these in.)

B.) My second reason is that, although these are wonderful insoles, great for work but I wish they came without the arch. I don't have flat feet, but I also don't have high arch and these would be perfect for someone with high arch feet. For me, they start to hurt after some time..I have normal feet with normal arch and I really don't need arch support in my insole.

Overall, it's a good product..it can be great if they consider the two suggestions I wrote up there (long enough to cover the toes and no arch support).

title: Really unimpressed
text:
The scale was really fussy to setup, and we setup hardware and networks for a living. It was doable, but not very smooth for a consumer level product. It is an expensive scale and they really should have done better than only supporting 802.11b.

The initial setup turned out to be the best part.

The scale does not appear to be very accurate. In tests against 5 other scales, including a medical balance beam scale it is 5 out of 6 for proximity to the other scale's reading, and the adding of weight when holding a known quantity weight.

It currently won't let anyone else get invites. Fitbit doesn't allow their support forums to be accessed by people who are not signed in, so an internet search did not turn up the problem. Eventually I logged into the site and discovered that it is a known problem, but a couple of days later it isn't fixed. Mainly the level of customer service is really disappointing. They suggest submitting a trouble ticket for a workaround, but they are very slow to respond to trouble tickets. Others are reporting responses to trouble tickets such as "check you spam box" when there is already supposed to be a known and acknowledged problem system wide where new invites cannot go out, yet clearly not all CS agents are properly informed.

The scale has also randomly spammed the fitbit account with a dozen weigh-ins within the same minute, of a completely erroneous weight, which caused all kinds of incorrect badges to be issued, despite the whole "matching" via similar weight making it so that it should not ever think that one person has lost 25 lbs in a single day.

The bodyfat reading appears to be based on a calculation of weight/height/sex which is sort of fine because none of the bioelectrical impedance scales really do an accurate job (although at least the ones with foot and hand sensors do (which this does not have) are a little more reliable.

Not worth the money. Not worth it at half the price.

title: ARIA Scale is AWESOME ! ! ! ! !
text: I have had my Aria scale for more than a year now.  It has always synced perfectly with my Fitbit.com dashboard and also with the Fitbit Zip that I wear all day to track my activities.  I love having more than a year's worth of information at hand on the fitbit website.  The Aria tracks my weight and body fat percentage.  I have read some reviews where they said that the scale was not accurate.  I do not find that to be true at all.  It should be noted that the body fat percentage is not going to be accurate until you are below 50% body fat.  So, if you are starting out huge like I did then do not expect to use that function until you are below 50%.  Once you have this scale synced to their website you will love it.  Set up was not difficult.  Just log into fitbit.com and get registered and follow the instructions.  By the way, my 60$ zip does track the number of active minutes per day so it is not necessary to by the more expensive unit to get that information.  Even if you do not buy this scale you can still register at fitbit.com and use their dashboard FOR FREE.  You would simply be entering the information yourself until you get a wi/fi scale and/or an activity tracker.  It is a great place to keep track of everything fitness/diet related. I can even enter all the food I eat and have a complete historical record. I give this scale 5 stars.
