title: Great addition to our lifestyle!  We love being able to see the trends over time.
text:
After having used this scale now ever since they first launched it, I can say that I love it! Having an everyday item in my life that seamlessly data logs an important metric (i.e. my weight and body fat) is awesome!

The scale is simple, modern looking, and easy to use.

Note that the first one I got did die shortly after I got it, but Fitbit replaced it for free and the replacement has been seamless so far.

Over time they have improved the software I think via firmware updates which I think among other things has improved the battery life.

Both my wife and I use this scale and it automatically detects who used it (based on weight), however, if multiple people that use it are close in weight it might get confused. In this case, you have to tap on the scale after weighing yourself to tell it which user to log the data under. My wife and I are far enough apart in weight that this has not been an issue except for a couple times when one of us accidentally forced it to select the other user incorrectly and then it gets confused (and you have to go manually re-assign data points on the web site to the correct user).

Absolutely would purchase again.

-Eric

title: pros and cons
text:
This is an interesting supplement that I've been taking on and off for a couple years. The thing is, it's the only thing I've tried that can calm down my heart palpitations; I'm prone to anxiety attacks and the palpitations cause me even more anxiety so as long as I can get rid of those I have an easier time calming myself down and the attack ending quick. So, for that reason this is a godsend for me. However, unfortunately it comes with some weird side effects for me. It affects me mentally to the point where I feel like I'm almost drunk (but not a good drunk), or sick, like everything is very slowed down and I almost feel like everything is going in slow motion. It's really strange. I'm not sure what this means or what I can do about it, I've experimented with different dosages, added sea salt to the water like the box says but I can't get rid of that unusual symptom. I am really sensitive to supplements in general so I generally try to avoid them and have paradoxical reactions to a lot of things (other magnesium supplements I've tried have actually made my palpitations worse, or brought on palpitations even when I was feeling fine, so maybe my body just has a weird sensitivity to this), so it probably won't apply to you, but just putting it out there.

To the people complaining about the taste, I really don't get it...it just tastes like slightly mineralized/salted water. You're supposed to dilute it in a big glass of water so you really shouldn't have a strong taste at all. I actually like the taste, but it's very subtle.

text: I've had A-fib on an off all my life, but it kicked into gear 24/7 last November and my family doctor referred me to a cardiologist. I had heard about the benefits of magnesium, but the cardiologist told me, and I quote: "Sure, I always recommend magnesium to my patients, but magnesium won't stop your A-fib." Well, neither did the two heart drugs that she tried, and I'm pretty sure she wasn't recommending cell ready liquid magnesium to her patients. I was getting pretty discouraged and panicky. I felt all along that A-fib wasn't the big deal that well paid doctors here were trying to tell me it was, so I began to research this in earnest, and that's how I came across Dr. Dean and her magnesium miracle. I ordered ReMag and ReMyte and her book on A-fib and pretty soon, my heart rate started to go down but not enough and not in time to prevent the cardiologist from sending me to to an "ablationist" (an expert in burning your heart in an often unsuccessful attempt to stop A-fib). By the time I got in to see the "ablationist" the ECG detected no arrythmia. He said there was no point in my continuing to take the heart drug. Let's see, I started ReMag and ReMyte at the end of March, after the cardiologist had given up on me, and got the good news at the end of May. That's two months. I feel better than ever, much stronger physically so I'm guessing that my bone density is greatly improving. (Just to add that the arrythmia started to diminish slowly, kicked up a bit within that last few weeks but not for very long, then appears to have just disappeared entirely.) I've got an appointment with the cardiologist tomorrow and will be curious to see how she handles the "news". My guess is that she will be not at all curious as to how I cured myself. (Turns out she wasn't. Imagine that!) Tapering off my heart drug is causing some electrical disturbance, but I hope to just ride it out using Dr. Dean's products.

title: Over engineered with quality that I expect will last years
text:
Functionally this is no different than cheaper pill bottles. It holds pills and can easily attach to a keychain. So why spend 10x more on this one? Quality. The rubber o rings make a satisfying and confident seal when the chambers screw together. The whole container is heavier than expected and has thick sides with equally thick top and bottom.

When you hold it you feel quality and expect it to last forever. Imagine the 1950's when things were engineered to 110% of their specifications and you have this. I've only have it a while but I think this is one of the "buy one for life" sort of things instead of the cheaper pill bottles "buy one a month" expectation.

The only trouble I can foresee is when the rubber rings wear out. But those are a simple $0.10 Home Depot replacement. And that's like complaining that the clutch or brake pads will eventually need replacing on a new car.

text:
Not the kind of person to leave harsh reviews but IDK what was going through the minds that created this flavor and decided to charge 50 bucks for it. Outright smells like my cat barfed.

Taste - 0 => Literally the worst tasking preworkout supplement I've ever had. My one other buddy almost threw up at the gym before he could finish sipping a scoop of this.

Mix-ability - 2/10 => Takes a while to mix, unlike most other supplements in this category which mixes readily by stirring once or twice, this needs a blender or robotic arm. I've seen this with cheap BCAAs, they neither mix and have that potent gross BCAA aftertaste.

Effectiveness - 5/10 => I loved the regular hyde supplement, mixed well, decent taste and effective. This on the other hand, won't give you those beta-alanine tingles nor the caffeine rush. The caffeine isn't overpowering like SuperPump Max where they don't tell you how much caffeine it has (shady). Doesn't keep you awake during the nights, no crazy noxplode pumps. It's just OK.

Packing 2/10 => I got this somewhat dinged up, the seal was intact but there was spill all over the bottle and it formed a oily sludge on the bottle due to the weather (snowing atm).

Bottomline, I love their Hyde preworkout and was looking forward to using this despite the packing and that awful taste. But this is just outright disappointing. And that taste !! I might just dump my bottle down the drain. If they charged the same price as regular hyde and worked on that awful flavor I might give this another try.

title: Useful add-on to my KneeRover Go Knee Scooter, but the mounting bracket doesn't hold it on securely
text:
When I chose the [[ASIN:B0743L5HW2 NEW KneeRover GO Knee Walker - The Most Compact & Portable Knee Scooter Crutches Alternative]] to help me get around while I heal from a broken foot, it didn't come with a basket, so I did some research to find an add-on basket. This basket is made by the same company and the description says that it fits the steering column of the KneeRover Go, however the mounting bracket doesn't hold it on securely. My fiance had to really work on making it somewhat secure, but it still loosens and slides down. It seems that the bracket was made for a thicker steering column. He's going to have to do some additional work on it to get it to stay in place.

The basket itself is useful - much better than not having one. However, if you are going to advertise it as being made to work with a specific model of your KneeRover scooters, the mounting bracket should be made to fit securely on that model. Your customers should not have to do extra work to make the hardware securely attach so the basket doesn't slide down.

title: Crisp sound directly from electronic devices
text:
A streamer that shoots sound (music, movies, computer) wirelessly into your hearing aids gives much clearer sound. For a while I bulked at the high price of the Oticon ConnectLine TV 3.0 for Oticon Opn. But I jumped for it when it went on sale (from Hearing_Aid_Accessories in the UK), and I'm glad that I did. The sound is awesome.

You pair your hearing aids once to the streamer. Pairing adds a new mode; so now I have NORMAL, CLASSROOM, and STREAMER; hold down the right HA button for three seconds to move to the next mode. Five minutes with no sound moves you from STREAMER to back NORMAL mode, presumably to save battery power; sometimes this is convenient and sometimes not -- but it takes only a few seconds to bring STREAMER mode back. The connection is very stable; if the sound starts breaking up, change the batteries -- they are almost dying anyway. You can move a pretty good distance and still keep the connection; this is good for doing exercise videos or for jumping on a trampoline during football games.

The photo shows my setup. My external speakers are on the bottom; the top has a 4-output amplifier on the left and the Oticon streamer on the right, both secured to the top by velcro strips. The wired amplifier input goes into the back of my TCL TV and gives whatever sound goes with the main screen (computer, TV, Roku streaming, whaever). Amplifier output 1 goes into the speakers underneath, 2 and 3 go into pillow speakers (these give quite good sound when your head with HAs rest on the speaker -- this is a a cheaper alternative but limits mobility), and 4 goes to the Oticon streamer (with the amplifier at max -- click the hearing aids to regulate volume). While I can adjust the sound of all four independently, I use the streamer most of the time.

If you want the sound louder, max the volume on your hearing aids and lower the audio going into the streamer. If you overload the streamer, the audio quality suffers.

For additional HA and streamer features, get the free OTICON ON app for your android or apple phone.

If you're on the fence, buy this device -- the sound is amazingly good.

title: Worth it!!
text: I had stripes going down the entire length of my car. Probably 6" wide each. A couple weeks ago I pulled the vinyl away with a heatgun, leaving a trail of residue. Since then I tried an eraser wheel, it only moved around the gunk. This stuff works great. I used a timer for 60 seconds, and scraped with an old credit card. I had to do each spot twice with the card, then once with a towel to polish up the job. Considering the car is parked outside and that adhesive residue had been soaking up dead bugs, leaves, etc. Needing 2-3 passes was worth it. The stuff does work quick, and you don't need to use much. I have 1/2 a bottle left, and I probably overapplied heavily (I'm compulsive and wanted to soak the area, which really isn't necessary). It's expensive for a reason, just buy it and don't mess with anything else. Also, the smell is mostly citrus unless you get too close, then you can tell there's some real chemicals in there. Leaves a good polish, but do it outside or in a well ventilated area. I rinsed my car with normal water afterward per manufacturer  recommendations.

title: Why the Smell? To be determined
text: There are a number of issues, that were missed when researching this product. Where was it manufactured? What is it made of? There is no information on H&B, no company address, no location... Bottom line, that smell everyone is mentioning, it's a Formaldehyde type smell, or  much like "new car" or "new carpet". Better yet that foam bed you bought.... I don't think I've ever smelled anything this intense outside a Laboratory. I suspect it is a Neoprene or polychloroprene type of material. title: Did not work for me: 5'2' pregnant with twins
text:
I wanted to like this support belt, especially after reading all the positive reviews from others who were pregnant with twins. However, it is terribly uncomfortable.
- First of all, it is difficult to adjust and as others have stated, the hooks at the bottom are spaced too far apart.
- Secondly, for me, being short and pregnant with twins at 25 weeks, there is no more room under my breasts. I cannot even wear a bra with underwire at this point, and the straps on this that go under your breasts are very very uncomfortable.
- Thirdly, it did not provide either the back support or the under belly support that I was specifically looking for with this belt. The underbelly band feels too narrow, and I felt like my large belly is just hanging out there.

After spending 43 dollars on it, I gave it several chances, and tried every which way to adjust it, but it just doesn't work. As this was my 3rd support belt and I am now on my 4th, I wanted to share my experience with the most recent one I got which is working well, just in case there are others like me who have severe back pain and feel miserable and heavy.
It is from BabiesRUs and the brand is BabiesRUs. It is this one:

[...]
It is only 30 dollars, but hey at this point I would have spent 300 if it meant I could get some relief. This belt has both large a large underbelly band and an extralarge back band to give excellent support to your back and your tummy. It is mildly complicated to put on because it has 3 parts, but it's better than this Prenatal Cradle contraption that made me feel like Houdini every time I tried to get in and out of it. It is soft and doesn't snag on clothing. And it's been great for both sitting and walking around.
Good luck!

title: An EMF Detector will not Prove These Work - But Here is My Experience
text:
Currently there is no scientific way for me to determine if these work. Diodes claim to neutralize rather than eliminate radiation. If the radiation were eliminated, your phone/computer/whatever wouldn't work.

Unfortunately that means a emf detector won't show a difference in the radiation going on.

Based on the above I cannot say for certain it works. Who knows, we may all be buying "snake oil". However, I will report what I've noticed since adding these diodes to my electronics:

Many people suffer from EMF symptoms. Brain fog, tiredness immediately after firing up an electronic, muscle pains, headaches, blurred vision and other things as well. I personally have a few of these. Mainly an inability to stay focused while working online, and brain fog.

Since adding diodes to my electronic devices, the inability to stay focused and the brain fog are mostly gone. If I am tired already, nothing helps.
I've also noticed my computer and phone doesn't get as hot while I'm using them.

I placed two diodes on my laptop and one on each phone. The small size of these are very convenient and hide nicely. Our phones all have hard plastic cases with a silicone case over that. I placed the diode on the hard case, under the soft case. Placing it directly on my phone didn't work as the hard case no longer fit.

If you need several diodes, this is probably about the best price you will find. If you find a better price let me know!

title: Less than advertised...
text:
It is not a Briar pipe(it's not even Myrtle as the "wax berry" name states, nor gourd as Calabash states, and on the subject of Calabash, is not vaguely gourd-shaped.), it's heavy, clunky, and more fragile than a high-quality Meerschaum.

The overwhelming solvent and pine smell let me know that it was not assembled properly(which also makes me hesitant on trying to use it to "break it in" for a worn look).

The stain is several shades lighter than the picture, and not a Berry shade either.

Under the porcelain bowl(which as others have noted, has a too small bowl for such a large piece of porcelain), was way too much glue to hold such a tiny band of thin cork, and the bowl was attached to the cork(most likely because they set the bowl and cork up, then pushed it into the bead of glue, hence the excessive puddles inside). As another stated, the stem, ferrule and screw tenon (in the shank) are hard, plastic and stink of the glue they used to attach the cork.

The Four pieces do not fit well, and after a lot of work, I was able to make it look decent(New Cork Band, sanding off the excessive puddles of glue, airing out the inner bowl to attempt to remove most of the solvent smells). I probably will get a new stem kit to make it look better(and do more fitting work to make it sit well).

I originally got it to be a prop for my son's Holmes costume, and had to do many repairs on it out of box to get even one good photo, as it fell apart upon posing.

Bottom line, with work, it's a decent prop pipe(to sit on a mantel in a pipe stand), but nothing more. If you are a connoisseur of fine tobacco, pass this one up, as it is not worth even trying to break in.

Just my 2cp.

title: Well, I like it so far!
text:
First of all: This is a really nice looking unit. And it *feels* like quality as well. The main device has a good weight to it, which gives the impression of quality. The back of the unit is very pretty. However, it does take fingerprints easily. But it looks so nice, I don't mind that at all. The cables feel durable, and the pads are very nice!
For my initial testing, I started with my knee which had been giving me some pain. I was having a slight stabbing pain in my knee when I would bend it. After the first use (about 10-15 minutes) I was pleasantly surprised to no longer feel that pain! A note about leg hair: I am not a particularly hairy man, but I'm hairy enough that band-aids and such have plenty of hair to rip out and cause me the standard discomfort that comes with hair being ripped out. I had 4 pads around my knee. 2 above and to either side of the knee. 2 below and to either side. The top 2 pads came off very easily (very minimal hair here). The 2 on my lower leg, however, had plenty of hair to grab on to. I moved steadily but slowly and felt some pulling, but, surprisingly , there was not a single hair stuck to the pads. As secure as they felt, this was shocking. The pads were still plenty sticky after use, and I look forward to many more sessions with the same pads.
I watched a couple YouTube videos for advice on pad placement. I'm very impressed with how it handled this slight pain. I have not had the opportunity to test on more severe pain yet, but my wrists and hands have a tendency to become incredibly painful when work gets very busy. For a change, I'm almost looking forward to the next pain flare up, so I can put this unit to work against it!
Again, so far sooo good! This is the only TENS unit I have ever tried, but I'm impressed. Having just recently turned 40, I'm sure I have more random pain to look forward to. Hopefully this thing does the trick. If I have any notable experiences with this device in the future, I will be sure to update this review!

text:
I've had some mixed experiences with this stuff. Usually it seems to do nothing, but once when using it I had an amazing weight training workout with incredible drive and bottomless strength, and a weird amount of confidence after the workout. Was it due to this? I have noticed no effects on libido either way.

Can I expect an effect after taking each dose, or must this be taken over a long period of time? Can this cause dependency and a testosterone crash after stopping? I'd like to hear more guidance from Momentous, especially on the bottle or product listing.

I chose Momentous because they make a big deal of name-dropping Andew Huberman, who I really like. He did endorse Momentous in one of his videos ("Developing a Rational Approach to Supplementation...") although that sounded to me like a paid endorsement. Though, in several other videos, he's said companies are misusing his face and name and he has no interests or relationships with supplement companies. It's not necessarily a bad thing, but I'd like the nature of the relationship to be clear when this relationship is used to influence my purchase of health products.

title: The most delicious pre-workout drink I have tasted (if that matters)
text:
Seriously, this is the best flavor I've had of any pre-workout drink. Don't buy it for that reason though, because that would be silly. It's just a nice surprise.

Most of the drinks I've tried focus on nitric oxide enhancers and stimulants, which... help a bit. This seems to be a little different, focusing on beta-alanine (muscle fatigue) and d-aspartic acid (supports testosterone). Beta-alanine I've used often and found that it gives me stronger workouts, but d-aspartic acid I've not noticed much effect from. Caffeine always works, and this only has a moderate amount, which I really prefer over huge caffeine doses.

With this formula I had decent - but mixed - results with. I've had it give me incredibly good workouts and also do very little, and it's hard to figure out what makes the difference (it may have been a supplement interaction). This formula, though, never made me feel weird or toxic which some of the other formulas do in their effort to blast you with herbs, stimulants, hormones, etc. So, this I will continue to use for some time.

title: This Stuff Really WORKS—has for decades!
text:
I’ve used BIZ for decades — it’s absolutely the best at getting out blood stains. As instructions say, scrub a bit of powdered Biz into blood stain and let soak for an hour or more in COLD water. (Hot water will only set the stain.) All stains are different: some need hot water, but it’s the opposite for blood. The sooner you pre-soak, the better, but Biz works on older stains, too. Then wash as usual with detergent if you want—though you don’t have to, because Biz has detergent in it, as well as enzymes (that’s what gets the blood out).
Others have reported a bad smell, but to me it’s not that bad. My skin is sensitive and I can get by without rubber gloves, so it’s not as harsh as some would have you believe. I guess it’s up to each person and their tolerance. I just noticed that the product description says it contains peroxide, too, however, which I hadn’t realized before, so you might want to use gloves if you don’t want your skin to absorb the chemical. If you want a product that WORKS, use Biz. That said, I’ve only ever used the powder form; didn’t even know (until I saw here) that it now comes in liquid form, too. If you look at the photo of the instructions on the box, however, it says to pre-soak with powdered form. Makes sense to me; that way it’s more concentrated, and you want to make a paste to cover the stain, scrubbing it in with a small brush like a toothbrush.

title: Great Company
text:
Great company with great customer service. My first bottle arrived broken (FBA so not due to poor packaging by BM Homeopathics). I contacted the company directly and they resent a bottle that very same day! Super impressed with that.

I think it's a little difficult to review supplements without taking them for at least a month, so my rating could change. I've been using this product for ~2 weeks. I put a few drops in my morning protein/vitamin/green supplement shake. No taste at all! I'm not sure how it would taste in water. It helps me power through my workout even though I am definitely NOT a morning person. Because I'm also taking a new vitamin supplement, I'm not sure if my energy and clear-headedness is coming from the supplement, or from my vitamins. But hey, I'm not complaining.

I'm going to increase my dosage and see what happens. Right now I'm only taking it once a day. I will start taking it in the afternoon during my post-lunch slump and see if it helps.

While I am losing the couple pounds I gained during the holidays, I'm not sure I can attribute it entirely to this product because I've been working out hard and eating clean. So, as with most supplements, this is meant to accelerate/aid progress within an already healthy lifestyle. You probably won't see results if you haven't cleaned up your diet, guys.

I have noticed a general increase in mood, which is awesome. I tend to get depressed in the winter. I did receive this product at a discount in exchange for an honest review. I've used this product daily for two weeks to provide the best review possible to possible customers. If at any point my opinion changes, I will be back to update.

My schedule tends to be all over the place, sometimes requiring me to be on call and up late at night, while at other times I'm having to get up early in the morning. This lack of regularity can reek havoc on my sleep schedule, particularly when I'm wide awake late at night knowing I have an early morning appointment.

I've tried various supplements and sleep aids to help me go to sleep. Almost all fall into one of two categories: they either a) take too long to take effect (an hour and half or longer), or b) they knock me out so heavily that I have a hangover the next morning and getting going is extremely difficult.

I decided to try this Kava product, and was very pleased with how quickly it works (usually a half hour to 45 minutes) as well as the fact that there's no hangover the next morning. For even better results, I combine one capsule with a single 5mg tablet of melatonin. I'm usually out cold in about 30 minutes and get deep, restful sleep with no lingering after effects.

title: Just about perfect
text:
I started looking for better options when I realized that with whitening trays I either whiten half the tooth or burn half the gums. I needed something that I could use frequently to control staining from daily tea and coffee drinking, not to mention the red wine I also enjoy occasionally.

Pros
1. Gel consistency seems about right - not too runny and not lumpy - easy to spread where needed
2. Gel formulation seems well balanced - it works gently on the stains without irritating surrounding areas
3. It is easy to control the amount of gel squeezed out onto the brush - makes it easy to work near the gums without burning them
4. The brush allows for adequate precision - a big plus for those with sensitive teeth
5. The pen is actually the size of a pen, which makes it convenient for daily touch-up use anywhere without the mess of using trays

Cons
1. The pen is the size of a pen and the amount of gel that fits into it is limited by its size
2. I wish the bristles were just a bit more firm for additional precision and to better cover areas in-between the teeth

Overall, this product was just about perfect and met my expectations. Needless to say I will not be going back to using trays.

title: Experience after 6 months
text:
This callus remover worked very well from the first day. It was powerful, easy to use, and very effective. After a little more than 5 months, the drive mechanism began to fail. The motor continued to run smoothly, but the connection between the motor and the roller began to slip. It made a loud, very unpleasant screeching sounds, and was basically unusable. The product came with a 1 year warranty, so I was somewhat optimistic.

When I contacted the manufacturer, Emjoi, they told me that the warranty was the responsibility of the company that sold me the product. At that point I realized that I did not buy this directly from Amazon but from a vendor called ShaveNow. A little research led me to an email address for Customer Service at ShaveNow. My inquiry was answered in a matter of hours. After providing copies of the relevant paperwork, I was given a mailing address for the return. I sent the unit in, and a couple of weeks later, they sent me a new Callus Remover. Not some refurb -- a full, brand new, retail package containing a new product.

I can't give 5 stars for a product that failed after 5 months of use, but overall, I'm still feeling good about the purchase. if I could, I would certainly give ShaveNow 5 stars for customer service.

text:
Living in a downstairs apartment + having sensitive ears = torture. After months of ear plugs and my upstairs neighbors loud stomping still distracting me from studying, I finally caved in and splurged on this sound conditioner. I was looking for a white noise machine that would block out the loud behemoth and obnoxious stomping upstairs. Neighbors, am I right -__-? The kid upstairs LOVES to skip, by the way. But enough about my neighbor troubles!!!

This machine has definitely helped. If it were a little less pricey, say around $30 or $40 , it would get more stars, but at $60 it's just okay. At first the noise was distracting, but with the machine on I was able to concentrate despite the loud click clack of hooves upstairs.

I'm a student and am permanently hibernating at home with my mountain of homework =], and this machine helps keep my attention on my studies. If you're an insomniac, this machine might also help, because even though I've had trouble sleeping, this machine makes me sleepy within ten minutes.

So the sound conditioner would have five stars if it were less pricey, but I'd say that it is *still* worth its price.

title: Great effects, but needs to be milled finer!
text:
I notice significant effects on my physiology while taking this powder - calmer nerves, tooth/gum pain has finally disappeared, good immune health, fast healing, and a generally 'sturdier' feeling.

Problem; its particles are ~.5 to ~1mm wide - like large beach sand.

Though the particles become pliable if you dissolve them in saliva for a few minutes, the experience is not pleasant, and is very gritty. I suspect a lot of this product goes through its user undigested.

I love the quality of this product, but in order to really call it 'powder', this should be put through another pass crushing - right now, this should be called "Bone Granules", not "Bone Powder".

EDIT: Upgraded this from a 3-Star to a 5-Star Review: I sent a complaint+suggestion about the particle size to TFM, and get a reply within a day. They said they will 'consider' milling it finer, but the product is highly-absorbable as-is.

title: With modification it can work
text:
I bought one of these as an impulse buy. No where on the out side of the package does it say "does not work with tinted windows". However the instruction sheet warns that it will not work with tinted windows in 3 or 4 places.

When placed in the back window of my Xterra the fan did not turn at all in direct sunlight. If I moved it to the front window where the tint is lighter it turns but very, very slowly.

I removed the 4 tiny screws that hold it together and popped the solar cell out. I glued the power cell to the outside vent portion of the device and now it works reasonably well. title: They worked as directed for me, I still felt under the influence while consuming drink
text:
The Reason for Selection:
I had read about these kinds of supplements a few years ago. Yours truly will step into the breach to give them a try.

General observations:
I sit here on an early Saturday morning after quite the Friday night. I should be hung over but I'm only dehydrated a bit.

The first pill went down the hatch at 6pm on an empty stomach. I set an alarm for 4 hours later to take the other as directed. I waited for a half hour before I started imbibing any spirits.

Your mild mannered hero reviewer then had a few cocktails before dinner and then a few glasses of wine with dinner. I noticed that the effects of the alcohol were not as intense as it usually would be for me after that much drink. I still did feel like I was under the influence so any driving was out of the question.

As the night went on, I continued to overindulge far more than I usually would for a Friday night. It was a fun night. I seemed to be able to consume more drink far too easily.

There was no way that these pills kept me from being impaired to operate a motor vehicle.

Saturday morning, no typical hangover headaches or other telltale symptoms. Just a bit dehydrated and still a little impaired.

The Good:
These supplements did exactly what they claimed to do for me.

The Bad:
Nothing Bad.

The Ugly:
Nothing Ugly.

Value for Price:
From my perspective and experience, the price of $6.50 per pill is high.

title: Try a Fitbit Flex instead
text:
I have owned a Body Bugg for years and it served me well, but I have gotten tired of wearing it on my arm, especially if I am in a short sleeved shirt, and I am not in an exercise environment. I have switched to the Fitbit Flex. It is worn on your wrist, and there is no monthly fee. I have worn both of them side by side, and I have noticed that the Body Bugg gives you a higher caloric count. One day in particular, my Body Bugg said that I burned 3200, and my Fitbit said that I burned 2900.

It's all going to depend on what you are looking for. I think the Body Bugg might be more accurate because of the way it processes information. Fitbit doesn't have a monthly fee. Body Bugg does. And after wearing the Body Bugg for all these years, I have a pretty good idea of how many calories I am burning anyway. I just need an estimation to make me feel better. I have found that the pedometer reads the same for both when I wore them at the same time.

Make sure to talk to people who have both to see which one will work for you. For me, the Fitbit looks better on my wrist, the readings are fairly accurate, and I don't have to pay a monthly fee. If you have any questions on either one, email me at Mykall514@aol.com and I'll try to answer your questions.

title: Ear Plugs that Take Volume from HIGH to LOW, While Maintaining Clarity in Hearing, Smart Design
text:
These ear plugs are great! They are made with a very very soft plastic material, which makes wearing them VERY comfortable. Even the slightest touch causes the three cone-shaped cylinders to bend to my fingers, and of course to my ears when wearing. Normal foam ear plugs expand and it feels like it's putting pressure on my ear. These do not do that.

When I think of ear plugs, I normally think about blocking ALL of the sound out. Normal foam ear plugs block most of it out and make close, loud noise sound muffled. These ear plugs are different in that they turn down the volume of the sound from HIGH to LOW. It's really great, because you can still hear conversations and music quite clear, but it's just turned down low.

There is definitely quite a bit of thought that was put into the design of these in order to create the volume decrease, along with maintaining clarity. I'm quite impressed with these.

My personal application so far has been variable. I've used these for listening to music, but primarily, I use them at night when sleeping. My neighbors have several dogs that bark at night. I'm a light sleeper and haven't been sleeping well as a result. When I use these, I can sleep really well, and yet still feel comfortable that if something was to happen in the middle of the night that was "off," I'd hear it and be able to wake up and respond to it.

This would've come in handy on my Kilimanjaro trek. I wish I'd have known about these then. Those porters are quite noisy at night. ;) That said, it's always nice to be aware of what's going on around you when backpacking and camping. To block out all the noise, is to block one of your senses. I really really like these in that it lowers the volume quite low, but doesn't completely block out my sense of hearing. It does a great job of maintaining it at lower volumes. Very impressed.

The carrying case is awesome for taking these around when traveling. I included a picture of the case next to a standard sized pen so you can get an idea of how big it is in relation to something. I highly recommend these.

I received this product at a discount in exchange for my honest review. This review is based solely on my use of the product.

title: Best cavity and broken tooth protection ever
text:
I have 2 teeth that are broken and when I discovered this "gum" a couple of years ago, I was amazed at how well it protected the teeth. In my case, one of my molars broke and part of the filling broke off as well, leaving the old cavity exposed. It got severely infected and since I can't afford a dentist I had to find another way to fill the tooth. I bought this gum and filled the hole with it. It's pliable so it's easy to cover all of the exposed areas. Then I put a temporary filling over it and voila - tooth and cavity are protected and pain free. The gum has benzocaine in it so it does help with toothache as well. It's not meant to be a permanent fix of course, but it does work for quite awhile and you don't need much to fill a cavity either. One application lasts quite awhile. Of course, you have to practice a bit to learn how to place it so that it doesn't pop out every time you bite on it but if you use the temporary filling stuff with it, you can keep one piece of it in your tooth indefinitely. I do change it out every month or so, but as long as it is covering the tooth, there is no pain and a reduced risk of infection. This is NOT a replacement for a visit to your dentist of course, but it works until you can get to one.
Another thing - it's very stiff and almost hard at first. I use a razor blade to cut off the portion I need and then I pinch it between my fingers to make it more pliable. Once saliva hits it, it does become softer, but this is what I have learned to do since using it.
I highly recommend this stuff if you need help with a toothache until you can see your dentist. Excellent product!

title: Not perfect, but you will want to buy it anyway
text:
This case is a no brainer. The old t:clip case was total crap, and I hated it with every fiber of my being. Every month or two I would sit down in my car a little sideways and the case on my belt would twist on the car seat and it would break it clean off the clip. As careful as I was, I usually had to buy a new case every few months because they constantly broke. And they cost like 25 or 30 or something ridiculous. I have probably spend $500 in those damn cases over the last 5 years, NO JOKE. Not to mention it was annoying every time you had to change cartridges, and it just didn't feel like quality. I was used to my old animas pump with the metal clip before I got the tandem and the clip was so much better. The crappy case quality has always been a dark shadow on an otherwise great device.

So this new case fixes virtually every problem I had with the old case. It's easier to change pump cartridges, it is lower profile so it doesn't stick out from your body as much when you wear on a belt, and it feels sturdy and protective without getting in the way, and the best part is the METAL CLIP. And the clip is even removable and you can attach it in either direction depending on if you prefer a vertical or horizontal pump orientation. I use mine vertical. I also love the blue color because when then the pump is inserted, it gives it a black look with just a slight hint of blue around the edges. It's kind of a nice transparent color. It's a very classy look, and I can wear the blue case in both a work and sporty environment and not have it be out of place. I was sick of having nothing but black all the time, although I'll probably get a black one of these as a backup anyway.

I only have two complaints about this case that keep it from being perfect. One is that I wish there was just a slight bit more room on the clip, because if I have a thick pair of pants or a thick belt, it can be hard to get the clip around it and slid all the way down. I never had that problem with my Animas back in the day, it seemed to fit every belt and pant waist like a glove. The clip needs a little bit more give/room to it toward the top. I hope it might stretch a little bit as I wear it in.

The other problem with the case is I feel the button overlay is unnecessary and causes it to be WAY too hard to depress the main button, especially when you're trying to do anything that requires multiple holds and presses, like an audio bolus. The cover on the button is totally unnecessary anyway because the button is already recessed from the case, so unless you somehow get hit with a thin sharp projectile straight at the button, there is no way anything is going to damage it. In the last case they left the button uncovered and I highly doubt they determined it was a safety issue that the button was uncovered after all this time. So there is really no need for the button to be covered. I'm actually thinking about taking an exacto knife and cutting out the button overlay. It makes it so much harder to press. I love the audio bolus feature but now I find myself thinking it's a hassle, because I reach to press and hold the button and you get no feedback that the button is being pressed, and usually I have to apply a crazy amount of force to the button to get it to register a press.

So not perfect, but it's still a no-brainer compared to the old POS case that I can't believe they produced for so long. With just a few tiny tweaks in the design it could be a perfect case.

title: Chocolate flavor is disgusting - get vanilla

**Please first read my extended review on this protein powder in the Mercola Vanilla Pure Power Protein user reviews for a more complete review of this brand of whey concentrate powders.**

This is a review specifically of the chocolate flavor of Mercola's Pure Power Protein. I raved about the vanilla flavor in my previous review (the banana was just ok), and said I would make an update when I tried chocolate. All of the other good qualities of this protein powder still hold true, but really there is absolutely no reason to get the chocolate flavor over the superior vanilla. This is the last time I will order chocolate, and my next order will be purely vanilla.

I'm still giving giving the chocolate flavor 2/5 stars because I still believe this is one of the best protein powders on the market, but it's clearly inferior to the vanilla flavor of the same product and you should avoid chocolate if at all possible.

text:
Straight out of the box this product has a musty, sour-like, spoiled smell. As if the product has gone bad. It smells disgusting. Truly pure essential oils do not go rancid; I do understand that they can lose their potenty over time. This bottle has lovely packaging but the company does not give dates of manufacture. Nor do they speficy where the lavender is sourced from; which was a bit of a red flag before I made the purchase. Nearly all of the REAL lavender oils I have purchased and used in the past state what country the lavender came from/is sourced from. I should have just bypassed it. My sole reason for stepping outside of the three brands I regularly use is those brands were out of stock.

So far the only pro to this product is that the packaging is quite pretty...that is not what I needed to be delivered to me. I needed lavender oil.

Per the box: “non-toxic; biodegradable; made in the USA; sustainably sourced; free from parabens, sulfates, preservatives, and synthetics; vegan + cruelty free” and “100% pure”....I have my doubts.

Truly good, worthwhile products have consistency; they are not hit or miss batch wise. Whatever I got is not a good or worthwhile, and due to my work hours I do not have time to be tying to make it to drop locations to return this stuff. Keep searching folks...buy a different brand; don’t waste your money.

title: Great scent and quality.
text:
Ever since I purchased a small humidifier – which doubles as a diffuser – I have been trying out different scents / essential oils to find out what smells I like. I found a couple which help with either a headache, sinuses, or just smell good. After receiving a gift of a mix of oils which help our daughter with allergies, we are going to be attending a “class” soon to learn more about how to mix them together for different aspects.

The oil comes in a nice glass bottle with a dropper. The dropper is a necessity to make sure you do not use too much. I quickly learned to start small with the oil I am using, and then add from there. Some of the scents (ex: Tea Tree) are very strong, and too much will overwhelm you. FYI: It does a good job for sinuses as well through the diffuser.

So far, I have only used the Tea Tree oil in my diffuser (small amounts!), and followed the advice of another reviewer, and put some in our outside trash can. Not only does it keep it smelling better, it seems to chase away the flies as well.

Overall, I really like this oil, and plan on continuing to use it. I am not an expert, but the quality of the oil seems to be very good. We plan on continuing to use it and try to learn additional uses for the oil.

title: This Makes My Heart Race!
text:
The Finger Pulse Oximeter is a wonderful little tool for sport and aviation activist. It gives your SpO2 and Pulse rate in just seconds. It’s very easy to use and small enough to fit in your purse.

It comes in a thick case for protection and the actual Oximeter is encased in a soft rubber covering. Simply slide the bottom cover off to put in the batteries and slide it back onto the Oximeter.

The Power Button in located on top of the Oximeter underneath the cover. You don’t have to remove the cover to use it. You just click where the button is and you’re ready to go!

Simply turn it on, place your finger inside, and wait for your reading. In less than 30 seconds you have your information. The numbers are big enough that I can see them without my glasses.

Another feature is it has 9 levels of brightness. This will be useful if you’re not in good lighting or for some reason in the dark. I guess if you’re running or cycling and need to check your heart rate, the backlight would be necessary.

Now I told you what the company made it for and the only thing they RECOMMEND use with it. But, I think you could use it for other things.

If you’re a smoker or have COPD, it would be a great way to get your SpO2 reading without having to go to the Dr. office. This would be an estimate but would allow you to know when you need to seek medical services.

Also, I have a friend who has a heart condition. Sometimes her heart rate seems like it is beating out of her chest. With this we can get a rate of how fast her heart is beating. If it is too high, call the heart Dr.

I could give several more examples, but they wouldn’t be for what Accurate suggested usage. But I think you get the picture on what else it MIGHT be able to do.

I have already used the Oximeter several times since I have received it. My son, the CNA, came over the other day and for fun, he took my pulse rate. We then used the Oximeter and they were the same. (Cool Eh?)

I feel better having this product in my home. I like being prepared. I am very satisfied with this Oximeter and I plan on using it quite often!

If you feel this review has helped in anyway, would you mind clicking the YES button? Thank you! It is appreciated!

title: IPX7 waterproof clipper for body grooming with ceramic blade. Rebranded Vikicon HT-871
text:
Note: Despite the name on the clipper, this is a rebranded Vikicon HT-871

Although this clipper looks a lot like other clippers sold on Amazon for general purpose cutting of the hair on your head, these are different because they're waterproof. As a result, you can use them in the shower, and they are well-suited for bodyscaping and other hair removal on your body/neck/etc.

Basic clipper technology is pretty low tech, and I have been pleasantly surprised to discover that just about all hair clippers sold these days--even by non-name-brands--do a pretty good job: They clip fine, and they feature lithium-ion batteries that last a really long time. This clipper is no exception.

Specifics of this kit:

** Rechargeable waterproof clipper with integrated light
** Upgraded ceramic blade
** Narrow gapping for reasonably close trimming
** 90 minutes on a full charge
** One multi-position length guard
** USB-A to USB-C charging cable
** Cleaning brush
** Very Cheap Travel pouch
** Stand (note that stand is just a piece of plastic--clipper will not charge in stand)
** Clipper oil
** Extra replacement cutting head

Clipper operation is trivial: There's an on/off button on the handle. And there's another button above it that turns the LED light on and off. That's it. There is no readout of charge level: No LCD screen, etc. That's too bad--most have that.

The clippers are about average in size, and feel fine in the hand.

I found that the clippers cut hair fine, and were able to cut pretty close to the skin line. If you want absolutely smooth, you'd have to run over the same skin area with a shaver. That's because they're not quite 0-gapped (see photos). But these will leave you looking clean-shaven. The functionality is close to a T-Blade clipper, but with a fully enclosed body around the rotation axis, which means both that it's waterproof, and that you don't need to worry about accidentally getting body hair twisted in the exposed rotating spindle.

The stand is a cheap piece of molded plastic, and it's not weighted, so it can topple over. It also isn't a charging stand. Honestly, I won't be using it, and I imagine most people will just throw it in a drawer.

There's no mechanical or electronic lockout mechanism, so these are not necessarily great for travel.

On the whole, they get the job done and they are waterproof. I don't find the integrated light to be of much value, but it's not a negative. These clippers are priced higher than similar clippers that are not rated to be waterproof, so you'll need to decide for yourself if you're willing to spend an extra $15+ (at the current price) for that feature. That's probably money well spent if you plan to use the clippers primarily for focusing on body hair. It's also nice that these feature an upgraded ceramic blade, unlike many traditional T-blade clippers. And this kit includes both clipper oil and an extra replacement cutting--itself worth about $10 if you ever need it.

Pros:
** Waterproof
** Includes travel pouch
** Includes three multi-position length guards
** USB-C charging port on clipper
** Includes clipper oil
** Includes extra replacement cutting head

Cons:
** No LCD readout of charge level
** Stand is not weighted and prone to tipping over by accident
** Not the cheapest option in this class
** Not 0-gapped

title: A decent rotary head shaver, comparable to entry level Norelco . IPX6 waterproof
text:
I have used Norelco 3-floating-head shavers for decades. Although I have occasionally strayed to other models featuring a traditional foil interface (Braun, Panasonic, Remington), and have even used top-end shavers from those brands, for day-to-day shaving, I always come back to the 3-floating-head design. The main reason is that the float head design works better on my neck and jaw-line regions. No matter how hard I try, the foil shavers don't quite get those areas. If I want to use only a single shaver, I’ll pick the floating head design. (Sometimes, I’ll use both types).

I own a top-of-the-line modern Norelco shaver and several older Norelcos that go from previous high-end to entry level. (Over the years, you accumulate a lot of shavers). So I have a pretty good idea of what a good rotary shaver can deliver, and of what an entry-level shaver provides.

First things first: This shaver provides a decent entry-level shave. It's comparable to an entry-level Norelco rotary shaver in terms of shave quality, ability to navigate the neck area, etc. Looking over the shaver, it's clear this is patterned after a Norelco, down to the three floating rotary blades in the head unit.

The area where this is superior to an entry-level Norelco is in the battery. The 800 mAh battery is rated for 90 minutes on a charge. While top-end Norelcos can better this, the low-end shavers still use smaller batteries and are typically rated for less than half of what this promises on a single charge.

Note that there's no integrated clipper on this shaver. It's ONLY a shaver. That's not a huge loss--the clippers integrated into shavers tend to be mediocre. But it's still a convenience that's missing.

The shaver comes with a plastic protector for the heads and can be put into lock mode for travel. The latter is nice.

In the kid:

** 3 rotary head shaver, IPX6 waterproof
** USB charging cable
** Second (replaement) head for the shaver
** Cleaning brush

My main concern with these unknown-brand shavers is how well the blades will hold up and whether you'll easily be able to replace them. My experience is that the blades don't hold up as well as with a name brand like Norelco, so you may need to replace them much sooner. It's not clear where you'd get a replacement blade unit, either. It appears that the entire unit needs to be replaced when the blades get dull.

On the plus side, they include a second (replacement) head unit. So when the blades do wear out, at least you can replace them one time without worrying about where to get a replacement. But it may turn out that when the shaving heads wear out, you may be better off just replacing the entire kit. It's not clear to me where you purchase replacement heads.

In terms of feel, the shape is comfortable in the hand, and features a nice rubberized coating that enhances stability.

Pros:
** 3 floating rotary head design works well on the neck and trouble areas
** IPX6 waterproof
** Decent battery life
** Lock mode and head cover for travel
** Includes extra replacement shaving head

Cons:
** Not clear where to get replacement heads and the cost thereof
** Does not use standard USB-C charge port

title: Decent hair dryer, feels good in the hand, three attachments. Rated for 2000W.
text:
This is a decent-quality hairdryer with typical mid-line specs. Although it is not noted anywhere on the packaging or the hairdryer itself, the listing on Amazon claims this is rated for 2000W. That's basically top-end for a decent quality home hairdryer (professional models can go up to 3600W). It claims to have three heat settings, but one of them (cool) appears to be "heat off", so in reality, you have low and high heat (some hair dryers offer more). You also have two speeds (some hair dryers offer more speeds, as well). There's a "cold shot" button that you can press to turn off the heating element (something, as mentioned, you can also do by picking the lowest temperature, so it's pretty much redundant).

Speed and temperature are controlled by rocker switches. The rocker switches are easy to operate. But I find this kind of switch is a bit too easy to toggle when you're using the hairdryer. I've owned other hair dryers that use a slider switch or firm buttons, and I find those better in terms of not accidentally changing the speed/heat.

There are no lights on the device when it's in use. Many modern hair dryers light up when in use. If you care about that, now you know. I personally don't care.

It's relatively lightweight and feels steady and non-fatiguing in the hand. The flow of air is decent.

The color/aesthetics are pleasing if that matters.

In addition to the hairdryer, you get three attachments: A finger diffuser and two concentrators. I'm a middle-aged guy, so I'm only gonna use one of the concentrators. But if you have long thick hair, you'll probably want the finger diffuser. The attachments do NOT screw onto the end of the dryer--they just push onto the end. I prefer attachments that screw on and lock in place. My experience with attachments that are just pushed on and held on by friction is that they have a tendency to come loose while you're using the dryer.

This hair dryer is only rated for US use (120V)--no surprise for a high wattage device.

Overall, it's a decent hairdryer. Other than the advertised 2000W power (vs 1850W for many others) there's not much that differentiates this one from a lot of others, so I'd say keep this one in the running if it's price competitive.

Pros:
** Rated for 2000W (high end for home hair dryers)
** Comfortable to use
** Produces a lot of hot air when in use

Cons
** Rocker (rather than slide) control switches
** Only two heat settings (warm/hot) and two airspeed settings (low/high)
** Attachments don't lock in place

title: Decent shave. Comfortable in hand. 8 heads but no increase in torque. Attachments a mixed bag.
text:
Let me note up front that I don't have a bald head, and I won't be testing this for bald head shaving. I'm testing it as a shaver for the face.

Like many of you who are reading this, I've used rotary blade cordless shavers for decades--mostly Norelco. These always feature three floating heads. I've always thought there must be something magical about three heads because that's what everyone presents :-)

I've tried shavers like this with 5, 6, even 7 heads. Now we have one with 8 heads. Crazy. What's crazier is that the basic shver isn't changing--just the cutting head attachment. That means that there isn't a more powerful motor turning all those heads, and there isn't more torque. And in turn, that means that each head has less power to cut through difficult beard/hair. It feels very much like a marketing idea (look! more heads!) and not one well thought on in terms of performance.

And I can tell you--haveing used all these different variants with differing numbers of heads--that the eight head model is certainly not any better than the 5 head model. And neither is actually as good as my entry level Norelco 3-headed model for shaving. And compared to my high end 3 head Norelco it isn't even close (but since that costs about 5 times what this one does, that's not fair). Anyway, the shaver is capable of providing an OK shave, but I'm not convinced all those extra heads are doing much to improve things.

Another annoyance is that there's very little reservoir under the cutting heads for shaved hair (see photos). This means you'll need/want to wash the head (it's water immersible) after each shave. And, more significantly, the middle head of the eight doesn't pop up. To remove it, you have to twist it off. It's a bit of a pain--and there's even less room under this head for hair than any of the others. Having used shavers like this before, I can tell you that that gets old pretty fast.

The last issue I have with the cutting heads is that there's no obvious way to replace them without simply replacing the entire shaving head assembly. So this may well become a disposable item after the cutting heads get dull. Oh, and these shaving heads don't (in my experience) last as long as those from Norelco--so you will wind up wanting to replace them.

In the kit you get:

** Eight head cordless shaver with LCD readout of charge remaining (and time used)
** Noise hair trimmer attachment
** Hair clipper attachment
** Two face cleaning attachments
** Some cheap length guides for the hair clipper attachment
** Charging cable (requires USB-A power source)

The non-shaver attachments are a mixed bag. On the plus side, the nose hair trimmer works very well. This is in contrast with the nose hair trimmers that come with clippers, which are worthless. The nose hair clipper here works as well as dedicated nose hair clippers I've used. On the minus side, the hair clipper is very poor--it operates at a low speed and struggles with any amount of hair. It's not very useful. The face cleaner attachments are probably OK, but I can't imagine using them.

On the whole, I'd consider this a decent kit useful for shaving your face and for nose hair removal. The remaining attachments are, in my opinion, not very useful. While it does a good job of shaving out of the box, my experience with these shavers is the shaving heads will get dull over time, and there's no clear replacement path.

Pros:
** 8 head shaver does a decent job on face
** Nose hair clipper works well
** Li-Ion battery: 1.5 hours charge for 90 minutes run time
** Comfortable in the hand

Cons:
** Hair trimmer doesn't work well
** Face cleaning attachments are not very significant
** Shaver doesn't provide much room for hair and will need to be cleaned after each shave
** Middle head of shaver attachment difficult to remove for cleaning
** No obvious replacement path for heads on shaver attachment--lifetime may be short
** Eighth (central) head in shaver assembly does not float like outer heads

Note that this same shaver under various names on Amazon. Shop around for price.

The shaver is branded as 4D WD-8860. The same manufacturer that makes this kit, makes shavers with differing numbers of heads. (And the attachments, including the shaver heads, for these models are interchangeable). I Shop around for price. Also consider whether you want 5, 6, 7, or 8 heads, remembering that with each head you add, you have less torque (power) per head.

title: Decent hair dryer, three attachments. Can adjust temp 50-90C in 1 degree increments
text:
This is a decent-quality hairdryer with an atypical feature: It has a LED screen and allows you to adjust the target heat temperature by 1-degree increments, between 50 and 90 degrees Celsius (122 to 194 degrees Fahrenheit). It's rated for 1875W power, which is close to the top end for a home hairdryer (professional models can go up to 3600W).

The controls on this hair dryer allow you to both adjust the target temperature, and to adjust the fan speed. You can also turn off the heating element with a short press of the power button. Note that when you do this and then return to heating mode, it forgets your previous heat temperature setting (annoying).

Also annoying is that temperature readout/setting can only be done in Celsius. There is no Farenheit mode. Weird for a US-marketed appliance.

It feels OK in the hand, although the handle could be a bit wider in my opinion. The airflow is strong.

In addition to the hairdryer, you get three attachments: A finger diffuser and two concentrators. I'm a middle-aged guy, so I'm only gonna use one of the concentrators. But if you have long thick hair, you'll probably want the finger diffuser. The attachments snap onto the end of the dryer, where they are held on by small plastic clips. This appears to be a fragile system that will almost certainly break over time. My recommendation would be to find a concentrator you are happy with and just leave that on.

The kit also includes a cheap travel bag and a cheap comb.

This hair dryer is only rated for US use (120V)--no surprise for a high wattage device.

Overall, it's a decent hairdryer. The LED display and ability to fine-tune the target temperature is interesting--although I wish they'd included the ability to use Fahrenheit. The way the attachments attach to the dryer--small plastic pins that are in the hot airflow stream--looks fragile and may not hold up.

title: 7 head shaver. IPX7 Waterproof. Decent feel in the hand. Attachments of varying value
text:
First off, I'm going to review this for face/beard shaving. I don't have a bald head (yet, anyway), so that isn't my focus.

I have used rotary floating blade shavers for decades (usually Norelco). They work best on my face, especially for the neck region. These shavers have always featured three heads.

Well, here we have seven heads. Seven heads!! I have used very similar shavers to this one with five and six-head shaver attachments. This is one more. The question is: Why do the high-quality venerable brands stick to three heads, and these shavers use so many more?

The answer isn't quality of shave. In fact, I was impressed at how well this shaver cleared the stubble on my face at the end of the day. It was comfortable, and managed to navigate the nooks and crannies of my face and neck as well as my low-end Norelco (if not better). But it's no match--not even remotely close--to my top-of-the-line Norelco (though that costs about 4x as much, so that's probably not a fair comparison). But--and this is huge--the ergonomics of the shaving heads leave something to desire. First off, there's very little reservoir under the cutting heads for shaved hair (see photos). This means you'll need/want to wash the head (it's water immersible) after each shave. Second, the middle head of the seven doesn't pop up. To remove it, you have to twist it off. It's a bit of a pain--and there's even less room under this head for hair than any of the others.

The third issue I have with the cutting heads is that there's no obvious way to replace them without simply replacing the entire shaving head assembly. Based on my experience with other shavers quite similar to this, expect the blades to get dull after a bit of use, and factor in the cost of an entire replacement head unit when they do.

In terms of seven vs six vs five heads? Well, the motors in these shavers are effectively the same. So if you have seven heads, the amount of power you provide to each head is less than it is in a five head design. That's going to affect the maximum speed and also the ability to easily tackle heavy stubble. Given that I don't sense a huge amount of improvement with seven vs five (or six) heads, I'd be inclined to veer towards fewer heads.

In general, I'd suggest that you can interchange the 7/6/5 head assemblies if you want to get a replacement.

In the kit you get:

Seven head cordless shaver with LCD readout of charge remaining and integrated activation lock
IPX7 Waterproof
Nose hair trimmer attachment
Hair clipper attachment
Two face cleaning attachments
Three length guides for the hair clipper attachment
Charging cable (requires USB-A power source; USB-C port on shaver means you can use cables you already own).
Small cleaning brush

Shave is controlled via a simple on/off button. You can lock the shaver by holding the button for 3 seconds (unlocking is accomplished by holding for 3 seconds, as well). This is convenient for travel.

The non-shaver attachments are a mixed bag. On the plus side, the nose hair trimmer works very well. This is in contrast with the nose hair trimmers that come with clippers, which are worthless. The nose hair clipper here works as well as the dedicated nose hair clippers I've used. On the minus side, the hair clipper is quite mediocre--it operates at a low speed and struggles with any amount of hair. It's about as good/useful as the clipper that's integrated into some shaver handles. Those can clip a bit of trim hair, but they are an exercise in frustration for any serious hair removal. Same here. The face cleaner attachments are probably OK, but I can't imagine using them.

On the whole, I'd consider this a decent little kit useful for shaving your face and for nose hair removal. The remaining attachments are, in my opinion, not very useful. While it does a good job of shaving out of the box, my experience is that the heads get dull somewhat quickly, and you need to buy a not-inexpensive replacement assembly. Also, cleaning the assembly is a nuisance.

Pros:
** IPX7 waterproof
** 7 head shaver does a good job on face
** Nose hair clipper works well
** Comfortable in your hand
** Li-Ion battery: 1.5 hours charge for 90 minutes run time
** Attractive styling
** Can lock the power button for travel

Cons:
** Hair trimmer has limited usefulness
** Face cleaning attachments not very significant
** Shaver head assembly doesn't provide much room for hair and will need to be cleaned after each shave
** Middle head of shaver attachment difficult to remove for cleaning
** Must replace entire shaving head unit when one/more blades get dull
** 7th (middle) head in shaver assembly does not float like outer heads

Note that there is a dizzying number of similar 5/6/7 head shavers sold on Amazon. As far as I can tell, having reviewed many of them, they are all made by a handful of companies and work pretty much equivalently well. The snap-in attachments even work across different models and brands. There are variances in features like level of waterproof and how the power switch works (and the body shape), but the function is pretty similar. So shop around for price.

title: Interesting kit includes both irrigation and toothbrush functionality. Non-standard brush head
text:
I was intrigued by this kit, which promises to be “portable” while also offering the unusual combination of both oral irrigation (Waterpik type function) and brush mode.

What you get in the kit is a rechargeable handle, two irrigator heads, a toothbrush head, and a periodontal probe, a short charging cable, and a rubber hose that connects the handle to a water supply for irrigator mode. There’s also a cheap soft-sided carry bag.

The function of the handle changes depending on whether a toothbrush head is attached or an irrigator is attached. For toothbrush mode, you have Low and High settings. For irrigation, you have a a few different settings (Normal, Soft, Pulse and DIY).

The handle is pretty chunky, but no more so than a low end Sonicare toothbrush.

What I liked:
** Both toothbrush and irrigator modes
** Toothbrush mode works fine
** Irrigator tools are small and can be packed for travel

What could be better:
** For irrigator mode, you need to run the rubber hose to a glass of water. The hose isn’t that long, and the first time I tried it, I accidentally pulled the glass to the ground.
** The handle is a bit too clunky to be attractive as a portable toothbrush
** The toothbrush head uses a non-standard connection to the handle, and it isn’t clear where you will get replacements.

I didn’t try the periodontal probe. I mentioned it to my dental hygienist, and her response was: “Put something like that, vibrating rapidly, near your teeth? You’d be crazy! But I’m sure the dentist will like the extra business when you chip a tooth or damage your gums…”

On the whole, I’d say that if having a portable version of an irrigator is what you’re looking for, this may fill the bill. But if the brush is your main interest, look elsewhere—the handle is chunkier than I’d like, and the brush heads are non-standard.

title: Decent inexpensive replacement heads, but not as good as genuine Philips heads
text:
If you're reading this, then you know that Philips uses the razor model for their toothbrushes: Sell the body for a decent price, then charge like crazy for the replacement heads.

I've been around this block a few times, and I've tried other non-Philips replacement heads before--usually to great disappointment. But I like to save money, so I keep trying.

These brush heads are far better than some I've tried. I mean, at least they are attempting to create a brush head that looks like the real thing. The brush head is about the same size as the genuine article (see photos). And it connects stably to the toothbrush itself.

In terms of feel, these feel a bit less soft than the genuine replacement brushes, but the difference isn't dramatic.

One key difference between these heads and genuine Philips is that Philips includes a metal ring at the base of the head. These don't (and most cheap heads don't--not sure if that's for price or patent reasons).

What I like a lot about these is that each comes with its own plastic brush cover, suitable for travel.

In the end, these are OK for the price. They aren't perfect replacements, but certainly good enough and far cheaper.

title: Produces strong red light at useful wavelegths
text:
The whole field of home-based red light therapy is one that is continually debated. Useful or not? There are plenty of studies to suggest both answers. Still, there are enough reasonably well carried out studies that demonstrate some red light / beneficial effect, photobiomodulation, that a lot of people have tried it--and many swear by it.

The development of high-powered, low-cost LED light sources has made it possible to develop red light therapy devices that are small and relatively inexpensive (compared to the cost of a useful device just a few years ago). This particular device promises a combination of 660 and 850nm red light in something the same size as a regular flashlight.

While I can't attest to any amazing abilities of red light therapy in general, I can affirm that this device is capable of generating a very very bright red light, providing irradiance of 200 mW/cm^2 at at start of the external beam. (See photos).

In the kit you get:

** Red light therapy flashlight, produces light at 660nm and 850nm in a 2-to-1 ratio
** 1 x 18650 Li-Ion battery , 2600 mAH
** Cheap tripod with a plastic adapter to hold the flashlight
** Small travel bag
** Charging cable
** Cheap sunglasses

To turn the light on, you just push the button at the end of the device. Push it again to turn it off. It will automatically turn itself off after 10 minutes.

I am not sure I can attest to the value of red light therapy, but if you're a red light believer, this kit offers a way to bring that technology home for a reasonable price.

title: IPX7 Waterproof combination body clipper and vaccum -- a novel solution to hair everywhere
text:
There is a huge number of options for hair trimmers on Amazon, some marketed specifically as body hair trimmers. But, honestly, any trimmer can be used as a body hair trimmer as long as it is maneuverable enough. That includes all the T-Blade trimmers and smaller head standard clippers.

That said, if you're trimming body hair, life gets a lot easier if the trimmer is waterproof (so you can use it in the shower). Because trimming somewhere else inevitably results in a ton of hair getting everywhere.

Well, until now. Someone decided to combine a medium-sized clipper with a small vacuum. The idea is that the vacuum will pull in the hair as it's cut. So the hair winds up in the device, not on your sink or floor. It's not a bad idea.

In practice? I found that this clipper DEFINITELY pulled in most of the hair when I used it. But it's not the world's most powerful vacuum, and some still wound up on the sink (or floor). So, in the end, this will help keep things cleaner, but you'll still want to do some cleanup.

In terms of functionality, you have one speed (on/off) and two speeds for the fan (low and high). Low seemed worthless--you'll definitely want to run it on high. As I mentioned, this is a lower power fan and you'll want all the power you can get.

In the package you get:

** Clipper/vacuum device with superior quality ceramic cutting blade
** Three clipper length guides (two of which are double-sided)
** A cleaning brush
** A USB charging cable (requires USB-A connection; connection on clipper is USB-C so you can use any USB-C charging cable you have)
** Cheap body sponge
** Cheap plastic hair cutting bib

Honestly, I am of two minds about this. While the vacuum is nice, it doesn't catch all the hair. As a result, I would still be more inclined to step into the shower and run the clipper (where the stray hair can be washed down the drain). But if you are the kind of person who runs the clipper outside of the shower, even though the vacuum does not catch all the hair, it catches enough to reduce the clipped hair mess. So this might be the extra cost over a standard clipper.

title: Basic IPL hair remover works well. FIDAC Model T2. A bit pricy for the basic functionality
text:
The latest craze in hair removal is IPL: Intense Pulsed Light. Owing to improved light technology, handheld devices that can provide the requisite intensity light to perform IPL at home and at an affordable price are now available.

I've tried a number of these IPL (Intense Pulsed Light) devices for hair removal. Compared to the others I've tried, this is one of the more expensive ones and doesn't seem to offer much in the way of differentiating functionality. As is typical, you get a IPL hair removal tool rated to around a million flashes. This one has a LCD counter of the number of flashes and the indicator of the power setting (1-5).

Operation is pretty trivial: You plug in the power supply, (the hair removal tool is NOT battery operated; you must have it plugged in), you choose the power level (five settings, chosen by rapidly pushing the bottom of the power button)) and then you aim it at a body area with hair you'd like to remove. It is recommended that your body is freshly cleaned and that the hair be shaved before starting. You can choose either on-demand flashing (via the button in the middle of the body) or else automatic flashing when skin contact is detected. Switching between the modes is accomplished by a long press of the flash activation button. The mode is indicated by a symbol in the middle of the screen.

The light is extremely powerful and could damage your eyes with continued direct exposure. Therefore, you should never look directly into the light and a cheap pair of folding protective eyeglasses are included in the box.

The light is triggered by a touch-sensitive metal area in the front of the device. Using very slow-motion photography, I was able to capture a snapshot of the light (see photos). But the light duration is extremely short.

You run the tool over the area where you want to remove hair, and make sure you exposure all the hair follicles in that region. You will not see any immediate results. The light signals your hair to stop growing, but it requires multiple treatments over several weeks before you will be expected to see results. Eventually, you should find a substantial reduction in the hair in the treated areas.

In the box, you get:

** IPL tool
** Power adapter
** Cheap pair sunglasses
** Inexpensive disposible shaver
** Instructions

This device only offers one mode: Hair removal. Other IPL devices offer other modes (skin rejuvenation and acne treatment). Whether that's a loss depends on whether you believe those other modes really work anyhow. The jury is out. Another thing you don't get with this tool is any attachments that can make it easier to address certain body areas. Some IPL removal tools include these. The actual value of such tools is subject to debate and the fundamental functionality (which is a flash of high-intensity light) does not change.

Overall, the device does what it promises to do. It's worth noting, though, that for a basic functionality IPL device, this one is priced higher than many. It's probably worth shopping around and comparing.

Pros:

** Hair removal IPL, simple to use
** LCD readout of number of flashes left and power level. Also indicates the mode (automatic, manual)
** Rated for 999,999 pulses (longer than you'd ever use it)

Cons:

** Somewhat expensive relative to other devices that only do hair removal IPL
** I prefer gun-shaped IPL tools to those, like this one, which are oblong
