title: Suttik T-Blade Clipper Model JM-700AL. Zero-gapped, works well. Kit has all the basics.
text:
There is a boatload of so-called T-Blade clippers available on Amazon. The secret is that a very large fraction of these is made by a handful of manufacturers. Some carry different names in the listing, but they are mostly just a small number of different models with moderate cosmetic differences.

The good news is that they are mostly quite decent. They feature 0-gapped heads (or at least close to it), 600 mAh batteries, a cutting head that can be rinsed in water to clean (although you should not submerge the body of the clipper), and a small number of cheap length guides you can snap on.

The only significant differences among most of these different listings are:

1) The charge level readout. The best ones provide an LCD display of the percentage charge left. The cheap ones do not.
2) Some provide a collar that can protect the shaft going to the T-blade. This can either be a plastic collar that snaps on, or, in some cases, an extension of the metal body around that area (hiding the shaft)
3) A ceramic cutting blade. This is unusual, but a few offer a premium ceramic cutting blade
4) The pattern/design of the body

That's pretty much it. Any descriptions or reviews that try to suggest other differences are usually mistaken.

This particular set of clippers is made by Suttik (one of the common brands), and comes in a Suttik-labeled retail box. The model is JM-700AL.

Specifics of this kit:

** Rechargeable cordless T-Blade clippers
** Zero gapped cutting head (cuts close)
** Three lengths of optional length guards
** Plastic collar ring to protect the rotating shaft
** Charging cable
** Cleaning brush
** Clipper oil
** LCD readout on clipper provides charge status, but not oil reminder (not a big loss)
** Metal handle
** Ornate pattern on the handle
** IPX4 water resistance (can be cleaned under the tap, but do not submerge)
** 1500 mAh rechargeable battery (per listing)
** Retail box suitable for gifting

Common items NOT included in this kit:
None. Pretty much a standard "complete" T-blade kit.

Clipper operation is trivial: There's an on/off on the bottom near the top of the handle. That's it. The clippers work well. The clipper feels comfortable in the hand.

Personally, I find the design of the handle a bit juvenile--it's not my taste. But, to me, that's a trivial issue. A 1500 mAh battery in a T-blade clipper is on the large side.

As mentioned, there are a number of sellers selling this same Suttik JM-700AL (or similar) clipper under various listing brand names. This is a good option for this type of clipper but shop around for the best price, as they can fluctuate pretty drastically depending on the listing. A typical price for this clipper would be in the range of thirty dollars.

title: Drooper portable woman's hair remover -- you'll be arguing over who gets it
text:
A battery-powered women's hair touchup device. "Who needs it?" was what I heard when I ordered this. After getting it and seeing how it works, the same people were arguing over who got it.

At the time I'm writing this review, the listing provides very little detail. So I'll provide some here and in the pictures. This is a Dooper brand women's portable shaver. It consists of an AA-battery-operated shaver with four interchangeable attachments (foil shaver, rotary shaver, mini clipper and rotary nose hair remover). The attachments easily twist off the end of the Dooper.

The Dooper runs on one standard AA-battery, which is NOT included. (Boo). Once you have installed the battery, you simply twist the bottom of the Dooper clockwise (relative to the top) and the attachment spins. The Dooper is IPX6 rated, so you can use it in the shower, as it's rated to be waterproof.

The design is cute, and the women in my life both wanted this when they saw it--especially when they realized what it could do.

In terms of the quality of the attachment, the rotary head and the nose hair trimmer work pretty well. The foil trimmer is not great, nor is the bikimi trimmer. There are much better-dedicated devices for those purposes.

To be honest, I think the most attractive use case of this would be for a woman to keep in her purse for those last-minute face touchups while you're out that you missed in the bad light at home. The women whom I showed this to both had that same idea, something they revealed as they argued who would get it! :-)

A nice little gizmo.

Included in kit:

Battery operated Dooper handle (AA battery, not included)
Four interchangeable attachments: Bikini trimmer, rotary shaver, foil shaver, nose/ear hair trimmer
Two cheap cleaning brushes
Protective cap for bikini trimmer
Protective cap for nose hair remover
Cheap plastic bag to hold Dooper

Shop around, as this device is available under multiple listings on Amazon. Be sure to compare prices.

title: Decent tasting low calorie (15 cals/glass) electrolyte+caffeine drink; contains sucralose
text:
I drink a lot of fluids during the workday, and "just water" gets really boring, really fast. I could go with all coffee, but that also gets old after a while. So I figured I'd give these Quench "Island Ice Hydrating Eletrolyte Rip Sticks" a chance.

I filled a glass with 8oz of cold water (and some ice) and stirred in one packet. The mix creates a cloudy yellow/white drink. It tastes fine--reasonably dissolved, not grainy.

The taste is good--strong and sweet. The flavor comes from the prickly pair, but if you've nevr had one of those, here it's pretty similar to pineapple. There's caffeine in these, and I did notice a little bit of a caffeine jolt in the mid-afternoon, but not like a stiff cup of coffee.

Now, at 15 calories per glass, I am not sure what they're talking about with respect to "replenish drained energy". But, honestly, at this stage in my life, I don't need caloric energy replenishment as much as I need a good-tasting drink that is low cal and gives me just a bit of a mid-afternoon bump. These seem to do the trick.

Note that in the fine print, the note that these contain sucralose, along with fructose, guar gum, and silicon dioxide. I'm OK with all that, and it does taste good to me. But if you're averse to sucralose, be aware.

I got these in 09/21, and the best-before date on the packets is 01/22.

title: Entry level clipper and kit
text:
I have been reviewing a LOT of men's hair/beard clippers lately. At this point, I have seen all types, from starter kits to higher end kits with all sorts of extras thrown in.

It turns out that most of the clippers are apparently made by only a handful of factories, with various nameplates attached, different boxes, and variations in what is included in the kit. The geneal quality of these clippers is suprisingly good these days.

This particular clipper package is pretty spare and I'd call it entry level. You get decent quality clippers in a metal+plastic body, adjustable clipper gap length, and a LCD readout that gives percentage of battery charge available and an oiling reminder (but no clipper oil is included in the package)

A summary of the parts in this kit:

** Clipper with metal/plastic case (lower part metal, upper part feels like plastic), adjustable headgap, LCD charge and oil-reminder readout
** Clipper powered by a 1500 mAh battery, which is smaller than the typical battery for this type of clipper (2000-2500 mAh)
** 4 plastic length guides, NOT color coded
** A USB-A to Clipper charging cable (charger not included)
** A small cleaning brush
** A plastic carry bag
** Instructions
** Retail box

Despite the brand name under which this is listed, the actual clipper is branded as Suttik, model JM-104. A lot of different clippers are available under the Suttik name on Amazon.

The contents of this kit are somewhat below average for this segment. The main attraction here is the clipper, and it's solid--although the construction of the upper part (the part with the LCD display) of the clipper feels like plastic, as does the gap length adjustment lever. I wonder about the long-term durability of the gap-length adjustment.

Given that this clipper and kit fall at the lower end of things (smaller battery, small set of clipper guides, no clipper oil), I'd hope to find this kit for a bit of a discount relative to other options. That said, the clipper itself is solid, and outside of the lack of clipper oil, this is probably most of what the average person will need.

Specifics of this kit:

** Rechargable cordless T-Blade clippers
** LCD readout / charge level indicator
** Plastic collar ring to protect rotating shaft
** Pretty orange-colored metal handle--good ergonomics
** Three detachable length guides, all black
** Charging cable
** Cleaning brush
** Clipper oil
** Simple, attractive design
** Retail box suitable for gifting

Clipper operation is trivial: There's an on/off on the bottom of the handle. That's it. The clippers work well. The clipper feels comfortable in the hand. Charging of the clippers is via a standard USB-C port on the bottom of the clippers. I like that a lot better than the non-standard power connectors on some clippers.

I have reviewed other Kezu & Lar T-blade clippers in the T-98 line (also with an orange handle, but without the LCD readout), and those appeared to be truly 0-gapped. So I think there's some variation depending on the particular modely you choose.

The clippers feel very good in the hand, with the all-metal handle providing good stabilizing heft. The shape and thickness are both very nice.

On the whole, I like these clippers a lot. In terms of ergonomics and having what I want (LCD readout of battery level), these are good. I wish the heads truly 0-gapped, rather than close, but that's pretty common and they'll still do a good job of trimming. Add to that the very unusual and very pretty burnt orange color. These would make a nice gift.

title: Attractive 0-gapped T-Blade clipper with large battery; wish it had a charge level indicator
text:
There is a boatload of so-called T-Blade clippers available on Amazon. The secret is that a very large fraction of these is made by a handful of manufacturers. Some carry different names in the listing, but they are mostly just a small number of different models with moderate cosmetic differences.

The good news is that they are mostly quite decent. They feature 0-gapped (or close) heads, a Li-Ion battery, a cutting head that can be rinsed in water to clean (although you should not submerge the body of the clipper), and a small number of cheap length guides you can snap on.

The only significant differences among most of these different listings are:

1) The charge level readout. The best ones provide an LCD display of the percentage charge left. The cheap ones do not.
2) Some provide a collar that can protect the shaft going to the T-blade. This can either be a plastic collar that snaps on, or, in some cases, an extension of the metal body around that area (hiding the shaft)
3) A ceramic cutting blade. This is unusual, but a few offer a premium ceramic cutting blade
4) The pattern/design of the body

That's pretty much it. Any descriptions or reviews that try to suggest other differences are usually mistaken.

This particular set of clippers is branded as Kezu & Lar T-98

Specifics of this kit:

** Rechargeable Cordless T-Blade clippers
** NO LCD readout/charge level indicator
** Plastic collar ring to protect the rotating shaft
** Beautiful orange-colored metal handle--good ergonomics
** Three detachable length guides, all black
** Charging cable
** Cleaning brush
** Clipper oil
** Simple, attractive design
** 1800 mAh rechargeable battery (huge for this segment)
** Retail box suitable for gifting

Clipper operation is trivial: There's an on/off on the bottom of the handle. That's it. The clippers work well. The clipper feels comfortable in the hand. Charging of the clippers is via a standard USB-C port on the bottom of the clippers. I like that a lot better than the non-standard power connectors on some clippers.

The heads are 0-gapped. This makes it possible to trim right down to skin level, which is valuable for clippers of this type.

My main complaint here is the lack of a charge level indicator. The battery is more than ample for days of use at home, but it would still be nice to have an indication that the clippers are getting low on charge.

The clippers feel very good in the hand, with the all-metal handle providing good stabilizing heft. The shape and thickness are both very nice.

The 1800 mAh battery (per the manufacturer) is far larger than many of the batteries found in T-blade clippers, which is also a plus.

On the whole, I like these clippers a lot. Only wish there was an LCD readout of charge level. But in terms of ergonomics, battery size, and the 0-gapped heads, these are winners. Add to that the very unusual and very pretty burnt orange color. These would make a nice gift.

title: A simple clipper kit with a premium clipper: waterproof and with premium ceramic blade
text:
Don't overlook this clipper kit. Although it does not have as many pieces as some kits, it has the pieces you probably need and--significantly--you get a waterproof clipper with a premium ceramic blade. It even incorporates an adjustable blade gap. Waterproof, ceramic blade, and adjustable gap are all features often not found on clippers, even those selling for considerably more.

This kit delivers, especially at the price.

How do they do it? How can they be selling a better quality clipper for less money than many other clipper kits? They don't load the kit down with accessories that look nice but that you'll probably never use. So, instead of a dozen length guides, you get four (2 x 2 dual size guides). You don't get interchangable heads that, honestly, rarely work well anyway. (Nose hair, foil shaver, etc--the ones you find in the more elaborate kits are mostly junk). You don't get a plastic stand/tray that will take up counterspace and offers no added value. You don't get multiple speeds on the clipper that you don't need and will never use.

Nope, what you get is the clipper, a USB charger cable, a cheap brush, some clipper oil, a comb and two dual-sided length guides. That's it. But that's probably all you need.

The clipper also comes in a retail box. So if this is for someone else, it's giftable.

The clipper works very well. An excellent deal at the current price.

Let me note that this is a grooming clipper with a somewhat more narrow head. It's perfect for trimming a beard/sideburns/neck hair/body hair. If, however, you plan to actually cut your head of hair, you probably want to look to clippers with wider heads.

I'll also add that the same kit is currently available on Amazon under a few brand names. You may want to shop around to ensure best price.

text:

The clippers and the attachments work equally well on all the dogs, and the clippers are very powerful and work nicely in getting all the fur trimmed even in areas that are very coarse or need extra attention. I am pleased with this, most especially. I had previously been using my own hair clippers on the dogs to cut their fur, and this wasn’t working out nearly as well, probably because my hair clippers didn’t have the power needed to trim dog fur correctly.

My only complaint would be the noise. While these are advertised as being quiet, they aren’t really any more quiet than regular hair clippers. My oldest pomeranian still was pretty scared of the noise, and while I will admit that she is a bit of a nervous dog anyway, I had hoped that these really would be quieter than regular clippers. They just aren’t though. I compared them to my regular hair clippers and my own hair clippers are the quieter ones. I felt bad for using these on my oldest pomeranian, but she is the dog with the thickest fur, and she really needs to be groomed with these dog fur clippers. These DID give her a beautiful groom though, as they did for all the dogs, so I’m still giving them five stars!

These clippers are excellent at providing a really perfect cut, and the attachments make it easy to do at home grooming for your dogs. Plus, I love that they are chargeable to use cordless while grooming. Highly recommend!
