title: Couldn't find certified FDA approvals, but it appeared to work on my scar
text:
ITEM: Elamei brand sold by Pephuca - Silicone Scar Sheets (1.6” x 120”)
PRICE: $17.09 per roll – (1.6” x 120” rolls at 8.9 cents/sq. inch)

Ironically, I had just visited my dermatologist to have stitches removed from what was an outpatient procedure a few weeks prior. I had a removal of a small item near the front of my neck and off to the side a bit. I asked the attending nurse what she knew about ‘silicone tape.’ She shared that their office recommends the use of the tape, but didn’t mention any brands. I understood how silicone tape worked on scars, and felt it worth trying on mine. I should have asked about FDA approved brands vs online, but didn't.

The first day I went to apply the tape, I found the roll-size was perfect. Its 1.6” width was just the right length for my scare. So I could cut the tape at 1” off the roll; 1.6” x 1.0” worked great in covering the scar and having sufficient overage to secure to my skin. The adhesive is strong enough to keep the cut-to-size bandaid type product on all day. And on my fair complexion, I can barely see the product on my neck. I was very impressed.

I’d recommend only wearing the tape for a few hours. I wore the silicone tape for about seven hours. And after removal I noted the area was irritated and itchy. I'd remembered the instructions indicated a shorter first-time use of 4-6 hrs. Maybe that was why an introductory short wear time would be wise. The irritation cleared that evening, and the following days I wore silicone tape from morning until early evening. And I have to admit that the scar was initially low-level. But after a week of applications, (new bandaid each day), I noticed a very flattened scar. I'll attribute some of that to the tape.

My only caution about this or any other tape is that I couldn’t find ‘direct reference’ to approval by the FDA anywhere on the tape or box. It was certainly inferred on the vendor’s page, but never directly shared certifiable endorsements or approvals. After having used this product, and not having any allergic reactions, I felt it was safe to continue use.

It is compact and fairly lightweight -- great for travel. The synthetic material is soft and the velcro closure does not scratch. If you have a small head or prefer a very tight mask, this could be an issue because the elastic strap is not adjustable and only has one velcro attachment point.

The inside of the mask has 2" diameter eye cups that relieve pressure on the eyelids and allow eyelash movement. It is quite comfortable. There is also a piece of fabric over the nose area that is designed to block light. Unfortunately, there is still some light leakage from the bottom of the mask and around the nose area.

Overall, this Cylomert sleep mask is above average and I do recommend it. However, it will not replace my go-to "Sweet Dreams Contoured Sleep Mask" from Dream Essentials anytime soon.

title: Good suplemental gummy vitamin - not intended as a complete mulitvitamin

The product is as promised...but I did not perform a chemical analysis to confirm the vitamin contents. The main problem with this product is that it is not a complete dietary supplement; it only contains vitamin B and C. Therefore, one would also need to take a general multivitamin to get the recommended DV of other micronutrients (based on a 2,000 calorie diet). The TULA vitamin also contains 3mg of biotin -- which is 10,000% the recommended amount of vitamin B7. This is excessive and will not be absorbed by the body.

Hard to tell about effectiveness of the nutraceutical ingredients (mostly placebo effect), but I would recommend for a nice tasting gummy that provides additional vitamins C and B to one's diet.

text:

I won’t say glitch is the type of energy supplement drink that is going to wire you up, make you want to pump iron, or do things you never normally want to do ;-). If that’s the case, this might not be a bad one to try, but definitely start with half a scoop and assess your tolerance and reaction to it.

Obviously given this is geared towards gamers, which I am not one of, I see why it has that effect and for that I think it’s a great product. Given I have actually used it as a pre-workout supplement and recently used it before a very long bike ride, i’m overall impressed.

The product mixes very easily and consistently. I’m not particularly crazy about the flavor but I really have come to not judge energy drinks by flavor so long as they mix well and are tolerable. title: For those of you looking for nasal relief...
text: Disclaimer: Maty's in no way states or implies that this vapor rub is meant to be applied inside the nostrils, and this might not work for everyone.  But for the past couple of years, I've had a debilitating sensitive nerve in one spot way up inside my left nostril.  When the air is cold and dry, this area of my nose becomes scabby and unbearably ticklish, causing me to sneeze uncontrollably, my eyes to water, and my nose to run non-stop.  It got to the point that, if I cooked dinner on the stove, the onions, garlic and/or spices I used would inevitably irritate that one nostril, leading me to feel sick for days after.  While doing research about this issue online, one commenter made mention that he found Vicks Vapor Rub to work wonders at alleviating the irritation.  I don't like using products with petroleum jelly in them, especially in a place like inside the nose, so I started searching for a more natural alternative.  I've been applying Maty's with a q-tip inside my nostrils off-and-on for a few weeks now whenever the flair up occurs, and it has been a life saver!  I don't know if it's the mint having a numbing effect, if it's the oils moisturizing my nose, or a mix of both, but I could kiss that commenter for recommending Vicks, and I could high-five Maty for creating a natural version. If you have dryness or other nasal problems brought on by allergies, cold dry weather, or a cold, you might give this a try.  It's very soothing, there's no burn or other negative reactions to the product, and the wintergreen scent is relaxing.  If you're nervous about applying it inside the nose, I suggest rubbing it directly under the nose.  My dad used to put Vicks under my nose when I had coughing attacks caused by colds, and as strong as the mint in Maty's is, I'm sure it'd be just as effective.

title: Decent flavor; fiber plus protein and vitamins and minerals; high in sodium
text:
I have both the vanilla and chocolate versions of this product. While I know that these powders are sold by weight, not volume, I was a bit surprised to see that the vanilla version took up a fair bit less volume. I’m not sure if the vanilla powder is heavier or if it was somehow more compressed.

So this product is meant to be a meal replacement and not purely a protein powder, so it has a lot more going on than what a typical protein powder might have. In addition to protein, it has a lot of vitamins and minerals and a lot of fiber. Flavor-wise, it’s OK. It’s got some chocolate flavor, and the sweetness isn’t off-putting. I’ve tried protein powders that were strong with the stevia, which is a sweetener that I don’t really like. This contains some of that too, but it also has cane sugar. I’ve certainly tried far less palatable protein/meal replacement powders. I’d probably rank this high up the list, though that isn’t necessarily saying a lot if you’re coming from never having tried these sorts of things to consuming a lot of them and just getting used to the not-very-good flavors. This does have some grittiness, though I make my drinks the night before, which allows for the powder to hydrate well. Also, given that this has more in it than protein powder, the grittiness should be expected. For example, this has a variety of ground of seeds, which is why it has so much fiber.

In comparison to the vanilla flavor, this has slightly less calories, but it has slightly more sodium, more fiber, and more potassium, so there is some difference between these beyond simply the flavors.

I’m not really keen on the fact that this is $37, is in a huge tub, but only has 15 servings. Granted, these sorts of products are all kind of pricey, so this isn’t overly so. The biggest negative for me is the amount of sodium this contains. There are 480mg of sodium per serving. I’d be a lot happier with this if it had maybe half that.

title: I have no idea if this does anything; if you're new to probiotics, may want to work your way up
text:
Does this supplement work? I have no idea. Are the ingredients of good quality? No idea. That’s sort of the problem with supplements. They all make these claims, but it’s largely impossible to tell if they actually do anything beyond give you expensive pee. Obviously, I hope this works and provides me with some sort of useful benefit, but it may be the case that the benefits, if any, are subtle or that they take weeks or even months of use to start making a difference. All that I can really say about this is that I have not experienced any negative effects from taking this. Also, this bottle says to refrigerate after opening, so keep that in mind.

This bottle says 50 billion CFU per dose (two pills) and 14 probiotic strains. If you’ve never taken probiotics before, you might consider starting with a probiotic with a smaller dose to see how that affects you before jumping in with this.

Further, regarding supplements in general, you should always pay attention to the dosage. First of all, you can’t be certain, unless you’ve come across 3rd party testing, that the dosage on the bottle is what you’re actually getting. It’s possible that the dosage could be higher or lower. This goes for all supplements. So, be careful and pay attention to any changes in how you’re feeling. Further, before you take any supplement, do some research. Just because something is being sold with a specific dosage doesn’t mean that dosage is safe, or at least safe for everyone. There are some things that have no upper limit when it comes to safety, but there are a great many things that do have tested upper limits, and there are many things that can interact with medication you may be taking or medical conditions you may have.

title: Sleek, sexy little headset doesn't sacrifice form or function
text:
The search for the perfect Bluetooth headset is never-ending, it seems. In the last 3 years, I've gone through more brands and models than I care to think about. Now I've tried the Plantronics Discovery 925, and tell you with no hesitation that it is in the top two of those I have used.

The Plantronics Discovery 925 is more an earpiece than a headset, with an earbud that fits inside the ear with surprising comfort, rather than an earloop that hangs over the ear. This means that it is much more comfortable to wear with eyeglasses and/or sunglasses. Indeed it is so comfortable that I sometimes forget I am wearing it.

Pairing the device is a snap, and while my old Jabra headset frequently lost its pairing (weekly at least), the Plantronics Discovery 925 has not yet.

The sound quality is tremendous. Audio is crystal clear from both my side and on the caller's side, if my friends and family are to be believed. LOL

Plantronics touts this headset as having great noise reduction technology, and I will say that it is better in the noise reduction arena than all but one of the headsets I've tried in the past. The only headset I have personally tried that surpasses the Plantronics Discovery 925 in noise reduction is the Jawbone headset.

What I really love about the Discovery 925 is the charging options. This headset comes with both an AC charger cable and a USB charger cable. Not only that, it comes with a compact charging case. You can charge the headset either in the case or directly, using the same cables for each. The beauty of the case is that it charges alongside the headset when you have it plugged in to electrical power. Then when your headset's battery dies, you simply put the headset in the case to recharge on the go - WITHOUT connecting either the case or the headset to electrical current. I've purposely let the headset's charge completely drain and charged it with the case, and found it worked admirably. And to top it all off, the Plantronics Discovery 925 charges fully in just a couple of hours, whether via electrical current or the portable charge case.

Now here is where I prove what a woman I can be. The last quality I want to point out is purely cosmetic - its appearance. This is by far the most attractive headset I've ever seen. It's design almost looks like a cufflink or tie clip. It is sleek, innocuous, and comes in three different colors: black, gold, and pink. Personally, I like the more unobtrusive black model myself, but for those who want a little bit livelier hue, the other options work too. Yeah, I know, the appearance is a pretty frivolous virtue, but as often as we wear these things nowadays, it is nice to find a Bluetooth headset that doesn't have to trade form for function.

For the best in noise reduction, Jawbone's Bluetooth headset is the overall winner, but Plantronics Discovery 925 runs a very close second in this category. In all other categories, I would choose Plantronics as the number one headset.

title: Kind of works
text: The Freefa hair eraser is an interesting device that kind of works as intended. The material surface feels like a slightly textured plastic, but is so finely textured that it feels almost smooth rather than sand paper like. I had my doubts on its efficacy at first, but it surprisingly did remove hair after some scrubbing. The eraser works, but it's a bit difficult to get a great result. First, the area is not completely clear of hair. It miraculously takes off hair down to the root but leaves like 2 or 3 half length hairs every square inch regardless of how much I scrub the area. I scrub it until my skin is slightly red (it doesn't really damage the skin since the texture is very fine) but pesky hair still remains like cactus in a barren desert. I thought it was because the skin dust clogged the texture (as it takes off A LOT of surface skin dust) so I washed and wiped it before trying again. That did help but after getting through an area approximately the size of the eraser it stops taking off hair again. That would be great if it works when wet, but it doesn't work so great even with semi-wet skin. I found that very dry skin works the best, and to work the eraser in a circular manner like you're polishing. It takes quite a lot of passes to make an area clean and smooth. Hair starts growing back after about a day or two. If you like taking your time with skin care, then this is the thing for you.

title: Just ok
text:
I'd like to start with I am in no way an expert like many homeopathic folks I know & learn from. This is just my opinion & what I've learned on my journey of natural remedies.
The case & little containers inside are fantastic. I also like that they include a tube of calendula cream. I've actually utilized the glass capsules for my dad's emergency heart meds & the big emergency medical remedies that should be in every kit, I've just replaced them with my own.
My thoughts-This kit is just ok.
I didn't find the book very helpful. So if you're a beginner, please do your own research & have homeopathic friends you trust to guide you.
The remedies that I use at home dissolve very quickly when placed under the tongue, as they're supposed to do. These remedies are very hard, like tiny pebbles & do not dissolve for quite a few minutes. This just tells me that in an emergency situation, the remedy is not hitting the system quickly enough. Also, if you're trying to dose a young child or a pet, I can't see how you'll keep their mouths shut long enough for these to dissolve without stressing out the recipients.
So, if the kit is just for you & you know what to do with what's included, this is a great compact kit to take with you in the car, hiking or anywhere you don't want to bring along anything huge.
I hope this helps anyone just starting out.

title: Good - make sure surface is clean and pad is well lined up
text:
Bought these to put on the heels of my Time Slipper Shoes that had worn down in less than a year. I wanted to be able to continue using the shoes, but take measures to prevent further wear through the soles.

So far, these have done pretty well. I cleaned the soles with alcohol wipes, getting into the grooves, to make sure I had a clean surface for good adhesion. I made sure to cut the pads to match the sole. Once I lined everything up, I pressed on the pad from one side to the next to make sure I had solid adhesion without bubbles. Then I took the shoe and stood on it for a minute or two to further press on the pad. Repeated process for the other shoe. Then I left then alone for 24 hours to let the glue “cure”.

I’ve been using the shoes off and on like normal the past couple of weeks. One pad has slid a bit, but it was also the pad that I didn’t line up as well when placing, so I’ll just pull that one off and do it again. I’m able to walk like normal with them and I’m confident with their anti-slip properties.

title: May work well for some but not others, depending on your foot issues
text:
I don't have plantar fasciitis. I have high arches, and often use orthotic shoe inserts to get adequate footbed support. I purchased this product because I sometimes get arch pain when not wearing shoes (eg: martial arts, Taiko drumming), and I have suspected this is due to stress from insufficient foot support.

This product has a compression pad located under the medial (inside) part of the arch which the packaging states is to "reduce excessive pronation" (walking with more pressure on the inner edge of the feet). Pronation is also not an issue of mine, as I am instead prone to supination (pressure on the outer edges). Wearing the product, I find I prefer to adjust it so that the compression pad is a bit more toward the center and under the highest portion of my arch, to achieve something more resembling (albeit vaguely) the behavior of an orthotic shoe insert. It feels a bit odd, but seems to provide some reasonable support; however I would prefer if the pad were a bit wider with tapered sides, like the raised area on a shoe insert. I realize, though, that this pad was not intended to serve as an orthotic arch support, but merely as a "wedge" on the inner side of the foot to inhibit pronation.

I like the adjustable feature, but the other issue I have noticed is discomfort (scratching) and irritation from the plastic backing of the velcro strap when wearing this product barefoot. I have to wear it over a sock.

It would be nice if this product were purchasable individually, not just in pairs, as I don't necessarily need to wear both. At $18.99 a pair, it's a bit pricey, though it seems durable.

For barefoot wear, as well as least bulky inside shoes, I find that the [[ASIN:B0002DUSV6 Pedifix Arch Bandage #P60]] (do a search for best price on those; $8.99 for one is a bit steep) is more comfortable, though it is not adjustable. Your mileage may vary. :)

Replace the small plastic roller with the big wood one (like 2" diameter ) and now the pedal is perfect. The company should include plastic rollers in different sizes for different cars.

This is our first digital scale. Prices have really come down in the last few years. We were a little apprehensive about the glass platform. title: These scissors will give you split ends.
text: These are very disappointing. I have hair down to my elbows and trim my own hair at home regularly to save time and money. I cut my hair with these and on close inspection noticed that my ends did NOT have a clean cut. The ends looked less than fresh, with a whitish speck on the end of each hair (like a split end waiting to split). The tension knob didn't help either. I'd say I had about 25% split ends I wanted to eliminate, but instead I created a full head of hair of 100% primed and ready to split hairs. Talk about unfortunate!! My goal of a healthy trim totally backfired. The $6 Goody brand hair cutting scissors I bought at Walmart are WORLDS better than these. I bought these Equinox shears to step it up a level from the Goody scissors, haaaaaa. Total fail. Goody for the win!! I have since gone back to the Goody scissors and I'm so pleased because they offer a quality sharp cut. The only advantage these "fancier" Equinox kind have are the pouch, the thinning shears (which I also don't trust considering the effect the regular shears had), and they look sleeker than the Goody brand (earning them 2 stars instead of 1). Overall, my advice is that if you want nice scissors and you're a hairstylist (and your clients will give you a weird look if you use Goody shears on them), get more expensive ones than these. I imagine it must be hit or miss with mid-level shears and these are definitely a miss in my book (considering these were terrible for me but the $6 Goody ones are cheap and amazing in comparison). If you're a regular person like me, do yourself (your wallet and your hair) a favor and get some Goody shears or any other cheap hair scissors (probably worth a try) at your local store.

title: Something changed
text: My husband purchased the LifeStation with fall detection in 2019 and he experienced excellent service from the device for two years.  We would test periodically and the responders were always polite and concerned.  Sometimes he would simply sit down too hard in his chair and they would call to see if he was alright.  Then, he took a fall on ice in Dec. 2021 and his device did not come on automatically.  He pushed to button and nothing happened. He was home alone and had to stay on the ice 20 minutes before he was able to pull himself up.  We contacted the company and they told us it had not worked since April of that year -- that we were supposed to test it monthly to ensure it was working.  This did not set well with us, but we kept the unit.  Now it tells us periodically that it is not working due to poor cell reception, however, we have excellent cell reception.  We are returning it, because it does us no good if we cannot depend on it.  Not sure what has changed, but something has, and not for the better.

title: Product Listing Is Inaccurate
text:
The product itself works just fine. However, I ordered the 2-pack and only received one box; after some back-and-forth with customer service, I realized it's because the title of the product says "42 count" (the number of capsules in one box) and doesn't specify in the title that it's a 2-pack.

So unless the person fulfilling the order checks the quantity and sees "2-pack" there (which is the only place it's listed), they're going to ship you one box instead of two. Again, the product works well, but the way the listing title describes it is inaccurate and can lead to fulfillment errors. Just a heads-up.

title: Just what the doctor ordered
text:
Med Sun® 7 Day Medication Planner

NOTE: This item is NOT what is pictured in the photo!

PRICE: On clearance for $6 at Target stores; online prices seem to run double that (plus shipping).

PROS:
* There's an individual case for each day, so it's easy to take along just what you need for a day or a weekend.
* The days are color-coded as well as labeled in English, Spanish and braille.
* Each daily case has 3 removable dividers for creating up to 4 sections.
* When divided into 4 sections, each is approx 1" x 1" x 1" -- more than big enough for several large pills.
* The box which holds all 7 daily cases seems sturdy, as does its latch.
* One of the color options is pink, and I love pink!

CONS:
* The sliding lid of each daily case is perhaps too easy to slide. If bumped around too much in a purse or briefcase, it sometimes slides open. (To be safe, I carry it in an interior pocket of my purse.)
* Most online sellers send a randomly chosen color, so it's possible to get a color you dislike.

BOTTOM LINE:
This pill organizer is great for people who take a lot of very large pills, either Rx or dietary supplements, and who want to be able to take just a day's worth "to go". If you take only a couple of pills or only very small pills, this would be over-kill.

After doing some research I came across studies showing that EEA supplementation had positive effects on blood albumin levels and edema. We started them and in 3 days I saw the swelling going down. In 2 weeks he lost a total of 20 pounds and in 4 weeks he was down from a high of 223 to 198 pounds. His doctors and nurses are amazed. More than just the swelling he's also regaining lost muscle mass and endurance. He's went from being able to walk 10 feet without having to sit down to around 50 feet before tiring.
He hates the taste but can't deny the good it' done him.
The best way we've found to take them is to get a small 4 ounce cup add a scoop into some milk add a small pinch of salt to help cover up the bitterness mix well with a baby spoon or coffee stirrer and then drink in one gulp and have something to chase it with.

title: Produspa Revolushine Styling Brush.
text:
I wish I could say that I am over the moon in love with this product and it solved all of my hair care problems. That obviously didn't happen, but it is still a good product so let's talk about all of the features.

Pros:
1. It is a nicely weighted brush. It isn't super light, but I've used it several times and my arms never got tired the way they do with a blow dryer and round brush. Super plus.
2. The cord is nice and long and rotates 360 degrees which makes getting the back of your head much easier. I love this feature because sometimes I feel like I'm twisting into a pretzel to get the back of my head properly. Any help in that area is much appreciated! :)
3. There are ELEVEN different temperature settings! Wow! I really think this was super smart on ProduSpa's end because there are so many different hair types and needs and they all call for different temperatures to keep your hair at its best and healthiest. I also really like this because I've switched to a low heat temperature at the end and it helps make my hair nice and smooth and I love it.
4. There are little nibs at the end of the bristles that serve a dual purpose. The first and probably most important, they keep you from burning yourself. Hello, thank you for that. I am just about the clumsiest person ever and I have only felt too much heat one time on this product and it was because I was stupid and tried to touch it at the base of the bristles. Pro tip here: Don't touch it where the heat is :) But to brush's credit, I STILL did not burn myself like I would have if it was on a curling iron or flat iron. It hurt for maybe a second and there was no mark. I love that!
The second reason these little nibs at the ends are great are because they massage your scalp! I love using this brush because it seriously feels amazing. I barely feel it when hairs get pulled out (because that always happens when you brush or comb your hair no matter what) and I'm sort of in a zen state for a few minutes as I just keep running it along my scalp. Between those comfortable nibs at the end of the bristles and the heat, I am in heaven.

Cons:
1. I think my hair might be too thick for this to be the perfect straightening product for me. It works, it definitely works no question. But it takes longer to use this than my blow dryer and round brush. So if I have a few extra minutes I'll definitely pull it out because I love that scalp massaging aspect I spoke about above, but I don't always have a few extra minutes to do that. That being said, I'm going to try different techniques because I've wanted one of these straightening brushes for what feels like forever and I know all new styling tools take a while to master. Still though, I feel like a medium weight or thin hair would knock this out of the park right out of the box.
2. Because I haven't mastered this yet, I'm still pulling out my blow dryer and round brush to finish off styling the hair around my face. I work in a professional setting and I need to have everything perfect all the time. I just can't yet seem to achieve the look I'm going for with a flat heated brush. And if it dried my hair faster this wouldn't be an issue at all. But the fact of the matter is, it has been taking longer to dry my hair than just using my blow dryer and round brush. I'm going to try sectioning my hair differently to see if that helps and I will update this review.

So to summarize, I think it is clear that I like a lot of things about this heated styling brush. There is a lot to like about this, and for someone else I'm sure it would work better. It just doesn't so much for me. What brings it down a few stars for me is that it takes way longer to dry my hair than the old way I was doing it and honestly, I am a very busy person and don't have extra time every day.

There is something that I wanted to mention. I actually ordered the pink color and got the black. It in no way affect how I use this styling brush, nor does it really change my opinion of it at all. But it is still worth mentioning because when you order something, you want to get what you are expecting.

I have to tell you that I received this at no cost or a discounted price for review, and testing. I was in no way compensated for a positive review, clearly. Every review I do is based 100% off of my experience with the product and I do not guarantee a positive review. In fact if you go and read all my reviews you will see that I give glowing reviews to the products I love regardless of if I received a discount when purchasing the product, and conversely I have given far less than glowing reviews when it was not a product I enjoyed. I want my reviews to be accurate and helpful! If you find my review helpful, please click "Yes" on the button below.

text:
Purchased charger the beginning of October 2016, it died beginning of February 2017 after only about 10 uses. Contacted company through Amazon and they promptly offered to replace it. That was nice of them but the return shipping cost was almost as much as the original cost of the charger. Into the electronic recycling bin it goes and next time I'll do a little more research and buy a better quality recharger. Junk, don't buy.

This is an update to my earlier review:

After posting my initial review, I was contacted by EBL asking if I would like to return the charger under warranty and have it exchanged for a new one. I stated sure provided the return shipping cost wasn't excessive. I looked into the shipping cost and found out it was only $10 less than the initial cost of the charger. It wasn't worth the cost to return it so I told EBL I would just toss it and buy a different one. They responded in a very short period of time and offered to send me a replacement free of charge. I stated to them if they were willing to send me one no cost I'd be more than happy to accept it. True to their word, within about a week I had a new unit in my hands. I've only had the replacement one for a couple of weeks now but it seems to be working nicely. It's to early to tell about it's longevity but I'm keeping my fingers crossed.
Thus I'm updating my review to a 4 star. Not so much for the performance of the charger, but for the performance of their customer service people. When they saw my initial review they immediately sent me an email asking if they could be of any assistance and followed through on their promise to send another charger at no cost. They were very concerned about my satisfaction with their product. In todays world it's a refreshing change of pace to see this kind of customer service. Kudos to their customer service team.

title: Nice smell.
text:
I received this product at a discount in exchange for an honest review.

I got this because nearly all the women in my family have kidney problems. My sister's have kidney infections all the time, and I thought this might be good to have on in hand in case I or they needed it.

The pills come with a nice little free pill holder, and the cranberry pills smell kinda nice.
I've been taking one everyday since I received them. The first day I took them, I felt like I got a bit of heartburn, but after that day, I don't think I've had any adverse side effects at all---other than I've been having to go number 1 a lot. My kidneys haven't been bothering me, and I feel pretty good. I'm thinking that they are a good product. I'd really like to test them on my sister's if ever the need arises, but maybe if they took them they wouldn't get kidney problems. I don't know. I'll have to tell them about this product and see what they think.

On the package it says that it's GMO free, and I hope that's true, because besides having vitamin c, vitamin e, and cranberry concentrate, it does have fillers (probably the outer shell of the pill) The other ingredients include soybean oil, gelatin, beeswax, vegetable glycerin. I'd much rather that it didn't have soybean oil. But if they help my kidneys, I won't complain.

I find it hard reviewing supplements only after a week of taking them, because you have to take them for several weeks to really be accurate. I think I'll have to update this review, later.

The Good:
- Elegant, clean design.
- Nice glass top (easy to clean)
- Bright display
- Easy to read
- Options for both Kgs and Lbs (button on the back changes the units).
- No slips pads on the bottom
- The batteries are included - 4 AAA's (always nice when companies take care of this for you)

The Bad:
- Plastic frame on the bottom with little to no protection from water. Since it is in the bathroom, I would expect the battery compartment to be a little less exposed. Need to be careful that water doesn't get in there and damage it.

text:
This review is for the Renpho rechargeable sleep machine. It's a really nice size and every time I see it I get the feeling of a well built product. It's also just pleasing to look at. I really think Renpho chose the right speaker quality and size for a sound machine, which makes me happy.

I also think Renpho hit the sweet spot with size. It's honestly the perfect size and weight for traveling and the fact that it is rechargeable is really cool. The user manual says it lasts 7 hours on a charge. I can't vouch for that as I have only used it on the auto-off feature which shuts it off after an hour. title: Biotin Believer - It really Works!
text:
Some people say that it doesn't work, but I definitely know that it does. There is no doubt that since I have started to take biotin my hair has definitely started to grow faster and healthier. I think some people see negative results when they start taking biotin because they make two mistakes. The first one is that they start by taking the full dose instead of slowly introducing the extra biotin to the body. And the second is that they neglect the importance of staying really hydrated. If you don't hydrate the body when you take biotin, the extra nutrients that the body doesn't need won't get flushed out and can cause issues that seem people talk about, like acne.

I started by taking just half of the dose of biotin for the first two weeks and then began upping the dose to the full amount. I also drank a bunch of water from the beginning. I have found that the biotin is not only making my hair grow faster (my hair stylist will attest!), but it is also actually improving the health of my skin, making it "glow" and even seem more elastic! I started seeing these results only a week after I began taking the full dose of biotin.

And, no, I didn't see any of the negative results some people are concerned about when taking biotin, such as facial hair growth, or thicker hair in any other areas of my body - just my hair on my head grew thicker and faster thank you very much!

After doing some more research about biotin I discovered that it seems to be something safe for everyone to take. I was interested to see that people who have PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome) can greatly benefit from taking biotin because it helps to counteract VLDL (a form of bad cholesterol) that is typically found in the blood of patients with PCOS. In doing so, women with PCOS typically see a reduction in the side effects. Of course, I assume anyone with PCOS or other health issues should consult with their doctor before taking biotin or any other supplement.

I hope this helps any other person on the fence about trying biotin. It really works! Try it for yourself!

title: Many options should satisfy almost everyone.
text:
***Full Disclosure*** I was given a coupon code to make the purchase of them all but free. I would not have purchased these ear plugs otherwise.

That being said, there is no way I could give these anything other that 5 stars. There are options for every situation and ear type.

The moldable silicon plugs will probably get the least amount of use, they reduce moderate noises to quiet, but that is their limit. They also effectively clean the wax out of your ears if you don't do it before they are inserted. I don't usually wear hearing protection in a situation where there isn't dust or dirt, so I don't see them lasting long because they are sticky and will become filthy to the point of not wanting to put them in my ears.

The dark green ones fit great in my right ear canal, but they slowly slip out of my left because it's much smaller. It's not designed for a canal as small as I apparently have. Quiets the noise drastically in the right side though.

The blue ones are easily the most comfortable. The 'stem' is a little long, so if I were to wear them while sleeping I would surely trim it back a little to avoid pressure on the stem while sleeping on my side. For sleeping they would probably make it impossible to wake up to an alarm.

The orange ones are my favorite, they do everything I think an earplug should. They fit deep into either of my ears, they don't work their out and they cut the noise of my mower to a gentle hum. The rigid plastic insert makes insertion easier and offers better purchase for removal. They also didn't bother my ears at all in the he hour I was mowing and trimming my lawn. I even left them in when I came inside so I wouldn't have to listen to my kids screaming.

All of the pairs having their own little case is another plus, no more picking lint off a plug before putting it in.

I think it's safe to say that these will satisfy 99% of people who buy them.

title: Great item, a little short
text:
I've tried numerous flushable liners and have decided I love these, even though they do have one drawback.

These are very soft. I'm not worried at all about how soft they are on my DS's bottom. In addition, if they're just peed in, they wash well and don't bunch or shrink in the washer. I'm able to use them 2-3 times if they're just peed on. I just put them through our washer and dryer. Other brands don't hold up to the washing machine. They either disintegrate too quickly, or they stretch out or crunch up and need to be spread back out again to be used, which takes extra time. These are lovely to use. I pre-load each diaper with one as I stuff the diapers so my husband doesn't have to do anything other than slap the diaper on the butt.

My only real issue with these, and the reason they get 4 stars not 5) are that they are not very long, front-to-back. They HAVE caught everything, but don't cover the entire diaper for my tall 2-yr old boy. This is only really an issue if I have to use diaper cream (in front) and want to make sure it isn't contacting the inside of my diapers and catch poo at the same time.

General impression: great to use once they're on solids. Makes cloth diapering much easier for my family. Very economical as pee only ones can be re-used after washing.

title: Seriously superior screens
text:
Chances are, you're reading this and thinking to yourself that these screens are too expensive... I know I thought it.

You can get 200+ glass screens for around the same price and this is for only ten but believe me when I tell you that these are actually more economical in the long run AND they are genuinely superior!

How are they better? Equally at home in your favorite pipe or bong, they let more smoke through with a cleaner pull and practically zero resistance. They're also a lot easier to use — sure the others aren't difficult but it usually takes a couple of goes to get them in the right way... These you just drop into the bowl and you're ready to add whatever it is you'll be smoking.

They're also better for cleaning. I use a tiny nylon brush (available here as part of a set for around $5) to poke the holes through after each bowl, quick wipe with the same paper towel that I use to wipe out the bowl and I'm good to get going again. I've also soaked them in alcohol once but there's really no need.

And this is also how come they are actually more economical — with regular glass screens (Jack, daisy etc) they are such a PITA to clean that, personally at least, I just throw them out after a single use.

I haven't compared these to steel or brass screens since all glass screens are better than those.

I didn't receive a discount or any free products in exchange for this unbiased review but if any company wanted to send me free stuff to review I would be happy to participate.

title: Small hiccup on delivery, but fixed quickly!
text:
This item has been on my bucket list for, literally, a decade. I started having seasonal allergies in 2008, and after some air purifier research, decided this would at some point be mine, when I could afford it.

Fast forward a decade through an Awful Lot of Life, to a point where I have a chunk of money from a deeply unfortunate occurrence (ie, once it's gone it's gone so invest it wisely), but the West Coast is pretty much one continuous fire and/or smoke bank. I have both funds and need, so I pulled the trigger on finally getting my bucket list air purifier.

It arrives! I'm thrilled! I unpack it!

The order was for The Great Wave. The box says The Great Wave.

The panel inside...is Water Lilies.

I am hugely disappointed. I send RabbitAir an email.

They immediately send the correct panel with a shipping label to put on the box to send Water Lilies back. I am deeply impressed with their speed and their willingness to believe I'm a decent enough person to send back the panel. I get distracted for a week (hey, my daughter started kindergarten, it was...a big shift), I send the panel back.

In the meantime, I've had a week of the correctly decorated panel. It's everything I hoped for. Outside we wear Vogmasks so we can breathe without coughing, but inside the air is sweet, even though really the purifier is only rated for doing the downstairs. It's REALLY quiet, unless toast gets burnt or something and then it kicks on with barely enough sound for us to wonder if the water is running somewhere in the house. It's gorgeous, it's smaller than I'd thought, and while I haven't had the energy to mount it on the wall yet, it does look lovely on the coffee table.

Bravo, RabbitAir. You're everything I've been dreaming of.

title: Pretty Comfy
text: My husband does tattoos and I purchased this for him to be able to do back pieces easier.  I was a little skiddish because of the price, but so far it seems to be fine.  The cushions are pretty thick and comfortable and it was easy to assemble. It actually came assembled except the head rest, but the way that it folds down for packing, I can see why someone would want instructions, but it is quite simple once you figure it out. You need to spread the legs so that it is standing and then lift the seat and drop the bar to the required adjustment, and then lift the arm rest and drop that bar to the required adjustment. Then you simply unscrew the screw on the bar with the headrest and insert it onto the top and reinsert the screw when the headrest is at the required adjustment.  My only worry is because the seat and the armrest just lift and drop into different positions with little notches, I worry if someone too heavy gets on it that it may just fall to another position, but we haven't had anyone heavier sit on it yet.  I will probably update once we've owned it for awhile. The other plus is I purchased it mainly for back pieces but it has made arm pieces easier also.

title: Be careful of the one-star negative review from 2016
text:
Don't be misled by the 2016 one-star review full of erroneous statements. One claim is that nothing kills MRSA. That is simply not true. According to the CDC, any disinfectant that kills Staphylococcus aureus will also kill methicillin-resistent Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). MRSA is Staphylococcus aureus that has developed a antimicrobial resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics such as penicillin derivatives and cephalosporins.

Another claim is that it is "disingenuous for the company to claim that (the product) is EPA approved as it is the CDC that evaluated disinfectants for effectivemess in killing organisms." Again, simply not true. According to the CDC, "The disinfectant’s label should have a list of germs that the product can kill, along with an Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) registration number." You can go to the EPA website to find the list of EPA registered disinfectants.

10 Seconds Shoe Disinfectant and Deodorizer has EPA Reg. No. 44445-67-75242

text: Creatine monohydrate, in capsule form, as you'd expect. Will definitely order more of these when I run out.

title: A decent natural mascara
text:
There are two things I look for when shopping for mascara: waterproof and volumizing. Waterproof formulation is better at holding curls which I need as I have't been gifted with naturally curly and thick lashes.

I have used this mascara now for a full week and while I am not too impressed with its volumizing claim, it is quite a good "natural" mascara. My lashes stay curled despite a few hours at the beach. It applies smoothly and two coats give the illusion of lengthy lashes provided you curl them first.

But since I was after a volumizing mascara and want va-va-voom lashes, I was rather disappointed with this. I find that I have to layer it to get some volume which means clumpy and brittle lashes, not to mention it becomes expensive. I have had better and pretty looking lashes from Maybelline's Full and Soft for a fraction of the price and without the brittleness.

title: 4.18 GPA despite depression
text:
I'm a college student who wants an extra-sharp mind. I take these in addition to Solaray's B-50 complex.
I'm a repeat customer of this product, and will probably continue buying it for years.

Last semester (first semester I've ever tried this regimen), I pulled four A+, the rest A's while taking 18 credits. Best grades I've ever had in my life. My college gives a 4.3 for each A+, so my GPA is 4.18 right now. Both vitamin B and Omega 3 supposedly help the brain to remember things better. It worked. I barely studied because I didn't have time, and was able to recall concepts from lecture with ease during tests.

I also wrestle with clinical depression. I take the full possible dose of wellbutrin, but it doesn't pull me out of my funk all the way. In addition to helping with memory, B-50 and Omega 3 also supposedly boost mood. Seems to help enormously.

And as far as isolating the value of Omega 3... I ran out for a week, and my anti-depressant pills just didn't seem to work as well. =) I know heat can render Omega-3's useless, and however these pills are processed and stored, they are definitely preserving the useful qualities of Omega-3.

title: Truly ridiculous, poorly made, but cured my car sickness
text:
Context: I bought these because for years I was getting carsick as a passenger. I would get sick literally anytime I was not looking out a window and there were abrupt changes in acceleration (speeding up, slowing down, any amount of turning, including lane changes). I carpool to work and the two hours of my life each day were being wasted because I couldn't do anything except stare outside. A coworker recommended carsick glasses and I chose this particular brand because this one size seemed to fit smaller heads pretty well based on the reviews and submitted pictures.

Results:
Somehow, my carsickness is cured. I don't understand why, at all, and I wore these things maybe three or four times tops. Each time they did help me while I wore them and was able to read on my phone without any issues, but wearing them was kind of a pain; they aren't super comfortable and they kept sliding down my face. Then, one day on the ride home, I was looking at my phone stubbornly not wearing them and realized the motion sickness never kicked in. I tested it the entire car ride home, and nothing happened. I carry these things with me just in case now, but I've been riding multiple times without them and have been completely carsickness-free.

Pros: My outcome using this product was probably better than average, but I don't think this brand has anything special beyond other brands, which is why this isn't getting more stars. If you have severe carsickness, I think it's worth trying this ridiculous thing out, even if you don't choose this particular variety.

Criticisms: Why these things do not have hinges is beyond me (I didn't see any other brands that did when I bought them, either). It is part of what makes them uncomfortable: having them 'open' on your face causes the nose area to pinch. Also, the rounded ends really do not hook my ears; I have to weave them into my pulled back hair to keep them from sliding off my face. Lastly, there should be a blanket ban on the one-size-fits-all concept. I have no doubt the revenue from this very specific device doesn't justify the expense of producing different sizes, but I'm still going to complain about it.

title: STOPPED GROWING PAINS IN MY KIDS.  AMAZING PRODUCT-  10 STARS!!!
text: This product is nothing short of amazing.  A couple months after my son had started kindergarten (3 years ago), he began waking up in the middle of the night screaming. Blood-curdling screams, the "make a parent's heart jump out of their chest and race to your child's room" kind. Then he would just cry and moan while I held him. This would last about 15-30 minutes but he would still be mostly asleep and I couldn't even get him to actually wake up enough to communicate what was wrong. And then the next day he wouldn't remember it, he knew he'd been crying but didn't know why. The only thing I could think of at the time was that he was having nightmares. Finally one night he actually spoke and said "it hurts", and he was holding his leg.  That's all I could get out of him but it was enough. I googled "kids leg pain only at night" learned about kids growing pains and how magnesium can help. First I bought 2 different kinds of  chewable magnesium tablets but they didn't seem to help much. And he didn't like the taste at all.  More research led me to this liquid form.  I was hesitant to buy it at first, as it seemed pretty expensive.  But I found one bottle lasts a LONG time.  I give him one dropper fill (1ml) up to the line, mixed in a little grape juice so he could handle the taste. Other juices didn't work- only grape juice.  It was a little bitter but he got used to it.  Once in the morning and once before bed, just to get his magnesium levels up. After a couple months I dropped down to just once a day.  The effects were immediate.  He did wake up the next 2 nights after he started taking it, but with only crying instead of screaming, which was a very welcome change.  Being woken up night after night by your child screaming is not a fun experience as a parent.  By the 3rd night he only whimpered a few times but didn't cry.  And that was it, no more waking up screaming after that.  He is now in 3rd grade and has had only one episode of growing pains recently and that was when I stopped giving him his grape juice every day.  I blame Covid for that, lol.  Now his little brother is in kindergarten this year as well, and while his growing pains have not been nearly as severe, he did start to complain about his legs hurting 2 weeks ago, so that is what prompted me to write this review.  At least his pains were during the day and he was able to tell me what was going on.  I started him on the grape juice & magnesium regime and got the same result as I had gotten with his brother. After a couple days the pain was gone.  Both of them are still eating me out of house and home like little Hobbits with their second breakfasts and Elevenses, but at least they are pain free now.

I recommend this case if 1) you are on a budget, 2) you don't do anything besides put it in a purse or glove box, and/or 3) you don't use it very often.

title: Remember the 80's...
text:
For some reason, I remember that series 5 was a big deal in the 80's. Was that the series where the cards were significantly larger? I don't remember, but I do remember that series 5 was a bit more special than the others. This is a throwback to the nostalgic toys of the 80's. I guess of Transformers, GI Joes and even Cabbage Patch Kids can make appearances in the 00's, why can't the 'evil, dirty' cousin, Garbage Pail Kids?

The Garbage Pail kids of the 80's though were HUGE. They were a blatant parody of the immensely popular Cabbage Patch kids of the time. Everyone wanted a Cabbage Patch Kid, and they all had the funny names and same style faces, etc. Then came a movie and a TV show (that never aired)... but unfortunately due to the likeness of the popular Cabbage Patch Kids, a lawsuit also tagged along. The series today features glossier cards, higher quality paper and a variety of other things that makes it an altogether more special operation. Unless you're really reaching for a piece of nostalgia, however, I'd say there's nothing particularly impressive to see here. :)

title: NOT FAA COMPLIANT!
text:
I purchased this in August of 2021. At the time the Amazon page sold it as suitable for airline travel, which seemed to indicate that I'd have no problem flying with it. At the very last hours before my flight, I learned from American Airlines that the FAA did not approve this wheelchair as sold. The problem is the battery, which is not FAA compliant (Exceeds 300 watt hours).

The battery that comes with this wheelchair is rated 24V20Ah. Translated, that means 24 volts at 20 amp/hours, (with "amp/hours" referring to the number of hours the battery can last). And that translates into watt hours as 24 x 20 = 480 watt hours. For a 24 volt battery to qualify under FAA guidelines the rating can't exceed 24V12.5Ah. (24 x 12.5 = 300 watt hours).

On such short notice, I ended up with no option but to cancel a trip I had planned for over a year. I like the wheelchair, but I think I deserve some compensation for the loss of my trip and hassles. There are FAA compliant lithium-ion batteries sold on Amazon that would provide adequate power yet are limited to 300WH. (E.g.: https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B012HHV2J6/ref=ox_sc_saved_title_4?smid=A2OTUJ24ZUUY7H&psc=1. There may be others but that was the first one I found.)

I feel that at the very least as a showing of good will, the seller should pay for or provide one for me, and then I'll let the matter drop. Otherwise, I'll be consulting an attorney about seeking the entire damages for the loss of a trip and air fare that I had planned and paid for many months before.

title: It's worth it...when it's on sale.
text:
I bought this to assist the ageing eyes focus on circuit boards and it works reasonably well.

First off, I'm not sure the 5x magnification rating is accurate since a 1" piece of paper measures about 1 1/2" (i.e. 1.5x) without distortion when magnified through the lens. But it's large enough for me to do work comfortably.

Quality wise the frame isn't flimsy, but it's by no means a professional grade lamp. Once the adjustment screws are properly tightened it holds it's position pretty well.

The lamp's 3 colour and 10 brightness settings are where this unit really shines since you can adjust both to find the perfect luminosity depending on what you're magnifying. In my case circuit boards usually look best with a shade of warm white and 3-4 brightness level.

A word of warning: This lamp cannot be plugged into a wall socket. It needs to be powered by a USB charger/adapter. At full tilt the lamp pulls more than 13.2 watts which caused my 5V 2.4A (12 watts) USB power adapter to go into over-current protection mode. Consequently, I run the unit at no more than 50% of maximum brightness to prevent the adapter from shutting down. I suspect that one would need a good quality 5V 4A (20 watts) adapter to comfortably run this at full capacity.

The lamp didn't come with a power adapter or a table-top base but at the sale price of $ 21.00 I didn't mind those omissions. However I've seen it retail above $ 35.00. At that price point there are better alternatives for the money,

title: Eneloop Vs Eneloop XX.
text:
The good:

1) Made in Japan.
2) Pre-charged & ready to use.
3) Rechargeable 1500X (X = times / cycles). I'm happy with just 500X.

The not so good:

1) 2000 mAh. That's not enough juice to provide stamina for power hungry devices.

Background:

For over 4yrs now, I've been using the 'made in Japan', Low Self Discharge (LSD) AA & AAA rechargeable batteries from Sanyo called Eneloop & Eneloop 1500. I use them with all the remote controls & electronic devices / gadgets that I have. I have over a dozen pairs of the Sanyo Eneloop batteries & I like to keep them organized. I have them all marked / labeled in pairs so that I don't mix the batteries when I'm charging them. The plain white color of the Sanyo Eneloop is a plus point here.

For remote controls, the Eneloops are perfect. A single charge c'd stay for more than a year. No complaints. It's when I use the Eneloops with the Canon PowerShot A590IS [[ASIN:B0011ZCDKS Canon PowerShot A590IS 8MP Digital Camera with 4x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom]] that I wish that these batteries had a lil' more juice in them. I c'd barely touch an average of 200 shots with a single charge. That's when I gave the Sanyo Eneloop XX a try & I'm impressed with it. The milliampere-hour (mAh), a measurement of the electric charge transferred by a steady current of one Ampere for one hour (check Google for more detailed explanation), in the new Sanyo Eneloop XX has been upped to 2500 mAh. This increase of 500 mAh really shows an improvement in my compact camera's performance. I've already taken over 400 shots with the first charge & I'm still counting. Even the refresh time between shots have reduced a bit.

Conclusion:

Just a few yrs ago, the Sanyo Eneloop (rechargeable 1000X) used to be priced @ USD20 / 4pcs. It's now selling for about USD10 / 4pcs on Amazon & is very good value for money [[ASIN:B000IV2WAW SANYO eneloop 4 Pack AA NiMH Pre-Charged Rechargeable Batteries]]. The newer Sanyo Eneloop 1500 (rechargeable 1500X), with no performance advantage over the original Eneloop, is priced @ about USD15 / 4pcs. I got the Sanyo Eneloop XX (rechargeable 500X) from B&H, NYC @ USD20 / 4pcs [[ASIN:B004DW7S06 Sanyo Eneloop AA NiMH Pre-Charged Rechargeable Batteries - new 2500 mAh --eneloop xx -- 1 pack of 4 batteries - Limited Quantity]].

I'm sure the prices will eventually come down with more competition & with newer models getting released every year. For now, the Sanyo Eneloop XX sh'd only be considered for power hungry devices such as compact cameras & remote controlled toys. For everything else, the original Sanyo Eneloop (rechargeable 1000X) is still a very good purchase & has not run out of juice just yet.

I find 1500X a lil' over exaggerated. Even if I charge a pair of Sanyo Eneloop XXs every week, 500X will last me over 9yrs. I know I'll replace / upgrade these batteries in about 5yrs or so with whatever c'd be the latest & greatest in LSD rechargeable battery technology then. For 2000 mAh LSD rechargeable batteries, I'd stick with the original Sanyo Eneloop (rechargeable 1000X) & save some bucks.

For best results, I'm using the Sanyo Eneloop batteries with La Crosse Technology BC-700 power battery charger [[ASIN:B000RSOV50 La Crosse Technology BC-700 Alpha Power Battery Charger]].

title: MAJOR DESIGN FLAWS - WHAT A NIGHTMARE!
text:
At first this seemed like an awesome medical ID bracelet - and I thought it would be far superior to the Medic Alert bracelet that I have worn for 10 years, especially since my medical situation has changed in some really important ways. I mean, how cool is it to be able to enter ALL your medical information, medications, medical conditions, previous surgeries, history, everything and have it immediately accessible, right?

WRONG! Depending upon the computer program and OS, this USB may or may not automatically pop up - and with epilepsy, time is brain - so I can't afford for some EMT or ER doctor to try to fiddle with the computer while he/she tries to treat me.
WORSE YET - you CAN'T PRINT OUT ALL THE INFORMATION!!!! HOW DUMB IS THAT?! Seriously, imagine me in a seizure, I can't communicate, some assistant is trying to get the USB to open up, when she/he finally does, she/he can't print out the information and must write it all down by hand?!? Because of all the different sections, will anyone even notice that I have a VNS implant and can't have electrical stimulation? That CPR is a much better alternative for me that a shock to restart my heart? OR which drugs are just going to make my seizures worse? Or that I am allergic to penicillin? Or have time to write a note to the doctor to tell him/her all of the 12 medications I am taking?? There are five different screens you have to tab through to even find the information, will the assistant (once they figure out how to start the USB drive going - it doesn't pop up automatically on my computer) even know which pages are the most important? And how much time will be wasted while my brain is dying? NO THANK YOU! Even the stickers that come with this bracelet are useless - I can only put one on there - so which disease is most important? Seizures or Diabetes? Either could render me unconscious or unable to communicate.

MACX - FIX THESE DESIGN FLAWS BEFORE IT KILLS SOMEONE! MAKE IT SO IT WILL AUTOMATICALLY OPEN UP IN ANY OPERATING SYSTEM AND PRINT OUT WITH A BIG, OBVIOUS PRINT MEDICAL INFORMATION BUTTON ON THE SCREEN.
I am just going back to Medic Alert to have a new bracelet engraved saying Epilepsy, Diabetes, VNS implant, drug allergies, hypertension, etc, because frankly, a phone call to Medic Alert will be much faster than having someone try to figure this thing out. You can't even use the PRINTSCREEEN button to get it to print, and when one of my doctors tried, it just crashed out his computer.

title: Loving these
text: Comfortable enough to sleep in, and the low profile makes them easy to wear during a variety of contexts without calling attention to the fact that I have them in. I've only used the silicone ends so far, and I can't remember what the difference is supposed to be with them. But the silicone lets me have a conversation, as long as I can see the person's face, while decreasing the intensity of ambient noise. The case is a problem, they are easy to lose and I use them frequently during the day because my ears have become quite sensitive to noise with age and hearing damage from years of abuse. I need them when my dog barks, when I use small kitchen appliances, when I walk past a landscape crew using mowers and leaf blowers. Lots of daily situations. I put the case on a sturdy chain that I wear around my neck and try to be careful to never put them down anywhere. Sometimes I wish they would block even more sound, but since they are designed to be worn in concerts (which I haven't tried) and other situations in which you want to hear, it makes sense that they don't. Though perhaps that's what the foam inserts are for? I'll have to check on that. Since the inserts are removable they are easy to clean, which I have to do since I use them all the time. And again, I'm able to sleep with them. On those nights in which every single sound makes it hard to relax (my husband snoring, even the dog breathing!) it really helps me have a nice deep sleep. Overall I'm really happy with them and find myself recommending them whenever the topic of loud noises comes up, and I bought a pair for my daughter hoping she will use them regularly at concerts and loud parties. I don't think she has, but young people don't really believe they will have hearing loss as they age. They feel invincible and don't really thoroughly believe their old parents about stuff like this.

title: A very tiny bit off but overall seems fine
text:
When I weighed a 15 lbs. dumbbell when I first got it, I think it showed 14.9 lbs. After many, many weeks, using it periodically for myself, I see that same dumbbell now shows 15.2. So I am not sure why the variation, and the change in over vs. under (maybe since near a radiator since I do not have a better location?) That said, it seems close enough to accurate, and it allows me to monitor my weight over time, even if it is not 100% accurate. It seems very close, which is fine considering the great price (also got on sale).

And as others have said, I feel more comfortable that the glass is enclosed by metal, as protection against shattering like others shown. To clarify, the metal does wrap around the four sides, so it is not just laying on top. But it does not go all the way down to the bottom of all sides; it covers about 80% of the height. Regardless it seems like the metal does provide extra safety and containment from any glass shatter risk. Also, the display is large and easy enough to read from above, and the size of the platform is more than large enough for me.

After going crazy searching for alternatives, and no good options for analog scales, like others reviewers said, the metal enclosure, price, and reasonable accuracy seem to make it a smart choice.

I have yet to see how long the battery lasts, but so far so good.

title: Very nice, quick, easy, and seeminly accurate!
text:
Awesome product! works well!

This wrist blood pressure monitor is very good! I just got it in, and it works well! First off, it's very accurate, I tried this on, ran the blood pressure check, and it gave me certain numbers, and then I went on to my more traditional elbow/bicep cuff blood pressure machine, and it gave me nearly the same blood pressure score, which leads me to believe that this one is reading accurately!

It comes in a white box which can be used as a carrying case, which the wrist cuff folds neatly and fits into, which is not too bulky if I am going to take this on the go with me. It closes well and won't open up by mistake in my bag, which leads me to believe that this will be a good product for the person who wants to have a blood pressure machine with them on the go at all times.

This product is probably very good for travel also because of the reasons mentioned above, and what I like most about it is that it's way easier to do and way less conspicuous, as you can put it on just like a watch, sit properly and prop your arm up to your heart level and push start and it can read your blood pressure.

The only problem I had with this product is that it can squeeze a bit tight, which however, is probably pretty typical of any blood pressure monitor, but it was a little more than i expected when taking my blood pressure. Maybe because it is a wrist cuff instead of a bicep cuff that it squeezes tighter, I'm not sure, I am not a doctor!

All-in-all, very worth it's price, and very convenient, and seemingly very accurate. Very good purchase for anyone who has high blood pressure or a heart condition and want ready monitoring with you at all times, as it is very easy to whip out and use.

title: Learning Curve
text: I actually purchased these a few months ago after discovering I needed smaller flanges. I had read good reviews and decided to try these instead of buying standard flanges for my pump. At first, I thought they were just okay and not really worth the price. They are tricky to get positioned correctly since they are angled. The downward angle does not work for everyone, apparently. After watching videos on the website, I decided to try turning these flanges sideways and it made a huge difference. I have been pumping for a few months now and have grown to like them more.  I primarily use Freemie cups, but there are days when I feel the Freemies are not emptying my breasts as well so I will use these for at least one pump session. They are great for releasing clogs and I do get a slight increase in the amount of milk from my slacker side by using them. I don't necessarily have to use lube for these like I do for the plastic flanges, but I will if I'm feeling a bit sensitive. I like that I can sit up straight versus having to lean forward with the regular flanges. They are a bit on the heavy side, so I wouldn't trust a hands-free bra to hold them very long once the bottles start to fill. I'm not 100% in love with them, but I do prefer them over the plastic flanges.

title: The Only Flavor I'll Dearly Miss If It Doesn't Return
text:
I've been using Glytch for over a month or so as well as trying out other Gamer(TM) energy drinks like Sneak and GFuel, and I can honestly say that I'm still impressed with how good Glytch is compared to its competition in terms of the quality of the product as well as the taste. Out of the 12 flavors I've tried--and I have a total of 16 sample packs and tubs--this is the ONLY flavor I would save from being forgotten into obscurity should it not return once its gone on Amazon. (The fact that I bought two tubs here should indicate how serious I am, and I might feel the same about Sour Grape Ape later.)

Speaking of the topic, if you compare Glytch on Amazon versus their website, you may be confused on the different packaging, supplement facts and flavor varieties and that's because there was a recent formula change around mid-September. Literally, I could not have chosen a better time to get into Glytch as I had the best opportunity to try out the old and new formulas with sample packs for a majority of them. The good news is that most of the flavors on Amazon have much superior replacements such as Berry-A-51 turning into Falcon Smash as well as old flavors remaining on the website like Aim Assist and Predator. Other flavors like Slaughter Melon don't really have alternatives, but it wasn't a very flavorful tub to begin with. This is entirely the opposite case for Sour Bomb.

There are two types of sour-flavored food and drinks: Those that are raw sour that leave no tastebuds left (like GFuel's Sour Blue Chug Rug) and others where it's very tart, yet still has a lot of flavor to enjoy. Sour Bomb fulfills the latter category with a sour-apple vibe, and it's almost in the same league for flavor as the other options such as Aim Assist and Falcon Smash. However, I don't think it quite gets up there for sourness and flavor, which is why I think it is the most redeemable tub from the lot.

Now as far as the old formula, it's a solid combination of active ingredients with likely adequate dosages. One of the big selling points with the new formulation is the fact that they list the amounts of each ingredient, but you can get a good estimate for most ingredients by looking at the labels carefully in order of the largest ingredients first. I wouldn't say that most of them are the most optimal dosage as they mainly meet the minimum requirements on one or two drinks, but considering that these products are meant for gamers/Esport-players I think that is acceptable. The old formula also had certain ingredients like Maltodextrin and Beta Alanine, which doesn't bother me but would be a problem for people concerned about their blood sugar or are on a Keto diet. (Also, I have never experienced any of the itchiness associated with Beta Alanine from the old formula on one or two scoops, so I can safely say
it's not enough to cause that side-effect and it's likely done for other manufacturing reasons.)

In comparison, the new formula focuses on a lot more on Gamer(TM) ingredients that are supposedly meant for gamers to increase their performance. If I sound like I am being sarcastic with these additions, I am not yet I remain optimistically skeptical; stuff like nooLVL do have a couple double-blind tests to prove that they are effective and I can definitely feel and tell a difference from my own experience when trying out other products with the ingredients in isolation. My issue is that after reading the studies on them I have no idea what that actually translates into for Esports or even the average gamer. You can also find some of these ingredients in isolation from one another such as Advanced GG and Glitch (yes, there's another gamer drink spelled differently,) but I think this is the only brand out there that combines Dynamine (to extend the caffeine effects at lower dosages), nooLVL (for added focus/cognitive benefits) and Cognizin (another cognitive boosting ingredient but also for eye-health like Alpha GPC.)

However, my ultimate decision for energy drinks comes down to three simple questions: Is this flavor something I really enjoy and can't get anywhere else? Do I notice any improvements as a result from it with little to no side-effects? Is it affordable for my budget? In all these cases, Glytch nails each one as I can have this in the morning with no crashes but also have a scoop mid-evening without impacting my sleep thanks to other ingredients to counteract the caffeine. Almost all the new line of flavors are absolute bangers, and with affiliate coupons and sales that means the price of each tub comes out to around $31 to $35 for 40 servings (or 20 if you two-scoop it), which doesn't make them prohibitively expensive. The added fact that this is a smaller business in the US is just the cherry on top for an exception product to begin with, and I am more than happy to continue supporting them for many years.

title: The Rolls Royce of vegan proteins
text:
Most vegan proteins taste like a cross between hot buttered ass and deep-fried garbage. Why? Two main reasons: nasty sweeteners, or too many weird additives as though the manufacturer wants it to be too many things to too many people. (Why does a vegan protein powder need a stupid "whole plant blend" with broccoli powder or whatnot in it?). And on top of all that, a lot of them have inferior amino acid profiles. What does this mean? It means that the proteins do not compare to animal-based proteins for how much they succeed at the ONE thing protein is meant to do: support muscle tissue.

Nectis has dealt with these issues admirably. Instead of releasing a product to the public that the manufacturers would never consume themselves (cuz it tastes bad), Nectis actually tastes amazing. And, instead of selling JUST pea protein with no other protein in it to improve the amino acid profile, Nectis includes rice hull protein, which gives it an amino profile much closer to whey or soy.

So, as long as they don't remove that rice hull protein from it, and as long as they don't start using crappy sweeteners that make it taste like boiled King Cone wrappers, and as they don't add a bunch of useless ingredients to it that do nothing but add bulk and reduce its effectiveness AS A PROTEIN POWDER, I will buy it. The end.

title: Great for cleaning
text:
I've used all three grades of Sandflex blocks, and I think they're excellent products. The only knock on them, in my book, is that the coarse block can break down pretty quickly if you're using it aggressively - the medium and fine blocks tend to last a lot longer. Basically, they're big rubber erasers loaded with abrasive grit, and just like erasers, they wear down as they're used. This is both good and bad: it means that they can cease to be blocks fairly quickly (again, mostly with the coarse) depending upon the shape of the surface you're cleaning, but it also allows you to shape them if you need a particular profile. When a block I've been using starts to break down, I typically hold onto any smaller pieces and use them for cleaning tight spots. I've even stuck pieces on a Dremel mandrel and used them that way.

My primary use for these blocks is tool restoration: they're a great way to remove rust, dust, and "patina" from a plane, chisel, saw blade, or what-have-you that's been languishing in somebody's damp basement or in the back corner of a barn. The coarse quickly breaks down the heavy stuff, and follow-up scrubbing with the medium and fine can take a pretty unsightly tool and make it look respectable. They're not going to work magic - the rust pits and other damage aren't going away - but they can get you back to clean metal. I find that the fine blocks do a good job of bringing shine back to brass, and even used one to remove some scuffs from the plastic bezel of a watch, which came away clear and looking almost new. However, like any abrasive, you have to exercise discretion: if you want to save an etching on a saw blade, for example, work gently with the medium or fine blocks, and keep a close eye on it for evidence of fading. I wiped out the etching on an old Marples gouge once with a couple strokes of the fine block - whoops.

Overall, I like these much better than steel wool for cleaning. You can't lap a plane's sole with them - you need a glass or granite plate and sandpaper for that - but they are very effective when used to keep tools free of rust, grime, and general build-up. I use them all the time.

These came the other day, and I was eager to try them out. They are BIG. I know it says 36 inches in the description, but take a moment to actually think about that in perspective. I've included a picture my sidekick holding the balloon to help visualize the size.

title: Excellent quality Irish Moss in Bulk!
text: This is at least my 7th or 8th pack ordered from this brand. I have been using Irish-Moss on a daily for over a year now, and can vouch that this product is very good and consistent in quality, with minimal smell and sand to wash off. Reviews that say it smells bad, must just not know how to process Irish moss properly for culinary use. It takes about 24 hrs total (with soak) for it to be ready. And once you do all the steps, like washing off the sand, then washing with a little baking soda, then soak for 30min, then drain and soak again for 30 min, then drain and soak in a large mason jar in refrigerator for 24hrs, this product has absolutely no smell, has expanded to its full size, and is very light in color. After this process, there is no smell, and it’s ready to be turned into gel or stored as is, in a glass jar in the refrigerator. I drain the water and save it for my mineral baths or face masks, because it’s pure collagen. Moss water works topically similar to Aloe Vera imo!
