title: High-priced Gadgetry that Syncs with Fitbit App
text:
The scale is not cheap. But it serves its purpose. If you're just looking to measure your weight, any $20 scale will do. Make it $35 if you want to measure body fat too. Then make it $130 if you want it to have WiFi and work with your Fitbit. But if you are already in the Fitbit ecosystem (I, personally, own a Flex and love it), and you have the extra money to spend, this scale is a good choice because it syncs flawlessly with the app on your phone, graphing your weight over time (surprisingly boring graph for people who are not trying to cut or gain weight), and your lean vs fat over time. And you can see it at a glance next to your steps, calories burned, active minutes, etc.

Setup was a breeze. The design of the white scale also fits in well with most bathrooms. (Highly suggest the white scale over the black scale for most people.) And the screen is backlit so it works well in the early morning and at night when you may be too lazy to turn on the lights.

It does work with multiple family members, and works best if your family members have weights spread at least 10 pounds apart because the scale distinguishes individuals by weight and body fat percentage (as opposed to being fully sentient). New users will be registered as guests on their first weigh-in. Then, just program each person into the scale via the Fitbit.com site, and the scale will automatically recognize them in the future. If two users have similar weights, they'll need to manually tap the scale with their foot after each weighing to cycle through the initials of who the scale thinks might have just weighed themselves.

My biggest gripes are (1) the price, and (2) that the scale's body fat measurement may not be the most accurate. Of course, no body fat scale on the market today works particularly well. But when your body fat typically only moves by 1-2%, and the scale might have an error range of 1-2%, the feature obviously will not be particularly helpful. But again, while its expensive, I paid the money for one, and don't regret it.

text:
I received this from Smiley360 to try for free. I have been using colgate white for a couple years and probably never would have tried this if not offered to test it out.

I felt like my teeth weren't getting cleaned.
I have been using this for 1 week now and following the instructions, it lathers better with the right amount. The taste is still very mild, I wish there was more minty-ness. However, I have noticed a great deal of improvement. I have VERY sensitive gums and use an electric toothbrush that more times out of not makes them sore or even bleed a little. My front teeth also hurt a bit from time to time when I drink sodas or have sweet things, I have noticed an improvement on that as well. Out of this whole week I have not had either of those problems at all! I didnt change any of my habits except for using this paste. I dont feel it has whitened my teeth any within the week, but i really didnt expect to see that by using just one tube of this stuff. Even though I received this for free all of my opinions are 100 percent my own!

title: Nice and quick - straightens well - would recommend
text:
I was both hopeful and skeptical about this brush. I've used this for the last couple of days and am pretty impressed. I have naturally curly hair, but it's not kinky. It does have a fair amount of frizz without products, etc. I use a pretty high end straightener that takes about 15 minutes to straighten straighten/curl my hair. I've included a naturally curly pic and a just after the first time I used this straightening brush pic.

I took another reviews suggestion and pushed both the up and down buttons to turn the temp to Fahrenheit from Celsius. I heats up to the full 450 degrees in the time it takes to brush my teeth. The first time I used it it took 6 minutes from start to finish and I was pretty happy with the results, though I realized later that I didn't do a great job on the middle back of my head - it was still wavy. I think this is a technique issue.

Overall, it gets my hair nice and straight, with no frizz. Interestingly it does require a touch up the next day - where my iron does not. Using the glove it is pretty easy to get a nice under curl at the end to provide a more polished look. I love how fast it is and it isn't a temptation to my 2 year old, who is obsessed with my straightening iron for some reason lol. I would definitely recommend to a friend, but I will also keep my iron for when I want to add curls. For the price this is a good tool.

title: Life Saver!
text: I ordered the iTalk Reminder Assistant(silver with amber numbers not blue) for my uncle who is Schizophrenic and takes medications six times a day! He Has extreme time confusion and depends on caregivers to give him his medications. Not only has it helped his caregivers keep the medications straight and on time, it has made him safer. We have had problems in the past with people taking advantage of my uncle by being late or failing to show at all. In the past he would remain unsupervised and would not get his medicine until we were able to check up on him. Now if the clock plays a recording of my voice and no one shows up, he knows to contact us immediately. We are also able to remind everyone of important safety information or doctors appointments. My uncle loves it too! He gets a chuckle out of it every time we talk back to it. It has been set off a few times by the television or a conversation but it merely asks "May I Help You?" in a pleasant female voice and then says "Goodbye" when you do not answer. It is easy to set both manually and verbally. I would recommend this product 100% to anyone with memory issues such as mental illness, Alzheimer's, Dementia, or even seniors who want to remain independent in their own home. If you are able to speak and can remember to say "Reminder Off" you can work this clock. Amazing!

text: This alarm clock has everything you want in a Sunrise alarm clock. When it works, I wake up more rested and energized. The problem is that it only works about 80% of the time. For some reason, sometimes even if I haven't changed a setting or touched it other than to push the button to turn on and off the alarm, it simply won't go off at all.... no light, no alarm, no nothing. Other times the light will come on (which does sometimes gently wake me up) but then when the alarm is supposed to go off the light suddenly turns off and the alarm doesn't sound. These are glitches that make me wary of using this as my only alarm and so I still have my old clock radio set for 10 minutes later just in case. Kind of annoying having two alarm clocks when one should be enough. Another annoying thing that isn't a glitch is that the snooze (a sensor on the side that you wave your hand in front of) immediately turns off the light. I wish you could set the snooze so that the light stayed on because it won't come on again. Also, the snooze doesn't always work. I have mine set for 10 minutes. After 10 minutes I can hear a little "click" that I assume means the alarm would like to sound but it doesn't, instead the alarm will finally go off after an additional 10 minutes. Frustrating. The technology behind this clock is great. I love when it works and I wake up to a "sun-lit" bedroom to the sound of birds gently chirping but I just don't trust the thing. I'm going to spend a little more money and get one that works 100% of the time.

title: Works, but takes practice.  Can compare to Remee.

There are a lot of customization settings so it takes some practice to get the lights just correct without waking you up. Not nearly as comfortable to wear compared to Remee. The Remee I feel lights up at bad times and is more disturbing to your sleep. However, I would recommend to anyone that wants to try either - download a REM tracking app for your phone. These programs are about a dollar and can give rough estimates on when you are in REM. Then you can try to set the mask accordingly - setting the delay correct. This mask does not need interval programing because it tracks you REM, but it does need delay and you need to adjust the sensitivity and brightness. I got it to work once, but not since. title: Beware the return policy
text:
Update 9/12/22: Return was delivered by UPS 8/22/22. It's now 9/12/22 and I have yet to receive my refund. These people are SCAMMERS.

I purchased the Smart Nora thru their website and not Amazon. I found that its DSP algorithm for determining snoring vs other ambient sounds in the room just doesn't work, and the pump would kick in when I turned in bed, thereby fully waking me up. I also found that the lift hurt my neck and the noises the pillow made when deflating were loud to my ears. I use a separate app to monitor snoring (an app whose DSP for snoring DOES actually work) and this did nothing to improve my score.

The biggest issue is the return procedure. You are given a link to a questionnaire to fill out, which is not disclosed in their return policy. The questionnaire seems more like a way for them to determine how they might be able to convince you to keep the item rather than just gathering data to improve the product. There was also a stated delay of 1-2 days to get the return shipping label. This is also not stated anywhere in their return policy. Check your state's laws on return policies to see if this process violates it. Seems like a shady company selling a half-baked air pump that is triggered by any sound in a room to me. One of the worst, most useless products I have ever purchased.

title: Amazing bars
text:
The ingredient list is refreshingly short, contains nothing fake or artificial, and you can taste that all the ingredients that went into it were fresh and raw.

Fair warning, much like giving up sodas for the first time, you might not find these very sweet if you're used to all the other "health" bars on the market that are loaded with sugar or sugar alternatives. After eating these for a little while, however, you will soon start to appreciate how rich and full the flavor really is when your taste buds have recovered and are no longer ruined by the garbage sweetened bars out there.

Sure, the shelf-life on these is very short (fresh for a week, refrigerated for a month, frozen for a year), so you should enjoy them now. After the apocalypse you can share all those other artificially-loaded, sugar-laden bars with the cockroaches. In the meantime, feed yourself well and truly with these and make it more likely you'll survive the apocalypse.

I know many folks will balk at the high price of these bars. Bear in mind that these are meal-replacement bars, not simply protein supplements or snacks like most bars on the market. You'd likely pay $6 or $10 or so for a lunch, and these are less than that. If you have a Whole Foods near you, you can get them there for less, and pay no shipping.

text:
So far is doing it's job flawlessly, aside from orerator error. There is a learning curve, but I was able to make good smoking cigarrettes well within a hour. Probably even faster I were using factory processed tobacco, because of the uniform shred, and cosistency. I am hand shredding natural whole leaf tobacco, which offers a whole other curve in itself. As I learn the tricks my smokes get better, and better. I'm sick thinking about the money I've wasted through the last 20 years. Remember these things when using this machine your first time. Don't over pack, it should be almost effortless to swing the arn over for injection. You will get the feel quickly. If you don't feel confident check out YouTube, there are many videos demonstrating this item, and many other similar injection machines. The other major selling point for me on this item is that almost every part is available for replacement, and extremely affordable to buy the spare parts....around $1.00-3.00. Apears to be very simple to repair as well, I don't think you would need to be a rocket scientist.... Anyway now making smokes for pennys, literally.... Happy!!

6-3-13 Still going strong. Couldnt even tell you how many smokes I've made with this thing thus far, lots, and lots.
A few things I have learned. 1- if the tobacco you are using is overly moist, thing will be difficult. Having the right moisture content is really key to making perfect smokes. After a couple weeks I can tell just by touching the tobacco. A tip if its to wet, I put on a tray into my toaster oven 30 seconds at a time. Too dry I put a few drops of water in the container I use and seal it up for a while.... you get the hang of it quick. 2- don't over pack the chamber, even if it doesn't jamb the mechanism, your smoke will not draw well....

Fair trade should be fair to both sides. This transaction wasn't.

title: Jack of all trades....master of none
text:
This is primarily a full, rotor, circular head shaver and the grip and hold of the base unit bears that out making it conducive to shaving your head. In that aspect it does an ok job. It does hit the areas and it actually performs adequately.

The battery life is good. Based on what you're doing (IE shaving head which takes longer than trimming nose hairs, etc...) you will get 15-20 uses out of it before needing a recharge. I like these new devices that give you a readout of how much life is left versus older models that just had a green light go red blinking. It will allow you to optimize battery life and more importantly know how much you have left.

The other attachments are interchangeable and allow you to trim your beard to varying lengths or even the hair on your head. It also has the aforementioned nose trimmer to tame your nose hairs. It even comes with a lathering attachment to apply shaving foam and gels before switching over to shave.

It is easy to clean and use but I found the nose trimmer to be subpar versus other dedicated models. The head shaving attachment requires multiple passes to hit every area and to shave it down. If you're looking for a clean look, you can get the job done with a disposable razor in a fraction of the time.

The lathering attachment does work, but I find it easier and quicker to just apply by hand.

My dedicated set of facial trimmers does a much better job than the ones included here.

Lastly, while the ergonomics of the base unit works best for trimming your noggin, it gets awkward and cumbersome when trying to use it for your nose and face trimming.

Does it work? Yes, and I could see if you have limited space traveling how this unit would be great to take with you as you will get a "good enough" job taking care of most of your grooming needs without having to take multiple devices with you but if you're looking for a better job at each you would be better served making more space in your luggage and taking along dedicated devices if needed.

I will use it to shave down my head when I get too lazy and the hair gets too long for a straight razor and I'll use it to get it to a length I can then shave with a straight razor. For everything else, I'll stick with my dedicated grooming devices as they do a better job.

3/5

The head strap is excellent. it is VERY wide on the sides so the entire mask is evenly pulled taut. the Velcro connector is wide, even and has a bit of padding on the inside so you don't feel the roughness. The strap too is wide and comfortable.

The description says, "heavy light blocking," and they aren't kidding around. I found myself just laying there going, "wow....." the darkness is that perfect.

You simply twist off the top and fill it with water, pull down the straw, and attach the water basin (aka the lid). The irrigating head folds up and you turn it on. It has two levels of intensity. I sprayed the inside of the large bay window on the front of my house. I plan on putting some cute window clings inside the rectangle that I applied to the window.

The further you stand back, the larger the spray area, the less likely it is to run. Also, the overspray area is quite large. My desired area ended up being about 4 inches wide. The overspray probably covered another 6 inches above it and below it. So, you’re probably better off using a piece of cardboard to prevent it from going where you don’t want it to go, instead of using a piece of tape. The tape probably won’t be wide enough to protect areas that you don’t want the product on.

Application is relatively fast and easy. Try not to go overboard, because the more you put on, the more you have to takeoff. There is a smell, but since I was in a large room, it wasn’t overwhelming.

title: It has a battery, and doesn’t always need to be plugged into work.
text:
[[VIDEOID:4db8e602e90dfe20b6133c1562962d3f]] Update- September 30, 2022: I contacted the company through Amazon, they have sent me a replacement unit. It works wonderfully. I have updated my review from four stars to five stars. I am very pleased with the customer service that I received from the company. This really is a great massager, and now the whole family uses it.

Update- September 16, 2022: So, last night I came in the room to find my husband using this massager. He wanted to know why it shut off, I had asked him how long he had been using it, and he said 15 minutes or so. I let him know it had an auto shut off feature and that it must be working. He then asked me how long the battery would last. I was confused, I told him it had to be plugged into the wall. He said, “No it doesn’t. Look, I’m using it without it plugged in.” I do vaguely now remember that there was a battery sticker on the box that it arrived in. Now I know why. I have moved this up another star, because it is even more portable than I originally thought. The instruction manual does not mention this feature, neither does the product listing.

Original Review:
I placed it in a recliner chair next to my hip, and it feels so much better. I have set it on the floor and put my feet on it, and I do like the motion. I do not like any of the tools that vibrate, so I appreciate that this does not have a vibration mode.

It can be used with and without heat.
You can easily change direction by pushing the direction button.
The instruction says it has automatic shut off after 15 minutes. (I do not know if that is correct, because I am usually done with it after 10 minutes.)
It can be used at home or work.
It can be plugged into any 12 V plug, including a vehicle or a camper unit.
It is fairly quiet.
The last page in the instruction manual says that it has a one year limited warranty.

Cons:
The instruction manual is different from the actual function of the unit when looking at the operating instructions section. It does not actually switch directions, unless you push the button.
The left side of my unit, the heat was having an issue, it does not have any contact information on the instruction manual for warranty purposes, so I will need to go through Amazon.

title: Warm, Funny, French, Family, Comedy.
text:
This is a cracking little French comedy made in 2009. It stars Maxim Godart as the little Nicolas and he is a talent to watch out for and has already made another two films. In this he leads what he knows is a charmed life, loving his parents, his home and his school mates – well all except the Teacher’s pet ‘cockroach’ grass one with glasses.

Then one of their class mates has a new arrival – a baby brother and he relays that life is now the pits for him, worse still he stops coming to school and no one knows why. Then Nicolas overhears his parents talking of a visit and they say he must be gotten out of the way. He now knows that not only will he be getting a baby brother but that they are going to dump him; possibly in the woods as the urban myths have it.

So he sets out on a charm offensive and all his school chums are going to help – badly that is. As his demise gets closer their plans become ever more urgent and funny.

This is set in the sixties and just oozes style and charm in equal dollops. The clothes the cars the primary colours and lack of office technology and casual sexism are all just brilliant, well maybe not the sexism. The acting is superb with a cast of kids that are all brilliant, entertaining and funny in all the right places. This is laugh out loud at times too and had me wanting more. Sandrine Kiberlain as their teacher deserves special mention as she is really good and well rounded as always. She is also in the ruddy excellent ‘The Women on the sixth floor’.

This is also one for the whole family as kids will definitely get it too. This tells the story and the reasons they do things all from a child’s perspective and the collective naivety that can come from kid group decicions, which is just great. So for a refreshing warm, family comedy in France based sixties, you need look no further - really warmly recommended.

Flashlight is of decent quality, actually better than I anticipated, but the battery was used, not new. And it would not take a charge - battery was toast. Even further, the cable that's supposed to charge the flashlight didn't work at all. No current would travel through the line.

After I used my own battery and my own charging cable, the light worked. Actually works ok for the money spent. But, the most notable issue is in the button to activate the light. You have to hold the button down for a few seconds to turn it on and off. Why it would be designed in such a manner is beyond my ability to comprehend. You can't turn it on and off quickly. Nor can you switch between brightness levels without holding the button down for several seconds. It's just odd engineering.

If it came with a working battery and a working cable, I would rate it higher. I'm not expecting them to respond to my inquiry, but I'll update this review if they do.

Poor quality control makes this a 1 star.

title: Magic on sticky greasy pans but the nuclear option
text:
I walked into my local restaurant supply store and asked for the strongest pan cleaner they owned. I was tired of the old elbow grease method with soap, degreaser, steel wool, and magic erasers. I'll admit I was still skeptical. So skeptical I didn't even take a before photo of this absolutely wrecked sheet pan on the awful front side. Gave it a good coating and left it for 15 minutes. Came back and rinsed it under water - chunks started coming off with just that much and a quick swipe with steel wool and it was 100% gone. Incredible. This was baked on polymerized grease that all the scrubbing wouldn't take off and it just wiped clean. When I flipped to the back I cleaned half and took a photo just to show the difference on the bottom cleaned half and top uncleaned one. Also unlike hand scrubbing with steel wool since it comes clean in just one wipe and you don't even get scrub marks.

Now to note this stuff is NASTY. If it can take grease like that imagine how bad it is for you when oven cleaner isn't even that fast. I did this in my sink wearing gloves, goggles, and a half respirator. The can warns you to be extra sure you ONLY get this on metal as it can utterly ruin nonstick coatings, paint, plastic, countertops, and will burn your skin on contact. I repeat do not mess around with this stuff but absolutely use it if you take the right precautions and want factory clean pans.

title: Absolutely do not buy this and avoid these pills like the plague.
text:
I am writing this review for both myself and on a good friend of mine’s behalf. I strongly advise that anybody reading this does not ingest these pills. How this product has an overall rating of four stars is something I cannot even begin to fathom. The amount of caffeine (205mg) along with an additional 25mg of ephedrine in a single pill is not only overstimulating, but makes me feel incredibly uncomfortable overall. It should be known that I am very experienced with high doses of many different types of stimulants. Just one pill from this bottle had my heart beating out of my chest, breaking out in cold sweats profusely, and had my anxiety levels through the roof. I honestly thought I was going to pass out, and it lasted for hours.

As for when my friend one, it was even worse. While she does not have nearly as much experience with stimulants as me (which I would assume the vast majority of buyers do not either), not only did she experience all of the aforementioned symptoms I did, but she also called me up more than four hours after she took one pill. She was breaking down and in tears. When I asked her why she was crying, all she could respond to me repeatedly was: “everything hurts, I’m so nauseous but I can’t throw up, I’ve been in bed all day, and I can’t even walk; everything just hurts way too much! I’m in so much pain”.

I can’t help but wonder if what’s in these pills is even ephedrine, or honestly, even caffeine for that matter! I take 200mg caffeine pills every single day and bought this to try a different brand, and despite saying on the label that this bottle contains about the same amount, it did not even come close to making me nor her feel the way caffeine usually makes us. Either that, or the combination of ephedrine and caffeine is not befitting.

In summary, coming from someone who is well-experienced with high doses of various types of stimulants, ingesting one pill from this bottle will make you feel like you poisoned yourself, and I’m not exaggerating. Do not buy these pills. Nobody deserves to suffer the way my friend and I did. Concluded.

text:
EDIT TO UPDATE:
I have cut these in 4ths and tried taking a smaller amount; the pills are scored so that generally indicates you can do so safely. I also drank a full bottle of water and took them with a meal. None of this made much difference. Taking my clonazepam that I'm prescribed at the same time kind of takes the edge off--KIND OF.
My boyfriend also took a 4th, and he weighs more than me, drank a whole bottle of water, and ate a lot more too...he got really sick and threw up.
MY ADVICE IS TO AVOID THESE PILLS AND ANYTHING ELSE THAT CONTAINS YOHIMBE.
_____________________________
Oh man, I wish I had read "yohimbe" before buying. I will try these again after eating a lot more, but I had a light breakfast and now I'm feeling like I wanna jump out of my skin. Came to write a review and saw "yohimbe." I've felt really bad from pills that contain this in the past. Just be careful if you're sensitive at all to stimulants bc that's the one that's given me trouble.
And don't under any circumstances do what younger me did...I used to exceed the recommended dose bc I had worked up quite a tolerance to caffeine and stimulants. I figured that would work the same with all diet or energy pills until I came across one with yohimbe and did that. Seriously don't. I got so sick. I don't do that anymore & haven't for years, but in case anyone else ignores labels and common sense please don't try it with anything that contains that.

By this point, I expect nothing less but fabulous from Goodness, Truth, & Happiness (products)… And as usual, Michelle delivers. The stones received are beautiful and prove that size isn't everything. :-) Very energetic, very willing to work with you. GTH is now my "go to" for crystals on Amazon. Because though not inexpensive, you do receive quality, and to me, for what I need the crystals for, that's more important.

It really depends on what you want to do with the specimens. If for just display, they're gorgeous, and will absolutely look fabulous in your living space. If to utilize, the crystals Michelle chooses for you have tremendous energy. I really don't feel you can go wrong with either.

And as I've said in other reviews for GTH crystals… I did find other, cheaper crystals here on Amazon that I also purchased (labradorite) and wound up spending a lot of time charging them because not only were they dull to look at, their energy was too. In absolute contrast to the bright, flashy, and lively labradorite I received from GTH. As such, I find myself reaching for that one more so than the others.

The same can be said for all of the stones I've received from GTH.
One tip: You get a lot of sand. I only used about half of it for the crystal placement. The rest I stored for future use...

title: OK for the price
text: I had a bad experience with a digital scale for which I had paid ~$50 and that broke down just after a couple of months and I was not ready to spend that much money for another digital one. After reading the reviews for this one and looking at the price (main factor), I went with this. First off, I agree with some other reviewers that it does not give an accurate result and that after using it for few days the pointer goes a little off from the "0" marker. But neither one is a deal breaker. It's really easy to set the pointer back to 0 marker and once you know how much off the scale is showing (which is always a constant), you can always add (or subtract, whichever the case is) that number from the value the scale is showing, you can get your accurate weight. Overall, this is an OK product.

title: Finally an accurate scale!
text: I bought this because I wanted a good basic scale without a fat measurer, memory, etc. and couldn't find the Tanita brand locally, so bought from Amazon. Shipping was speedy and I'm very satisfied. My old scale was all over the place--different weights when stepping on and off within seconds, and several pounds lighter than when I weighed at Weight Watchers. This scale is the same no matter how many times you step on it. I'm actually trusting it the first time and not having to step on multiple times each morning. Also, it's been dead on accurate with the Weight Watchers scale the last three weeks; not even .2 difference but the exact same weight at home and at the center! No more anxiety about whether I'll be within my 2 pound window for lifetime membership! My only complaint is that its footprint is very large, so I had to move it to a more prominent place in the bathroom rather than the small space between the toilet and tub. It also cannot be read in the dark as the display is black on gray not bright red like my old scale. But accuracy is fantastic, and that's what you buy a scale for anyway!

title: Hack for leftover pieces
text:
First off, I love this deodorant! I have been using it for over 2 years and now that I found a solution to my only complaint, I love it even more.
When the bar gets towards the end it becomes very hard to hold. I saved up all of these little pieces because I didn't want to waste them. I didn't know exactly what to do with them though. I'd read that some people had melted theirs but wasn't sure how and was afraid of the mess.
Then I had the idea to put the pieces in one of my silicone cupcake liners. I put the liner on top of a plate, and put the whole thing in the microwave (the oven on a low heat would probably work too). 30 seconds was more than enough to melt all of the pieces together. After an hour in the fridge I had a new bar! It was super easy and had no mess. I'm glad that all my pieces will get used now, zero waste!

text: At first I didn't feel much (if any) difference or improvement with my weight lifting, but I did a little research online and figured out that my 1 scoop a day wasn't nearly enough to feel the benefits of creatine. I preloaded with 4 scoops a day for a week, then dropped to 3 scoops as I read conflicting recommendations and didn't want to use more than I needed. After 5 weeks of use (only 2 weeks have been the 15-20 grams a day) I have finally broken my bench press plateau by 10 lbs, and a few other minor weight lifting numbers have increased as well. Nothing to write home about, but considering I've been stuck for 5 months at my max bench press, it was a big deal to me. I have no idea if I'll see more gains from it, but I haven't changed anything else and suddenly my strength is increasing, so I'm hopeful.

title: It's okay....but nothing to write home about
text:
I received this product at a discounted rate in exchange for my honest review.

I started using this supplement exactly 2 weeks ago, and while it hasn't shown to have any noticeable ill effects on me, I haven't really seen any noticeable gains or benefits while taking it. I still workout every other day for 60-120 minutes and I try to cycle on the exercise bike at least a few of the "off" days, and I'm not seeing any better results than I was before I started taking this supplement. I can say that I have been able to increase the weight on a few of my lifts, but I've been training a little different over the past week (shock them muscles!), so that factor alone could be the reason for my minor lifting gains. My dimensions haven't changed drastically and I appear to be making the same (slow/steady) gains in performance and size that I've been making over the past 12 months by relying solely on a decent diet and consistent workouts. No miracle pill here and luckily, I didn't have all that high of expectations in the first place.

title: DO NOT PURCHASE
text:
Please head the warning of bad reviews. I know it looks like a good deal (as did I) but these vacuums have hundreds of issues!

First off, the Bluetooth DOES NOT WORK. It will work at first, but you will find yourself having to fiddle around, closing the app, etc.

Second, the battery does not maintain itself. It other words it's fine as long as you use it regularly, but if it dies and you perhaps leave it for a month without charging. It will not work, Roombas will automatically cut off power, this one has a switch on the bottom that you have to turn off if you intend to leave it for a month.

Third, NOT WELL PROGRAMMED. This vacuuming aspect is fine, I will say it does vacuum much better than upright, but you have to make sure your home is compatible with this robot. While Roombas might be picky with black rugs, this robot will get stuck in certain chairs, it will not detect some wall trim and may get stuck, it will not like rugs, it cannot go over ANY floor dividers, the list goes on.

THE ONLY REASON YOU SHOULD PURCHASE IS IF YOUR HOUSE HAS A PERFECTLY FLAT FLOOR AND YOU ARE ABLE TO HANDLE TAKING IT APART FOR MAINTENANCE. I've replaced the battery twice, which you can't just buy you have to rebuild it. I've also had to take it apart to clean the sensors twice in the past two years.

ROOMBA IS A MUCH BETTER INVESTMENT, EVEN THE CHEAPEST ROOMBA.

title: WARNING !!!  VITAMINS FOR SUCKERS !!!  WARNING !!!
text:
A friend who knows I compete in Triathlons asked me if he should buy this stuff called Beyond Tangy Tangerine being "Promoted" to increase energy and lose weight. I had never heard of it so we went to the company's web site to check it out.

First thing I noticed was that this stuff was "REEE---HEALY EXPENSIVE"!!!!

I pulled a bottle of generic multi vitamins out of my cupboard to compare ingredients and cost.

My generic multi vitamin & mineral supp cost approx. 4 cents a serving.
Beyond Tangy Tangarine approx. cost a WHOPPING $2.50 a serving for a 100lb person!!!!!
WTF !!! This couldn't be true so we checked our math and our numbers were correct.

HOLY CRAP!!! These vitamins were like SIX THOUSAND PERCENT more expensive!!!

After more research it turns out that Beyond Expensive ... I mean ... Beyond Tangy Tangerine is part of some kind of selling plan where the sales people can win "Dream Cars and Vacations" for conning lots of people into buying the stuff. This looks to be a Hard Core Sales Business complete with Celebrity Endorsers pushing this stuff on the trusting public.

My buddy decided against taking on another monthly car payment by buying this stuff and was more than a little embarrassed he was almost suckered by a cheezy sales pitch based on deception.

If you have a bottle of Multi Vitamins laying around you can go to the company's website and compare the Supplement Facts in less than 5 minutes for FREE. Below is the Comparison we did between the two Fact Sheets.

Supplement Facts Comparison of Beyond Expensive Tangy Tangerine to my bottle of generic Multi vitamin

---------------------------------------Approx. cost per serving-----------Vitamins & Minerals listed
Beyond Tangy Tangarine----------$2.50---------------------------------21
COSTCO generic daily multi-------$0.04 (yes 4 cents)----------------24

As for effortlessly losing weight and increasing energy by just chuggin the stuff, I visited CONSUMER REPORTS website and they had this to say about vitamin supplements:

title: Unreliable and Inaccurate
text:
Like so many others, I started off the new year with a resolution to lose some extra pounds and improve my level of fitness. Determined that I would actually follow through this year, I looked for ways of making the process more interesting and more fun. I enjoy technology, so I added some new apps to my phone, shopped for gadgets that would help to measure my progress, and looked for other ways to maintain motivation.

I already had a very good (and accurate) beam scale, just like the ones that you used to see in every doctor's office, but the idea of wirelessly recording and tracking my weight loss, especially since I was already a user of a Fitbit One, was very appealing. Anyway, I ordered the Aria Smart Scale, and a couple of days later, Amazon delivered it.

Setup was very simple with my iPad, and within a few minutes of opening the box, I was up and running. Very cool -- I thought I was all set. I moved the old beam scale down to the basement where I have a couple of pieces of exercise equipment, and installed the Aria scale in its place in the master bathroom.

Stepping onto the Aria, I got a reading that was about a half a pound less than my previous day's weight on the old scale, so I thought GREAT, I'm making progress, and the Aria seems to know what its doing. The next day, back onto the Aria, and damn, how could I have gained two pounds overnight? I stepped on again, and now I was only 0.4 pounds over the previous day's weight. Further attempts provided even more disparate results. What am I doing wrong?

I went to the Fitbit website to check for some tips on ways to improve accuracy, read the FAQ's, and noted that the scale is supposed to be accurate within +/- 2.0 pounds, which in my estimation, isn't very helpful when you're trying to lose weight. Nevertheless, I followed all the website suggestions -- none of which improved the accuracy of the scale. (NB: I never pay any attention to the body fat reading -- which seems to vary widely, each time you step onto the scale)

Today, I weighed myself 5 times in the space of an hour. I didn't eat or drink anything between weigh-ins, I wasn't engaged in any strenuous activity -- and I ended up with a different reading each time that I stepped on to the Aria scale. While this might be acceptable if you simply want a general indication of your weight -- when you're watching every calorie you put in your mouth, when you're exercising regularly and working hard to reach a goal -- a half pound one way or the other is serious business. It's very discouraging when one day your scale says you're making progress, then the next day, slaps you down by recording a weight that you thought you'd left behind 3 or 4 days earlier. I don't think that it's unreasonable to expect a scale to be consistent!

Needless to say, the Aria and my old (and accurate) beam scale will be swapping places.

If you're on a weight loss regimen -- I would NOT recommend the Aria Smart scale!

[[VIDEOID:7299c9b19f2ae30e8f9681317a8619f]]I have curly hair.....some days it is a blessing- think cute bouncy curls....others its a trial that needs to be tamed. Sometimes I just want a diffenet hairstyle that is completely different from the normal for me. My hair is very thick and curly. Most days it goes up in a bun or ponytail. I wanted this straightener to try a new look. I will say that I was impressed. The wand itself seems to be pretty standard in shape and looks. As I was using it, or my daughter for the parts I could not reach, when it is held naturally like a brush in your hand, your fingers naturally land on the buttons to increase or decrease the temperature. Whenever we used it, we had to be careful on hand placement because we kept switching the temp. The window that shows what temp the straightener is at is on the back of the brush with a lighted window. I liked that it heated up pretty fast- less than 5 minutes. From use, it goes up to 220 degrees celsius. That seems to be the high limit for coarse thick hair. Lower settings are called for when dealing with fine or thin hair. The "bristles" look like a normal brush bristles in color, but are thick. Be careful- the tips tend to get warm/hot and can startle you if they are pressed too close to the scalp or neck. Not burn you, just gives a gentle reminder its hot! The results are very good, even if it is only you doing your hair. Obviously results are better if you help. My hair was not frizzy and the straightness held for several hours, actually closer to 24 hours for me- going to bed ruined it. I would definitely recommend to friends.

I received this item at a discount to evaluate it and provide a honest review based on my experience. Keep in my mind that my experience is uniquely my own, but I endeavor to provide factual information regarding usage to you.

title: Very sturdy and well designed
text: I bought this tray for a friend after his knee replacement surgery, on the recommendation of his OT. It was the perfect solution to a basic problem, i.e., if you need to use a walker around the house, you will not have the ability to carry anything. You can't get from the kitchen to the dining table with a plate of food or a cup of coffee. You can't carry a book across the room from the shelf to the couch. This tray is very sturdy and easy to install and it folds down out of the way when you don't need it. This feature is great because with a walker tray in place you can't see where you need put your feet. Outside of the house, we just folded the tray down out of the way and he had a clear view of the sidewalk or the door threshold or whatever. The Yunga tray has a good-sized, deep cup holder for the aforementioned cup of coffee and the sturdy washable liner makes clean up easy for the inevitable spills or drips. I would highly recommend the Yunga Tart Flippin Tray. Be sure to measure your walker to make sure it will fit. I think most modern, hospital-issued walkers are consistently sized but older models or specialty walkers may not be.

If you are only interested in something inexpensive for ballpark estimates, then this is for you.

title: Take time to adjust to cushion, it's so worthwhile!
text:
Give your body time to adjust to this different type of support. You may sit differently than with other cushions/chairs, but that difference could end up feeling great. It does for me!

The straighter I sat, putting more pressure on my backside/upper thighs, the better I felt. On previous chairs/that pressure would have been uncomfortable. I actually now walk straighter/taller, because am so stretched out while sitting.

Tried Purple's Double cushion because it's larger (since no rounded edges, it provides a few more inches width), but it wasn't as comfortable. The Ultimate was too hard, and I didn't like the indentation. It lowered my hips and felt like it reduced the support in that area.

Wish the Royal with its rounded edges was a little wider. But it's still the best support I've found.

title: Setup was terrible
text:
This device and the software that accompanied it was clearly not tested well. There are stupid mistakes that a third grader could have tested for. Things like having an apostrophe in the name of the scale will cause the setup application to not allow you to continue but will not tell you why. Naming my scale "Geordie's" didn't seem like all that bizarre a thing to do...

Once I got that working it took me about 10 attempts to get it to start working with my Wi-Fi. My Wi-Fi setup couldn't be simpler. It is an Apple Airport with no security enabled whatsoever (I live out in the country). The scale was within 4 or 5 feet of the access point the whole time. Eventually I was able to get it to sort of work where at least it was showing up on the website and my intials showed up on the scale when I weighed in. None of it actually got uploaded though. This morning I removed the batteries in an attempt to set it up again. When it started up it asked if I still wanted to use the wireless network I had set and when I said yes suddenly it seemed to be able to upload my data. We'll see if it continues to work.

Accuracy is variable by a pound or two which makes the fact that it measures in tenths of a pound pretty stupid. Same thing for body fat percentage.

After I have had a chance to use it for a few weeks maybe I'll update my review.

The glass that it's made from is thick and after 3 months of wear and being thrown around is still in one piece no cracks.
I personally have had zero trouble with the floss falling through. pulling a little extra out and wrapping it around the slicer is easy and effective.

The floss itself is wonderful. Strong, clean doesn't get flaky and stringy as you use it.
and the amount of floss you get at one time is wonderful. Lasts for such a long long time even for the most committed flosser. I do wish that they did have a somewhat thinner option for people with crowded teeth or children.
So if you are looking for an easy, ethical, pain free way to cut back on your plastic use this is a great place to start.
Highly recommend

-You will use it daily. We were a little worried about the novelty factor for such a big purchase. LOVE IT!

Cons:

-Massage can be intense on your lower back. My wife and I don't carry much extra weight. We found adding a towel in the lumbar area works like a charm. Once you've used it a while, you realize it might have been too hard because you were too tense. I do agree with some of the other reviewers that the first sitting was both pain and pleasure. -The strength of the massage is not evenly distributed. Feet, back, and lower shoulders are all similar intensity. Head, neck, and upper shoulders are a little weak for my taste.

As many have suggested, it's not light or easy to move. However, it's packed well. With two people it was moved up two flights of stairs without much issue. As a note, it's 28" wide. If you don't have AT LEAST a 30" door, this guy isn't coming in. Need at least 36" turn radius on all sides for a staircase. Happy that I measured ahead of time. At the end of the day, you get a massage after moving it, so it's not all bad.

text: I've been working with wood all of my life and have tried many products looking for the best finish that brings out the character of the wood and that lasts a reasonable amount of time.  Up until now Watco oil has been my preference.  In my opinion it really does justice to the wood however it gives off a strong unpleasnt odor until it is dry and can even auto ignite if left on wadded up rags.  Tung oil is also a good finish and is a natural oil from seeds of the tung tree.  I recently bought a pint of Skidmore's to try it out.  When I opened the can I immediately liked the odor and the feel of it.  It seems much more natural than Watco.  I believe they both use tung or linseed oil which both go well with wood but Skidmore's uses beeswax instead of VOCs like the varnish in Watco oil.  So far I have only used Skidmore's on a small picture frame but am really pleased with the result and it was a pleasure instead of a nuisance to work with.  If I continue to get results like this I will definitely use it on the interior of the house we are building and other future projects.  So far no negatives only positives.

title: It’s a Thick Seat Pad
text:
After a few years of sitting on my chair every day, its built-in padding is getting a little worn. I’ve been musing either replacing the chair or getting a padded seat cover for a while. I saw many ads for the Purple pads, and decided on the Ultimate because of the size of my chair’s seat. That it’s quite thick also let me think it might elevate me a little, as I’m tall and even all the way up, and with “higher than normal” replacement wheels, I find the seat just a little lower than I’d like.

It comes in a display package, requiring the simple installation of stuffing the rubber pad in a cloth sleeve. Then placing the pad on the seat allows it to be used immediately. As expected, it’s a bit taller and softer than sitting in the chair without the pad. I even had to lower my seat from its top setting to be a little more comfortable.

It was immediately more comfortable than without. It’s a different feel than the solid foam padding of the chair, especially since that’s been so compressed. It is definately more comfortable, and I found I sat a little more upright than before.

Two tiny knocks, and both are more about my chair than this pad.

The first is that there’s nothing securing the pad within its cloth sleeve. The seat on my chair tips ever so slightly forward (or it can be adjusted to tip much more forward), so sitting on it and shuffling normally sometimes causes the pad to slide inside the sleeve. The sleeve has a textured bottom, which grabs nicely on the chair seat, but the pad moves a bit and has needed to be adjusted occasionally.

The other is that the pad is thick, and so the arc on the back of the chair and the arms hit differently. I’m able to lift the arms a little more to make up for it, but the back of the chair doesn’t move enough to hit the lumbar in the right spot. Not unexpected, getting a very thick pad, but something to keep in mind.

Overall, after a brief time with it, I’ve adjusted enough stuff, and gotten used to occasionally shifting the pad around, and appreciate my chair again.

title: DownBeats compared against LiveMus!c & DUBS: Not Protective
text:
I have the unique perspective of having the opportunity to try these DownBeats, as well as [[ASIN:B00NW1IZ5Q DUBS Acoustic Filters ]] and the [[ASIN:B00H2F87I8 LiveMus!c HearSafe Ear Plugs]].

TTL;DR: Don't bother with these. Compared to LiveMus!c, these offer pathetic protection. You might not ever realize this, though, if you don't try out other brands.

My belief is that if you're going to go through the hassle to research earplugs, buy them, remember to bring them with you and actually use them when you are at an event, they ought to work really well or else that's a whole lot of wasted effort for nothing.

I don't often write reviews - I specifically bought these for TomorrowWorld and was so frustrated by their lack of protection that I thought it was worth expressing. It was my first festival to bring ear plugs to! I thought I was ready. I thought wrong. There's not much else to say. They're comfortable, the case is nice, they're not that expensive, but when it comes down to it, all that matters is protection. Even before sound quality, in my opinion. You're not wearing these for style. If you disagree, then this review might not apply to you.

Earplugs are unique in that they're difficult to test in your home; you can't exactly recreate an actual concert environment in your apartment (or probably shouldn't). So when you take these to an event, you might believe they're effective since you have nothing to compare it against. This false sense of security is dangerous! Especially if it's your first pair.

I thought these were also on par with my [[ASIN:B00NW1IZ5Q DUBS ]] as well. Comfortable, cheap. but you truly don't know what you're missing until you try the [[ASIN:B00H2F87I8 LiveMus!c]] plugs.

I think the perspective of comparing this to two other brands is quite valuable. I am not some crazy earplug freak - I bought these for my festival, tried the DUBS, and then my friend let me borrow his LiveMus!c. If protection is most important, spend the extra $15 - don't cheap out on your cochlea.

title: Good taste, stays "clumpy". $$$
text:
I ordered this product as it was listed as a "buy one, get one at half price" promotion, and it was created by the folks at Speed Keto, so I figured, sure, why not?

Pros:

Taste: I was looking for something other than chocolate, and this strawberry flavor is pretty good. it is very sweet tasting to me, although not overpowering. I like to add ice to it after blending and making an iced smoothie - yum!

Ketosis: I don't have this every day but on days when I do, I have not noticed any problem remaining in ketosis as indicated by ketone measuring strips. It isn't designed to be a meal replacement although I have used this as a meal replacement on days when I have fallen out of ketosis to get back on track again. So, it works!

Cons:

Price: When I purchased the product, the cost was $44.95 for one (about $67.43 for 2, or $33.71 each on promo). The non-promo price has since dropped by $5.00 to $39.95 each. I think it's way overpriced, although one can argue that everything that says "keto" on it is too expensive.

Blending Power: Not good at all! Even when I use a "Ninja Professional" mixer to try to dissolve all of the powder, I end up with too many clumps of dry powder within my drink, as compared to using Slim Fast's Keto powder in the same blender (which blends quite well, but really isn't all that keto friendly, but that's another story entirely).

The Bottom Line: In spite of what I think of the price, and the subpar blending results, I still ordered another container of their product: the salted caramel flavor. Overall, the impact to staying in ketosis is a big plus in my book. I also realized that there are plenty of similarly marketed keto-shake powders available on Amazon.com which are just as expensive, if not more so (per serving), than this product. If the manufacturer could just work on the recipe so that the resulting drink isn't filled with so many undissolved powder balls, then I would likely rate this product four stars, if not higher.

title: Barely Works with Nikon D810
text:
I bought this instead of the crazy expensive [[ASIN:B0076UXKDG Nikon MB-D12 Multi Battery Power Pack]]. This Vivitar pack is $250 LESS than the Nikon pack. Though all my lenses and batteries are Nikon-branded, I was willing to cut corners on the battery pack and grip. Big mistake.

This Vivitar pack doesn't always fully engage with camera. It only works about 20% of the time. I've had numerous, reoccurring problems getting it to supply power to the camera using both the AA tray and the EN-EL15 tray. I can sometimes wiggle the battery pack or unscrew it and screw it back on to get the camera to recognize the pack but not always. I've tried [[ASIN:B00MXCIK32 Panasonic Eneloop Pro AA Batteries]] as well as typical alkaline batteries. I've tried Nikon-branded EN-EL-15 batteries and generic equivalents.

I just got back from a ten-day trip the the American Pacific Northwest in winter. I bought this battery pack because I knew I'd be out hiking a lot away from a battery charger. That, plus reduced battery capacity because of the extreme cold meant I was going to need more power than the internal battery. You can imagine how frustrated I am having carried this Vivitar pack on planes and with my gear all over Mount Rainier and Mount Hood just to have it never work right.

I'm returning the Vivitar battery grip pack today. Before I give up completely or buy the Nikon MD-D12, I'm going to try another third-party pack. Given the horrible experience I just had with the Vivitar grip, I'm not even willing to give a replacement unit another try.

title: It's Simple: Read This Book!
text:
A caveat: I am not the target demographic for this book. I am a middle-aged male who happened upon it via recommendation, and am I glad I did. What could at first blush (if one is inattentive; I've been accused of that) be a simple romance novel is in fact a complex, deeply layered and intensely felt dramatic story. The protagonist, a young Native American woman, lives in a place between two worlds. While a devout Christian, she comes from a cultural background rich with metaphysical manifestations and rituals. Add to this that prior to her complete conversion she lived with the equivalent of a playboy shaman and you have one complex girl. She is now heading to her home territories (it not her literal home) to pursue a ministry within the tribe. But the pastor is an old flame, and one which will kindle anew. Throughout she is metaphorically haunted by her past, and quite literally haunted by the forces of her tribal past.

This is a story that could quickly sink into fantasy or gimmickry. The author allows neither. She quite skillfully blends the supernatural events with real life situations until we do not know where reality ends and magic begins. This is consistent through the book. These potentially sticky themes are handled with a delicacy and grace rarely found. Even at the end, we are not quite sure where this line is drawn, and that is a good thing. A bit of creative ambiguity nourishes the mind and primes us for the next installment... something I look forward to. I just have to make sure to keep this book tucked under a copy of Popular Mechanics to keep my (probably imagined) macho image alive.

A tip of the hat to KB Schaller!

title: Smart looking yet tough and comfortable
text:
I bought the medium and large Jet Set pet carrier through Amazon for my Chihuahua and Dachshund after looking at all the other carriers in New York pet stores. I simply wanted an attractive and rugged dog carrier that could genuinely withstand the rigors of travel and protect my dogs against inevitable knocks and jolts. It needed to be well padded and offer far more protection than the most popular soft carrier but also be able to squeeze under an airplane seat. However at home, I needed something that wasn't so utilitarian that it needed to be shut away but instead could function as a subtle and sensible den.

On the whole, I found almost all the competition either too feminine bordering on the stupid and/or too flimsy for serious consideration by anyone not just considering flying with a dog, but for any travel whether by car, subway or even bicycle!

The Jet Set carriers have proven themselves as very tough and practical. I like their well padded interiors and simple tough exterior (though I wish they came in other colors especially black or dark brown). The floor, side walls and ceiling all have what feels like at least a half inch of foam padding on a semi-rigid backing. The interior padding is covered in a soft black cloth. I wish that the floor was removable or there was a fleece lining I could buy so I simply line it with newspaper and cover with an old folded bath mat. The exterior shell in tough thick ballistic nylon (that as I mentioned I wish came in other more muted colors). On either side are windows with roll-up cover flaps and both ends have zippered soft nylon mesh openings. These offer a good mix of ventilation and privacy that some other dog carriers don't - either too much or too little. Also my Dachshund has chewed through the soft plastic mesh of other brand dog carriers (that I was unhappy with for all the reasons I like the Jet Set) but at best, just flossed his teeth on the Jet Set's mesh.

I completely endorse and recommend the Jet Set bag. I can't imagine there is a better dog carrier on the market - I certainly didn't find one in the dozen or more pet stores I visited in Manhattan ranging from Petco to very high end designer shops. They've performed amazingly well and at about $110 were excellent value for money especially compared to both cheaper and much more expensive carriers that look foolish and don't offer your dog enough protection on the move. I've seen some people on airplanes that have "fashion" dog bags that one could see were completely inadequate and inwhich the dog was uncomfortable and miserable. My dogs love their Jet Sets as dens at home (tucked under dining chairs in the corner of a room) and inasmuch seem just as relaxed and happy curled up/stretched out in them on the subway, in a plane or car.

title: You get what you pay for.
text:
Overall, a good product - glad I bought it - beats hand plucking!

It works well; I would like to add some more fingers. The key is to get the scald correct.

The only true criticism I have is it did not come with instructions of how to actually to use it to pluck a bird. I think instructions on scalding and plucking would be greatly beneficial. Planet Wizbang [...] has excellent scalding instructions. I bought this plucker since it was only $100 more than the parts to build my own using the Wizbang Chicken Plucker plans; well worth the $100.

I used it to process 25 Cornish Cross on 6/1 - worked very well on the big (7+ lbs dressed weight) birds; broke the wings on the 5 pound females. By trial and error, we figured out pulsing it on the smaller birds works better. Detailed instructions from the seller may have shortened the learning curve.

Helped my neighbors process 30 Freedom Rangers 6/14. We had some improper scalds; and I think we were using too much cold water in the plucker (again, detailed instructions would have helped). Regardless, the Freedom Ranger are just a harder pluck compared to CornishX, and we had to hand pluck the backs of most, if not all, the birds. We broke the legs on many birds; think we left them in the plucker too long trying to get off all the feathers. Again, the seller should have provided instructions to help with these issues.

A bit of an issue getting the thing. CC ONLY did not provide full contact info so when I missed the call, there was no email for the shipper to use; it went into storage, but ultimately arrived fine. Make sure your contact info in Amazon is up to date.

title: An excellent help to sleepers bothered by external noise and light!
text:
I have sleeping issues so I get some shut-eye when I'm able, day or night. I bought these because they also had the Bluetooth connectivity as well so I'm able to fall asleep to a baseball game or music or white noise. It really helps to mask the noise of cars driving through the neighborhood. Since I have the music or whatever on a timer I generally use these for a couple of hours at a time. I generally charge them every two or three days which is just fine. I don't think I've ever run out of battery. They're comfortable and easily size adjusted with the Velcro/elastic straps. Light is 99% blocked; only a tiny bit is visible right around the flare of my nostrils. I don't even notice unless I'm looking for it. Sound is fine. These aren't high-end headphones, and I didn't expect them to be. Probably on a par with an old transistor radio you used to listen to the ballgame on while sitting on the back porch. (If that's unfamiliar sounding to you, that's an unfortunate loss on your part.)

To improve this, I can only really think of three small things: 1. Put something like fake fur along the lower border so that the curves will be cushioned and the tiny light leaks will be absorbed. 2. Make the pockets for the speakers smaller so they don't have as much room to shift around. They generally stay put but sometimes will shift around a bit. 3. Move the charging port to someplace besides the front eye. Granted, this is more stylistic than anything else, but it would look much cleaner without the tan piece of leather. At least maybe color it black. (3a. Consider also changing the layout of the buttons to be more readily identified by touch. The on/off/pairing button in the middle is fine but the volume up and down on either side are about five millimeters away and don't have any easy means of location unless you know exactly what you want to do.)

But overall these are totally worth it and I would certainly buy them again!

title: Read review carefully. Do not purchase this one. Save yourself the money and time.
text:
Pay close attention to this review before you purchase this. This will be long but will be accurate to help you not go through what we went through.

We had to buy parts from Home Depot (and we looked at Lowe’s too) and replace a lot of parts that would not work from its own product/box. We spent around $60 on parts for this. I wanted to send it back but was on a time crunch.
The reviews and Q’s and A’s about installation are WRONG. This product is easy to install but hard at the same time. I will explain why.

Installation- when it comes to your drain line, the drain line itself would not screw on to what’s known as the bowl portion of it. So we had to buy a new bowl and a new drain line. The water line is a 3/8’s. Your source if installing in your laundry room comes from a 3/4, then you have to buy an elbow that reduces it down to 3/8. No big deal. We knew this before purchasing. But what we didn’t know is this product is made in China. What does that mean for you installing? Their 3/8 is not the same as ours. So u have to purchase more parts to convert over to our 3/8’s. Well why buy another if their 3/8’s can attached to ours? It can attach but it will not be correctly attached and will start to leak. Water will follow the least past of resistance meaning as it is forced from the incoming line it is constantly pushing to flow out and it will start to slowly leak which will lead up to a bigger leak and if you install this behind your wall, you will have a leak and who knows how long it will be prior to actually seeing your leak. Your water bill will indicate a leak but until you see the water coming down the ceiling or on your floor, it can stay within your wall structure and joints/beams. So you have to make sure to purchase one that thoroughly screws on when installing and make sure you use Teflon tape. So you install the drain lines, install the incoming water lines. Is that it? Yes. From this point you can turn on your water line with minimum pressure and test it one side at a time. Checking for leaks. If everything is good then you are good to go.
This is by far the worst product I have ever purchased on Amazon. The only way I would give this a better review is if the company itself gave me a refund for what I had to spend at Home Depot for their parts that would not screw on/work. Even if they did, I still would not give it a 5 because it wld not be right to the next person wanting to buy this.
I highly recommend you looking into an American built one for the sake of saving you money because every house and everything sold at Lowe’s and Home Depot will work together through that. If you don’t purchase you have to buy a couple adapters per line. A new line, and hopefully your drain line fits to the bowl that goes under your sink. So overall the most important pieces for this did not work.

title: More IS better!
text:
These things are PERFECT for your house. The 1" create too much resistance on a high MERV rated filter, especially when it is getting dirty.

These work perfect and in the end I will probably break even ($) on this 5" VS the 1" filters I was replacing every 30-45 days.

A trick I am using. I went to Lowe's and purchased a foam pre-filter that is supposed to go on a window AC unit. It is a thin gray/black foam sheet. I have it over this filter as a "Pre-Filter" to catch all the LARGE debris that would ultimately shorten the life of the 5" filter. 1x/month I take the foam filter and rinse it out and lay it back on the 5" filter. The foam is so thin it creates VERY little air resistance.

Another thing I noticed is the HVAC is quieter with these filters. When I would install 1" there was always a "whistle" as the air passes through the filter, even when it was new. With this 5" is is quiet, much less resistance.

The filter fit perfect into the 1" filter housing, no modifications needed. I did add a foam rubber, self adhesive weather strip (like this [[ASIN:B0025KUSXW Duck 1297116 Self Adhesive Weatherstrip 17 Feet]] to inside face of the 1" metal housing. This created a better seal between the filter and the surrounding housing. Making the air go THROUGH the filter, not AROUND it.

title: Great for travel! And still pretty great just for sleeping in general
text:
I bought an eye mask like this a few years back and it was super helpful for a long flight from the Dominican Republic to my home here in the US.

The fact that it has extra room for each eye due to the concave shape (unlike traditional eye masks) means you can wear makeup and not worry about looking crazy exiting the flight!

I liked it so much I started using it nightly since blocking the light helped my sleep so much. That one eventually wore out so when I started looking for a replacement I shifted gears and bought one of the copper eye masks. That one was fantastic for nightly sleep, but this one wins hands down for travel.

Now that I have this company’s version of the structured eye mask here are my thoughts (I received a discount on this product in exchange for an honest review):

This mask I think is best for travel as it’s not quite as comfortable as a silky mask. BUT travel is where it really shines because it truly does block out all light if you position it right and it’s still quite comfortable.

I noticed that the Velcro on the back can sometimes get stuck in my hair or be a little uncomfortable when sleeping so those are the minor cons.

But really, for the purpose of travel specifically this mask is awesome! And the regular price is great. I think I paid the same amount for one mask in the past. And it seems like the quality of this mask is better than the one I had purchased before.

I had to eventually buy a new one because it started to split down the seams and this one doesn’t like seem like it will have the same issue.

I highly recommend this product. The fact that you get two masks and the earplugs makes it a great gift for travel loving friends - especially women. But it’s also a good idea to keep one or two of these around for trips. Like a travel pillow, once you’ve tried it it’s super hard to go without!

title: Really wanted to like this
text:
I recommend you read Winter's one-star review of this product.

Sadly, this stuff didn't work for me. I have some Durango boots I've been wearing for about a year, but they've picked up a slight funk.

They are not terribly stinky, but it's enough that I've become self conscious about it. I only wear wool socks with my boots, so I was surprised my boots have started to stink in the first place. Furthermore, because they are leather boots and not sneakers, there are fewer places for the sink to accumulate, so disinfecting/deodorizing them should be pretty simple.

I have thoroughly saturated the boots with this product, and all efforts have met with temporary success at best. I've tried soaking the boots in chlorinated water and sun drying them (wore them in the pool and sloshed around), and nothing has worked. Foot powder still works better than anything, but I don't like the mess it makes.

My plan now is to buy a boot dryer and just use that every time I take off my boots. I'm giving this product two stars because it is mildly effective, and perhaps it is more effective at preventing shoe stink than it is at removing it. But it did not work for my intended purpose.

I purchased the two-pack.

* * * * * UPDATE * * * * *

The boot dryer is the way to go. To encourage the process, I added just a few drops of "clean linen" fragrance oil (Yankee Candle Co.) on either side of each insole. No more stink. The boot dryer was $59. If you have a similar problem, I'd recommend skipping this product and going directly to the boot dryer to take care of the conditions that cause the stink in the first place: sweat.

title: Frankin NO Scent
text:
Arrived quickly. Brand new condition. It was as appeared in the ad.
I got this for shoulder pain as well as for the scent. After it arrived,
I opened the bottle, and immediately, without holding it to my nose, I could smell Frankincense. When I did hold it to my nose, the smell of frankincense was even stronger. So far so good. I put about 4 drops in a CLEAN diffuser, turned it on and went about my day. I forgot about it for a few hours. Later, when I remembered I had it in the diffuser, I sniffed the air in my apartment. It didn't smell like frankincense. I checked, and my difuser was still running. Some of the liquid had evaporated, but still half full. I never noticed a frankincense smell.

Next day, I tried it again, only this time, I put in 6 drops. I had errands to do, so I figured I would leave it running. My thoughts were when I opened the door after being gone a few hours, I should smell it really good. Not the case. No scent. There hasn't been any pain relief as yet either. I'm going to try massaging it directly into my skin.
Frankincense is normally a strong scent. This brand smells no different from others when you put the bottle to your nose, but it doesn't work in the diffuser. The scent disappears when it leaves the bottle. Strange. I won't order this brand again.

After I bought 4 solar repellers and placed them in the backyard. Two (2) days later, the gophers and squirrels left the backyard and run to the front yard to dig holes. I knew it worked. The next day I put one repeller in the front yard, too. It repelled them away. This a great product to protect your gardens from small animals.
FYI: When this solar gopher repeller works, you may hear buzzing for 2-3 seconds each time.

The cord in between is rather long on the dog but I'm able to coil it up and keep in contained on the backside of the diaper where it stays clean.  When the dog urinates a little the alarm goes off and he does not like that!  He now goes to the front door and whines to go out rather than risk setting off the alarm. She also chronically removes her disposables and has accidents around the house, but so far (4 days and counting) hasn’t removed the cloth diapers once! The biggest issue has been with night time leaks. It seems as though they leak pretty well out of the leg hole. My child is a usually a side sleeper and has spilled out of the side if she goes in this position. BUT it’s better than her taking the disposable off and going freely (as she’s been known to do). And I haven’t had an issue during the day when she’s standing. I have yet to try doubling up on absorbent pads, but plan on trying this in the future. And as a bonus, her rash seems to be improving!

title: Great product - you must have if use a full face mask!
text:
I bought my first pair of covers through their website directly not long after I got my CPAP machine. I use a ResMed AirFit F10 full face mask and really, really struggled to get comfortable with it for the first 3 or 4 nights. I even called my sleep therapy place to request a different mask. The mask silicone was very uncomfortable on my skin and anytime I got even a small leak, it would make the dreaded fart noise. I didn't sleep at all for the first 3 nights.

Luckily, when I was getting my mask, there was a brochure in the office for the CPAP Comfort Cover. I had grabbed it and kept it, but luck. I ordered my first pair and received them a couple days later.

I cut my first cover too much and probably ruined it. Please be careful when cutting out the hole. They provide very good instructions, but I went off the ranch a bit. The second one is perfect and completely covers the silicone. When I wear it, I have no problems at all breathing. I probably could even have gone smaller with the hole.

These covers probably saved me from giving up on the CPAP system, that's how bad it was. Until I put the cover on, I was miserable. Now I have three nights in a row with perfect MyAir scores and I'm sleeping like a baby.

Can't recommend this product highly enough!!

title: Followed the instructions as best as I can figure
text:
According to this device, as I sit here writing this, I have, apparently, already passed out long ago without drink, and, with only a half-cup of wine, it says that I am in danger of dying for the past hour.

I Just received it in the mail today. Followed the instructions as best as I can figure. I did a test first with no drinks. It registered me as .2+
Although I had not had any alcohol, I waited 20 minutes in case it was from what I ate at lunch - still .2+ (even higher than before)

I drank a few sips of wine, maybe 16% alc. I waited 15 ~ 20 min. It still said .2+ an that I should be almost passed out and severe memory loss.

I drank a little more - didn't even finish the cup - and waited over an hour without eating or even drinking water in order to not skew the results and to test it said that I now am .3+ and that I am in danger of dying. If that happens, please alert my next of kin as to why.

UPDATE:

Day two and I am getting the same dubious results. It told me I was .2 in the morning, (down from .5+ the night before a seven hour sleep and nothing to drink for hours since i was apparently supposed to be dead after my half-drink. This time I am using it in combination with other track your drinking app I found on google play that lets me input what and how much I drank and estimates you BAC (no blowing). The results from this app (although estimations) seem much more realistic in terms of the effects.

I will give this a few more tires, but since there is no way to accurately test it other than buy a few other brand devices and test them all together it is quite frustrating.

text:
I bought this for bathing my dog, and it works great for that purpose. It was easy to install, although the instructions that come in the box are a little vague. I just unscrewed my existing shower head, put the rubber gaskets in the hose, screwed the head onto the hose and the hose onto my shower faucet. If you were trying to use this with an existing shower head it might be more difficult. You also have to make sure that the head is switched to flow (try moving the silver bar on the head) to make sure the water is flowing. It didn't leak at all when I used it, although it seems some other reviewers have had problems.

title: Go-Go Scooter is great
text:
I waited until I used this daily for a full 6 months to write this review. Not a single problem. Works very well. Totally reliable and dependable.
Before I got this, I had a Golden Scooter, same size, and had so many service calls I eventually got a new one. Same story on the second Golden. So glad I switched to Pride Go-Go.
Arrived quickly, little bit of assembly, no problem. Runs well and dependably.

Carefully look at the dimensions, turning radius, and ground clearance to see if it will work for you. All these dimensions are available. I called customer service at this company and was told this scooter is not recommended for use in a home, since it does not have a very tight turning radius. (It can't turn the same tight corners an electric wheelchair can). My home was built in the 40's and is not ADA compliant. The interior door widths vary from 28.5" to just 26.75" wide. The main hallway is only 36" wide. As a result, I have some limitations to the way I drive the scooter in and out of some rooms in my house. For example, I have one doorway I can only get into by making a right angle. So I have to approach that door with the door on my right side.(That requires that I turn around in another room if I am coming from the opposite way.) I was aware of the limits and that was ok with me. It would work easily if you want to use it in newer homes, apartments, commercial businesses, etc. Or if you use it to help sometimes and you walk in tight spots. Take care to determine if these specification will work where you want to use it.
For me it works great and I appreciate how reliable it is.
