title: They helped me and my poor heel — to my surprise.
text: At 59, I had painful bone spurs of the first time — in my left heel. I really didn't know why I felt pain like this off and on. It was hobbling me at work. A wonderful podiatrist x-rayed the foot, gave me Powerstep insoles and a set of easy-to-follow exercises. The best exercise was designed to stretch the calf muscles. (See? The leg bone IS connected to the heel-bone.) In any case, the pain disappeared within days, as I recall, and I was active again, even resuming my walking exercises. The insoles are firm and fit nicely in my main shoes and running shoes, but in some shoes I own there wasn't room for the insole AND the foot, and it's not practical to remove the shoe's original insole. In other words, you need enough room between the sole and upper; that's the only thing to watch out for. Buying a larger size shoe won't be the solution. In any case, my feet have felt so much better that I can wear shoes without the insoles on occasion without the pain returning. (But I'd prefer to wear them).

title: Cool features, unreliable readings
text:
I've been pretty happy with my Fitbit Ultra device which I received as a gift about six months ago. As I've started dieting more strictly, I decided to give this scale a try. Considering the price, I was expecting high quality.

The scale looks and feels good with a sleek, sturdy design. Setup was relatively simple, with only a minor hiccup (you need to use a laptop, phone, or other device connected to the same WiFi network the scale will be). Once done, I was able to easily integrate the scale into my FitBit.com profile. I've even been able to convince my boyfriend to start up an account, and adding his profile to the scale was also simple.

Weighing myself is nice and easy, and the WiFi feature has proven very convenient. However, once you get past all the bells and whistles, I find I'm disappointed by the scale's performance. My boyfriend and I have both noticed fairly large inconsistencies in both the weight and body fat measurements. Even consecutive weigh-ins yield wildly different results (this morning, I weighed in three times with a range of 12 pounds!). The body fat readings are even more erratic. I've found that for "official weigh-ins," I still need to use the more consistent scale at my gym, and that really is a disappointment considering the $130 price tag.

title: Not accurate on weight measurement
text:
I purchased this Fitbit Aria scale, since I have a FitBit Ultra that I'm very happy with, so thought...what the heck...I'll get the scale too so that I'll have a happy marriage between devices and fitbit.com....well, not exactly the case. I've found that the scale is inaccurate on not just the weight but also on the fat percentage. Not to mention it can take a long time just for it to figure out what your weight is and or fat percentage (10+ seconds sometimes, ain't nobody got time fo dat)....and it confused me with being a Guest after I lost a couple of pounds wtf! The two things that you care the most about a scale doing...this one does not do well!!!

Here are my list of pros/cons:

Pros:
- Sleek design
- Fairly easy setup with wifi
- Display is friendly and easy on the eyes
- Uploads measurements automatically to fitbit.com

Cons:
- Weight measurement off by 6-9lbs (my other scale I've been using for years shows the difference and I even used dumbbells to check and it said my two 25lb dumbbells weighed 52.4lbs)
- Inconsistent when on different surfaces, floor, tile, wood, carpet
- My fat calipers tell me I'm at 24% body fat, the scale goes from 28%-31%
- Confuses easily between you and Guest account after a couple of lbs of weight change

Overall, the scale is a nice idea but it needs a lot of work. I think I may try out the Withings scale or something. Sadly I cannot recommend this scale but hopefully that will change in the future. There is a possibility that it can be calibrated and I missed that step? But I can't find any information on how to do so and why should I have to? Hope you found this review helpful and think twice about making your smart scale choice. Good luck!

title: Chalazion 4 days of treatment
text:
So back in late November I developed a stye on my lower lid. I treated it like normal. (Cleaned it daily, applied warm compresses.) Normally for me these clear up in a week or so, but this one did not. The head went away but the stye turned hard and was somewhat painful by the end of December I went to my eye Dr. He said the stye had turned into a chalazion and that more than likely I would have to have it cut out. He gave me a heavy dose of antibiotics to take along with an expensive eye drop Azasite ($60 after insurance). I was also to continue to do hot compresses 3 times a day. He said if by the end of January if there was no improvement he would schedule the removal 😬 (He seemed very sure that surgery would be my outcome). By January 23rd I had not noticed any improvement at all.... the chalazion hurt when I cleaned it or pressed on it in any way. I ran across this product and placed my order...after all what did I have to lose right?!? I received the product quickly by the afternoon of the 26th I did my first application which was when I took the first picture (top). I continued my hot compresses as well ( also taking fish oil tablets by this point as well). By the second day my chalazion felt really like it was going to explode so I took this to mean there was definitely something happening within my chalazion. It was very sore when I rubbed in the oil that afternoon even more so than before. By the next day the size had a noticeable improvement and all scoreness was gone. I could literally press very firmly with a q-tip and have no pain (3 days in using this product) . I am at day 4 now (2 pic bottom). I definitely feel I am on my way to getting rid of this. I will continue using this product til it clears up and possibly some after to make sure. I will update as to my outcome and how long my process took. But for now I can say it is not an overnight fix but it seems to work and I wish I had used this in the beginning because I feel like it would not have drug out this long. I recommend this to anyone who wants to avoid surgery.
*** Update Day 5****
Woke up this morning to a head that has appeared on the chalazion!! This is a great sign☺️ (pic 3)
***Update day 6****
The chalazion had two heads that had appeared yesterday this morning one popped after applying a hot compress the other popped while I was applying the oil to my lid. I am seriously impressed with this product!! I am not going to take a photo today. There is still some redness but the hard bump in completely gone!!! I will wait til tomorrow to take the photo and update on where I am. Amazing!!!! So happy to avoid surgery 😁😁😁

title: Simple, easy to use, and easy to clean
text:
Disclaimer: I received this product in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

This trimmer has a full plastic build with a glossy finish. It seems others may not have noticed it immediately, but as the product photos indicate, the on/off for this trimmer is the center black switch which slides up for on and back down for off. The top protection cap can be popped off while the bottom battery cover is a twist on/off cap.

The trimmer itself relies on the inner knife to trim. As such, the nose outer shell serves as a nice protection for your skin. With that being said, don't expect a close cut as if you're shaving as there is a slight tiny gap between the outer shell and the inner knife. This can be twisted off and pulled out along with the nose knife inside to easily rinse and clean.

I have never needed the LED on this trimmer however from what I could tell it was quite dim so don't expect to use it in total darkness should you for whatever reason be inclined to do so.

Thus far, the trimmer has trimmed effortlessly and works as intended.

title: Nice bag. Good for all the right reasons, not perfect, but what is?
text:
Good bag. Nice and bright, lots of room, even has some different little compartments for stuff inside and on the sides. Would be better if it had a zipper top, but I suppose the open top and side buckles plays into the "rapid response" angle. It's got a pretty good capacity--room for plenty of gauze, bandage wrap, tourniquets, slings, and that kind of stuff. Even room for a few bandaids and other kiddie-level first aid gear. For what I paid it's definitely the top-tier of cheap first aid bags.

A little theory for you: I reckon if you need a first aid bag, it needs to be obvious and look the part. This is obvious and looks the part. That helps you and everyone on the scene. It needs to have some room for useful things besides bandaids and alcohol wipes. This has room for real supplies. It needs to be handy. This is handy, with a nice carrying strap and some different pockets.

When you need some actual for-real first aid, someone's probably bleeding, maybe badly. If it's a knee scrape of a bee sting they just need to suck it up. That's what your little pre-made kits are for. Skip the pre-made little kits and stock this baby with some serious gauze, ace bandages, tourniquets, and vet wrap. Most of your "real" first aid is just staunching the bleeding and keeping the subject calm. If a person is badly wounded, there's gonna be some blood, and you don't wanna be ripping off your tshirt to use for applying direct pressure. You need actual sterile gauze, and lots of it. This little guy will help you keep that stuff handy. I've got mine configured for intermediate=level trauma. If you're badly lacerated or punctured, this rig (full of the aforementioned gauze and bandages!) will keep your gear handy while you help things from getting too nasty until you can get to a real hospital.

Nice bag overall. The best of the "around $20" bunch for sure.

title: A bit pricey at retail but worked for me :)
text:
I wanted to jump start my exercise and diet program so I decided to try out this product made by Healthy Body. (My personal review is near the end)

There are 60 capsules (2 per serving per meal) so basically min 5 day/ supply max 10 day.(NOT THE 30 DAY listed on the sales desc ) Recommended 1-2 caps before or during each meal.

Each serving has a combination of :

Yacon Root Powder
Guarana Seed Extract
Acai Berry Powder
Green Tea Extract

For a total of 1015 mg per serving.

The above ingredients are a typical blend of all the latest herbal / natural based weight management products out there. In addition to those ingredients the bottle lists:

Gelatin, Dicalcium Phosphate, Vegetable Magnesium Stearate, and Silicon Dioxide. This product is GLUTEN-FREE.

-=-=-=-=-=-
My personal experience
-=-=-=-=-=-

I started out by taking 1 pill with my first 3 meals for 2 days and no other supplements except my daily Vitamin C pill. I didn't see much in terms of feeling anything unusual with my energy nor appetite. It's possible that it could take more time. So I upped the dose to 2 pills per meal. After the 2nd meal (lunch) I did feel that I wasn't as hungry around dinner and didn't have a post lunch zzz monster attack :D

On the 2nd day of taking 2 pills per meal. I noticed that I didn't feel like I was starving before the next meal. I didn't feel tired or sluggish and at the same time, I didn't get any jitters typically associated with taking caffeine based diet pills. There was no peak rush nor was there a wear-out period where I would be exhausted. Overall it felt very natural and balance and I was able to curb a lot of my cravings. Sure I ate a piece of hard candy here and there but I wasn't craving to snack in between meals. I finished out the bottle roughly at 9 days (skipped out 1.5 days because I was out of town). I wish there were more pills left so I could do an actual 30-day review.

My results at the end of the trial was I had more energy and less cravings. There was no urge for a late night snack which is great! In terms of weight loss... I didn't notice much except about 2 lbs but that could be water weight or small fluctuations. I think a 30 day supply would have better weight results.

Would I buy this product again? YES! but only if it was sold at about $8 a bottle or less. At $18 a bottle on a 30 day supply = $108 which is waaaaay too much for this product. At their retail price of $40 per bottles ridiculous. SUPPLIER I HOPE YOU READ THIS! I almost left 3 stars on this review based on the unattractive price but thought it would not be fair to your company.

Full disclosure: I bought this product at a significant discounted price for an honest review. Please not that when it comes to supplements etc., each person reacts differently to the products. I hope that my experience has given you an idea of what to expect. I hope you enjoyed my review and please respond if you have any questions.

title: Good service, but product was not what I expected.
text:
Arrived fast and well packaged. When plugged in, one of the AIDS would not charge. I did the obvious and checked to make sure the fault was neither the charger or battery in the unit. Notified the mfg who referred me back to Amazon.com to arrange a return.
Returned item and got immediate refund back, so on that end I can tell you if you order thru Amazon you are better off if there is a problem .

I did however get a chance to check these hearing aids out and in my opinion they were only moderately decent. While they most certainly did amplify as promised.....they amplify everything! So background noise, hums, and anything in the area gets louder. The lack of any filters or tone modification makes everything sound loud and like an old staticky transistor radio. They amplified zero bottom end frequency which made everything sound terribly unnatural. The manual was a bit cheesy and was obviously a poor translation to english attempt.

While my hearing deficit I believe is more tinnitus driven than anything else, I felt moderate amplification would help my a bit and was a bit disappointed with these. However...for the modest cost they could be a great value to someone that needs straight volume boosting and is impartial to the lack of frequencies below the 1000 hz range.

Based on their good replies to me emails and return policy, I will look into their other products that may be better for filtering out background noise. The website really gives no information on the types of filtering options for the digital devices so I am a bit unsure about reordering and trying the better versions

title: Excellent tick protection and safe for kids
text: I used Buzz Away Extreme while teaching a three-week field research course in the Long Island woods in the height of a bad tick season, sharing it with my mother and 2-year-old son who were tagging along. We used the spray on hats, cuffs, and exposed skin before leaving in the morning, and reapplied around lunchtime. By the end of the course, most students and professors had been bitten by ticks, and three had to be treated for Lyme disease. We were three of only five who were not bitten, even though many of the others were using DEET-based insect repellents. We also escaped without any noticeable mosquito bites. Because ours was effective, and a low-toxicity formula, I didn't mind using it regularly, whereas many of those using DEET-based repellents were hesitant to use it more than necessary. I did make sure my son washed his hands just after application. The spray has a strong odor of geraniol, citronella, and mint, but it isn't unpleasant. I plan to keep using it when bug repellant is needed, but I have noticed that it can be hard to find by midsummer, so I plan to stock up.

text:
I love the Best Bottom system. I have been using their diapers for over 4 years now with two different kids. 4 years ago, they did not have the bamboo option. I opted for the Stay Dry because my daughter was sensitive to wet and they dried really fast, even though I don't care too much for microfiber. However, by the time my second CD baby came along, they had the Bamboo. But it took me a while to buy them, since I already had a stash. Baby 2 doesn't have a sensitivity to wetness, so she doesn't need the stay dry like her sister did. So when I saw these on sale, I thought, "why not try them?" I'm really glad I did. These Bamboo Inserts are so soft! They absorb a tun. They are super thin. They dry in a normal amount of diaper drying time. And on top of all of that, they are natural materials. What's not to like?

As a side, these diapers inserts look a little odd when you first see them. The texture reminds me of the terry found on baby wash cloths. It made me skeptical at first, but I've since gotten over it. Love these inserts!

title: Helped with the pain of a severe burn and wound healing.
text:
I didn't take photos but I wish I had because I attribute part of my rapid recovery from a painful burn to this product. I burned three knuckles on a metal pan while cooking because I didn't realize how long the material held heat after removing from the oven. The pain was severe and lasted for hours. I was frantically trying everything I knew to dress the skin that I knew would get worse as the burn persisted, and taking over-the-counter painkillers for the pain.

Having exhausted all of the typical options for a situation like this and still dealing with the severe pain of the burn, I decided to try this product to help with the burning sensation that would not stop. Let me tell you that within an hour after taking this product, the pain started to subside. I was so relieved, amazed, and thankful. In less than 2 hours the pain was completely gone.

I continued to take this product as my wound healed, along with a soothing dressing of Medihoney covered with a hydrocolloid bandage that I kept held firmly in place with gauze wrapping. Being a person whose skin develops keloid scars from injury, I was terrified of having an ugly, disfiguring permanent scar on the back of my hand forever. But to my surprise and amazement, the wound healed with no noticeable scar whatsoever. A first for me.

I will be forever grateful for this company producing this product along with the companies that produce Medihoney and hydrocolloid dressings. You saved a woman's vanity by keeping my hand scar free after a painful accident.

If you sit anywhere for extended periods of time, whether it be an office chair, car, or couch, it helps to have something that supports your back and is comfortable to lean against. title: Cute, great for multiple allergies
text:
This is actually 2 bracelets, one toddler sized, and one child sized, with the big 8 allergy "charms" and one medic alert "charm". The bracelets each have 5 holes, so you can put up to 4 allergy charm in if needed. If your child has more than 4 allergies, you would either need to buy another bracelet or find a way to make more holes. Also, if your child has allergies that are not in the "big 8" (wheat, milk, soy, shellfish, fish, nuts, peanuts, eggs) you may have to purchase extra charms for your child.

My peanut and tree-nut allergic daughter is 3 years old, and just starting to venture away from my watchful care. She is not yet in preschool, but does go to a few church activities, and I am constantly worried about her being in trouble over her food allergies. I looked at a lot of options for a medic alert type bracelet or necklace, and this seemed to be the best suited for a toddler. It is waterproof, durable, and cute. It is not super-girly, nor super-masculine. The bracelet is a bright orange, which is quite easy to see on a child, but is not SO distracting as to make their beautiful face or clothing fade into the background. It is also trendy-looking, since it looks like all those other "sayings" bracelets kids are into right now.

My favorite part about this bracelet is that it is EASY to see AND easy to read what the child is allergic to. With several of the other medical alert bracelets, you had to flip the bracelet inside-out and read something etched into it, or it would only say one allergy.

There are only 2 downsides so far.
1-my daughter likes to take it off herself. I anticipate we will spend time searching for this, before she gets used to wearing it ALL the time. But that is just because she is a very take-charge 3 year old, and you may not have this drawback.
2-it is fairly expensive for 10 pieces of plastic. Especially factoring in shipping. However, my child's health and life is infinitely valuable, and this product is much cheaper than an ER visit, or even an Epi-Pen copay. So in my mind, it is worth it since I like it and my daughter will wear it. But if you can find something less expensive that meets your needs, go with that.

title: This is my second type of straightener from them and I am completely in love and I know who I will be recommending to ...
text:
RoseMyst has definitely done it again when it comes to their straighteners. This is my second type of straightener from them and I am completely in love and I know who I will be recommending to everyone I know. First, the brush is a beautiful gold color and looks like any other brush you may have, inside the box you also have a heat resistant glove, carrying bag, and a small cloth to place the brush on when using. The buttons are on the inside of the brush, instead of on the side which was a huge plus since some other straighteners have it on the side I am constantly hitting them. You can set your setting all the way up to 450 degrees if you pleased, I tend to keep mine at around 410. Another huge difference that I've noticed with RoseMyst is that the heated bristles are flat, and the tips do not have a large round ends which is where my hair would get caught and pulled when using and that was horrible. My hair is thick, wavy and an overall pain to straighten so with this straightening brush it has cut my time down to about 20 minutes, with a baby around that's a miracle. I am overly impressed with this straightener and I highly recommend it.

title: Must have whether you are a gym rat or simply on the go person
text:
Whether you are an gym rat or just someone that lives a busy this muscle roller is a must for you. The Mava Sport muscle roller has 2 comfortable grips on the side and 9 small rollers in between the side grips that allow for easy rolling throughout your body that you can do by yourself. The material used in the making of the muscle roller is stiff, but it's perfect to actually roll out any tightness and I believe it's more effective than the foam rollers. I was first introduced to a muscle roller from my personal trainer at the gym a couple of years ago after being sore and having noodles as leg. What he would do is simply roll it over my calves and thighs to release the knots and that would allow me to complete a work out and not walk around all weird. Now fast forward to the present. I decided to get the Mava Sport muscle roller in hopes that it would allow me to relax my legs after a long nursing shift. Being 7 1/2 months pregnant and standing on your feet for about 10 hours a day takes a toll on you legs and feet. At night I simply use my handy muscle roller to roll over my calf muscles to help with the relief of any knots that's may be forming, but more importantly to improve the circulation in my legs. Using the muscle roller at night I have had a huge decrease in muscle cramps that would previously wake me up in the middle of the night due to uncomfortable/pain of the leg cramp. You can also use the muscle roller on your back and shoulder to loosen up any tightness that you may have. I also use the muscle roller on my 7 year old son when he complains of any growing pains or simply just to give him a nice little massage once in a while. I highly suggest this muscle roller to anyone that to help relax at the end of the day.

title: Great for protein bars.
text:
I use to order this brand straight from the manufacturer. Now they moved all US orders to Amazon and jacked up the price. Still a good value however. I order the 6 pack, 15.8 lbs and it lasts me months since I only use about 30g a day.

My preferred protein bar recipe(s):
30g of VitaFiber IMO Syrup
30g of Protein Powder (Any Flavor)
10g of Hershey's Special Dark Chocolate Cocoa
10g of Water

or

30g of VitaFiber IMO Syrup
40g of Protein Powder (Any Flavor)
10g of Water
2g of Flavoring Oil (Mint, Coffee, Caramel, Coconut, etc.)

Mix the ingredients up and form into bar (use a mold, it is easier) and refrigerate.
I typically make one at night for eating in the morning.

Final Bar: ~80g and 190-200 Calories depending on protein powder.
Total Cost for me is under $1 when I catch a good deal on protein.

title: Buy this if you're just getting started with Soylent
text:
This stuff is great; balanced nutrition and tastes good too! Or to be more correct it has very little flavor and I can't imagine anyone saying it tastes bad. This container is really convenient and not a bad deal; this is a great way to try Soylent if you're not sure how much you'll drink it. If you decide you want lots you should switch to ordering the pouches for a better price. I ordered this huge jar to start with and now I just refill it from pouches so I get the convenience of the jar with the value of the pouches.

My preparation tip: I use a sports drink sort of container with sealing lid and a mixer ball in it. I put in about 8oz of warm/hot water and two scoops of soylent and shake it all up. Then I add another 10oz of cold water and shake some more. That's slightly more water than the official recipe, but I prefer it that way. Starting with warm water seems to really help it dissolve better. Also it will have a slightly smoother texture if you let it sit for an hour or so but it's also fine to drink immediately.

title: Don't Waste Your Money
text: My husband and I are both nurses and routinely work night shifts. Whoever is not sleeping during the day is running our household with three children. I purchased the Marpac because of its wonderful reviews and actually kind of "blew off" the few negatives I read. What a mistake. While it is small and has varying pitches of sound easily adjusted by twisting the outer shell of the unit, it is absolutely NOT loud enough to cover everyday household noise. During the day I "slept", I heard my children playing, the microwave and kitchen doors closing, our garage door going up and down, the garbage truck, and the school bus (just to name a few). This unit is perhaps suitable if you only need it at night as white noise to sleep better, but if you are a shift worker who needs it to cover noise during the day, skip it. I am purchasing another Honeywell fan to replace the one I've had for the past 10 years and cost me $15.

title: LEAKING EVERYWHERE
text:
I purchased this Arctic Cove 3/8 in. x 12 ft. Professional Misting Kit (Model MAC3812K) from a "big box" store, not Amazon. Nonetheless, I wanted to give consumers everywhere the benefit of my experience because I am so very dissatisfied with this product. If you purchase this product, I think you may have wasted your time and possibly your money. Many of the reviewers on the "big box" website state that the product leaks a lot (only 50% would recommend it as of February 1, 2020). In my case, it leaked at every connector (see picture of two connectors). Given there are others that are satisfied with the product, I tend to believe that Arctic Cove has significant quality control issues with this product even though the external look and feel of the product is good.

I contacted Arctic Cove and their service representative had a couple of suggestions which were essentially the same as what was contained in the user manual. I went ahead and tried them again but to no avail. I then ended up sending Arctic Cove 13 emails to request a refund from early October to late December before finally receiving a response. They said they couldn't refund my money but would send me a new misting kit (same model number). I tried this new kit and obtained the same results with leaking at every connector. BUYER BEWARE!

title: I have used the SmartGuard Elite for two months now and I am very happy with it
text: I purchased this night guard after purchasing and returning a different night guard which I realized, upon its arrival, was meant to cover my top and bottom teeth.  I've used a night guard for about twenty years and I knew there was no way I could stand that.  I have used the SmartGuard Elite for a week now and I am very happy with it.  The molding process was easy (you definitely need to use a fork or a wooden skewer to hold the guard WHERE INDICATED when you place it in the water... the guard will melt to tongs or other devices) and the fit is snug and comfortable.  There has been no "break in period" to get used to the guard.  The guard's width is small (it really only covers the front 6-8 top teeth) but it is thick and sturdy, yet comfortable.  My previous two night guards were purchased from my dentists.  I'd tried an over the counter version in between those but I was not happy with it at all.  I am very happy with the SmartGuard Elite, though, and will continue to use it as a much cheaper and even more comfortable alternative to the version available from the dentist.  The function and comfortable of the SmartGuard Elite is the same or better than the last one I got from my dentist.  Very satisfied with this purchase.

title: Effective, but not perfect
text: I got the medium size b/c it was the only size available through amazon that offered the straps that didn't cross in the back (to ensure my shoulders weren't bearing the weight). I'm 5'3" and my pre-pregnancy weight was 128. I'm now in my 31st week with twins and am up to about 158lbs. Though the cradle is advertised to begin at a weight of 150, I had to start on the middle of the 3 waist settings offered for a proper fit. I've now outgrown the middle setting (comfortably) but am not big enough for the last setting. Despite this inconvenience, I noticed an immediate difference in my fatigue level upon wearing it and have had less strain on my back. It hasn't eliminated all my back pain (which is a bit more severe than is common), but I wear it everyday and know that it is helping. I don't mind that the straps show through all of my clothing b/c I didn't purchase it to be fashionable, but to help me to have less pain. It serves that purpose well and I'd recommend it (as my chiro did for me) as a prophylactic for pregnancy back pain as well as after you're presenting symptoms. Know that it might be an awkward fit, but effective for its main purpose.

That turned the lump of concrete into powder. I then opened the package and poured the contents into a small jar. The powder smells a little fruity and the color is a burnt-orange. text:
These are the perfect multi vitamin. You really can't go wrong with including these into your daily routine.

I would recommend these to ANYONE even if you're not working out!

Two capsules is a serving. I like to take one when I wake up in the morning and the other shortly before I go to bed. If you're purchasing this product, you probably care about your health a little bit and you'll probably want to do those things anyways.

If your skeptical on the effects, try taking these regularly for a month, then stop completely for a week or two. You'll shortly notice that you'll go back to your less productive, less happy, more lethargic self that you were before you started taking them. As I mentioned, the full effect will slowly start to set in if you've been consuming these regularly - you probably won't even notice the benefits you're experiencing until you stop taking them and return back to normal. text: Over the past couple of years a combination of hip replacements and operations on my spine for cancer has limited my mobility.  I have been using wheelchairs and another walker.  Recently my oncologist recommended that I try to regain as much mobility as I can for as long as I can. Using a walker instead of a wheelchair would strengthen my legs. The factors that influenced the purchase were the ease of folding, the size of the wheels and the general appearance and quality.  It does not disappoint.  It arrived in a compact box, requiring only minutes to unfold the wheels and adjust the height of the handles.  I was able to do it myself.  I am impressed with the simplicity of the design and the quality of its construction.  The handles are positioned at the midpoint over the wheels which gives it great stability.  The larger size of the wheels makes it easy to negotiate uneven ground and high thresholds.  It easily folds up like wheelchair.  It is comfortable to sit in.  It has become my main aid in getting around and already I feel improvement in my legs.  A friend who also requires a walker is planning to purchase one because if folds up so compactly.  I have wrapped some led armbands around the sideposts for night visibility.  All in all I am very happy with the product.

title: Great for live music!
text:
I've been swing dancing Tuesday nights at a 1930s social club where [[ASIN:B00002060M Stompy Jones]] plays every week. It isn't as loud as a rock concert, but after three hours of music I've been going home with ears ringing and sometimes ringing in the morning. I wore DownBeats this week!

Unsurprisingly: no ringing in the ears.
Surprisingly: I think (just maybe) it was easier to hear my dance partner talking than without. I usually have to ask girls to repeat themselves endlessly. (The only problem was I had to remember to talk loudly because it brings everything down to a normal level and are comfortable enough to forget about.)

* Visibility: Obviously not invisible. I'm not sure how visible they are, but no one commented on them in low light of the venue. Definitely not visible to someone in front of you.
* Frequency attenuation: Seems very even across spectrum (listening to voices and acoustic instruments). But surely not enough protection for spending three days at a music festival. Also perfect for motorcycling or driving in convertible (cuts down wind noise just enough). I tried wearing them to the grocery store; it was pleasant as background noise fades away, but missed a few words when talking to the checkout clerk.
* Comfort: Very comfortable at the point where they are sealed and working correctly. If you push them in quite a bit further (to where they are probably barely visible) they get a lot less comfortable. They are a tiny bit adjustable--You can leave them a little loose and they will dampen sound some, but not fall out! The stem doesn't stick out far enough to interfere with motorcycle helmet--and I just tried laying on pillow and that is perfectly comfortable too.
* Practical: Easy to insert and not difficult to remove (I can't figure out why other reviewers want tweezers to pull these out); washable plastic; key-chain container is helpful and better thought-out than most ear-plug containers.
* Size: I occasionally use ear plugs that are too big and uncomfortable; I've never used any too small. I can imagine these could be too big for small ears; the core of these is a hard plastic shaft that doesn't taper down.

Favorite feature: short stem = discrete and can use while sleeping or under motorcycle helmet.

I'm totally delighted with the product, and although it seems like you should get two pairs for your $14 (or maybe a half-off coupon for another pair), the quality makes them a very reasonable price. But expensive enough I'm hoping that the soft plastic eartip piece is durable enough to last a couple years.

** Update. I've been using these a couple times a week for nearly a year. The ear plugs are holding up well. The key chain case occasionally unscrews in your pocket, but obviously not a big deal. I will concede that for riding my motorcycle, I prefer a pair of MSA Tri-Seal Ear Plugs which fit further in your ear and have three flanges, features which prevent them from backing out (these occasionally get loose and have to stop and take off helmet to reinsert...).

title: Disappointed
text: Disappointed is the only word that comes to mind, when trying to describe this Dental Water Flosser.  I was quite excited to find a rechargeable, portable model... and couldn't wait to try this one out.  Unfortunately, I am unable to tell you anything useful about it. First-off, in unboxing the unit and reading the manual, I discovered that the kit I received was missing the toothbrush head- prominently referred to in the manual. That wasn't so bad, these things happen... and I already have a toothbrush, anyway. I finished reading the manual, and plugged the flosser in, to charge it up. The power display is tiny, but readable. With the flosser now fully-charged, I attached one of the six supplied flossing heads. According to the manual, the device should recognize the attached head- and indicate so, on the display- putting the unit into 'stand-by'.  But... nothing happened. I tried a 'short' press of the power button: Nothing. I tried a 'long' press of the power button: Nothing. I tried the "Mode" button: Nothing. I tried another flosser head: Nothing. I tried the "nose cleaning" attachment (really??): Nothing. I re-read the manual... twice: Nothing! I even tried powering it on, while plugged in: Nothing. But the display kept saying the battery was fully-charged. On top of all of that, tipping the flosser assembly- even in the slightest- resulted in water noticeably leaking past the rubber seal on the reservoir- making a mess! I only filled the reservoir, two-thirds full, because the manual warns against overfilling- saying not to exceed the fill line... but, what line? There's no indication on the reservoir, at all! I didn't mind the missing brush head, I could even live (begrudgingly) with the leaking... but a brand new product, that's DOA?... Disappointed... that's putting things mildly.

title: Really, really wanted to love this scooter, However:
text: For starters, the first one arrived with a battery/charging problem, making for 3mile max outings.  One brake worked a little until it didn’t work at all, the other grabbed like a stick through the spokes.  The left rear taillight was on backwards.  It dripped a permanent stain where it was parked. There was a pronounced grinding sound from the right rear wheel and the front wheel pulled aggressively to the right. Maximum speed 18? Ha! Forget that. 12, tops. But I really, really wanted to love it,  sooo, ..  (First I should mention the note tagged on the new scooters. ‘Call 800-whatever for tech support’.  The # rings ewheels, no matter who you buy it from.  It’s a phone tree on a loop - no humans - and I never got a single call back - the seller stepped up, thankfully, and arranged for a replacement. All thanks &props there, Seniordotcom!)  The replacement arrived two days ago. (That’s a month and a half since the first was deemed defective and a replacement initiated btw. It wasn’t the seller holding things up, mind you; it was ewheels. Who helped make every step of this ordeal as inhumane as possible)  I must say the difference between the first and second scooter is notable, except for the brakes, which, having been both a bike and motorcycle rider, I’m acquainted with. Fact is, the brakes are dangerous. One works until it doesn’t, the other grabs like a stick in the spokes, just like the first scooter. Okay. Believe it or not, I STILL wanted to love this scooter.  And with the help of the seller, I did finally get a call back from ewheels, re: fixing the brakes and why no 18mph. Answer? these scooters do not go 18mph, what’s advertised of them is wrong - they only go 12mph.. . Re: the brakes, they may need adjusting and if I can film them malfunctioning, someone will determine whether ewheels will have some one of their nationwide specialists do something.  Thing is, I’m no stunt rider and I’ve no idea how to film this brake problem.  Bigger thing is I’m so disappointed at the prospect of such an evidently dreamy scooter appearing to be just another cranked-out-for-a-target-audience-‘til-bankrupted- from-injury-lawsuits money-maker.  Buyer Beware, right?  As for the warrantee and tech-support, you can take it from me that unless yours is as obviously defective as that first one I had, if you need help with it, you can expect to be on your own.

title: Loving It
text:
For me personally, when I look for a fat burner pill I'm looking for no jitters but quality energy.

The 5 stars is due to the fact that even when I take my 2 pills in the morning I have ZERO jitters throughout the day but I still have enough energy to smash a rigorous 2 hour workout - and then some.

The energy feels pure and clean. I could still take a nap if I wanted to but I'm not dragging through the day. It also doesn't suppress my appetite to an unhealthy level. The edge stays off all day but I still have the hunger to eat my post-workout meal and to eat throughout the day to keep my energy levels up. Fuel is a big part of weight loss and muscle building and with working out being such an integral part of my day if I couldn't eat properly on these fat burners it would be counterproductive.

I've only been using these pills for a week so I can't comment fully on how much fat I've lost but in the week of taking them I have gone down 2lbs. My abs are more defined for sure.

TL;DR: Clean energy, no jitters, still have an appetite but not to where I want to eat an entire pizza after I workout. 10/10 would burn fat again.

title: Works great, but the price gouging easily kills it

I personally need a lot of water to dilute it to a less hardcore flavor, but it tastes great when diluted and put in ice water and so it's great to sip on throughout the hours. HOWEVER, the cost of these things is absurd. This is the most expensive salt packet (average 3x to 5x the cost per packet [~$1.60 ea] versus others) I've ever bought and I'm not sure if I'll continue with much of any purchases after this. I might have a few on hand for a long hike as they do stay good over long periods of time, but definitely not making this the standard.

title: Like Using Nothing at All
text:
I have been using this detergent for nearly a month and, as of yesterday, I must say that my suspicions were confirmed--this product has been like using nothing at all!

Over the past seven years, I have used many different types of green laundry detergents. All have cleaned with varying effectiveness but none were ever as good as non-green detergents. I am okay with that. From it, I've learned the importance of using stain treatment and laundry boosters. So, as you can see that I am not oblivious to how these green detergents clean.

In my opinion, Nature's Simply Clean has been one of the worst performing laundry detergents that I've tried. When used as directed, it consistently caked in the dispenser and I was left with the nagging feeling that my clothes were not coming out as clean as they had when I used Planet and Charlie's Soap. Both of those detergents were very good at cleaning my laundry. . .but Charlie's was exceptional for my cloth diapers and towels! Prior to transitioning over to Nature's Simply Clean, I had found a perfect routine and amount of detergent to get all of my clothes "clean", smelling fresh and stains about 90% out. The reason why I wanted to give Nature's Simply Clean a try was because I wanted additional fragrance--which Charlie's does not have. I was hoping that it would add something to the faint smell of the 7th Generation Lavender Fabric softener that I've been using (I love for my clean sheets to have a fragrance).

Well, I must say that this detergent was a complete fail in every way that I could have imagined. First, the fragrance was barely noticeable on my laundry when I removed it from the washer. . .and once dried, there was virtually no lingering scent. The thing that got me the most was that my laundry never seemed clean. Stains were rarely removed--maybe slightly faded--and they did not have the crisp feeling to which I have become accustom when using Charlie's Soap. I assumed that this was primarily due to the added oils (i.e, coconut, olive, palm and essential), which Charlie's does not have. On a positive note, I did notice that my laundry had less static (not static-free as stated on the container) compared to when I used Charlie's. Perhaps this was due to those extra ingredients.

In regards to the cleaning capabilities of Nature's Simply Clean, I must say that it has done a VERY poor job of cleaning my laundry. Despite adding it directly to the drum, its effectiveness was still subpar. My whites never appeared to be cleaned. Most of my children's socks remained dirt-stained--unlike when I used Planet and Charlie's. And, food stains. . .WOW! This detergent was a complete fail. If I did not use pretreatment and manipulation, the stains would be consistently left behind. Yesterday while I was preparing to put away my kiddos laundry, I noticed that any food stain that I did not pretreat (and scrub) was left behind. The worst part was when I checked my daughter's leggings and had a solid bit of food (ex. like syrup) still attached! Additionally, the knees were still dirty from her crawling around on them. That alone was beyond unacceptable. Lucky for me though, I had already gotten the memo and ordered a new detergent to try--Savvy Green. It arrived right on time. . .and I rewashed ALL of my kiddos laundry from the week that had been washed with the Nature's Simply Clean. So far, so good! It removed over 90% of the stains that the Nature's Simply Clean left behind. And like the Charlie's Soap, it left them feeling and smelling "clean." Now, only time will tell how well it will work on all of my laundry and if it will supersede Charlie's!

So, based on the addition of fragrance and the inability to clean simple stains, I rate Simply Clean Lavender Vanilla Dream a 2 out 5. Despite the lack of residual scent left post-drying, I decided to give this detergent a 2, instead of a 1, because I love the idea of using essential oils in green detergents for fragrance.

title: Great quality and fit, but a little warm
text:
I ran across the meo lite mask and needed to try it because to my knowledge it’s the only mask that uses wool as it’s filter, which just sounds awesome. Also this mask is supposed to do a great job filtering coronavirus, basically as well as an n95 or kn95, but is reusable to save costs if you’re just using it to run to the market every so often.

A little background on me: I currently live in an area that is hard hit with coronavirus. I usually only use homemade masks because I have a pronounced nose and wear glasses and store bought masks really have not fit well. I’ve been looking for a better filtering reusable mask since kn95s also do not fit me well.

The meo lite mask feels well built. There are simple adjustments on the ear loops and the fabric is thick, soft, and well sewn. The filters themselves are also think and replaceable. They feel a lot more substantial than most reusable filters I’ve used, and the pocket where you place the filter is secure, much better than Velcro I’ve seen other reusable masks use.

Wearing the mask is a little warm probably due to the wool, since it’s winter it hasn’t bothered me. It doesn’t feel like wool, and you don’t actually have the filter against your face so if wool itches you that shouldn’t be a problem. The mask is easy to breath through as well and for me it formed a solid seal around my face without fogging my glasses.

The one downside I found is the medium mask does not cover under my chin. I personally prefer masks to hug the bottom of my chin because just feels more secure to me. text:
So here are my initial impressions.

First I want to address a comment made by another reviewer. The reason the thing will keep beeping is because it is above the selected temperature. So, if your water is at 105 and you select 95, it will beep till it cools down. A little annoying. But at least it stops eventually.

I do not like the fact that you cannot select the temp down from current temp. You must cycle through the entire upper range before it cycles back to lower temp. Up and down arrows would have been much better.

I really wish there were cutouts for your calves. Since the tub is pretty tall it gets a little uncomfortable. From all the other ones I’ve looked at, I didn’t notice any with cutouts but I just might take my dremel to mine.

Massagers feel pretty good, bubbles seem to just add a little bit of sound, but whatever, they aren’t jets. Lol

The temp control is awesome. If you want hot water, this thing will do it!

I’ll probably remove the wheels since it sits so high already, might cut out some holes for my legs.

Overall, pretty good, I’ll dock a star for the lack of up/down arrows for temp selection.

title: The Perfect Heated Buddy for those days that I'm not Feeling Well!
text:
[[VIDEOID:a8affc5edc42cd13b0e53fa0cc3ed00c]] [[VIDEOID:b9aa00a6d71a1e8a5399ef305d52a7e7]] The Transparent Hot/Cold Water Bottle by NIPPOO comes with a cozy Deer design Knit Cover. It measures twelve by eight inches in height and width. The bottle is a transparent blue color and the cover is black and white in color. The bottle is made of Thermoplastic Polyurethane. I tried doing a search on this and know it is a type of plastic but what I don't know is, whether it's a toxic plastic or not. When I initially took it out of its package, there was a very strong plastic smell to it, but after several uses, the smell was not as strong. At the top of the bottle, there is a white plastic screw on cap. When I was younger and living with my parents, my mother used to fill up a wine bottle with hot water, and we would wrap it in a towel and keep it close when we weren't feeling well. Well this NIPOO hot water bottle is a much better way to use for medicinal purposes. It does appear to be a heavy duty bottle that will last a long time and once I put the cover on it, those old memories of home come rushing back. The bottle needs the cover and combined they make for the perfect heated buddy. So, this combination works great for my needs and helps me feel better. I do recommend this Transparent Hot/Cold Water Bottle by NIPOO.
I received the Transparent Hot/Cold Water Bottle at a discount, in exchange for an unbiased opinion. This review is 100% my own.

title: My eyelashes are amazing after using this!
text:
I am IN LOVE with my eyelashes. I used to have great eyelashes when I was in highschool but after having children- and now being 30 years old, my eyelashes were not my best feature. 2 months ago I started using Rapidlash which really helped my lashes grow longer. After seeing the increase in length I started to be more interested in getting a lash lift. After watching several videos on youtube I decided I could do it myself. Disclaimer- I did go to cosmetology school so I already feel comfortable with this type of a product.

This kit includes so many items- everything you could possibly need (well, I did use some q-tips as well) and a lot of pieces that I didn't use too. I recommend doing 1 eye at a time and taking your time to be very careful to not get any solution in your eye.
-I used the largest size of the pink silicone molds and cut them to fit my eyelid.
-I put a little glue on my eyelid and a little glue on the back of the silicone mold. I waited a minute or two for it to get tacky then placed it on my eyelid as close to my lash line as I could and then held it in place for a couple of minutes to make sure it was glued. I had a slight problem with the edges not staying glued down but this didn't negatively affect the perming for me.
-I then put some of the glue on the silicone mold and waited a minute for it to get tacky.
-I then used the metal tweezers to glue my eyelashes onto the mold making sure they were all straight on the mold and fanned out evenly (this is very important as it will be permed the way they are placed onto the mold- so don't rush through the step). I used a little extra glue to make sure all eyelashes were stuck in place.
-I then put on solution A (perming solution) with one of the green "brushes" that came with the kit. Once applied I set my alarm for 11 minutes.
-After 11 minutes I used a damp q-tip to wipe off Solution A, redampening the q-tip with each wipe to get the solution off.
-I then applied solution B (neutralizing solution) in the same manner as solution A was applied- again setting my alarm for another 11 minutes.
-After 11 minutes, I used a new damp q-tip to wipe off solution B.
-I then applied solution C (glue remover) with a q-tip. Once the eyelashes were loosened from the silicone mold I then used the solution to remove the mold from my eyelid. I ended up having a lot of sticky residue that wasn't fun to get off but was totally worth it.
-solution D is supposed to help "restore" your eyelashes- I'm not sure it really does anything...

With all perms you don't want to use any other chemical or cleaner on it for the first 24-48 hours so I would not recommend washing your face directly after. I did get in the shower and they were exposed to the water with no problems.

It has now been 2 weeks since I have done my eyelashes as I have not touched my eyelash curler in those two weeks. My eyelashes have a more natural "c" curl to them instead of a crimped curl that an eyelash curler gives. I'm 100% happy with the eyelashes I have right now. They seriously are amazing!! I also recommend getting a "tweezerman" metal eyelash comb for when you apply mascara, it really helps to get the clumps out and keep your eyelashes straight and fanned out.

There is enough product in this kit to do your eyelashes dozens of times- well worth the money. The pink silicone pads you can just wash off and reuse.

title: Single Button Operation is not Ideal
text:
Bought this to replace an older one (from different manufacturer) that started to develop battery problems. This one certainly works and does what it says. It's also well built and does not feel cheap. However, there are 2 things I don't like about it.

1. This model (FTV40D) has only 1 button, which cycles between Low-Medium-High-Off. If you want to take it out of your mouth before the tank is empty, and for instance you are on the low setting, you must cycle through the higher intensity modes before reaching the off position. Cycling those higher powered modes might be too strong for comfort. And, taking out of your mouth while it's running will squirt water everywhere. My old one had separate power and mode buttons, which is more preferable in my opinion.

2. The charger is a (very) cheap wall-wart type which is a bit fiddly getting seated into the connector on the device for charging to engage. I had plugged it in for a few hours only to find it did not charge and had to wiggle and rotate it to get a good connection. I question the long-term durability. Further, the power connector is on the bottom of the flosser, which means the unit has to lay on its side while charging. For comparison, the one this replaced had an induction charging stand that was simple and no fuss- just set the device on the base and it starts charging.

If the above does not concern you, then you should be happy with this device.

title: After about three weeks of use the water started tasting funny, so I got out my hacksaw and cut ...
text:
I developed a phobia about tap water in the 1980s after I read an article about how every drop of water that comes out of your tap has been through the water system 17 times. At that time I bought a simple carbon filter that screwed right onto the kitchen sink spigot. After about three weeks of use the water started tasting funny, so I got out my hacksaw and cut the unit open, and it was literally full of raw sewage. It stunk to high heaven.
So, I love the portable reverse osmosis system I bought from Reverse Osmosis Revolution ten years ago, and I regularly buy replacement filters from them. After hearing about what happened in Flint Michigan, I can't figure out why everybody doesn't have a reverse osmosis system in their house. R. O. systems clean out something like 99% of lead and dozens of other toxic contaminants that creep into the water supply system.

title: Small price for life
text:
Failure of intubation is the nightmare for every body who is working with critical patients.
As a neonatologist,failure of intubation means potential loss of a baby and even a lifelong suffer for the whole baby family.
As NRP(neonatal resuscitation program)recommends intubation in less than 30 seconds;this may not be enough for junior doctors who feel depressed once they failed in intubation.
Intubation in the Labour room is of critical importance for a neonatologist,however tragedy may appear when you face a situation with a difficult intubation such as in cases with abnormalities in the upper airway or facial anomalies(as in Pierre Robin syndrome).
Videolaryngoscopy is of great help in such situations and will be a life saving tool.
The price despite high,isn't comparable to the priceless baby life.
Videolaryngoscopy also is of great help in teaching intubation for junior doctors who are eager to see the beautiful view of the larynx to insert there first ETT(endotracheal tube)
This laryngoscope should be available in every unit that deals with critical patients and also in every operation room.
The reason that I didn't give five stars that I didn't try it personally to write a full review based on actual experience with the product

title: Just don’t!
text:
Im so confused sometimes about Amazon products. This one had me stumped. White tea is my fav of smells. I have 3 different diffusers and ise high quality oils. Im no dumb dumb when it comes to smells.

This concoction- is white tea mixed with a chemical. It’s like a cleaner solution. You can barely smell it but it’s there. I have 4 Maltese dogs and if I spray this near them or on their beds- they go In to a sneezing frenzy. It’s scary. They sneeze and. Act weird too long.

When sprayed on the sofa etc- the smell is nice but it’s all oil with that big t of chemical something. So if your wondering how this works- it’s like spraying scented olive oil around your house and on your bed - linens etc.

The smell does last on the fabric a day or so. But don’t expect it to be in the air. You have to really shove your nose in to that blanket and smell it. The spray does NOT mask smells. So if your blanket you just squirted smells like wet dog- it will still smell like wet dog mixed with white tea and some weird chemical something smell.

I really can’t wrap my head around this concept. Spraying smelly oil mixed with chemical that doesn’t last more than a day or so- around your home and on things. To each their own I suppose but this is not my cup of tea.

text: My partner is a pretty heavy smoker, and it can be frustrating walking around with the smell trailing him wherever we would go, especially dealing with my asthma and how any remaining particles can irritate my throat and lungs even up to an hour afterwards. It gets into fabrics, hair, any porous surface you can think of, and it can be pretty frustrating no matter how careful he tries to be with cleaning up and using sprays and whatnot. This wonderful little tube, however, makes everything a million times better. There is next to no odor at all apart from what is actually lit, no smoke at all comes out the end after being passed through the charcoal beads, and you can't even tell he's been smoking afterwards with a breath mint or two. The smell is gone from the house since it is no longer rubbing off on the furniture and I've been able to deep clean, and KEEP clean, everything fabric. No more irritation, and I can give him bear hugs anytime I want. Most importantly, I can go back to stealing his sweaters without smelling like an ashtray and having a coughing fit for half an hour. Highly recommend!

title: Clinical Trial is useless as described
text: Lots of nonsense in the "Clinical Trial" section, if you are familiar with clinical trials.  A clinical trial in which all participants use the product being tested has no control group, and is statistically useless - no useful results can be scientifically drawn from it.  No details are made about if or where the clinical trial was published, which means that you can't review it yourself and in all likelihood nobody has.  Finally, note that it was a "double-blind study on the USC Campus", which means they probably just set up a booth in a public space and have no actual university affiliation.  Conveniently, no university can sue them because "USC" can refer to multiple universities (University of South Carolina?  University of Southern California?)

title: Decent product but NOT great without modifications!!!
text: How it works, and why it's useful seems to be the question. There are two little probes. You will place the tips of the probes at the fill level desired. When the liquid makes contact with the two probes, it completes the micro circuit and sounds the alarm. Who needs it is the question? Some older people with poor eye sight, "like my grandmother." Perhaps the blind, if they don't want to stick their geeky fingers into their drink. My wife when she fills the bath and forgets she's running it. The problem is that the alarm is not loud enough. Sometimes she doesn't hear it. It would be great if there were contacts to plug in an external speaker to it. I opened mine up and soldered in speaker ports on all three and have made probe extenders. I use one on the duck pond. I use one on the horse trough. I use one for filling water drums and the bathtub. This item frees me up to do other things while they fill without overflowing. To those people who will say there are auto fill float devices for the horse trough and duck pond. I change my duck water every three days and clean the pond. I do the same for the horse trough. I don't want to dump a full trough; "it's heavy!" To those that will criticize my water consumption, I'm on a 14 foot shallow well for the lawn and animals. The water I dump will percolate back to the water table in less than a week and the rocks and mineral scrub the water to its formal glory. I'm on solar, so there is no electric waste to run the pump either.

title: They Do Work!
text:
I'm a streamer, and one of my biggest problems while gaming is getting motion sick when I play a first-person game. Within minutes I'll feel so sick that I can't play, and then will continue to feel nauseated for the rest of the night.

I ordered the double pack of the Sefudun Motion Sickness Patches with some big hopes and small doubts. I'm pleased to report that they do in fact work! They're easy to apply, and stay in place well. It's super obvious that you're wearing them, so if I have my hair up you can plainly see them behind my ears (I was uncomfortable wearing them around my navel). Also, if you're someone who has complicated sensory feelings, this might be hard for you. For me, it felt the same as feeling a tag sticking me on the back of my shirt, and I kinda couldn't wait to take them off. Since I only need them for short periods, I can deal with that bit, but I don't know that I'd be able to wear them multiple days.

I think this is definitely something good to keep on hand if you have motion sickness, though.

title: Fall out every night. Too soft.
text:
They fall out easily. I have normal sized ears. I've used earplugs, nightly, for decades. They are soft and comfortable, but perhaps too soft and comfortable. Maybe I'll try two per ear tonight. I would prefer a larger, less soft product. I'm looking for a Flents product that fits this bill for a while now. I had some a few years ago. I'm not concerned with the sensation of "I can feel something in my ear." In fact, not feeling something in my ear would bother me and keep me awake. I will stick with a foam-style ear plug for nightly use. For sleeping, plunger-style plugs feel weird, and they are too $ for daily use. Silicone plugs work well, but get dirty quickly, and, like plunger-style, too $ for nightly use. Silicone plugs are fantastic for swimming.

I would use the "Super Sleep Comfort" plugs for occasionally firing a gun. Just a few shots though. Otherwise, I'd use professional ear protection. Outdoors, taking them in and out, they get dirty really quickly. They would be useful at a loud concert or sporting event. Plunger-style plugs work well for shooting guns and cutting wood, but, like foam, just for a short amount of time. I have Husqvarna ear protectors. They are great! Highly recommend them. Your ears will thank you.

title: Works exactly as expected
text:
I really like this as I like to do a Epsom salt and or baking soda food soak now and again and I just wanted something simple with a handle and had hoped for something taller so that I could have water up around my ankles. This is perfect! Very easy to use, large enough for my odd wide in the toe feet. I haven't had my husband see if his feet would fit length wise yet, but I think they would, this is fairly good sized.

I was especially pleased with the way it pours. When done you can pour the water easily out of the heel side as there is a bit of a notch in the toe side in the lip of the "bucket" to tip and pour everything out, then rinse and slosh with some soapy water and rinse out clean and let it air dry before the next use. After a few uses I will clean it a little more thoroughly with a rag or possibly even see how it fairs in the dishwasher. Anyway, when you pour the water out nothing dribbles down the sides or anything, the foot/bottom of the bucket stays dry unless you've gotten it wet or set it in a puddle yourself.

The only thing that I wish was different was the ridge down the middle of the bottom. I am guessing this is more so built in support to make the bucket more sturdy, but it forces you to keep your feet straight forward, whereas I would much rather be able to move them around more, but like I said, that is very minor. Oh, and there's also little arch support bumps along the middle, not a high enough arch support for my feet, but probably would be for most. Also, large bumps, kind of like pebbles on the bottom, I imagine this is to keep your feet elevated so that the soak will get to the bottoms of your feet. Unless you are standing in the "bucket" they are very comfortable.

title: Use them for anything but pills.
text:
I bought the set to pack away in several bags for grab-and-go convenience while traveling. I can honestly say I'm not pleased with these. The material is sturdy, the dividers are convenient and the colors are nice, but those are the only good things.

For one, even after a few weeks of having these, I could never remember which side was up, and which side was down. Both sides look the same and you have to remember the latch orientation. Choose wrong, and your pills end up spilling out into the lid and on to the floor. And like with most situations, the bread always lands jam-side-down.

The latch itself is not sturdy and comes off at the lightest touch. More than once I've had it come undone in my purse and had to completely clean out the purse, sort the pills and put them back in their respective compartments. That's more work than I'm willing to do every few days.

The gasket seal is more for show than anything. One of the first things I did was run the (empty) pill case under tap for about 30 seconds and check the inside. Although the case didn't fill with water, there was definitely water in there. It only takes a few drops to completely destroy your pills. Since it didn't manage to pass this test, I didn't even try to fully submerge them.

On the plus side, they're good for storing other things. I've removed the dividers completely and the cases have been relegated to my toolbox to hold spare picture hanging nails, odd screws and spare small drill-bits.

title: Met my expectations
text:
I'm very happy with this Cellto hair straightener brush.
It definitely met my expectations.

The brush is great. It is easy to use. You can control the temperature in increments of five degrees Celsius.
You can easily switch the display from Celsius to Fahrenheit by pressing both the temperature up and down buttons at the same time.
The digital display tells you the heat setting and the exact temperature as it heats up. The rubber tips on the bristles and the outside bristles make it difficult to burn yourself by accident.
It's not super heavy. It does take some practice to get good at using it.

When I first started on my hair, I had no idea what strategy to use.
I ended up taking large sections and smoothing those out. Then I split those large sections into small sections so I could get close to the roots.
It took me a long time to get everything done to my satisfaction this first time, but I'm sure it will go faster next time since I know what I'm doing now.

It took about fifteen minutes to get through everything the first time, which would normally take about half an hour to get my entire head, which is still about half the time of a regular flat iron.
I could speed up the process and get straighter hair by using a higher heat setting, up to 450°F.
At least at this temperature, my hair wasn't as straight as I get it with a regular hair straightener, but I like the way it looked.
It has just the slightest hint of wave to it, especially near the tips.
My hair has a tendency to fluff up, but it wasn't too fluffy when I was done.
It had just the right amount of body. It was still frizzy, but I expected that.
My hair is frizzy most of the time. I was able to smooth down the frizz by using just a couple of drops of argan oil.
I was satisfied with these results.
I had to clean out my straightener brush when I was done.
I shed excessively. So of course I had to pull a bunch of hair out of the brush, but I have to pull hair out of every brush I ever use.
Oil in my hair left some residue on the straightener brush. It came off very easily.
At least for me, this straightener brush does not require any more cleaning than any of my other heat stylers.

My final thoughts are that this won't entirely replace my old straightener, but it will be a nice alternative.
I still need my classic flat iron when I just want to fix my bangs and when I want my hair to be perfectly straight.
This brush is great when I need to straighten my hair but still want a slight wave.

Plus, it doesn't leave crimps like a regular straightener does if you accidentally hold it an angle for too long.
It's just great to have another good option for doing my hair.
Awesome set up!  10/10

title: THE most AFFORDABLE fountain pen
text:
These are THE most affordable fountain pens that work I have ever used. The nib and nib structure are so well made, these will work as student pens. The reservoir is tiny. Again, as a person who loves a fine line to interact with text... these are magnificent little gems. I recommend them for first time fountain pen users. Make yourself some pen flush- 80% water, a couple drops of dish detergent, and the rest ammonia... rinse it through when you switch colors of ink, or if your pen sits for a long period of no use... flush after with water alone, and you will get years of fabulous use from these sweet, elegant little numbers.

title: Very good light...
text:
I generally review 3 kinds of stuff: (1) knocks my socks off, (2) annoys me, or (3)has some feature that hasn't been mentioned but I think should be. This lamp doesn't fit into any of these categories but it's a good lamp. One feature that I like is the 2-light-level switch. I often use the lower level to augment available daylight and the upper level when I'm reading with an overhead light on. I'm not fond of using it as the sole light source. This is partly due to the fact that the light from the lamp looks unusually cold (think of the "white", glary headlights of a modern car). And partly it is due to the smallish "pool" of light given off by the lamp. If you're reading a book or knitting, a small pool of light works well. For a newspaper, however, not very. Would other lamps work better? Probably not.
Bottom line: Am I happy with it? Yes. I like the little platform thing, which I use for a pad and pen. I like the adjustability of the light (the goose-neck feature, which, because it's a floor lamp, I won't change very often). The whole thing seems sturdy and well-made. I like having two light levels. The diffuser that attaches under the bulb to prevent the light from shining directly in your eyes is also a nice touch.
It just didn't knock my socks off.

The cushion is a little too thick that it disrupts the natural curvature built into my chair. My back is now resting at a bump in the curve where it fit perfectly along my spine before. The cushion also slips forward constantly which is incredibly annoying. When it slips, I notice I start slouching which causes me even more back pain, thus I am adjusting it all the time. This may be unique just to the chair I own, but I would definitely consider these factors before buying. For the time being, I've thrown my cushion on the floor and my back is already feeling better.

title: Regional Umbrian Cuisine As It Was Intended To Be
text: Food is never better than when it fulfills its intended function as nourishment for the body and a pleasure for the soul.  And nowhere does food fill that intention better than in the diverse regions of Italy.  A Kitchen with a View embodies the simplicity, the rustic elegance, and the joy of life that is the Umbrian country side.  Letizia Mattiacci recreates the atmosphere of her renowned cooking school and inn on the outskirts of Assisi with recipes and stories that speak not only to the palate but also to the heart.  Her love of the region shines through on every thoughtfully written page.  In an age where Italian food on the international stage has too often morphed into unnecessary culinary complication, Letizia maintains a grounded, realistic approach, focusing on the quality of the ingredients, the direct manner of preparation, and the seasonal nature of rustic fine cooking.  The photographs bring the entire book together, singing the chorus of what is the real, true Umbria. If you love to cook regional Italian foods, then this book must be in your kitchen.  Brava, Letizia!

title: Needs a bigger velcro area
text:
Based on the measurements I ordered the xxl (my waist is about 33"). It is slightly large, and not as adjustable as I had hoped. I probably should have gone down a size.

I found the material the front half was made out of to be very itchy, but that might just be me. I wish the outer elastic straps could overlap and still stick to each other, but they need to be attached to the small velcro area. The velcro is only 8.5" by 3.75". It would be better if it was a larger (taller) piece as it seemed to be rolling up and down a bit, especially when bending.

While I was able to tighten it fairly well, I didn't think it had a very symmetrical profile. It's also pretty thick in the front and the velcro doesn't feel super secure if I over tighten it, so I don't think I'd be very comfortable wearing it under clothes.

All that said, the boning in the back felt very strong and I did think it gave me good back support. It's also way lighter and more breathable than a latex or neoprene style trainer. It may just be that I have the wrong body shape and type for it. It would probably work best on a less curvy woman with a shorter torso.

I was fortunate to receive this item at a discount, provided I was honest and unbiased in my review.

title: Best Bang For Your Buck --- 3 In One Muscle Massage Roller!
text:
The Massage Pro 3-In-1 Foam Roller comes in --- guess what? 3 main parts: 1) Papa roller (outside), Mama roller (middle), and Baby roller stick (center).

My wife and I have several other muscle rollers, but the 3 in 1 is the most versatile of the bunch, with the added bonus of saving storage space. The rollers combine to form a trio of powerful tools to help your muscles recover from work outs and massage targeted aching muscles. The big selling point to me is the convenience of 3 different rollers in one package.

If you're reading this you are probably familiar with the benefits of roller therapy, so I'll concentrate on the goods and a few not-so-goods of this particular roller set. The design and build of the individual rollers is very good and works it's magic as expected. Unfortunately our set was both TOO easy AND TOO difficult to take apart. Let me explain --- the textured orange Mama roller slipped out of the outer Gray Papa roller like a screaming kid in a water slide tube. However, the smallest Baby roller stick with the handles and pull-out strap takes a lot of tugging and pulling AND more tugging to release from Mama roller. The strap is a definite necessity to pull the inner 2 rollers apart! Once apart, the individual rollers are great!

In all fairness, our set was perhaps an anomaly and the tight/loose thing was for our entertainment, and ours alone. ;-)

Might I suggest to the designers some way of incorporating a way to easily carry this as one unit by enabling the strap to be used as a carrying strap to transport in the vertical position? As it stands now, Baby roller and Mama roller would travel conveniently as one (because of the super-tight fit), but Papa roller is Waayyy too loose-y goose-y and will slide off.

Pros:
>Convenient "nesting" storage
>3 rollers in 1

Cons:
>Fit of "nesting" rollers could be better
>Need easier way to transport as one piece

This review is my opinion - and your experience can be totally different - depending on your applications. I received this product at a discount in exchange for my honest opinion. I'll try to report back if updates are needed over the months ahead. If you have any questions please feel free to contact me and I'll try my best to answer in a timely manner.

title: A love hate relationship
text:
If you're reading all these reviews you'll notice a common theme. This alarm takes a lot of time to master! It took me about 2-3 hours, in between tv watching, to figure out how to work all the functions. I was so sure I had gotten a lemon & was ready to pack it back up to get a refund. Luckily, or unluckily, I decided to keep trying to work with it & then finally figured it all out.

I do LOVE it. I love waking up to LIGHT! I was worried the strength wouldn't be bright enough for me but it is. I like that there are nature sound features although I really think they could have done much better in the quality! I only use 2 of the sounds. I like that it has a radio feature where you can program stations or wake up to them. I love being able to also use it as a stand alone lamp without taking away more precious dresser space.

What do I hate? I HATE the backlight display! It is way too bright to sleep in. You have the option to turn off that light but you do not have the option to dim it. Therefore, I sleep with it turned off & can not see what time it is so I have to use a second clock for time reference! This alarm is so great for me with the huge exception of the back-light & COMPLICATED function features.

Would I buy it again? Probably. The biggest hassle, in the long run, is the bcklight. I can live with having an extra clock in the room.
