title: Try the plain flavor!
text: While I appreciate all the comments about the flavors this product comes in, why are people complaining that it's too sweet?  Just buy the plain and sweeten it to your taste - it's so simple.  I make a basic smoothie with flaxseed milk, a big dose of cinnamon and another of turmeric (antinflammatories do wonders for my little bit of osteoarthritis pain in my fingers), and small squirt of Jordan's Salted Caramel sugar-free coffee flavoring.  I've made pumpkin spice with 2 tablespoons of pumpkin puree and pie spice, I've added a  dollop of nut butter and a bit of mashed banana or applesauce - the possibilities are endless, and you control the level of sweetness.  I put the powder and my spices and add-ins into a small glass bowl, add a bit of flax milk, and beat the heck out of the mixture with a wire whisk - I could also use my little beater thing which I've forgotten the name of, but I'm too lazy - the whisk works fine (it's actually from my electric mixer!).  I put the liquid  in a sports shaker I found in my pantry cupboard (!), top it off with the rest of the flax milk to 8 ounces, shake it once more for good luck, and drink up.  I love this product.

title: Like this product
text:
I bought 2 bottles of this one for myself and one for a friend who said she liked Elderberry supplements but was not finding the one she liked anymore and I thought I would try it as well. I deal with a number of issues one of which is arthritis and 3 bad disks, one in my back and 2 in my neck. I take a medication for them but it alone does not always prevent my pain. I bought this primarily for general health but am finding that it seems to help with the inflammation as the pain caused by the bad disks has lessened since I started taking this product. I dropped the rating by 1 star for one reason only. The company claims to offer a free bottle when you purchase one for trying the product. When they arrived, there was a sticker on one of the bottles with a web site and stated that I could get 2 free bottles. The website then stated that I could only get 1 bottle free and I had to leave a review. So I left the review. Then I got an email saying for my free bottle I needed to leave a review on Amazon, screen shot it and send it to them and still it only talked about 1 bottle. I honestly, don't care about the free bottle but this is getting to a point of being ridicules. I like the product so I may even order again but if you are going to make free offers, then 1. you need to live up to what you claim. Period. 2. If you wanted an Amazon review, I should not have needed to fill out the review on your site and you should have linked me to my order and then just seen who is leaving reviews on your product. I should not have to screen shot it and email it to you.
So I no longer care about the free bottle. But if you are going to make free claims for goodness sake live up to what you offer. But again I did find the product to be a good quality.

title: Poor customer service from WHC ruins a decent product!
text:
Review is for Citrulline Malate Powder 500 g (167 Servings) sold by Wholesale Health Connection (WHC).

The powder itself is ok. Dissolves easily in water and seems to do its job. So why only two stars?

a) The bag was beat up - crumpled, dirty & unsightly. Like it was in storage forever. They could've at least dusted it off before shipping. The bag contains a product for human consumption, I expect that it looks clean & hygienic at the minimum. Minus one star for dirty packaging.

b) The expiry date was only 11 months away (May 2018). This a 500g bag which usually lasts me a year or so, and I still have my old stock that is good for another couple of months. IMO 11 months is too short an expiry date for a health & fitness supplement product. I only noticed the expiry date on the pack while discarding the bag after I used it for a few days and transferred the product into a glass jar. It was bit late to return it. If I saw it before I opened the bag, I'd have returned it for sure. My previous bag from BulkSupplements had a nearly 3-year expiry period ending in 2019. So now I am trying to use up the WHC product before expiry. Minus another star for the short expiry period.

c) I docked the 3rd star for poor customer service. To clarify, even though I was disappointed with the above two points I didn't complain and was minding my business. But two weeks after the purchase I got an email from WHC asking for feedback on the product. I told them about the dirty bag and short expiry date and I expected them to do something about it. Instead they simply said "Sorry about your issues, but we can't do anything. Contact Amazon."

Why did they contact me and ask for feedback if they won't do anything about it? I think they just want to hear positive feedback and since mine was not good, they ignored it. They also asked me to leave a review on Amazon about it, so here I am with my review.

There are plenty of other vendors on Amazon & other marketplaces who supply the same product at similar prices and provide much better customer service if you are unhappy with the product. It is all made in China anyway, and these vendors just buy in bulk and pack it in their bags.

I will not be buying any product from "Wholesale Health Connection" again.

title: If you want to get well again
text:
This is a cross-review of Samsara's Lyme and Biofilm formulas: After reading others' reviews, I debated whether or not to go the "liquid" route for medication, which is what these herbal powder formulas become when adding water or another liquid of choice. Liquid medications and I usually do not get along. At 53-yo I still have to hold my nose and chug 'em down to get it over with quickly.

I gave careful consideration to the comments about the taste because of the heavy concentration of Stevia. I use Stevia and I know what it means to use too much. Long story short, the cost of antibiotics on my body and pocketbook far outweigh the costs of gagging on liquids or the possibility of Stevia overkill. The plus side to purchasing the Samsara Lyme and Biofilm herbals is that I recently read Stevia is proving to be a Lyme bacteria killer. I decided to go for broke, so to speak.

First, I tried the two formulas with Keifer thinking the sour/salty flavor would tone down the sweetness of the Stevia. It's okaaaay, but nooooot great. Didn't do that again. Next, I tried it with 100% juice - cran-raspberry and that still didn't float my boat (at all). Didn't do that again either. Then, the bells went off! (You already know that Lyme Disease causes cognition issues... slow thinking, right?)

I am a decaf (unsweetened) iced tea drinker. Wow .. that was a game changer! I held my nose at first, but discovered it really wasn't necessary. Drinking it this way reminded me of buying (won't mention brand name) bottled teas at a convenience store; not really tea IMHO, but they work if you are thirsty enough. Same incentive in this case, but replace the incentive outcome with "if you desperately want to get well again the natural way".

I didn't go full out according to Samsara's recommended dosing; rather, I followed the same LLMD treatment protocol (M, W, F 1st week of 4-week cycle) as if I was taking the prescribed antibiotics. I had very mild- to almost unnoticeable herxing which was "mildly tired, but still didn't have to go back to bed" the day after dosing.

The founder's story of being a Lyme patient really was the number one factor in deciding to go this route. To me, that is credibility enough. Plus, judging by the success I've had thus far, I'm pretty sure I am headed in the right direction with having taken this route. Incidentally, I started with the 2 oz package to be on the safe side, and now I can safely say I will move up to the more economical 8 oz. bag with my next purchase. Blessings to you on your road to recovery!

title: Ceramic Coating in a Tin Can
text:
[[VIDEOID:575eb85ad33e140d7e7cdfba32c83395]] This is by far my favorite paint protection product I would recommend on any car as of now! I have tried other products in the past, but nothing has come close to this Soft99 Fusso Coat in terms of protection, longevity, and value for the money. However, there are some tips and information that you will need to know before, during, and after applying this product.

Make sure you wash the car by using a strip wash. I used dish soap to remove the previous Soft99 Fusso Coat wax, and it surprisingly held up multiple hits which are quite good. Use an iron remover and clay bar on the car to remove any further decontamination. Dry the car and inspect for any swirl marks, marring, and faded paint. Be sure to do an IPA wipe down before starting the compound and polish if necessary. I did both of these steps to the best of my ability with the tools I had. This process could take up nearly the whole day depending on the condition of the paint. After compounding/polishing the whole entire car, do one more IPA wipe down to remove any polishes and residue left on the paint so it is all fresh.

Before applying, be sure to soak the foam applicator and wring it out so it is slightly damp. That way, you will get a better application and use less production. Divide each large panel into sections like half a hood. I would apply the wax to different spots of the section before starting to move the product in a crisscross/cross-hatch pattern. Remember, less is more so twist the applicator a few times in the tin can and wipe off any excess wax in the tin can before starting. Apply a thin layer which is crucial to get the best performance out of this product. You can apply this product to 3-4 sections before having to buff off the first section of the car. Curing time for summer would be 5 minutes maximum and 10 minutes for winter. Ideally, you would want to buff off the wax in the 5-8 minute range. It is better to buff it off a little earlier than it is late because it will be difficult to remove the excess hard wax if left for too long. Be patient and take your time in this step.

If you want to, you can apply a second layer on top, but be sure to wait for at least 6 hours to let the first layer cure properly. If you do not have that much time, you can apply it after an hour, but it is highly recommended to wait at least 6 hours for the best results. You can apply as many layers as you want, but make sure to leave at least 6 hours per layer. You can safely use the Fusso Coat Speed and Barrier spray to wipe off any excess wax and boost the protection of the wax without interfering with the curing time of the product. Be sure to not apply any other types of waxes because it can compromise the water repellency of the wax. I recently contacted Soft99 about the usage of these products so be sure to take this information into consideration. You can also apply the wax on headlights, tail lights, and rims as well.

After 12 hours of fully curing, it is now safe for your car to be exposed to rain, dirt, and outside elements. One layer of this product should give you around 8-10 months of protection, assuming that you live in an area with relatively stable conditions and do not use the Speed and Barrier spray. With the spray, you may be able to reach around 10-12 months as the company has claimed. I applied 3 layers on my car which should give around 2-3 years of protection on the car which is the equivalent of a cheap ceramic coating. If you do reapply the wax every year, you could get up to 20 applications with one tin can on a mid-size sedan. This product is also extremely chemically resistant so dish soap, brake cleaner, and iron remover will not be a challenge for this product. For the value, it is amazing how this wax can deliver, and I would honestly recommend this product if you just want absolute value for protection that you would find on expensive ceramic coatings. The water beading and water sheeting are equivalent to these professional ceramic coatings. There is no other form of paint protection I would recommend for anyone. Of course, ceramic coatings, and especially graphene coatings will outperform the majority of waxes and paint sealants on the market. However, this wax is by far the best bang for your buck with a good price, exceptional, performance, and great durability that you can find on more expensive products!

The black version does have a little bit more fillers for black cars, and the older version has more solvents which does last a little longer. However, it doesn’t matter which ones you get for any color, and the new one probably only lasts like a month shorter but not by that much. Any Fusso Coat wax will work!

What I recommend is rinsing them off and then soaking them for an hour with normal lense solution inside a normal horizontal lense holder. It will hurt all day if you don't get all the residue off after cleaning them.

Besides that I would urge all contact owners to use this method to extend their lenses and prevent bacteria or calcium build up.

One final point: some prior have expressed concern about heavy metal poisoning due to the lead in bentonite clay. The manufacturer has a response on their website. title: Nerdwax, not just for nerds
text:
I have at times caught myself pushing my glasses back up my nose, especially when doing paperwork, since my face is constantly looking down of the desk. When I look up, my glasses have slipped from their regular comfortable position, and so it's time for the 'single finger spectacle repositioning maneuver'.

Nerdwax is a proprietary blend of beeswax and other cosmetic grade natural and organic ingredients which come in a lip balm style tube. It is applied to the nosepads of the glasses, to create a high friction layer which prevents the glasses from sliding down the nose. You can add as much or as little as you need depending on your daily needs. Use a little for a quiet day inside with the cat and a good book. Use a lot for mountain biking, beaver hunting or jet-skiing and other typical outdoor nerd activities.

Applying Nerdwax was very simple, but at first I wasn't sure how much to put on so I started out just adding a little bit to my nosepads. I had to reapply frequently to maintain the slip-proof layer and keep my glasses in place. The directions suggest that the more you apply the longer it lasts, but that didn't work for me. Whether I put on a thick or a thin layer, my glasses were sliding again within an hour.

Nerdwax definitely works, but it doesn't work for me for longer periods of time. But even with the regular applications, it does not leave any residue on my face or on my glasses, so using it 4 or 5 times a day doesn't do any harm.

Overall this product does a great job, and if they could get Nerdwax to last all day by making µs>1 (to use a nerdy science term) then it would definitely get a 5 slap review.

Disclosure: I received this item for free in exchange for the honest and unbiased review above.

title: Great quick breakfast on the go.
text:
I use this as a meal replacement in the morning as I don't take the time nor have the appetite for a conventional breakfast. Before this it was coffee and whatever I grabbed when I got to work, usually a leftover cookie or croissant sort of thing. I discovered this at my local co-op in single use packs for mixing with your beverage of choice. I use coconut or almond milk and a sport shaker, 2 minutes and I'm on my way. This 2.2 lb canister is much more cost effective than the smaller cans available locally, and MUCH more than the single use packs. Now I feel much more clear headed and energetic in the morning than I did on the caffeine and sugar diet.

The ingredient list is outrageous! They have packed every nutrient in the world into this stuff by the looks of it, from spirulina to schisandra root whatever that is. Seriously though, I was looking for a natural healthy protein shake and this delivers the goods without any refined sugar or carcinogenic sugar substitute, nor any nasty artificial chemicals at all. The flavor works for me, it's just sort of rich and malty when mixed with my milk substitutes. I can down an 8 oz (2 scoop) batch quickly, although the instructions suggest making 2 batches using 1 scoop each and taking it twice a day. One thing of note- only mix up what you intend to consume right away. The mix continues to thicken while sitting, after a few hours it becomes a gelatinous goop that you definitely don't want to drink.

title: We love our new white noise machine & highly recommend it!
text: For years we've been using an app on my iPad for white noise at night, and it works fine. But, oftentimes my wife goes to bed before I do, and I am still on my iPad in the other room. She complains to me that she can't fall asleep without the white noise. So I found this little white noise machine that checks all the boxes we have and more: it's small and very streamlined - doesn't take up a lot of space on the nightstand. It has both white noise (29 different sounds with volume control) and a ring of light with 7 different colors (plus a blended gradient display using all 7). The light is a really cool added feature that we don't get on the iPad - as a matter of fact, my wife also didn't like the fact that with the white noise app on the iPad, you also get a really bright picture that keeps her awake. The light on the Renpho machine is much more soothing & has an adjust button to make it as bright or dim as you would like (or you can turn off the light completely). The machine also has a timer with a choice of 30, 60 or 90 minute auto-off or you can leave it in continuous mode if you want the white noise & light setting all night. The only other feature that would be a good addition is if you could set the timer separately for the white noise vs. the light (we'd like the light for the first 30 minutes or so, and the white noise all night long for example). But that's a small quibble... We love our new white noise machine & highly recommend it!

title: Great Value
text:
I purchased this product to clean the dirty carpets and floor mats in my car. The car is a 2000 and had a variety of things making my carpet dirty. There was Sand, Old worn plastic/rubber, and dirt. The brush that comes with it has no issue picking up things from the carpet. The actual cleaner itself works pretty well and doesn't smell too chemically.

For $5, this removed almost every stain and discoloration my 20 year old carpets had. I would 10/10 recommend this to anyone looking for an affordable cleaner. I would not say it's anything crazy, however for it's price it definitely outperforms itself and will get the job done.

Here are my tips for using this product.
- Do a "dry" brush before you spray the cleaner. This will pick up anything on the surface and create less of a mess.
- This stuff dries kinda quickly. So be sure to spray an area that you plan to scrub within 1 minute.
- When the can is empty, keep the brush. This will allow you to have 2 different brushes for different applications.

title: Would have given 5 stars if I had spare screws!
text:
These glasses are super cute and I got tons of compliments on them during the two weeks that I was able to wear them!!
They came in nice packaging, the frames look to be much higher quality than they actually are, and they're heavier than I expected for such a cheap pair of glasses, so they FEEL like they're good quality too.
They work quite well for filtering blue light. I'm a law student and spend 69 hours a week staring at my laptop. Every day I wore these, I had noticeably fewer headaches throughout the day, rarely experienced eye redness/dryness, and even felt less fatigued in the evening.
HOWEVER... The other day, a screw fell out of one of the lenses (from the frontside of the frames) and I wasn't able to find it. Sadly, I can no longer wear them because I can't reattach the lens to the frame.
The glasses came with a nifty little screwdriver-type tool, but it doesn't really help me when I don't have a screw to screw-drive. So, it's possible that they normally come with extra hardware and it was just a fluke that my order didn't come with any...
Either way, I'm still stuck with these cute glasses that I can't wear anymore because of a missing screw :(

Overall, though, I would definitely give these glasses a 5-star rating if I had a way to fix mine!

title: Could be better
text:
So I bought this to replace an electric Primo bottled water pump that only lasted a year before the motor inside of it seized up and stopped pumping.

First thing you'll notice, is that every single word on the box is in spanish. It does have a factory seal on the box showing whether it's been opened or not, and every once in a while Amazon will send you something that someone else has already returned for whatever reason.
The data sheet inside of the box however was mostly in english... But there are absolutely no instructions telling you what tools you'll need or what the hole size needs to be.
Opening the box, I saw that packaging was non-existent and as if they just grabbed everything and threw it in the box and closed it up.

The control/pump box or enclosure is NOT UL listed and neither is the power supply. It's all pretty flimsy and feels cheaply made.
The plastic mounting block for the faucet is very poorly designed, because if you run the switch wire through the hole with the mounting screw and nut, you're going to pinch the switch wire and possible short the wire causing the pump to constantly run.

So... Since I wanted to drill the smallest hole possible in my sink, I removed the plastic mounting block all together and modified it to work without it.
In the sink is the faucet only, and since I had drawers that opened in front of the sink with plastic "cups" inside I mounted the switch as pictured.

Installation is very easy if you have experience with simple plumbing and an imagination.
I just received it today and after everything was hooked up the way that I wanted it, I tested it and it seemed to work good with no visible water leaks.

I live in the boonies and have well water which has a three stage water filter system plus a water softener, but I can still tasted the salt from the water softener so I use the five gallon jugs for coffee and all of that kinds of stuff...
So after I've gone through a few jugs and know that everything is still working good, I may update this review.

I don't expect a whole lot considering the price of what I got, but being that it plugs into the wall and is surrounded by water I would expect it to be at least UL listed and a little better quality.

title: Perfect solution for hair that won't keep a curl!!
text: This curling iron is amazing! I've been wanting to buy a similar product but the $100 price tag always held me back. I have very long hair and it never seems to hold a curl no matter how much product i put in it. With this curler i was able to curl all my ends and curl all my 4 yr old daughters hair in 15 mins the first time out of the box! It's been a few hours and the curls are still holding up beautifully with no product at all!! I was skeptical about this curler when it first arrived. It came in a plain white box with just a sticker saying the brand and name of the curler. It came with directions and 2 black velvet covered plugs/prongs that seem to fit into the curler where your hair goes. The directions don't mention using them at all so I have no idea what they're used for. The directions themselves are a bit vague but its pretty easy to figure out after a few attempts. You'd assume your hair feeds in from the ends up to the root but that's not the case. You need to place a small amount of hair in the machine starting at the root or half way down the strand, where ever you want your curl to start. Then the iron will wined up your hair from the starting point to the ends NOT THE ROOTS. I only had trouble once when i tried to use too much hair it snagged. The machine stopped immediately, then I unplugged the curler and was able to work my hair out of it. All in all its a wonderful curler and I'm very happy with my purchase.

text:
Bottom Line: well made and very comfortable

I am really happy with this purchase! I was originally hesitant to purchase an insole that I could not feel or test out before purchasing online but I am happy I took the leap and got these insoles. They are awesome and I already want to order another pair.

First of all, these insoles are very well made. I was happily surprised at the weight and thickness of these insoles. They are thick enough to provide adequate support but at the same time are not too thick so they fit in all the shoes I have tried putting them in. Additionally, the weight of them is indicative of their high quality. These are definitely not some flimsy insoles that you will have to replace soon after purchasing. I think these will last a long time, which makes the already great price even better. After looking around online, I think this price point is a great value, especially for such well made insoles!

Second of all, and most importantly, these insoles are incredibly comfortable! They are not made of foam like many of the other insoles on the market. Since these are made of gel, they really contour to every nook and cranny of your feet. Additionally, the insoles pop right back in to their original shape as soon as I take them off. The old foam pairs I used to have would start to lose their shape after even a few times wearing them.

I believe that these insoles run true to size. I usually wear between a 5.5 and 6.5 shoe size. So I purchased the size 5-6 and it is perfect.

The insoles arrived quickly and on time. Additionally, they arrived in perfect condition – they were well protected in packaging (the insoles were also in their own plastic zip-top bag to ensure that they arrived in perfect condition). These insoles look just as they do in the picture so there was no surprise there. I am very happy with the purchase of these insoles and would certainly buy another product from this company. text:
The reason I bought this brush was to clean the pollen on our vinyl siding house, fences and deck. I would always do it with a scrub brush and ladder in the past. I thought this was going to be the year to buy an electric power washer but too many shortfalls and questions left me thinking about options somewhere in between.

I could not be more happy with my choice of this well made and very affordable product. I just finished cleaning my siding and could not wait to share my review! I had read the brush head was small and had been voiced as a negative opinion in another review. The small brush actually made it easier to reach some nooks on my vinyl patio railings and posts. It was also of similar size to what I had used manually so worked great for me but if you are looking for a large brush to do a sweeping area, this is not it.

A fabulous feature that I didn’t realize when I ordered is it also has a pivoting head attachment so the brush can be set to any angle you choose. The handle has a nice quality foam grip that makes it comfortable to use and the telescoping feature couldn’t be easier, with two easy paddles to open and close for extensions. There is no turning the pole lefty loosely or righty tightly to get it to extend.

Extremely happy with my purchase! If this sounds like it suits your needs, don’t hesitate to buy it.

COLD SPIZ WORKS BETTER

It seems common sense that drinking a cold drink on a hot day would work better in terms of performance than a lukewarm drink........right?: Well I have been telling athletes to drink SPIZ as cold as possible for years during training or competition because I was pretty sure that would create a lower core body temperature which would enhance athletic performance under hot weather conditions. Well a study looking to scientifically answer that questioned was performed and published in the Medicine & Science, Sports & Exercise journal a few years back.

These researchers took eight healthy moderately active subjects who were NOT use to heat. These men were asked to cycle to the point of exhaustion in a laboratory set at 95 degrees Fahrenheit and 60% humidity. Every 3 minutes the subjects were asked to cycle a little faster and every 10 minutes they were given a beaker containing 100 ml of sugar free lemonade. One one occasion the temperature of the lemonade was 39 degrees Fahrenheit (cold) and on the other occasion the lemonade was 98 degrees (lukewarm).

The results revealed the subjects could cycle 63.8 minutes when drinking the cold lemonade and 52 minutes drinking the lukewarm lemonade on average. From the 30th minute on the skin temperature of the cold lemonade drinkers was 0.4 degrees cooler (confirming core body temperatures had to be lower as well) and their level of perceived exertion (another way of saying fatigue) was also significantly less across the 63.8 minute cycle time.

So this proves that drinking any sports drink including SPIZ as cold as possible will improve your performance and create less fatigue, in the above example just 3 degrees above freezing. That may be difficult in certain unsupported exercise conditions, but if you can use insulated bottles and add some ice when you mix your SPIZ up and drink it cold while exercising in warm or hot weather conditions.......you can expect to see a 10 -15% improvement in your race time.

That is huge of course!!

Until the next time may the breeze be always at your back!

title: Not as small as it seems, packaging just makes it seem like less than other deodorants
text:
Update: Scent is awful at the end of a day's wear. This won't do at all. Rubs off easily on fabric. Maybe this works well for others, but this one definitely isn't for me.

Value: Here's the kicker, it seems small. 2.47 oz seems like it isn't much but my old spice is 2.6 oz. The price is different, but not by much, about 3 grams in weight or less than 5% more than this deodorant. The form factor I think just makes it seem less. So the biggest barrier here is the price and visual presentation, but for those who want to minimize not just plastic but paper waste should appreciate this packaging as this is as minimal as you can get minus not using dyed and bleached paper.

Packaging: minimalism is good but my bar had signs of something pressing down on it, so it was somewhat crushed before arriving. Due to the minimal packaging there's bits of deodorant stuck to the box edges and lid flap. It was also kinda sweaty, there was a noticeable amount of moisture collected on the top when I opened it up.

Scent: I got the lavender bar, and while it does have some lavender to it, I notice this other smell like glue sticks. The lavender is good, reminds me of the lavender I used to grow on a farm years ago, but the glue smell bothers me a bit.

Application: I'm not sure if I am being too gentle but I read other reviews saying it doesn't last long so I gently applied it on a corner, a lot more gentler than I would with standard deodorants. I would prefer to have something to hold it with to apply it so I don't get any on my fingers. I ended up applying it to hair rather than directly on the skin but I felt like there was enough to put my arms down and move them back and forth to rub it in.

Overall: I'm going to keep looking at alternatives as well as learn how I can make my own deodorant from organic supplies and cut down the cost that way and minimize my carbon footprint by not ordering things from the other side of the world (made in New Zealand). For those who don't want to learn to make your own, this is a viable option but the fact that it has to be shipped all the way from New Zealand does mean there's a carbon footprint from shipping. You'll have that carbon footprint with almost everything, but probably not as much as you would with something shipped from an island country on the other side of the world. A good step in the right direction, so I certainly appreciate the intention.

title: Lots of positives for this little bulb
text:
I purchased a number of different LED lights to compare, including this 10.5W Philips LED. It seems like almost every LED light has some limitations and works better in certain scenarios than others. I personally found this little light to be quite versatile though. Its main limitations are:

1) It cannot be used with a dimmer. Most of my lights are not on dimmer switches anyway, so this wasn't a significant limitation for me.

2) It is somewhat directional, as it directs more light away from the base and somewhat less light to the sides (though it's not as directional as some other LEDs I have tried). One thing to be mindful of is that it may look a little funny in certain scenarios (e.g. when inside of a globe fixture that you want illuminated evenly in all directions). In those types of scenarios, it may be better to go with a light like the [[ASIN:B00APTS03K Philips 424382 11-Watt A19 LED Household Soft White Light Bulb, Dimmable]] (which is a light that has neither of these limitations).

With those limitations stated, there are many things I do like about this little light.

1) It puts out a lot of light - supposedly equivalent to a 60W light bulb, though I think it looks brighter.

2) It's small and doesn't put out much heat. Many LED bulbs that I purchased are somewhat large and put out lots of heat. This is the smallest light of the 5 types that I bought and actually slightly smaller than a standard incandescent bulb.

3) It's quite efficient at 10.5W, and it has a good Color Rendering Index (rated at 80).

4) It comes on instantly when you turn on the light switch. Half the LEDs that I've purchased have about a 1/2 second delay when you turn on the light switch (which makes me second guess whether I hit the right switch sometimes), but not this one.

5) It has a 6 year warranty. Some other LED brands have much shorter warranties. If I'm paying this much for a light bulb, I want a good warranty.

6) For an LED light, it's pretty reasonably priced at this time.

Some final thoughts: This light bulb has a color temperature rating of 3000K. Incandescent bulbs are around 2700K. So, this light will look a little "whiter" than a standard incandescent bulb. Whether you like or dislike this is largely a matter of preference. I generally like the color.

I have one of these bulbs mounted pointing upward in a lamp fixture that directs light towards the ceiling in a room with tan-colored walls. Items in this room and skin tones look natural to me. I have another bulb mounted pointing downward in a ceiling globe in a room with baby blue walls. I feel like skin tones in this room look a little off to me. That's my subjective opinion though.

I generally like this light and will find uses for it in many fixtures in my house.

title: Light Weight and extremely easy to use
text:
Background:
I am a Scout leader in Washington state and have been on Cpap therapy for nearly 20 years. I love the outdoors and for many years this meant that I would have to suffer through many nights without my Cpap to be able to take scouts out into the wilderness. Several years ago while searching for new ways to be able to bring my Cpap with me I found the K5 by Max Oak. This was a game-changer at 4.4Lbs I was able to take this with me and use my Resmed Air-Mini to have a restful night sleep on this battery I would get 5 to 6 nights and while this is great for longer trips most of our outings are only two-three nights and carrying a 4.5lb battery wasn't really needed. My normal settings are in the 12-13 cmH2O and with the added altitude the Air-Mini has to work a little harder to keep the pressure up. This means that any battery that I might use would not have a run time as normally listed.

Personal Experience:
In our most recent outing, we were at 3500ft which I know is not super high but it's high enough to notice the difference. We left out Thursday and came back on Sunday. We had ordered the Freedom V2 (For Resmed Air-Mini) earlier in the week and were awaiting its arrival on Thursday to be able to leave for the outing. When it arrived at about 2:45-3:00 PM I took it out of the package and noticed it was at ~70% and needed to be charged. We had some running around that needed to be done so I pulled the power plug on my AirSense 10 and plugged in the Freedom V2. It was only on the charger for maybe an hour when we returned and were ready to head out. If memory serves, it was somewhere in the 90's for percentage when I took it off the wall charger, I grabbed the DC charger for my Air-Mini and plugged it into the car's 12volt system while we drove to the trailhead (Please note that the Air-Mini DC plug is NOT a standard item and must be purchased separately, until this point I had never actually used it, I think it was $80 for the DC plug it will accept 12vdc or 24vdc to provide power to the Air-Mini). using the DC converter plug it was fully charged in no time. I was very impressed with how fast the Freedom V2 charged. I never sleep well the first night but after the first night the Freedom V2 was still at over 60%. I knew ahead of time that based on the statistics that the manufacturer listed it was VERY unlikely that I would get 3 nights out of the Freedom V2 but I had a plan for that. We needed to move more food from the car to the campsite over 3 miles apart on Friday so we left one of the K5 batteries in the car in a day pack to be retrieved when we went back for the additional food. because the Freedom V2 uses an adapter cable from the Air-Mini to charge I was able to use the normal cable from the K5 for my Air-Mini to input the 24VDC into the Freedom V2 and fully charge it. This worked GREAT and I was able to easily fully charge the Freedom V2 in a matter of only a few hours. Then on Saturday some of the members of our party left and they took the K5 back to the car and I was able to sleep two full nights at about 7hours the first and 8-9 hours the second and the Freedom V2 had not depleted the charge in fact there was still 8-10% left.

Conclusion:
At 1.35Lbs and with nearly 100WH of power this little battery packs a punch. I always see more power drain on the trail than when testing at home (due to being at altitude and many temperature fluctuations) so being able to get two full nights from a battery that is 3lbs lighter than the Max Oak K5 is amazing it will make shorter hikes much more enjoyable. The price is par for the course. As these are advertised at "Medical Devices" I think it's really just an excuse to bump the price up an extra $100 but the build quality is nice and the interface is much better than that of some of the other options. After reading many reviews I settled on trying the Freedom V2 and so far I am glad I did. I only have 3 nights on the battery right now so I will reserve comments about how well the battery holds a charge over time and whether or not there is any degrade in performance over time. I intend to do a three-night sleep test here at the house this next week and will post any useable data from that. At this point, I am extremely happy with the quality and weight of the unit and am looking forward to any updates that Freedom may come out with in the future.

Other considerations:
To address one of the other reviewer's comments about the internal parasitic drain of the battery. This is normal to some degree with any battery that has electronics hooked to it. Most times it is very negligible and not noticeable. If it becomes noticeable I would reach out to the company for a replacement as one of the cells may be damaged. But it is not uncommon for batteries to slowly discharge over time (many weeks or even months in storage) even lead-acid batteries do this (the effect is made more evident when you place a lead-acid battery on concrete). Please consider discharging to ~50% and recharging any battery before use if it has been in storage. If the battery won't discharge then hook it to the charger and allow it to awaken the cells as they may have been placed in hibernation/storage by the electronics to prevent damage.

Its my pleasure to use this battery and I look forward to many overnights. If anyone has any good ideas on other ways to charge this battery out in the field please contact me as I am always looking for ways to extend our trips.

Nick V.

I’ve very curly beard hair and although it doesn’t make them straight as an arrow it gets them pretty darn close.  Just a quick pass in the morning helps me get the comb through my beard all day long.  Something I’ve never been able to do until now.  Pros: I like that it has a lock feature so you don’t accidentally change the temperature.  Also really like that it has soft silicon-like tips on the ends of each tooth so you can press the brush against your skin without burning yourself.  I’ve found that the trick is to oil your beard when it’s bone dry and move the brush through it very slowly.  Takes about two minutes.  I was worried about the heat damaging my hair, but after a month of daily and semi-daily use my hair seems to be just fine.  I use it set to 180 degrees Celsius.  It’s nice and small and easy to stow and use.  It comes with a nice little drawstring bag to put it in.  I can get about five days out of a full charge using it every morning.  Con:  slow to charge.  It takes about four or five hours to charge it from 30% to 100%.  So if you want to charge it for only a few minutes to get a run out of it, you’re out of luck.  No big deal.  Just keep it charged.

title: Brush is OK but not for me
text:
So I got this brush with the following in mind... I don't really like straightening my hair or using a lot of heat on it BUT I generally wake up with an overall disheveled look and like the idea of just "brushing my hair" with a straightener. I was so excited when I got it yesterday and last night I plugged it in and brushed away! Unfortunately my excitement was short lived. when I got it, the packaging was fine...but then I saw the brush and the plastic was kind of like plastic you'd see on your kid's toy car... not the highest quality. Ok. I can look past that. It's not like it was $200...

I plugged it in and let it heat up. Immediately I did like the LCD display and that it has a F and C toggle for the temperature reading. There are buffer bristles if you will so you don't scald yourself. I never felt the heat directly on my head at any point.

Now, I did read the directions before I started use so I noticed that the included pamphlet says not to use the brush at the highest setting for more than 15 minutes or you will overheat it - con: it doesn't have a safety turn off or overheating feature. Also, when I started brushing, my hair would catch and pull... a good 20 hairs or so were sacrificed.

All in all I really didn't "get" the product. I felt like it was one of those things like an extra kitchen appliance, It's interesting to have but really just takes up space. The only major feature (which I'm still trying to decide if it's worth it or not) is it does work great for my bangs. They're short so they didn't get caught and they straightened my bangs beautifully, just not the rest of my hair.

I will say this as my final thought, I have long hair (almost down to my waist) and it's natural 99% straight and very healthy. If you're looking for hair on the product package (sleek and super straight) as advertised, you're not going to get it using this brush. That look comes from a flat iron. If you're looking for something that will help tame the frizzes and fly aways this product will work.

I received a discount on this product in return for writing a honest review.

title: Ok operation, but possibly defective?
text:
I bought this as a bday present for my... friend. :)

I showed up at his place for what I thought was a 5 person *small family dinner* which ended up being a 12 person massive family dinner. So discretion was key. My local shop had recommended this prodect for twice the price. Needless to say that wasn't an option, so I took a chance with the Amazon no return policy. That being said. It WAS quiet, its noticable in a very very quiet area while on one of the very high settings, otherwise it's fairly silent.

Now, the drawbacks. There's no way for the operator to tell if the product is on or off. Or which speed it's on. When you move it moves, now I didn't go for the internal fun... so I don't know if it's different inside, but for me, it moved everytime i got into the car, or sat or stood... which can be a bit tickly. The last drawback is that it doesn't seem to be able to turn on and off as reliably as I'd like. I could tell he was trying to turn it on occasionally when he would get an evil glint in his eye... but it wouldn't flip on. Conversely it would go on when I least expected it... so his family thought I was a complete weirdo by the end of the night.

In short, its excellent for sound, but unreliable for the on/off switch. The various speeds seem to always register, so once you get it on and off... that works well at least.

Also keep in mind it does take some harder to find batteries, they give you 12 watch batteries and 2 remote batteries, but neither are regular size. So when you buy this toy keep in mind that it only runs for a few hours continuously, make sure you take out batteries when you're done playing, and think ahead, if its going to be more than 6 hours worth of play... buy more batteries. They give you enough for 2 play sessions (12 watch batteries, 6 at a time and 2 remote batteries, 1 at a time).

Hope this helps everyone out there! And happy playing... I sure had fun... until he sent me home without dessert :(

Stephanie

title: Great for nurseries, surprisingly effective, but WAY overpriced...
text: I'm glad I held off on reviewing this item until we'd had it for a while because when I first received it I almost sent it back. I bought this for my son who has always needed background noise to sleep well. We have just used a fan in the past but his room is the coldest room in the house so I was looking for an alternative to the fan that wouldn't make his room even colder. When you turn it on, it sounds way too quiet to believe it would mask any background noise. And at first, it really doesn't seem to block out any noise. But once it's been on for a while, you honestly don't notice any other noise but the sound of the machine, which itself is quite soothing. It's not that it masks or blocks the noise, it just seems to trick your brain somehow into not noticing the noise, if that makes sense. And the nice thing is we can take it wherever we go unlike the fan. We took it to our summer home to use up in the loft where the kids sleep and it really helped them fall asleep even with all of the grownups downstairs talking. I would love to buy one of these for every room in our house but that's the downside--the price is WAY to expensive to justify purchasing more than one. Especially when fans are just as effective and you can buy those for 8 bucks at Home Depot. Which is really too bad since I could see every Mom in America having one of these in their nurseries if it were more affordable so I'm not sure why the price point has to be so high. I'm still giving it 5 stars though because it's definitely an effective product so if you have money to burn then go ahead and splurge!

title: Excellent workout tool!
text:
I would like to mention upfront that I have received this set FREE, in exchange for an unbiased review. Although the workout instructions were missing in the box, it was pretty straight forward to figure out how to use this product.
Generally speaking, my regular workout routine includes a wide variety of bodybuilding equipment and free weights that support active development of the entire musculoskeletal system. Therefore, I believe, this particular product could benefit multiple categories of new and potential users of body resistance bands. The most important is that this simple and inexpensive set of bands, including support pieces like door anchor and ankle strap are practically replacing majority of gym workout equipment allowing users to train and stretch virtually the entire musculoskeletal system (separately and in compound exercise) without ever leaving their house. For example with proper positioning of the door anchor (either locked in the upper door side or midway on the door side) one can work out his/her triceps (with triceps cable pushdowns or cable bent over extensions) as well as abs development with kneeling cable crunches. The included multiple resistance bands nicely support individual strength development, so the fitness newcomers as well as experience bodybuilders in the same household can use the same set of resistance bands.
My overall opinion (after using this product on daily basis for a little less than two weeks) that the directed use of these resistance bands can support full circle of healthy resistance exercises, starting with full body stretching (with relatively low resistance band), strength training (with moderate resistance band) and even trigger the muscle growth by training specific muscle groups to failure (with high/combined resistance band(s)).
I would like to also mention once again that the exercise chart and starter guide were missing in my shipment and, although, it did not create any problem in my case, it could be a potential drawback for the beginners who’s improper (uneducated) use of the product will lead to overall disappointment with the product and quite possible with resistance to exercise in general.

title: Sunpentown Giddyup Core Exerciser dual motor
text:
Product: Sunpentown Giddyup Core Exerciser dual motor

As an equestrian, I must say this first; this product does not mimic or even come close to mimicking the movements of a real horse at a walk, trot, etc... I purchased one because I thought it might help me improve my posting (I don't have access to an indoor during the winter months to ride my horse - so was looking for something to use indoors at home). Because of the uneven, odd, or even violent "jog" of the exerciser, it makes it nearly impossible to make any attempt at posting because there's no constant rhythm to the movement that you would normally feel on a real horse. Okay, enough about that.

What it's for?

This device is meant to work your abdominal muscles, quadriceps, and hamstrings by way of counter-balance; this is a type of exercise that is meant to develop muscles by constantly putting the rider in a state of being off-balance and the muscles used work to keep the rider upright and "in the saddle".

Does it do this? Kind of. The first time I sat on the core exerciser for the 15 minute session, I could feel the muscles in my abdominal region working to keep my body centered. To increase the usefulness of the device, I practiced upper body movements that I learned during my Classical Dressage sessions with my trainer, keeping the upper body quiet and "separate" from my seat, or what would be called developing an independent seat. I did notice that my back was a little sore after each use. (see the video on YouTube: look-up giddyup core exerciser)

How it looks

What you see is what you get. The device looks exactly like the photo. It has a basic "saddle" shape, more like a giant bicycle seat than a saddle for a horse. It has two grab straps: one in front, one in back. These can be used as hand holds for those who need them or to pick up and move the device (though - I suggest getting someone to help move it rather than lift it by the handles). The model I have had two tone blue and gray materials on the seat and a dark gray base. The exerciser does not come with a foot rest of any type and would definitely benefit in a future design to apply stirrups.

How it functions
Plug the device into a normal wall outlet and turn on the power switch (located on the back of the base). A very simple control panel is set into the pommel or front section of the "saddle". You can select the amount of time you want to exercise (base time is 15 minutes and cannot be changed once you start without hitting reset or powering off the unit) and select the speed of both the front/back action and the Figure-8 action (dual motor version of device). Push start. It's that simple. It comes with a DVD that can be found on YouTube: (see the video on YouTube: look-up giddyup core exerciser)

Pros
* Easy to use
* Relatively Small foot print
* Different speeds
* Can somewhat randomize the two different motions (figure 8 and front and back)
* Front and rear grab straps
* No pain or stress to the knees

Cons:
* No stirrups
* Doesn't move like a real horse
* Not for really tall people. It seems that it is more suited to people in the height range of 5'-0" to 5'-6". Taller folks may have an issue as to how to place their legs. If you place your feet on the base (not recommended by manufacturer) or on the floor it may defeat the purpose of the exercise.
* Not for people who are prone to motion sickness - ever taken a long road trip and once you stopped, when you closed your eyes, you could still feel the motion of the road? Or walked on a tread mill for 30 + minutes and when you got off, you felt a little "weird", it's the same type of sensation with this device. If you get ill on boats...this is not the device for you.

title: The part that made it swivel was not meant for long term sitting
text:
I ordered this item because my father and a close friend both had surgery recently and I thought this would help them getting in and out of chairs. My dad tried the seat inside of my mom’s Dodge Caravan and he didn’t like how it fit in the captain chair of the van. When he tried on his dining room chair, he liked the extra cushion of the seat for the time it took him to eat a meal. My other friend tried it in both her Mitsubishi Mirage and her roommate’s Nissan Altima and the seat fit in the chairs; however, she complained that it made her back pain worse after about 20 minutes. She agreed that the cushion part was nice, but the part that made it swivel was not meant for long term sitting-especially if you don’t already have some natural cushion in the back end. The cover material is soft and it’s great that you can remove and wash.
Disclosure: I received this item for free in exchange for my honest review. My experience was not influenced by that discount in any way.

title: Some improvement ... jury's still out whether worth the ongoing maintenance costs/investment
text: I've had trouble with my rgp lenses lately where after 8-10 hours of wear they're almost unbearable ... uncomfortable/gritty feeling, and vision blurry.  Even when I first put them in-- some days are better than others-- but they're often uncomfortable, right off the bat.  Tried lots of different lens cleaners/solutions/etc... some better than others, but still having issues with discomfort and blurry vision.  Figured it was time to pony up the $$ for this VueSonic kit to see if it might help.  Been using it a few weeks now, and have noticed some improvement. The lenses just "look" noticeably cleaner & clearer after running through the VueSonic (vs. cleaning by hand).  When I put the contacts in my eyes the next morning, it's quite a bit more comfortable... and they do seem to "wear better"... i.e. feel comfortable and look clearer for a little longer than they used to.... I can make it through a full day at the office at least, without running into issues.  More recently though the VueSonic doesn't seem quite as effective as it was initially.  I run the VueSonic every night, and do use the self-cleaning pads every time afterwards.  I'm still a ways off from the 3 month mark where it's recommended to replace the silicone components... but wonder if the system is just not as clean/sanitized as it was initially, and so performance is degrading a bit over time.  The lens cleaning pads, and the silicone replacements are ongoing maintenance costs with this system, and that makes it a bit of an investment to keep using this.  Jury's still out for me on whether the ongoing investment will be worth it, or if I should "keep looking" for a better solution.  I think if the performance continues to degrade, and/or if it ends up I need to be replacing the silicone parts more often than 3 months to keep it running up-to-par... this system may not be worth it long-term.  Spent the initial $80 for the kit, so I'll stick with it awhile yet /continue evaluating....time will tell.  Oh ... one pet peeve, and something to keep in mind if you buy this kit....  the lenses have a strong tendency to "get stuck" at the top part of the system (the "lid" ... as opposed to staying down in "the case").  If you're not very deliberate and conscious about what you're doing when you clean your lenses, and as you flip the lid over to peel off the silicone cushions, and grab the lenses, it's easier than you might believe it would be, to mix up the right and left lenses. Been wearing rgp for many, may years and never once had an issue with a left/right lens mixup until I used this kit. As a workaround, I ended up putting a piece of black duct tape on the top of the lid over the right lens spot, as a more "vibrant" reminder when I flip the top over (if needed...if lenses are stuck to the top/lid) that the right lens may now be sitting where my "muscle memory" would normally expect to find the left.  This is a bit tough to explain....  And if someone had given me this warning, I would've ignored it ... "not gonna happen to me ... I'm not that dumb".  But, trust me, if you're kind of "going through the motions" ... talking to your wife or kids at same time you're cleaning your lenses, and you get distracted ... it's easier than you might think, to accidentally mix up the left and right lens.

title: Like another reviewer said, it's sex for your feet
text: Suuuper happy with this purchase. I've had plantar fasciitis from wearing Sketchers Shape-Ups for the better part of a year and and I've already splurged for one massage, but I don't make enough that I can do that on the regular. I saw an open-box deal on this item, so I just went for it--I figured it's about the same as what I'd pay for a 90-min massage. Boy, did I make the right choice--I'll probably never go out for another massage. The compression feels absolutely incredible. I can handle the first two intensity settings (steady blue and flashing blue/red) but the highest intensity is just a bit too, well, intense for me. It's true that you do have to wear some sort of thick sock or else the knobs on the rollers may be a bit too pokey. It's really amazing how the rollers and the compression work together to hit all the best parts of the foot. As far as fit, I'm a Women's Size 9 and my feet fit comfortably in the foot holes. My father also tried it when visiting (Men's Size 12, I think) and his feet fit, too, but it was a much more snug fit. It has a setting called 'Ozone' and I don't know what's up with that, so I just leave it off.

title: You need the proper meter to measure dirty electricity, a Graham/Stetzer Microsurge Meter.
text: They work as they are proclaimed to do. Someone above was complaining about the filters not working. He is not checking the right thing when he uses a Gauss meter as it seems that he is. A Gauss meter measures RF field strength, electromagnetic radiation, and electrical radiation, three different types of EMF fields. The Stetzer filter addresses the problem of dirty electricity on power lines primarily and a different meter is used to determine levels of dirty electricity; the proper meter is a Graham/Stetzer Microsurge Meter which measures average (dv/dt) high frequency, non repetitive electrical noise on the wires. I just used my Stetzer meter to measure the circuit that her reading floor lamp was plugged into (no filter) and got a reading of 148 microsurge units with a maximum of 50 being the target. After installing a filter reading dropped to 30.

title: Not a miracle pill, but could be helpful
text:
I thought I'd try these out as a cheaper alternative to some thyroid supplements my mother-in-law bought for me. I didn't read dosage amount, so it actually comes out to be close to the same price, unfortunately. They work about as well, at least. The pills are smaller, but they do have a mustardy smell (to me). I do seem to have a bit more energy and I'm not losing quite as much hair when I shower. I haven't really had a problem with brittle nails or low sex-drive, so I can't say much about it fixing those.

If you're buying this expecting a weight loss miracle, I wouldn't recommend. If you're having issues with your thyroid, it will help out and you'll most likely be able to lose at a steady pace with exercise and good eating habits. It's a decent alternative to medicating, but it won't help as quickly or as efficiently. (The plus side is no side effects.)

I don't know that I'd buy again, simply based on the fact that I'm already getting quite a few of the ingredients from another supplement (B-12, iodine, zinc, cayenne, etc.)

title: Not good for irregular cycles
text:
I've had my LadyComp (actually have the BabyComp version) since 2007. I initially liked it but I've grown disillusioned with it over time. My cycles are quite irregular and while it can be used if you don't have regular cycles, it really isn't practical. I never get any green days after day 6 of my period until after I ovulate, which could be as late as day 25-30 of my cycle. Even though in all this time I've never, ever, ovulated anywhere near day 14 it still seems to take the ultra conservative approach and give me red days after my period.

The interface is not intuitive and I often find myself having to consult the manual because I forget how to enter data. The user manual is not well written and does not explain a lot of the data the machine records. For example it records "planning hits". What in the heck is that? No idea b/c it isn't explained anywhere.

Also, it is very, very expensive if you need to replace parts. I have an old version of the user manual which said you can choose to leave the unit plugged in or unplugged. Turns out that leaving it plugged in all the time drains the battery - and the new version of the manual tells you not to leave it plugged in all the time. Also, the new version states you should recharge the unit monthly when it is not in use. My version of the user manual did not say that. So, I left it alone after my daughter was born and when I was ready to use it again when she was about a year old the battery was completely dead. You have to send it to Canada to be replaced for about $50. It came back and then it turned out that my power supply plug no longer worked. That was about another $50 to replace. Supposedly they can retrieve your historic data off the machine when you send it in in for repair, but they could not get any data off of my machine. Now I think my thermometer is going bad because my temps are very erratic, but I've decided it's just not worth it to put any more money into this contraption. On the plus side, RaxMedical customer service is very good and can often help you troubleshoot remotely.

I got pregnant with my daughter (planned) on a yellow day. I'd already been using it for over a year by that point but it was still trying to interpret my cycles. It might work great if you have predictable cycles but it does not with irregular ones.

To me it is really just an overpriced thermometer. It's nice that it stores your information, making it easier to chart on paper when it is convenient for you instead of needing to record your temperature right away after you wake up. But, it's just not worth the price when you can chart for free on Fertility Friend.

PS, I accidentally discovered a feature that is not mentioned in the user manual. If you press the + button on the right hand side repeatedly about 20 times it eventually goes back to temperature taking mode and you can take a second temperature for the day.

title: Got to feed your microbes!
text:
About seven months ago I began a quest for better health, starting with an Atkins-style low carb diet. Just recently I began supplementing my diet with probiotics and prebiotics, and Gut Garden has become an important part of my regimen. The only downside to Gut Garden is the ridiculous price. You can buy unmodified potato starch for about 12¢ an ounce. Gut Garden, which is primarily potato starch, is about $2 an ounce. The recommended daily serving of three scoops of Gut Garden is $4!

Lately I've been adding several prebiotics to my diet as a food source for beneficial gut bacteria. Approximately every 36 hours I mix 3/4 of a scoop of Gut Garden into 8oz of sparkling water and drink it quickly. In addition I've incorporated other sources of prebiotics such as green bananas, dark chocolate, plain potato starch, cooked & cooled rice, etc.

The good news is I've lost close to 40 lbs and my overall health is improved. Improved gut health is important for one's immune system and serotonin production, which improves sleep.

title: I definitely feel more sore
text:
So a little bit about me. I'm in medical school and first read about arachadonic acid when I was a grad student. It's involved in a lot of metabolic processes and the body and just generally researching it when I saw several studies that showed it had a measurable effect on strength and size. From what I could see the research was solid and it seemed safe, so I went ahead and got it.
On the first day I didn't really feel much but on the second day...... OUCH!!! It was a soreness I had never once felt before. I wasn't really "Wanting" it to work and the pain was wayyyy too pronounced for it to merely be a placebo effect. I do feel the effect wear off if I take it for a while so I tend to use it for 2-3 months and then stop, some people talk about how it should be cycled. I don't really know much about that but that's what I do. And if I've been off it for a bit and take it again, I definitely feel the soreness.
Some people say you should only take the liquid capsules because *insert sciencey gobbledey-gook* but honestly I've always felt it more with powdered capsules like these so that's what I'll continue to buy. Take that for whatever you think it's worth.
I'm not competitive enough to track 1-rep maxes and stuff like that so I can't speak to that but definitely feel more of a "pump" and subjectively at least I do feel bigger when I'm on it.

title: Great product at a great price!
text:
I've been taking inulin regularly for a couple of years and have tried at least half-a-dozen different brands, but this is the best I've found. Here's why:

Bang for your buck: I take it every day, so being able to buy two large containers in one shot is a real advantage. With other brands, I constantly had to have it on order. Also, the price is significantly better.

The flavor: The flavor is extremely light and pleasant. It's sweet, and tastes a bit like toasted marshmallows. Some of the others I've tried had no flavor (these seem to clump more) and some were slightly chemically (I threw those away). I actually enjoy the subtle sweet/toasty flavor this gives to almond milk. It makes it much less of a chore to take.

The dissolvability: It dissolves well in cold liquid, and even better in hot. I take it regularly in cold almond milk. It'll clump a bit if you're not vigorous and immediate in your stirring, but, compared to other brands I've tried, it dissolves extremely well. I do not enjoy clumps of fiber in my beverages, so this is important to me.

Effectiveness: I find it difficult to gauge things like this, but it seems to work as well as any other brand of inulin I've ever tried.

Overall, this is an awesome product at a great price. I've ordered it several times (and will continue to do so) and have never had a problem. The shipping is fast, and the price is right.

title: Did you enjoy your mop head?
text:
Amazon asks, "Did you enjoy your new replacement mop head?"

Yes, Amazon, more than you could imagine. Some folks might just use their mop heads to clean floors. Not me. Mine is confirmation of a life well lived. I am fortunate to have the means to afford a ten dollar mop head while others make due with less expensive models. In my youth, I cleaned floors with mops with sponge heads and folding wringers like a peasant. I was ashamed but it was all I had. Gradually, I worked hard and earned enough to buy a string mop and I thought that I was someone. It did its job, but I had to wring it out by hand and the head was attached and couldn't be replaced. Then I saw an infomercial late at night for a string mop that would wring itself with the twist of its handle. I sold my old mop, picked up some overtime and I bought one of these marvels of engineering. It seemed like 6-8 weeks that I waited and finally the UPS man left a long, slim box leaning up against my mailbox. I ripped open the box, giddy with excitement, only to find that it was cheap Chinese junk. Flimsy and plastic. I was devastated. Then and there I vowed that I would never again clean floors with inferior equipment. I took a second job and saved my money until I could buy a commercial mop, bucket and wringer like the pros use. It's a yellow Rubbermaid unit that is built to last. It has wheels on it and warnings in English AND Spanish to let people know that the floor it wet. There is a clever baffle in the bucket that keeps the water from sloshing out should I have to stop abruptly. I have arrived. I can mop my floors with my head held high. This mop head is more than a tool. It is a reminder that I can do anything I set my mind to. Thank you, Amazon. I hope to be buying these fine mop heads from you for years to come.

title: Okay if micro measures not required;  weirdly SLOW delivery from Amazon
text:
This is an OK product for generalized measures. See pic - product is on left side. NOT okay if you are administering- for example: 0.13 ml to a tiny animal. I do a fair amount of rehab and medical fostering of animals - and these syringes are fine for larger species like cats or large breed bunnies who - generally speaking - are OK if you pull for ex: 0.76 instead of 0 .75. Also OK for tiny guys so long as the substance administered is benign in the event too much is administered. But - for little guys who weigh only 1.5 - 2.2 pounds - the syringes are problematic for the administration of certain drugs because the measure marks for 100ths are even numbers only.
Also - don't count on speedy delivery. Occasionally, I'm swamped - taking care of 7 - 10 animals with various medical needs -- going through 12 - 20 syringes per day. Sometimes I slip up on ordering supplies. My last order on these syringes will take over a week to get to me. Sure - you can sterilize and re-use (not recommended), but what a hassle when you've got other meds to administer, SubQ fluids to give, injections, re-dressing wounds, changing out comfort pads, monitoring temps, etc... I'm finding another supplier because of this.

title: Great small humidifier for any small room!!
text:
I purchased this with a low cost air purification unit for our master bedroom. It works extremely well and puts out a strong flow of cool vapor from normal tap water. I have had it just over 2 weeks now and really love it. I wake up in the morning with clear non dried out nasal passages so I know it is working great. The flow of cool vapor is very strong and it does indeed run approx 8 hours from a single filling. The vapor nozzle is adjustable to you can aim it in any direction. Some people have commented that it is noisy but I find it to be fairly quiet and even a little soothing with a tiny little bubbling sound that I can barely hear with the TV and air purifier off. One of the biggest advantages I am finding is that the top unit that you fill with water fits in the bathroom sink under the faucet which you wont be able to do with larger units. Filling it is a 20 second task.

I really like this unit and would definitely buy it again and recommend it to anyone looking for an inexpensive, easy to operate and maintain humidifier.

title: Very impressed. Meds and bag are much better quality than the pictures!
text:
I did a lot of research, and even spent an hour going though this product with my sister who is a medical nurse.

Not only does this check all the boxes and come with a great bag, but the quality of the medical materials is very good! I was originally hesitant, but after sorting the packages, and even breaking the seal on a few duplicate items to assess quality I've been very impressed. Many items are name brand, the rest are their "Lightning products" brand which seems to be very comparable. NONE of the items seem to be low quality or something I would not want to use in an emergency.

Bag is water resistant and is made of a plastic lined material, comfortable padding/adjustment when worn, Molle and sealing "military" zippers is a huge plus as well. (pic)

Although I feel most any 'normal' circumstance is fully covered and then some, I went the extra step and wanted to include treatment for more grizzly wounds such as working with chainsaws, machinery, and firearms. I added:

- MOST IMPORTANTLY a headlamp. 50% of earth's rotation is night, every medkit needs a hand-free light!
- Permanent Marker
- *Additional individual sterile gloves
- *Second Fishing Forceps
- Medline 35 Wide Skin Stapler
- SAM Bleeding Control Kit (Better for heavy bleeds and better *tourniquet)
- *SAM Chitosan Hemostatic Dressing (Better bandage for large wound clotting)
- *SAM Chest Seals (lung puncture "sticker" to seal/stabilize against collapsing)
- *Additional Israeli bandages for wrapping
- Petroleum bandages for continued care on healing wounds
- *Antiseptic Silvasorb Silver Hydrogel for continued care
- *Additional Israeli bandages
- Saline Wash

* Items in kit but purchased separately for additional quantity or better quality

Also to note. Everything will fit in the bag EXCEPT the Pulmonary Resuscitator, CPR Mask, Stethoscope, and Blood pressure cuff will NOT! You'll want a separate (similar sized) bag for those items as even when unpackaged they are too bulky and either don't fit at all, or would require displacing large amounts of the other items.

title: This is the best seat cushion ever!
text:
I am an office worker, and I sit at least 50-60 hours a week in an office chair. No matter the quality of the cushioning of the chair, eventually, I get sore and shift a lot. In 100 dollar chairs, I bottom out quick. In 1000 dollar chairs, it may take most of the day, but eventually i will get sore. With this Purple Ultimate Seat Cushion, it does not happen. At the end of the day, i don't have sore spots, and I really dont' feel like I need to get off my butt. It makes a HUGE difference. If you suffer from a bad chair, and you can't afford a nice one, this cushion might be all you need. I also sit crosslegged, and my feet or legs might go numb from pressure points, but with this cushion, my leg just sinks into the cushion, and I never get pressure points.

I recently drove 9 hours to and from a remote town in my Tesla Model 3, and I used this seat, and it was AMAZING. I felt like i could go days and days with no seat problems. It does raise you 2 inches, so you have to compensate for that, but since the car does most of the driving, i didn't mind. The material does seem soft and slightly sticky in there, so don't leave it in your car on a hot day, or there's a possibility of it deforming or melting.

The "rubber" square pattern has a good sense of medium firmness, but it has a good side to side "squishiness" that allows the large seat cushion to form/fit into my current office chair seat as well as the tesla seat. The size is big, but perfect for me because it is more important it fills the entire seat pan. I'm 5'7" and med/large when it comes to things like this. I've tried other foam and memory foam material before, and most might feel soft, but they eventually squish to nothing, but this has a structure to it that never 100% squishes, so it still offers great support, and must like a rubber grid lattice, I don't expect it to lose it's structural integrity over time like foam would.

I do wish they made office chairs with this type of padding, so it's not 2 inches extra of padding I'm sitting on. I'd buy that chair in a heartbeat.

First, let me say that the wax in this product is great. It made my glasses stick exactly where I wanted them to. I was thrilled! Then I left the product in my car. I've done this with many chapsticks before and it's never usually an issue. I usually angle them upwards so the stuff doesn't go everywhere when it melts and then next time when I twist the tube, it all pushes up and life is good again. However, the next time I went to use my Nerdwax, the twist at the end moved, but the product wasn't being pushed out. After taking the whole thing apart, I now realize that this product is SOOO sticky that when this product melts, it will solidify around the push bar and it will actually cause the product to break itself if you try and turn it. I'm giving this product 2 stars because it's a great wax but the product could be improved dramatically with a different delivery method.

It' a great product, just don't expect to be able to leave it in your car next to your sunglasses.

text:
The Little Bath (the makers of the baby Zen and other kid products) are great. I have bought their products now for over two years and will not use any other shampoo or conditioner on my daughter. Also, for both the conditioner and body wash / shampoo, a little goes a long, long ways, especially with the detangler / conditioner.

For shipping, experiment and order more than one bottle and combine into one order. You can usually get a few bottles for the same shipping price. Find the bracket that suits you and shelve it till you need it.

title: Excellent Product for Readers with Neck Pain
text:
Long have I struggled to find the perfect posture for reading. It often seems that, whatever position one assumes, some limb or another is stressed, tensed, compressed. These glasses expand the possibilities. They are primarily intended for reading in bed, with the book resting on the chest, but I have also used them sitting in an armchair or recliner, head tilted back, book in lap.

The design is sturdy, the frame heavier than I expected, and, after a few days of adjustment, the glasses are easy to use. I forget I'm wearing them. At first, there was a slight soreness in the eye muscles, but this quickly dissipated as I became comfortable focusing at the short distance the glasses require. After several days, there was no sense of eye strain or fatigue. Though several other models of prism glasses are available, these are an excellent product for the price. People who do most of their reading on an ebook reader or mobile device will also benefit. The possibility of using the glasses with a laptop also strikes me as intriguing: supine, laptop on chest, wireless keyboard at arm's length.

Anyone who is disabled or forced to remain reclined or supine for long periods will especially love these.
