At first, there was a slight soreness in the eye muscles, but this quickly dissipated as I became comfortable focusing at the short distance the glasses require. After several days, there was no sense of eye strain or fatigue. Though several other models of prism glasses are available, these are an excellent product for the price. People who do most of their reading on an ebook reader or mobile device will also benefit. The possibility of using the glasses with a laptop also strikes me as intriguing: supine, laptop on chest, wireless keyboard at arm's length.

Anyone who is disabled or forced to remain reclined or supine for long periods will especially love these.

title: UPDATE: Caveat Emptor & Mixed Feelings
text:
UPDATE: 7/26/2020

Sitting on the Purple Ultimate Seat Cushion for a few months relieved some stress on my lower back but not by much. I also began to notice that I started developing back pain in the middle of my back, so the pain shifted from my lower back up to the middle of my back. I also noticed I developed stiffness in my neck and it would begin to make a cracking noise when I bent my head back.

Worrying that I was making things worse and not better, I actually had to reverse the divot from the back of my seat to the front which improved things quite a bit. I decided to test this by going back to the divot side and my same neck problems occurred again. I'm not sure what the problem is with the divot but Purple probably needs to create another version without it. I don't understand why all their other smaller seat cushions don't have a divot but this one does. I think it's time they researched and redesigned the Purple Ultimate Seat Cushion for better ergonomics and back support. Overall, I am happy with my purchase but they could do a lot better in my opinion.

-------------------------------------
I purchased the Purple Royal before opting for the Purple Ultimate. The Purple Royal was a nice cushion with rounded edges which I appreciated, but it was just too small for my body. I returned it and decided to get the Purple Ultimate directly from the Purple website since this item has been showing as unavailable for months. I thought that was awfully strange.

So, I have now been using the Purple Ultimate for 3 months. I liked it at first and it made sitting more comfortable but I was hoping it would help my lower back, ankle and foot pain. It really has not helped at all. Also, the divot for the cushion doesn't really allow you to place on a seat that also has a cushion. It has a tendency to slide forward and my body ends up sitting behind the cushion. It's impossible to get it to lay correctly on my office chair. I have to stuff it underneath the back but it doesn't really work for very long. I also noticed that it causes pain and stiffness in my neck. So I now have neck pain where I get a cracking noise in my spinal column. I don't know if this cushion has made things better or worse.

title: A Trip Down Memory Lane...
text:
I was so excited when the first edition of this cookbook arrived to me in the mail from Italy. You are all very lucky that it is now available via Amazon, because it is just too good to keep hidden for only Letizia's former guests. Back in 2013 I spent a week at Letizia's B&B and participated in one of her day long cooking classes. The entire experience, of which, was the highlight of my 3 week stay throughout Italy and France. I made many notes and shot a lot of photos during our class, and although most of her recipes are available on her blog, there is something about touching the silky pages of a printed cookbook that also includes page after page of gorgeous photos. I read cookbooks like they are novels, so for me A Kitchen with a View was almost as enjoyable as eating the actual meals. Every time I open it, I am immediately whisked back to Umbria and Letizia's kitchen. The rustic and delicious Chocolate and Ricotta Crostata with Candied Orange has become a family favorite, and her tips for making fresh pasta are like no other I've encountered. It is perfect every time. I also recently made the Roasted Eggplant Ricotta Dip. When I served it to a friend, her response at first bite was exactly as Letizia described it, "a sort of Italianized baba ganoush.

title: Great for baby's room (and your room!)
text:
We bought this for our daughter when she was a newborn. She has always slept with it and I think part of the reason she is such a good sleeper is because of this! For the first little bit she was in our room and I have really missed using this at night to sleep! I almost bought myself one!

Why this is perfect for baby:
-The sound is not recorded so it doesnt repeat the same pattern over and over.

-I love that it just has an on/off switch, I didnt want a sound machine that was going to turn off after my daughter fell asleep

-It helps cover noises in the rest of the house. My daughter will sleep through the doorbell ringing and the fire alarm going off but as soon as I go into her room and turn off the sound machine she start to stir

-It's pretty portable, we always take it on vacations/ trips to grandmas

-You can change the sound by rotating the top part or the sides, if we know things are going to be a little louder we can adjust the sound conditioner accordingly

Other thoughts:
-I like to sleep with a fan so I found the noise this makes to be very soothing. If you like to sleep with a fan then you will love this!

-Dont expect this to cover up every noise, thats not really the point, it will help drown out other noises so if you are asleep or working you wont be distracted by them. I know some people complain about this, but to completely block out all other noises that sound conditioner would have to be really loud and I think that would be worse than the offending noises. It's sort of like wearing earplugs, you can still sort of hear things but they dont bother you anymore.

-Be to follow the instructions not place the sound conditioner right next to your head (like your nightstand) and it will work better. This seems counterintuitive, but it works.

Bottom line: This is worth every penny! For us, this was a splurge. We didnt have a lot to spend on baby stuff but this made the cut and was WELL worth it, still in use today (1.5 years later). We are about to have another baby so we just bought another to have in our room when she gets home from the hospital and I am excited to keep it when she shares a room with her sister! Don't be surprised if you buy this for your kid and end of stealing it from them!

title: Decent chair, but the contruction could be better
text:
The chair looks nice and is generally comfortable. But there are some caveats. First, it's an inexpensive chair, and when you take a closer look, you can see why. The reclining mechanism is entirely manual. In other words, you move the back rest up and down with your body weight. There are two friction knobs you can use to lock it into place. They're a bit of a pain because of how long it takes to screw in two knobs to get them tight enough to lock the sliding mechanism.

The other problem is with the construction of the base. The base is slightly to the back of the chair in order to keep the center of gravity properly aligned when it reclines. The problem is that when you're getting up, the base is slightly behind you. If you're on the heavier side, you run the risk of the chair tipping forward if you put your weight too far forward.

Lastly, unlike better recliners, the front of the chair doesn't move when the chair reclines, only the back rest. The reason a recliner has the seat itself move is because the it needs to be angled differently in a reclining position versus a normal seated position (it needs to be angled up when reclined and perpendicular to the ground when normally seated). Because the seat in this chair doesn't move when reclined, the seat is permanently angled up slightly. It isn't too bad for the reclined position, but for the seated position, it means the front of the seat is angled up slightly, and for shorter people like me, your feet might not comfortably reach the floor. Also, it means you're in a slightly tucked position since your legs won't be parrallel with the ground but rather angled up. That might not be comfortable for some people.

Also, this is not for heavier people. It says the max weight is 250lbs, and I believe it. If you're anywhere close to that weight, I'd think twice about this chair. The base is wood, but it's ultimately connected at one point on four screws. And the fact that the base is farther back means there's a lot of flex when you get in and out of the chair as the whole thing bends forward a bit as you slide your butt on and off the front of the seat. I suspect for bigger people, this will risk the wood at the base cracking.

The heating feature is nice, and the massage feature vibrates strong enough so you can feel it. For the price, it's a nice chair, but you really should think twice if you're large or if you have active kids who will want to jump around on chairs (if a kid jumps on and off this chair, at best the chair will tip over, at worst the base will snap).

The clip is the key. Yes it does seem strong enough, but the product gets a 2 out of 5. The clip does not hold a heavy shoe even when it can fit over the lip. The clip can not be pushed over sneakers and wider material shoes when only holding the handle. If you have to bend over to pick up the shoe, the product is nothing more than a funny commercial.

Also the shoedini handle does not collapse very much. You maybe only save 1 foot. I am 5'2" and I still need it extended all the way so I do not see any benefit to the telescoping handle. In its collapsed state, you gaining much storage ease.

I have bought 2 foot plastic shoe horns in the past. There are other long reach products you can find for less. You do not need shoedini if the feature of the clip can not be used. The clip is what sold me on the idea.
But since it is too tight to fit over most shoes and sneakers, I returned it.

title: Attention Curly-kinky haired Girls
text: I actually love this product, though I do not use it as intended. After reading the reviews from my fellow curly, kinky-haired girls, I knew this product would not straighten my hair to perfection. If your hair is super curly and thick like mine, you won't get the same sleek finish as a traditional straightener. It also does not get the roots of your hair very well since it is kind of bulky. Also, the button placement is awful. I was constantly having to fix the temperature because I kept knocking it down. That being said, this product is great to use this in place of your blow dryer (your hair should be completely dry before you do it, though). It takes significantly less time and effort than working your hair with a brush in one hand and a blow dryer in the other. I have zero upper body strength, so when blow drying I constantly have to take breaks to give myself a rest. It's also great for minor touch ups. When I unwrap my hair in the morning, it takes out some of the bends that sometimes happens when you take your hair down. So, if you're happy with your blow drying routine and are looking for a product that will get your hair bone straight-- if you're hair is naturally curly, thick or kinky-- then this is NOT the product for you. If you're interested in something that will supplement your hair straightening process/routine, either blow drying or minor touch ups, then I would recommend this product. When this big zit on my forehead goes away, I may post pictures.

I own my own bath and body business, so I try just about every new and hyped-up product on the market in order to compare and contrast. Listed ingredients are really nothing that spectacular as the ones beneficial to the skin are in small quantities (according to ingredient list); worse still is the cream appears to get its emollient factor via the addition of petroleum, glycerin and mineral oil, making this an over-priced version of Vaseline.

It's a moisturizer, period, no miracles to be had, so don't buy into the hype gals! If its moisture and smoothness you're looking for, just use a good serum and crème within your budget.

title: A great, healthy alternative to ADHD meds!
text:
I was being "treated" for years with the usual pharms for ADHD... and while I was able to maintain focus, I was not doing well in many other ways. No matter how much sleep I got, I felt exhausted. My blood pressure was very low. I came to the realization, with the assistance of a Resident in Psychiatry, that something had been and was terribly wrong: I listened to her concerns, then did the research and found all of the evidence that I was suffering from Dopamine depletion. I made a decision to stop the pharms and as soon as the L-Phenylalanine arrived, I took one capsule. The results have been amazing. I used to feel cold so much of the time, it was absurd. An hour after taking one capsule, my body felt warm and vibrant and I no longer feel cold in what would be considered warm temperatures. In the past months, my sense of humor has returned. I am more organized and am able to focus quite well PLUS do not have the feeling of being a machine that is pushing itself beyond what is natural in order to concentrate. What's more is that as much as I am energetic, I am calm. My thought processes are no longer tangential and I'm able to stay "on topic"... not so with the Psych meds I'd been taking. I look back and see that I was a MESS. I have been "pharm-free" for nearly three months, now -- and although I have a supply sitting within easy reach, I've no desire to take the stuff again.

I still have "Attention Deficit", but this product seems to be the answer to the majority of problems AND it is not destructive to my mind and body. The difference in my moods and feelings of well-being are most impressive! I recommend that anyone who takes amphetamine or Ritalin buy a bottle of this and at least "vacation" for a week on the L-Phenylalanine and be aware of how you feel. It's a worthwhile investment! This is especially true if you read this review and recognize that you are having the same sort of problems I was experiencing.

title: Great shaver for the money.
text:
This shaver is pretty good. I was looking for something that could quickly change from a shaver to beard/hair trimmer and nose hair trimmer. This one had it all. Comparable trimmers were quadruple the price!
The battery life is excellent and the digital read out screen on it looks high end and an unexpected touch for the price. The shaver itself is good. I would not say it's great but given the price it's good. It takes several passes over the same area to get all the hair, no biggie but probably wouldn't be an issue with more expensive shavers.
The attachment system is great and is a breeze. Simply twist and lock and it changes from my most commonly used trimmers in seconds. The hair/beard trimmer without a guard only works ok, it does not shave very close to the skin and sometimes leaves stubborn sideburn hair. The nose hair trimmers work very well. This thing is also waterproof, which again given the price point is surprising.
Lastly the build quality is good. It is very quiet and I have had no issues with it's functionality yet. The only knock I have against it is the materials are very plasticy and the shaver feels very light. I'm not sure about the longevity or how this thing will look in a year with a cheap feeling exterior but we will see? They chose to use a metalic paint on the outside to make it look metal which it is not. They should have done straight black as I feel it would age better. I have a feeling this cheap metal paint will eventually crack, scratch and chip, but again we will see?
All in all a good shaver for the price!

title: NATURAL?? Who are they trying to kid?
text: I just came across this Antiperspirant/Deodorant and was confused/excited. Confused because I was fairly certain in my knowledge that aluminum is the only chemical that acts as an anti-perspirat. So for those of us who aren't keen on willingly putting a heavy metal, like aluminum into our bodies have always just had to settle for a deodorant, without anti-perspirant properties. I, then, became excited at the idea that perhaps I was wrong, and that maybe there was some natural ingredient that acts as an anti-perspirant. WRONG. I looked in the description and saw that the first active ingredient is aluminum! I am baffled. I mean, come on! Who do they think is going to buy this? The kind of people who are seeking out a "Natural" product are not the kind who are ok with having aluminum as a main ingredient. And the type of people who ARE ok with aluminum are not the type who are going to seek out a Natural Deodorant, (or pay $7 for it). If a person doesn't care about harsh ingredients, then they're just going to pick up some whatever brand at Wal-Mart. What were the Tom's of Maine decision makers thinking?! Apparently the demographic they are selling to are those who care about natural ingredients, but don't mind aluminum? WHAT FAR OUT BRANCH OF LOGIC ARE THEY WORKING FROM???  Actually, after reading some of these positive reviews, I realize that the target demographic are uneducated people who see the word “NATURAL”, and read no further. To these people: educate yourselves and then read the ingredients label. Is there a way to tag all of these unknowing 4 and 5 Starers to make them aware that aluminum is the most harmful ingredient in ANY anti-perspirant? Including this falsely titled "Natural" product.

title: Great Choice for Multiple Sound Options
text: I've been using this sound machine for a little over a week and have used 2 different brands of sounds machines in the past (Homedics & Big Red Rooster).  The size of this machine is nice but what sets this sound machine apart is the number of sounds available.  You have multiple nature sounds (rain, birds, ocean, fire, train, etc), musical options for baby and 7 white noise sounds as well as 7 fan options.  In total, there are 29 sound options.  I honestly don't use the night light feature but from testing, it's a nice feature to have and would likely be very useful for many people.  There are multiple color options and you can dim the night light.  The only way to have the night light on without sound is to turn the volume off.  I did not find another way to just use the night light without the sound machine option.  The volume could be a bit more consistent between the different sound options and I am extremely light sensitive, so I actually place a cover over the menu buttons since there's 2 light indicators for power.  Essentially, I want the room as dark as possible and even that small light on my nightstand is bothersome.  The only other consideration would be to provide the base of the sound machine in different colors (ie. black).  In addition, the size is good but for travel, the other travel sound machine I have from Big Red Rooster is almost 1/2 this size.  The only issue is that that one requires batteries whereas the Renpho is rechargeable and states it lasts up to 7hours fully charged.  It also has an option for batteries too.  Overall, if you're looking for multiple sound options and you could use a night light, this would be a top choice for you!

title: A revelation
text: Am in my mid-40s and I have never owned such a thing before, but wise internet folks strongly advised earplugs for upcoming concerts at the Rose Bowl. I picked these primarily based on design (I am very short and have a weird fear of being elbowed in the head, so the kind with protruding stems gave me much anxiety), but was a little sad that they did not come with the kind of carrying case that can attach to a keychain because reviews would lead one to believe that one should always carry earplugs on one's keys in case of impromptu concert-going. Last night I had the chance to try these out at a concert at a much smaller venue than the Rose Bowl, and they were amazing. Comfortable, very easy to use, and best of all, I could still hear when we left the theater. In quieter moments during the show, I'd pop one out so I could hear the difference--the sound was understandably a bit less crisp with them in, but the instant silencing of the screams was just so neat. As for the case, it is really cute and squishes nicely into my pocket. Since I don't carry keys anyway, I'm not sure why I even had that moment of sadness.

title: Probably a scam - Dosage refused
text: WHen I purchased the product I didnt see any dosage in the listing. As with other products I assumed the bottle would contain this VERY important information. It did not so I emailed the company asking very specifically what the dosage amounts per serving of each of the graviola and the Cat's claw was. They responded "the reccomended dosage is 10 drops". At first I assumed she did not understand the question so I rephrased it asking specifically how many milligrams of Cats claw and how many milligrams of graviola per 10 drops. I never got an email response. So I called the company and posed the original question. I got the same answer as in the first email about using 10 drops. So again I specifically asked the millgrams. Her answer was that the FDA does not require them to divulge the information. Why would someone respond this way unless they are selling a product with barely any of the 2 ingredients at all? People are buying this product to help in their treatment of CANCER and this company refuses to divulge monumentally important information such as dosage of the herb they are selliing? I am appalled and will be filing a grievance with amazon, the BBB.

title: I like the product, but it's NOT 20 servings
text:
I've been using this product for several months, and while I do enjoy the flavor and perceived health benefits from it, a monthly re-order cycle will leave you well short of product if you use it daily, as I do.

As an exercise, I began charting how many servings I was ACTUALLY getting in comparison to the "about 20 servings" listed on the container. The charting was done using the last 3 containers purchased through Amazon, and the number of servings ranged from 14.5 - 15. I used the manufacturer supplied measuring cup and ensured that it was precisely level - not heaping.

Given those findings, the best case scenario customers can expect is your ACTUAL number of servings will be twenty-five (25) percent below what you are expecting to receive. That's a SIGNIFICANT shortfall, in my opinion, and something the manufacturer clearly knows about and seems comfortable misleading the customers about. Plan and budget accordingly.

title: For me, it has provided pain relief for mid-back arthritis
text:
Have had this a month or two and have used it a dozen times or so. It's not a pleasant feeling (when first using it) and it takes some getting used to. But it does offer me relief for acute mid-back arthritis pain.

I've been told by MD specialists twice now that chiropractors are unlikely to provide significant relief for a degenerative spinal condition, and that a massage would probably be more beneficial. I can't afford to go to a masseur a couple times a week, or even once a week. What am I saying--I can't afford once a month! So I decided to try this contraption. Obviously it's not going to replace a massage from a human, it's a machine. But so far I have to say this has been a good investment and using it for 10 minutes or so--repositioning it up and down my spine every couple minutes--really does provide pain relief for me.

Without revisiting the sales page, I think that this was intended for neck pain. It works for me on my mid back. It's a bit awkward to use and at first feels almost violent, but once you let it do its job, it works.

The only reason I'm not giving it 5 stars is I haven't used it long enough to report on how it will hold up--which I think is important. If I haven't updated this review, assume the thing is still working for me. I'll only revisit the review if it fails. So basically 5 stars unless you hear otherwise.

The pills look pretty much the same from the two manufacturers. I am taking the supplement for egg quality rather than for blood pressure or any other measurable parameter, so I can't speak to how well they work compared with other similar versions. I assume that if they are the same formulation, the effectiveness should be the same.

title: Hobby Kit
text:
Construction: Bowl: Ceramic, annoyingly heavy and draught hole is bottom center. Takes my thumb, but only to the knuckle, resulting in 45 minute smoke max. No capacious 2 hr. Calabash smoke here. It was held in place by tack glue. Removed, underside of bowl is threaded, but soft wood surface does not bode well for repeated removal,sealings. Probably best to clean here quarterly. There is also a gap the thickness of 2 sheets of newspaper, when bowl is in place.
Pipe Body: This is NOT BRIAR. Unbelieveably . . . it is made of BALSA WOOD! Top of pipe body is hollowed out with a floor at mid body and a 2nd Draught Hole at the back, 1/4" above the shank.
Stem: The stem, ferrule and screw tenon (in the shank) are hard, plastic, not Vulcanite. It has a chemical taste to it initially. End of Bit is not round, but somewhat flatted and this makes for an air gap top & bottom when inserted into the ferrule. After first use, the screw tenon in the shank came loose. Wood glued it came loose a second time. Will probably need to resort to JB Weld to keep it in place. Gluing the stem to ferrule receiver to cure that air gap, is not an option, as you don't know where the pieces will line up when threaded back on the screw tenon. I subbed a bent Vulcanite stem, but there was still an air gap, but not as bad as the stock unit.
Useability: I gave it 2 stars, as it is smokeable. That overtly top heavy bowl requires some dexterity. It always wants to fall forward. Hard to light, due to weight, bulk and center draught hole. Czech Pipe tool handy when loading. Once going, draw is medium tight. This can be improved by opening 2nd draught hole to 5/32nd.
The knock on Ceramic pipes, is the heat they generate. Here, the light wood body, gives a cooler surface to hold while your tobac burns cleanly in the Ceramic bowl. This is this lowly pipes' saving grace.
I looked for lowest price ($23.90 with Ship)and waited for the leisurely, 3 week, International shipping. Still, I paid too much by half, judging by product received. This pipe made by committee has a goofy charm for those who like to tinker, but I believe it is not worth the money or the aggravation to most pipesters.

title: Big and bulky for so little storage
text:
I bought this because of other positive reviews and the design looked good. Unfortunately, function follows form in this case. It indeed looks good, but that's the only thing in it's favor when compared to other options. Here's why I don't like it:

1. The compartments are so awkwardly designed that you can fit very little in them, and in fact work against the shape of most pills. Therefore a lot of space is wasted in each compartment when you have larger pills such as vitamins or Omega 3s. A dollar-store pill case I own is half the size but holds more pills. Why? Because each compartment on the dollar-store model is flat and square, allowing me to use much more of the space allotted.

2. Yet for so little storage space it has a very large footprint. The outer case that holds all the daily compartments is not compact. In fact, it could have been made narrower because the individual daily cylinders have much more room between them than is really needed. Another waste of space.

3. Finally, the color coded day labels are nice, but the type face is too small and too faint to read quickly on most of the cylinders. This is a nit-pick, but still, it's another sacrifice they made in favor of making it look good.

I ordered the [[ASIN:B000E17M38 7 Day Pill Pack - Medicine Organizer Dispenser]] from Amazon at the same time as this one, and while it isn't as pretty, it's far more functional. It's boxy (like an old Volvo), boldly colored, and yes, you could even say somewhat ugly (like an old Volvo). But it's built like a tank (again: Volvo), still has the individual days in separate boxes that can be removed from the set, and best of all, it holds all the pills I need in each compartment. And in case that one isn't even big enough it comes in a double-sized version, too.

So, if you don't have a lot of big pills to take, and prefer pretty over useful, by all means buy this. But if you're like me and prefer function over good looks, do yourself a favor and look at other options.

title: Great Hydra killer
text: I had a problem with hydras that somehow came in on some plants from the LFS.  I had a 10 gallon with shrimp and snails.  I did a 25% water change first.  I took a 1/2 cup of aquarium water and put one full packet into that 1/2 cup and stirred it into a milky white solution.  With an eyedropper I took 1ml of the solution and dropped it into my 10 gallon tank.  This was repeated in the evening about 10 hours later after the first dose.  I continued this for about three days until I could see no more hydras in my tank.  I did a 25% water change again after the hydras were gone.  I did not see any ill effects to the shrimp or snails.  It has been over a month since this incident and the hydras have not come back.

title: The worst is that if you have any overlap at all ...
text: This is the least forgiving wood product that I've ever worked with.  I tested several application methods and opted for rags and rubbing.  I applied this on refinished (sanded down) red oak and was shocked how quickly it took the stain.  You have just a second or two to spread out the stain, if you let it sit beyond that, you have dark splotches.  The worst is that if you have any overlap at all between strokes, you have double the stain, even if you wipe it off instantaneously.  Also, "walnut" is a very generous term for this color, maybe closer to English walnut.  It may be possible to achieve a good finish with this, but unless you're going for super dark, avoid this like the plague.

I've been mixing Vega Complete Whole Food Health Optimizer (berry flavor) with Gatorade (any flavor) for about 2 weeks now, and I can report no ill effects. The Gatorade seems to temper the taste.

Take a good swig of the Gatorade (to make room in the bottle for the Vega) then add the Vaga, cap back on, good shake, and you're all set. I actually take this to the gym with me as my workout drink.

However, I do not take a full dose. In fact, I only take one quarter dose (one half scoop). I think the full dose (2 scoops) is a bit unreasonable and might just be a marketing ploy to help "move product."

Overall, I'm happy so far. Hope this helps.

title: Overall Best Night Golf Ball
text:
A good light up golf ball is hard to find. LEDs are great, they put off tons of light but don't swing over 95mph, otherwise they fail pretty quickly. Glow stick balls don't give off great light and are hard as rocks, you can't use woods with them because they will break them, I've seen it first hand.

The Glow V2 ball isn't as bright as the LEDs but still gives you more light than the glow stick which was more than I thought. I had no trouble tracking it, but the best part is that they hit just like a standard ball. I was hitting them the same distance as a standard ball. No need to club up or leave my drives at home. I've only tested them one night on about six holes. I charged them with a UV flashlight for about 30 seconds which is a shorter time than recommended. This gave me a bright charge for a couple shots but it will hold a dim charge that lasts a long time which is still traceable and I believe still brighter than the glow stick ball. I played 3 holes on one charge and had no trouble tracking it.

Overall I was looking for a ball that is dependable, plays like a standard ball and I could keep track of it in the dark. And this one does all of that.

title: Nice lamp. Probably wouldn't buy it again.
text:
I bought this because I work in a windowless office. Additionally, I am susceptible to S.A.D. and I can't stand overhead fluorescent lighting. I was looking for a lamp to provide natural looking light in my office. I'm not dissatisfied with the purchase, but I probably wouldn't buy it again.

Maybe I should have figured this out, but "natural spectrum" does NOT mean it looks like sunlight. It is much "cooler"--very similar to the ghostly white cast by overhead fluorescent lights. That said, it is superior to standard office florescents in every other way. No flicker, no buzz, no glare (thanks to diffuser grate). Additionally, it's not bright enough to light much of a room. I don't think it could be a sole source of light in any situation. I ended up getting a couple of floor lamps for general lighting in my office (with standard incandescents for their warmer glow), and placed this light next to a work table for additional task lighting. Since it's only supplemental, the white-ness of this light doesn't bother me much in this setup. I also have it cast on a little palm, which seems grateful for the wide spectrum.

One more thing: I don't think this works as a therapy lamp. The product page is unclear as to if it is intended to. Verilux makes nice therapy lamps, and it seems like this lamp uses the same type of light, so it might have some benefit. However, my understanding is that for therapy lamps to work, the light needs to hit your retina directly. This lamp really can't do that in normal situations. I have a directional LED therapy lamp on my desk for my S.A.D. treatment.

Given all this, yes, it's a very high quality lamp and is what is advertised. However, if I were to do it over again I would have gotten a brighter, cheaper lamp for my purposes.

title: Laundry Soap Sheets work great if you know how to do hotel laundry.
text:
In a normal sized hotel sink, two sheets washes about four-five pairs of socks. Or three-four pairs of underwear. Or two polo shirts as long as they are synthetic. The comments about lack of suds are missing the point. The only purpose of any detergent is to reduce the surface tension of water so that it can penetrate your fabric and enable the water to lift out the dirt. You want to use just enough detergent to do that. Anything more is a residue that you have to try to rinse out. I travel frequently in Europe. My 7 to 10-day pack is four pairs of socks (synthetic or bamboo fiber), three polo shirts (synthetic), three pairs of underwear (synthetic), and 2 pairs of polyester/cotton slacks. The slacks typically last two wearings each unless it's grossly hot out or I'm doing a lot of walking. (I'm actually sitting next to my pack in an Eastern European hotel as I write this, having just finished my laundry and noticing that I'm running out of these laundry sheets. I am currently on a 9-day leg, and have zero concerns about clothes or laundry.).

Usually every night or possibly I'll skip a night, I spend about 15-20 minutes soaking all the clothes in hot water in the sink while doing other stuff. ("all the clothes" is usually just 1-2 pairs of socks/underwear, a shirt, and every other day slacks). That part is important - presoaking seems to loosen the fibers and at the same time get the lion's share of sweat / dirt out of the clothes. Empty the water, wring the clothes lightly out in the tub or sink, then refill with hot water. Dry your hands. Dry them again. Let them air dry a little. Or if you have tweezers, use those instead -- all the comments about how water sensitive these laundry soap sheets are nailed it. Any moisture, and they become a solid mass. Fill the sink up with about 2 quarts / liters of hot water. Put in two laundry sheets. Wash your underwear, using squishing / wringing action to force water mechanically through the fabric. The mechanical action, not the chemicals or suds in the soap, is what gets your laundry clean. Probably 10 or so squishings or squeezing or wringings for socks and underwear. Put them to the side.

If you still have enough water (you should), throw in a polo (or a cotton dress shirt). Same deal. Squishing and wringing and squeezing. Mechanically force the water through, paying special attention to the armpits where the residue of your deodorant will build up and hold odor. Cotton is not a problem except it soaks up water like a sponge and doesn't release it easily. And it takes forever to dry in even a moderately humid climate. Put this to the side. Add more water, enough to handle your pants. Add two more laundry soap sheets. Repeat the squeezing squishing wringing action, although this will take longer since pants have more fabric. Wring them out. Empty the sink.

If you have a shower, throw all the clothes in the shower, and take a shower, using the shower to rinse your clothes out. Turn off the shower and while still undressed wring them out as best you can. If you have a pack towel (for backpacking) or a chamois towel or even a microfiber car towel with you (strongly recommended), lay wet clothes out flat on the towel, roll up, and then wring them dry into the towel. These towels will keep soaking up water even when they're wet, and you can just wring them out over and over again. Hang the damp clothes to dry. In a hotel, use the hair dryer to dry your socks if you will need them quickly. I have never had a problem with dirty clothes using this method and these laundry sheets.

title: Keep moving, nothing to see/hear here.
text:
This item is listed at $540 with a 90% discount taking it to $54. Honestly, a 99% discount would have not been enough. The main body is made from low quality plastic. I suspect this was chosen as compensation for the rather cheap internal components. Typically, you will find that in order to reduce size and weight of electronics, you must use more expensive metals and base board components. These devices went with larger, heavier internals and had to utilize the thin external case. This also had an effect on the fit and finish of the product. It almost seems that these devices were made by hand. Not experienced hands but shaky, clumsy hands that you might expect belong to uncoordinated and underfed pre-teenagers.

The volume control knob on one device would rotate freely without any resistance which resulted in gravity alone being able to adjust the volume. If you turn or nod your head, the volume might shift. The other device was the exact opposite. It required some considerable effort to adjust. The power switch on both devices felt loose in the frame and as a result either device might turn off because the switch slid down from the on position without being directly manipulated. This also meant that when sliding the device into the charging slot, the power button might be shifted up into the on position. This, we discovered resulted in a longer charging period as the device is discharging the battery at a rate that almost exceeds the charging capacity.

Finally, does the device at least amplify sound as stated in the description. Yes, the device amplifies sound. All sound. Background noise is amplified at an equal level to speech, music, and any other sound. Add to this the fact that because of the poor engineering, low quality components and shoddy manufacturing the device introduces a rather noticeable and annoying hiss that overrides any potentially beneficial effect of the amplification.

I do not recommend that anyone purchase this device from any source or vendor. Take the $54 and buy a megaphone to give to your family. Or perhaps you might be better off using the $54 to buy lotto tickets as an investment in good quality hearing aids. Another option might be to roll the money up in a tube and have others shout through the tube while pointing the open end directly at one of your ears.

text: This is by far the VERY BEST physical sunscreen my daughter and I have tried.  We are allergic to chemical sunscreens and their stabilizers, and almost all mineral sunscreens cause our skin to become dry, scaly, and flaky.  My daughter even developed painful, itchy eczema from the severe drying effect of some of the top-rated sunscreens that are purportedly safe for kids with sensitive skin. title: Beautiful, well-built bench, wherever you put it
text:
Okay, let’s start with a full confession: I knew this bench wasn’t going to fit in my narrow bathtub, but I ordered it for a different use — to be a sturdy, handsome, and modest-priced bamboo accessory for my bedroom. That’s what it’s turned into, and that’s exactly where it sits right now, at the foot of my Tempurpedic. Spoiler alert: I LOVE IT!

The unit came disassembled but turned out to be a cinch to put together. The instructions are hardly necessary. There were stickers with letter coding on the legs and body that showed what went where, and an Allen wrench for the stainless steel screws. There was even an extra wrench and set of screws included. I think it took me five minutes from start to finish.

There were only two minor imperfections I feel obliged to mention. The first was a rough patch on the bottom of one leg. A little sanding took care of it, but it’s something I think should have been caught in quality control before it left the factory.

The other issue had to do with the soft rubber feet that affix to the bottom of each leg. An improperly pre-drilled hole in one of the legs meant that I ended up stripping the notches in the head trying to get the screw securely seated. Not a huge deal, but still…

For those considering it for bath use, my experience may be instructive. A couple of years ago, I realized I really needed to be able to sit down while showering. I saw (and purchased) the Oasis Space model in the accompanying photo here on Amazon. It’s perfect for my situation. The legs are only 13 inches apart, which means they can sit flat on the bottom of the tub, and the circular seat measures well over 12 inches, which is ample for my gluteus maximus. It also has a number of different height settings.

For my bathtub, this bamboo version is wider where it needs to be narrower and narrower where it needs to be wider. Instead of 13 inches, the legs are 18 inches apart, making it impossible to place it securely on the bottom. And the slatted seat, while comfortable, is over two inches narrower than the diameter of my existing shower seat. Finally, while an application of Tung Oil would probably retard mold, I’ll be much happier using this bench as a bedroom accessory.

I continue to be impressed with the Oasis range of products and the company's excellent customer service.

title: Not exactly as great as I thought it would be
text:
I will say that the light feature is neat. My kids did like that very much, and had a bit of fun picking out what color stars they wanted the first night we used it. However, the sounds, aren't that great. For starters the volume on some of the sounds is way too loud even on the lowest setting. It gets super loud but doesn't quite lower to a comforting level that acts as a 'white noise' type of sound. Not that birds chirping is white noise, but turned down low enough it's a great filler sound for little ones that have a hard time falling asleep in an otherwise super silent room. The sound that we have used with this is the birds chirping. Any other sound either bothers my kids or scares them (to be honest). My children are 5 and 7, and have active little minds, so have a hard time settling down at night. I myself need some sort of 'noise' to sleep be it a TV set on low volume or the A/C running or music playing softly, so I thought this Dream Tones sound therapy machine would be great, esp with the built in night light projection. The sounds it plays are (off the top of my head)- Rain, heartbeat, birds chirping, crickets, ocean waves, running water/stream. The birds are what I assume they are calling "Forest", the "Summer Night" are the crickets and "Babbling Brook" is what sounds like running water to us. The thing that gets me is that some of these sounds are irritating to even me, and since I can only turn them down *so* far I cannot take the edge off the sounds.
The chirping birds "Forest" is the only sound my kids are okay with and seem to drift off to very easily. The other sounds vary in response from my children.

Ocean Waves- Sounds more like a nasty thunder storm and scares the living CRAP out of my 7yr old daughter.

Crickets "Summer Night"- has a horrible metallic echo sound to it in the foreground and it's a noise that really hurts our ears.

Heartbeat- well it is a heartbeat, but it's not that fabulous swooshing soothing sound you hear on some of those infant teddy bears that you place in the cribs of newborns, it's an actual BEAT like a creepy horror film beating heart sound that scared the living daylights out of my 5yr old son....and well, ME! That baffles me, wtf was Conair thinking? Have they not seen those infant heart sounds bears? ((shivers at the creepy heart sound))

Babbling Brooke- the ony thing this sound was great at was making my kids need to pee every 10 mins. It sounds more like someone left a faucet on than a "babbling brook".

Rain- same as babbling brook, only it also freaked them out cause they don't like rain storms.

Birds Chirping- the only tolerable sound, if you don't mind listening to chirping birds on a constant 10 second loop. It would honestly annoy the living crude out of me if I was using this thing, but my children seem okay with it. I do wish you could turn the volume down more because the SHARP chirping carries out of their room, down the hallway and into the living area...it's that loud even on the lowest setting.

So basically it's a really good night projector that makes annoying sounds that either scare your kids or make them need the facilities and is so loud the whole house has to endure the 10 second loop. I'm going to keep looking I suppose. Great idea- as it's portable, battery operated so no cords to mess with, has a great star night light projector, and is compact. It's just the sound execution is awful!

Second, the toe box(?) of the sock is so loose that when you tug on the strap to flex your toes, the bottom/sole of the sock simply starts to come up over your toes.
Even with that said though, I think the sock barely functions the same way as the name brand sock. It just doesn't feel well made. The name brand sock is more like a support sock with Velcro strap reinforcements, while this sock feels like a craft project by my 10 year old.

title: I prefer Nite Pants by Comforts over all others!
text: These pull ups are my favorite! We have tried all the brands (Huggies, Good Nites, Mother Nature, etc) and these are the only ones that hold the pee more reliably. After having two boys and dealing with wet pjs and sheets nightly, we tried everything. My boys are off the charts for their ages. When they were two, they were the size of a three year old and when they were three they were the size of a five year old. Finding pull ups that fit them, held their pee through the night,  and were a good price was hard to come by. These fit the bill perfectly! I can only find them at our local QFC.  What I like in addition about these pull ups, is that they are plain white, no designs. There is no arguing over which design they are going to wear to bed. When we were using brands that had designs, there were always two different designs in a pack, it was inevitable that they preferred one design over the other. So when they used up all of the first design, they begrudgingly wore the less desired design. When both my boys wore the same size for a while, they argued over who got the desired design.  It was just one more thing to have to negotiate with them before they went to bed every night, making bed time routines miserable for all of us. And the kicker was, the design was on the back, and the kids never saw their own butt! Why argue? I like plain white. I like nite pull ups that hold all the liquid. I give these 10 stars! I wish they were more widely available in all stores.

title: Seat bought for sciatica issue
text:
My husband was having a leg issue with his right driving leg on long trips (over an hour) when a pain would flare up (not every time but enough to be annoying and noticeable) that he would then place his right fist under the leg to relieve the extension of the muscle by shortening it in the space - not an ideal solution to maintain this positioning for hours! I bought this cushion over others because it has plastic embedded inside skeleton to make it structurally firmer, essentially recreating his hand position. He only uses it in the car because car seats are notoriously uncomfortable and ill-suited for long trips. (He also has a long commute to work every day.), especailly Subarus, which he likes for the 4-wheel drive and wagon features.

This cushion was tried for just a week and he has remarked on how much more comfortable the car seat is now with the cushion versus without it. The pain hasn't flared up at all, although the longest trip so far has only been 2 hours, but still it's a good sign that the seat is working for my intended purpose - to keep the pain from occuring in the first place.

I would have rated it 5 stars, but am holding off because it's only been a week and I want to see how the cushion holds up over more time. $55 is a bit pricey for a seat cushion, so I reserve the highest rating because with a higher price comes a higher expectation on duration, which time will tell on that aspect.

I would recommend this cushion for this purpose largely for the internal formed plastic structure piece. This was the only seat cushion I found with this valuable feature, which appears to be a solution for warding off the sciatic issue,.

title: Fixed Oculus Quest 2 Controller Drift
text:
I bought this Electric Cleaner in hoping it would fix my Oculus Quest 2 Controller Drift and I'm happy to say it did, some quick tips is that it comes out really fast so just be careful.

If you're using it for the Quest 2 Controller Drift issue, here's what to do, take out the battery's, slowly release the cleaner into the bottom of the joycon base and use quite a bit but not too much where it's everywhere, then move the joycon around and click it in and out and do that for around 1 minute per joycon/controller, then put in the battery's again and test to see if it worked.

Please keep in mind that you should try not to get it in the buttons as I've heard they will start sticking but mine do not have that problem so just proceed with caution (2/17/22).

Update #1: The Electric cleaner works great still, I've had to re-apply it around 3 times since I first bought it but it always last me around a week before it begins to slightly drift again, keep in mind that I play more intense games and I'm quite clumsy so I'm always banging the controllers on something so results may vary, but every time I've re-applied it, it has fixed my drift again, it's such a small amount used to and the can will last me ages and is well worth the $10 (USD) I paid for it rather than buying a new controller for $70 (USD) every other month, So I definitely still recommend this for the Oculus Quest 2 Controllers or even PS4/PS5/Xbox Controllers as I used it on my Xbox Controller and it fixed it's drift to, this stuff is amazing and you need to buy it ASAP (3/20/22).

title: I am woefully disappointed in Das Gro
text:
I am woefully disappointed in Das Gro. I did not buy it via Amazon, but purchased it directly from the Das Gro company - more than twice, as I used their own e-mailed discount codes. Nonetheless, I've still paid way too much money to this company to see absolutely ZERO results in almost 7 months! Yes, I'm now into my 7th month of diligently taking these vitamins twice a day. (I'm almost OCD about it -- I even try to space my intake as close to 12 hours apart as possible!) Okay, so honestly I am a 56 year-old woman who's finally starting in on menopause, but after reading so MANY positive reviews, I'd had high hopes that maybe I'd FINALLY found a product that would stop my hair loss (AND promote NEW hair growth!), but NO! My daily hair loss continues (after over 6 months of daily Das Gro consumption) at an alarming rate. At this point, even my family & friends can finally see that my hair is drastically falling out. "Hope springs eternal in the human heart," and I was just about to re-order even MORE of this stuff, but after reading all the 1-star reviews, I won't be throwing any more money down the drain! One more thing: at least 3, if not 4 of my bottles were full of vitamins that were badly cracked - even "split open." Desperate for a change in my hair loss, I religiously took all of them anyway. But come on! WHO sells vitamins in that kind of condition on such a large scale as this?? Yep, this whole deal sure seems "scammy" to me now!

THANK YOU, Amazon, for upholding The First Amendment and allowing consumers the privilege of truthfully proclaiming our experience! (Unfortunately, this also allows some people to lie - and even to lie for money or free products evidently!) I sincerely hope that neither Das Gro nor Amazon removes this review as I only wish it to be helpful for other budget-conscious consumers.

title: FAKE REVIEWS, BUYER BEWARE
text:
I bought this device for a few reasons that all turned out to be fraudulent lies:

1. High stall force
2. Long stroke length
3. Long attery duration
4. high RPM
5. Low decibels (quite)

The only thing they didn't lie about were the attachment heads which are pretty good.

Device used to be quite, but noise started coming from the motor after about 30 min of light use.

The HR monitor always reads 99 lol. It's a joke and Idk why anybody would want this feature. Useless tech.

Not sure what the temperature gauge is for either or what it measures. Not skin temp lol. Also it jumps up and dowm from 80 to 100 randomly when it's not even working. Doesn't make sense.

no reason for there to be a calorie counter on this machine and it doesn't work either (big surprise). The number just goes up with with time while the motor is running.

These are all useless gimmicks that don't work and are used as marketing tactics to increase the selling price of the machine.

Btw, this device appears to be functioning as intended, the functionality is just trash.

Doesn't last 7 hrs.

The stroke length is much less than 15 mm. Closer to 8 mm. Half the length. What liars.

The stall force is not bad, but definitely not 70 lbs, and the machine does not like being stopped and gets MUCH louder after being stopped.

Search profiles of people reviewing anything from china. Almost all of them are fake. Always sort by 1 star reviews first and look for well-thought-out, methodical reviews.

EDIT:
"review hidden by sensitivity filter". Low ratings are being hidden to boost sales. Amazon turns a blind eye, because they make more money this way too. Looks like the quality of the items bought on amazon are going to go the way of the content found on Internet forums before the gentrification rush of the late 2000's. RIP amazon.

title: Tea tastes better and you can more clearly discern subtle elements on ...
text: One never knows for sure without exhaustive testing, of course, which haven't done, but we have done some taste tests with spring water untreated vs 27 minute treated (my default setting), and there really does seem to be a significant softening of the water which gives it a smoother and shinier look and feel. Tea tastes better and you can more clearly discern subtle elements on the palate. Water is pretty important stuff. If anyone is interested in low inflammation diets, working with Lyme and suchlike, then they might want to consider something like this as the alkalinity, not to mention purported hexagonal molecular 'structure' of course, greatly helps reduce inflammation. I feel quite good about this purchase even though ultimately I would prefer a whole-house solution from a company that makes copper tubes with internal guides which create a double-vortex - albeit no mineral additions - which would reduce the processing time. title: This chair is a beast!!!
text:
I wanted to write this review for all those like me who scour reviews before taking the plunge! I do have an advantage regarding this chair over someone looking to buy this chair sight unseen. I have been able to tryout this specific chair for about a month... I work part time in the ER of a hospital and the hospital has this exact chair in the staff lounge. If you are looking at this chair and wondering if you should purchase is.. I say YES!!
FEATURES:
Not only is the price very reasonable; this chair had all of the basic functions I felt were necessary in a massage chair. Zero gravity, L track massage, which means this sucker will roll from shoulders, down your back, over your booty and to your thighs(heaven on earth). It also has heat which was very important to me. Shiatsu, kneading and rolling, air compression for your calves and forearms and 4 preprogrammed settings. I can sit at zero gravity with just heat and foot rollers going or choose preprogrammed relax, recover, extend or refresh. So many options. Other features outside of these would just be bonuses to me but would also push up the price point and I am not interested in paying 3-10k when this chair has what I believe are necessities.
DELIVERY:
I ordered this chair on a Sunday and received it the Friday at noon...5 days!! It would have been 4 but weather delayed the driver. The shipping company was awesome R&L.. I had a tracking number and received a phone call the day before delivery then the day of 30 minutes prior. Couldn't have went more smoothly.
BRINGING IT IN:
This chair is a beast... very heavy but my son and husband brought it in the house Then down the hall to the den. To get it in the den they did take off the door and trim as our door is small and we wanted no dings or scratches . They probably could have laid the chair on its side and pushed it in the door like an "L".. if that makes sense but I'm not sure you want to tip over a 225 -250 pound chair. Once in the den my husband said it was just 2 pieces to put together and it was super quick.. plug and play. This chair is strong and powerful. Start on low.
I have to say that I am thrilled with everything about this purchase another side note... this chair is "big calf friendly".. there are other chairs that have skinny looking calf massagers... you'll have no problem being comfy in this chair if you have wide calves. I hope this review helps someone decide to buy... or not to buy.

I actually think it smells pretty good, but if you are not into perfumed smells, you will NOT like this product. I have a 12 week old puppy, and for the most part he does not pee in the house, however, if he gets too excited he sometimes can't make it to the slider door. I have rugs/towels, by this door, because if he does have an accident, this is where it is going to happen. I sprayed the rug presently there with this spray, immediately after Kobe had a small accident. I used this product and a wet rag, and a paper towel. I absorbed the urine up with Bounty (the quicker picker upper), and then sprayed the area with the product. I let it sit for a 30 seconds or so, I then rubbed, patted, and blotted the area up. The discoloration was minimal to begin with, and after this treatment it was not visible at all. The urine smell was gone, maybe masked by the perfumed smell, who knows. but it didn't smell like urine which was a plus.

I was unable to try this product with an old stain, mostly because I change the rugs/ towels frequently either by washing them immediately, or if I get home to a wet/or dry urine area, I just throw the rug/towel away. I will mostly use this product on a new fresh urine spot.

BTW, this spray has NO ingredients on the bottle. I have small children and prefer to know what I am spraying in my household. This was a big NO NO, in my books, and for that reason, It was given a 3 star rating.

I am going back and forth between 3 and 4 stars. So let me be clear, this stuff DOES WORK!!! I feel great when I can get it down. 3. The smell is horrible. I cannot breathe in the smell while drinking this or I won't be able to drink it.

That being said, within one day I felt a change in my energy plus my skin looked glowy and I have had other feminine changes. Based on my understanding of hormones (I'm not a doctor, just what I have read in The Hormone Cure: http://www.amazon.com/Hormone-Cure-Vitality-Naturally-Gottfried-ebook/dp/B008J48S94/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1408025742&sr=8-1&keywords=the+hormone+cure) this stimulates the production of Estrogen.

The Maca team says it stimulates hormone production in general (along with other benefits), but based on my response I would say estrogen was the main hormone stimulated. I am only 30 so I am not taking this for menopause, but I had a tubal and really bad pregnancy / last minute c-section and my hormones are all jacked up and I am trying to get back to myself! That being said I researched the TYPE of maca to buy, there is cream, red, and black, and I brought this specific kind because it is a mix of all three. If you want to know what each type does, the Maca Team does a great job explaining on their website found at www.themacateam.com. They explain the types and the processing differences between pills and powder and the benefits. This is the best choice if you can get it down. If you can't get it down, you might as well take the pills cause they are better than nothing!

So, know that it works, but know that if you are sensitive to taste / texture / burn / smell at all get the pills. I wish I would have!! I am going to try to choke down the rest of this bag, but like this morning I had to give up after a few sips of my smoothie. I just couldn't do it.

Nature's plus has my undying gratitude in the form of my lifelong loyalty as a customer. I've always loved Five Hour Energy, but if that stuff puts you on the moon, this stuff has you orbiting Neptune.

title: Nicely organized first aid kit
text:
As a mother of 2 small children,  I can't stress the importance of being prepared in emergencies whether it be in the park or a drive to the supermarket. Before purchasing this kit, I looked through the list of items it contained:

Large Gauze Pads
Small Gauze Pads
Gauze Wraps
Large Bandage Wraps
Small Bandage Wraps
Triangular Bandages
Large Bandages
Small Bandages
Emergency Blanket
Cold Pack
Latex Gloves
Eye Pads
Medical Tapes
Tweezers
Scissors
Iodine Prep Pads
Antiseptic Towelettes
Alcohol Pads
Cotton Swabs
Tongue Depressors
Glow Stick
Whistle
Compass

This set comes in a durable nylon bag with most of the items you could think of when an accident occurs, except I added some packets of neosporin to the kit. There are 4 separate compartments that unfold. The items are arranged in a way that you wouldn't have to struggle and rummage through to get what you're looking for, everything is very accessible. Although the kit has most of everything you would need, it contained an unnecessarily large amount of q tips and tongue depressors. The tweezers were of poor quality plastic and fragile as were the tiny scissors and compass. The whistle reminded me of a kid's plastic party favor but was loud enough. I liked that there were 2 pairs of gloves as most other kits only come with 1. What I liked most about this kit is the way all the items are organized. I am giving this first aid kit 4 stars due to the quality of some of the most important items and excess of the not so useful ones.

I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for an honest and unbiased feedback. No monetary compensation was received for my review. Product ratings are based on performance, durability, and overall value.

title: Works well but takes some effort to install on Bauer jig saw
text:
1) The massage bit does fit a Bauer 20v Hypermax cordless orbital jigsaw from Harbor Freight.
2) The shank on the bit is thick, and it does not fit the chuck easily. I did not have to grind it down as I've read in other reviews. Some people will not agree with what I did, but I was able to install the bit by tapping it in with a rubber mallet. As you can see in the pics, it does fit completely within the chuck, and it is stable and solid. I may have to use pliers or something to remove it when the time comes, but I bought the jig saw almost exclusively to use with the massage bits. I have another jig saw for cutting but it's older and doesn't use T-shank bits/blades.
3) The tips themselves are great. I was a little concerned that they might be harder and smoother than I wanted, but they are perfect. The surface is rubbery not plasticky, and the material is somewhat soft. I can squeeze it in my hands. Firmer than an racquetball or tennis ball, but not as firm as a lacrosse ball. That's what I wanted. I didn't want to be beating myself up with the tips. The texture of the ball is slick enough that it doesn't pull hair out of my skin. I had read a review that some tip textures have done that to others.
4) I was surprised that I could use it at high speed on the jig saw. I thought I'd have to take it easy, but the higher speed actually works better I think. You just have to be aware of how close you hold it to the muscle so the stroke doesn't have the tip hitting deeper than you want.

Overall, I think it's great. Great value. 6 tips, a bit, and an extension (if you need it) for only a few bucks more than sets with 1, 2, or 3 tips. You may want to have someone assist with hard to reach areas like triceps or hamstrings. I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 because of the effort needed to insert the bit into my Bauer jig saw. I've seen videos of these types of bits popping right into other jig saws with no effort at all, so if you have one of the ones known to be compatible, it'll be an easy install. And for those of you like me where he bit seems to be too thick, try tapping it in with a rubber mallet.

text: I had an embarrassing problem.  Some external hemorrhoids appeared and were sore and itching terribly.  Additionally, the skin in my intergluteal cleft (i.e. butt crack)  and on my perineum was sore and itchy and a couple of fine red lines appeared on the skin in those locations. Still, the problem would not go away.  Then, I read advice online where several people suggested keeping the area dry with powder, instead of using creams or ointments..  I didn't feel the area was particularly moist, but I figured it couldn't hurt to try.  So I tried this medicated Caldesene powder.  Within hours, the itch and sting were completely gone.  I applied the powder 2 or 3 times a day and by the third day when I took a look at the area again with a mirror, the external hemorrhoids had gone completely down and the red irritated lines were gone.  Pretty amazing.

title: THIS STUFF ACTUALLY WORKS!!!!
text:
Several years ago, I had a sink that was draining very slowly. I had tried other kinds of "big-name" drain cleaners, but they didn't do much...and one night, I saw an ad for this SuperFast (maybe on QVC), and I ordered some...not expecting much...but...it worked. Cleared the sink drain over night.

More recently, for several months now, my shower drain has been getting slower and slower and slower...until I finally got tired of standing in water up to my ankles every morning. I came here to Amazon, and have to admit I was confused by all the various Amos products, but finally decided that SuperFast was what I needed...so I ordered it.

But it still took a few more months for me to actually get around to trying it...over this last weekend. I poured in the recommended amount in the middle of the afternoon...(there was no standing water) then I just left it until the next morning. Got up, ran some hot water into the drain slowly...and glug glug glug...the water was actually flowing down the drain.

I let the hot water run for several minutes, and now when I take a shower, the water goes down the drain just as it should.

I have to admit that I was surprised...in a good way.

title: Great, But Maybe Not For Nursing!
text:
I like absolutely everything about this watch but two and a half things, and they are important for many nursing positions.

The light is only on as long as you are pressing the button. The only way to take a pulse, count respirations, drops/minute, etc, in dark or dim light would be to take the watch off, hold the watch within view and press the button with one hand, and use the free hand to take the pulse, feel the chest, etc. Not very handy!

There is no mention anywhere of water resistance, so you must assume that this watch could drown very easily. It apparently cannot swim, or even tread water. So, if you need to wash your hands often, buyer beware.

Finally, it is something that you could get accustomed to, but there is a logo/design on the face of this watch which has long thin lines on it which can be confused with the hands of the watch, maybe every time you look at it, for who knows how long?

But I really do love this watch otherwise. It has a large (1") face, almost ¼" larger including the bezel. The white leather band is substantial and lovely. I would say I am wearing it right now, but I tend to take it off when I am doing any substantial typing.

text:
This kit definitely exceeded my expectations. In this price range, I was expecting flimsy. That is definitely not what I got.

Cuffs- Hand and ankle cuffs were thicker than expected with sturdier rings than more expensive items bought at a physical store.

Ball gag- Sturdier plastic than the one I have from a previous purchase. That one would bend when squeezed, it was roughly the consistency of a ping pong ball, this one is a harder plastic that does not bend.

Collar - A little tall for my use. Thick and sturdy like the rest of the set. The lining on the inside was soft and made it more comfortable.

Paddle- A little harsher than I was expecting. It has a spine built into it to improve it's sturdiness and it is effective.

Whip - Not as strong as I would have expected, given the quality of this set. Not useless, just not the same quality.

Nipple clamps - I was surprised to find that these were the more comfy adjustable type. Non-adjustables are just too painful to wear and I expected these to be a useless item for me.

Eye mask - Pass. This one is cheap and flimsy feeling. Does not block vision and is uncomfortable. This is where I removed a half star.

Leash - Pass. This is the worst piece in the kit. A small piece of (vinyl?) that can not be used. This is where I removed a half star.

Feather tickler - Meh, not my thing. Came with the kit. Seems to be decent quality, but not really sure what the purpose is here.

Over all, I was surprised and pleased with this kit. This is perfect for someone just starting out and not wanting to invest a lot of money before learning what they are into. The smell is atrocious when it first comes out of the box, but that is to be expected. Would definitely recommend/ purchase again. title: Great for vegan pregnancy
text:
I am currently pregnant and a vegan, as well as gluten free. Because of that combination it's been more difficult to get enough protein in my diet so halfway through my pregnancy, I started using the shake & go smoothies and they have been great. I have it on days where I feel my protein is a little lacking and I often mix it with organic soymilk to add another boost of protein. For those avoiding soy, it's also great with almond, rice, hemp milk, etc.

Before purchasing, I did extensive research on many different protein powders to try and find the safest one for pregnancy that was high quality, affordable and had a flavor. While it is a little pricey, this was the best product for me. I started out having a sample of the vanilla almondilla and the taste was a bit different to me, but I had it mixed with water. After that I purchased the chocolate flavor, which I really liked, but have recently started to get tired of, so I decided to give the vanilla amondilla another try. I have to say that I think it's the better tasting of the two - I think the trick is to add it to some non-dairy milk, not water. It's much creamier and I think tastes way better and is less chalky.

It feels good knowing that I am able to use a safe protein product during my pregnancy that is also full of great nutrients for the baby!

title: Leaky Gut Relief! If only I had started sooner....
text: I've been battling SIBO and food sensitivities for a few years.  Constant reflux and bloating.  Literally-everything gave me reflux.  After multiple treatments for SIBO and thousands of dollars in high end supplements, this has helped tremendously in just a week!  The trick to L-glutamine is DOSING!  One resource suggested starting at 10gms and building up to 40gms a day.  DO NOT DO THIS!  I started with 2.5gms twice a day and increased my dose by 2.5gms (twice daily) every two days.  I am now up to 30gms (split into 15gms twice daily) for five days and I am tolerating it well! Once I finish my 30gm daily doses, I will decrease the same as I increased and do a maintenance dose of 5-10gms daily.  Trust the process of starting slow and building your tolerance.

title: Excellent Under the Bed Restraint System!
text:
The Funux Under Bed Restraint Bondage Straps are wonderful for people who don't have a place to attach restraints on a bed! We have a bed with railings in the guestroom (which we have used for restraining before) but we prefer our own bed, which is a sleigh bed. There is no place to hook restraint straps on our bed, so this allows us to still play with bondage sets by putting the straps under the mattress and then hooking the restraints to the clasps on the edges.

This set comes with wrist and ankle restraints as well. They use Velcro but they are very strong. The long Velcro area allows it to be adjusted to all body types. I have big wrists and ankles and these fit me fine. The side that goes against your skin is very soft and comfortable. There is a hook on each to easily attach to the under the bed restraint straps. However, if you have another pair of restraints that have a hook on them, you can use those instead of the ones that come with this set. This set works perfectly well though! The set also comes with an eye mask. It is thin but solid so it does block your sight. It has a soft fabric on one side. It isn't adjustable, though I found it comfortable.

This set comes packaged very discreetly in a plain box. Even when you open the box, you will find a plain silver package that it's packed in so that no one else will know what you've purchased except for those you choose to tell. Everything is very durable and holds up nicely. We have had a lot of fun with it and recommend it to couples who don't have a place to attach restraints. It's wonderful for spicing things up in the bedroom!

The next day we were doing ventilation drills with chainsaws. I put these on and watched my instructor draw the cut pattern. I guess, to be more precise, I watched a cloudy version of my instructor as the lenses began to fog up. Wait… weren’t the lenses anti-fog? I chalked it up to being in the warm apparatus bay, but brought along my regular safety glasses just in case. I checked the vents and one of them had slid closed, so I reopened it. I wiped the lenses with my thumb (since I was in full gear) and put them back on. While I was waiting for my turn to cut, they started fogging up again. So I put them on my helmet and used my glasses.

I took them home that night and brainstormed how to make them work. I liked the way the amber lenses cut out the sunlight and they looked cool. I really wanted to make these work. I reasoned the vents closing (they had slid closed again several times) was the problem. So I removed the covers so they were always opened.

A couple of days later we were doing extrication work on a MUCH colder day (in the teens or so). I slipped these on and they still fogged up off and on. But when I started doing any kind of work, they fogged over again. So I retired them to the back of my helmet for the rest of the class.

The plus side is since I put the goggles on my helmet backwards, people started calling me Wildcat. I've noticed the poor reviews of this product, and its similar iterations. I wish they existed before I bought these; I wouldn't have wasted my money.

title: Mixed Reviews From My Household
text:
First, I bought three different brands of diaper liners, and I see no substantial difference among them. This one is a bit stiffer than he bummis at first, but once it's all sweaty/wet, it seems about the same. It does not stand up well to washing in my washing machine, but that's probably good if it claims to be flushable. It does stand up to hand-rinsing, so if you want to get extended use out of a wet one, I recommend rinsing it and hanging it up to dry.

Here's where it gets a bit graphic, so if you can't handle the poop talk... oh, nevermind. You're reading about diaper products! Clearly you can handle the poop talk!

My mom loves these, so I make sure to put one in my daughter's diaper before my mom comes to babysit. Mom claims that it makes things very neat and tidy, and makes it easy to dispose of the poop.

In my experience, it is true that the liner makes it easy to lift out a formed poop, but I find it easy enough to get formed poops off my diapers even without a liner. I basically just roll them off into the toilet using the diaper itself (formed poop sticks to itself better than to the diaper). It's not the formed poops I'm worried about: it's the soft or liquid poops. For soft or liquid poops, the liners don't offer much advantage. Sure you can lift SOME of the poop off the diaper, but I generally get messy hands doing so, and a lot of poop is left in the diaper despite the liner. It just oozes around the edges and up the front or up the back beyond the confines of the liner. I end up having to spray or wipe the diaper anyway, and at that point, it doesn't feel as though the liner saved me anything.

So there you have it. One brand seems much like the others to me, so you might as well buy the cheaper ones. My mom loves them and swears by them, and anything that keeps her happy about my choice to use cloth diapers is a good thing in my book, so I'll continue to buy them, but when it's just me dealing with the diapers, I don't use the liners at all because I don't think they make a huge difference.
