title: I will recommend this to my patients
text: As an eye doctor, I can't tell you how many times per day I have a conversation about dry eye treatment with my patients. We are all victims of too much screen time and our eyes suffer the consequences of our long work days staring at the screen and too infrequent blinking, which all contribute to ocular surface irritation. For years I have recommend cool compresses to my patients to relieve symptoms of tired/irritated eyes and inflamed/puffy lids, but traditional cool compresses can be a hassle to keep up with (who has time to pop a compress in the fridge hours ahead of use and clean it on a regular basis?). I love how portable the Cornea Care Rescue self cooling hydrogel cold compresses are - no need for a fridge, just take them out of the packet and they are good to use on the go. It works for my busy schedule and relieves my tired eye symptoms. I also appreciate the simplicity of the ingredients including natural plant extracts and refreshing menthol. I only use preservative free products around my eyes and recommend the same to my patients when possible. CorneaCare Rescue cold compresses meet my eye care needs and so far I haven't found anything as portable, user friendly and effective.

text: This provides some relief, but no miracles. I had used the Medela velcro maternity support through my first pregnancy and into my third trimester this pregnancy. It worked better than nothing, but I was doubled over in pain from stretching abdominal ligaments and pubic and sacroiliac joint instability. My OB prescribed me this Prenatal Cradle at about 34 weeks. My insurance covered the cost, but it had to be purchased through a medical supply company. They ordered me a medium based on my pre-pregnancy weight and pants size. They didn't tell me this also comes in tall (5'10"+) sizes, which are available through the manufacturer's website. It doesn't come with any instructions, but the manufacture does have a You Tube video demonstrating how to put it on. I can comfortably wear the belt on the middle set of hooks (my belly measures 42" at the navel), though it tends to ride up in the back. I've tried wearing the belt tighter and the straps looser, but it still rides up. Because it usually sits half above my hips, this does nothing for my back pain. However, it helps noticeably with my lower abdominal pain and I can almost stand upright again while wearing this. I've worn this belt for 3 weeks now and it's starting to fall apart. I washed it on gentle in a lingere bag, per the tag, but the fabric that the belt's hook fasteners are sewn to is fraying at the top. In summary, this belt is better than the Medela support, but cheaply made.

title: Don't waste your money.
text: I had my first experience with hair chalk a few weeks ago using Profess Xtra L Chalk (Red) which comes in a container that looks like eye shadow palette. You have to rub your hair against the color while holding in the palette. The cost is about $15 for one color so I thought the Monster Chalk looks like it would be easier to use and I can get 24 colors for the same price. Well, perhaps the ones I received came from a bad batch but the colors did not go on nearly as well and it added a weird texture to my hair. I have no idea how anyone could give these 5 stars. I had both the Profess Xtra Chalk and the Monster Chalk in my hair and you could tell the Monster chalk was... well, Chalky and flaky and I followed the instructions precisely. The Profess Xtra chalk was a harder to apply (due to the packaging) but overall it looked smooth and polished. It also washed off my hands easily whereas the Monster chalk stained my hands for a couple of days and as mentioned the Profess Xtra was much less flaky. I don't work for Profess Xtra, but I wanted to share my experience with one that was more expensive because I think someone mentioned that you can use straight up chalk and get a nice effect. That is completely incorrect. The more expensive one is the way to go if you want something that looks smooth and natural.. well, as natural as blue hair can look =)

And that's really the story of MuscleEgg in a nutshell. I have used maybe 1/3 of all orders because there is always something wrong with the packaging making it unusable. From holes in the bottles, to ice chunks that will not go away - the product itself is great, when you deal with the shipping process that simply doesn't work.

title: great concept, very poor technical QA
text:
I must also count myself amongst the "IT Professionals" with a bad experience with this product. Or, a bad string of experiences.

It started out so nicely. It connected to my home network consisting of two Cisco Aironet 1252 WAPs (running a WPA2 key) using the OSX installer from my laptop. It worked great. We all used it for about three weeks.

Then, it started saying it couldn't sync. Nothing had changed in the network config or topology. So, I decided to try to put it into setup mode and have it re-connect. It was never able to "re-connect."

I used a packet sniffer, as well as turning on debugging on the Aironets, and found that the device was actually able to successfully connect to the wifi network, to the point of getting a DHCP assignment, sending a few frames to the internet, and getting a few response frames from fitbit. It then continued to say it was unable to sync.

Customer service, to whom I provided a pcap file and cisco debug logs showing what was happening, was not at all helpful, although friendly, they only were able to offer the sort of inane technical help you have probably come to expect.. things along the lines of move the scale, replace the batteries, etc (all of which i did, with the expected lack of change in behavior).

I gave up on it for a few weeks, and then decided to try again and do a deeper packet dive into the exchange it was having. I used a desktop mac to try to get it out of setup mode, and failed. With the install utility, it was able to talk to the scale, but it never got it back out of setup mode. I eventually got it to get out of setup mode after failing with the installer on my osx desktop, failing with the web installer on my osx desktop in various browsers, failing with the installer on my laptop (which had worked previously), and failing with the web installer on my laptop unless i was using safari. Finally, having gotten it to move beyond the "setup" screen, it absolutely refused to advance (or to provide any feedback that it was failing to advance) beyond the attach to network stage, the same network and same config which had originally worked fine.

Eventually, I pointed it to a cheap netlogic WAP that I happened to have set up and unprotected for some unrelated testing work. From the laptop only, from safari only, it finally attached to the network. I've decided to leave that junky WAP online for now & unprotected just to keep the scale online.

In summary, if you can get this thing to work, and if you can get it to remain working even though it may appear to be working originally, it is a great product. Good luck with that, though.. this is seriously some of the worst QA'd hardware/software I have worked with in many years, excepting the junk that comes from China.

Finally, I have an offer for fitbit. I live in the bay area. I have your product here. I am a network engineer with an EE & CS background. It still cannot attach to my home production network. Send someone over for dinner. I will feed them, and then show them & happily let them debug what is clearly a major set of QA issues with your product, in my house. I can & will help with the debugging, packet capture and analysis, and trying alternate configs to isolate the issues that so many customers are having. Seriously. I want this thing to work, I spend good money on it, and it presently does not. I am also not, by any means, the only person experiencing these issues. So, here is a live testbed for you to fix your broken firmware & installers. Please, please, take me up on this offer. Thanks!

title: Works for most things but...
text:
I have owned one of these for a couple of years now, and for the most part it works well, but there are a couple of service issues that most people do not think about or do not know about.

1st. You need to own 2 battery packs, then run the battery pack all the way down and do NOT put the vacuum on the charger mount! Why? Because the charger will charge the battery pack in the vacuum, no matter what the discharge level is... in other words you are burning out the limited 1000 charge/discharge cycles for nothing. So use one battery pack until it is depleted, then swap it out for the other battery pack for a LOMG OPERATIONAL LIFESPAN on the batteries. I wish they would provide these with the newer LiFePo4 batteries instead, as I do not like the fact that manufacturers are still dumping their inventories of older batteries with newer units.

2nd. You need to take the rollar out occasionally to clean, AND remove all hair which wraps around the rollar brush.

3rd. For a cleaner smelling usage of the vacuum, just sprinkly a tablespoon or two of baking soda on the floor after each filter cleaning, and vacuum the baking soda up.

I use my vacuum all the time, on tile, hardwood, and carpet.

title: Comfortable; simple to place on your toes; can be worn in your shoes
text:
I didn't know what a bunion was before until I had it, and it was a very painful experience trying to walk. If you look up the cause to bunions, you will find that there are different theories. Some people think it is the result of a tight shoe and others think its genetics. Either way they concluded that it deals with the big toe leaning toward the second toe rather then pointing straight ahead as it should. Because of this, the bones are thrown out of alignment producing the bunion you may have forming around your big toe's joint.

From my personal experience of dealing with a painful 2 week bunion, you will definitely need a toe separator, proper doses of ibuprofen for swelling, and an ice pack to also keep down the swelling on your bunion. This toe separator will probably be the most important thing you will need to correct the problem. It will help align your toe into its proper place which should prevent an even worse bunion from continuing to swell around your big toe's joint.

This product from my personal experience has a huge advantage over those you may find at Walmart. The first thing I like about this product is that it is very comfortable. The material used isn't a hard plastic or a very tight product. This toe separator is made of a gel like substance that can stretch out over your toes without the fear of it tearing in your hands. If you go to your local Walmart they have some similar products but they are made of a bandage material and are very tight and very difficult and painful to put on. You may also find other products that have to wrap around your foot to keep your toe separated. Although they do the job, you can not walk around with it on! That is why I simply love this product. It is so simple that it allows you to continue walking around without having to remove it. It is also nice that they give you two different products both with an extra toe separator. All in all a great product, good to keep with your medical supplies because bunions can always come back. I did receive this product for free for my honest and unbiased review.

I would also like to point out, in case you never had a bunion before, it is important to place ice on the bunion to bring down the swelling. I would also suggest taking ibuprofen and following the dosage shown on the label to help with pain and swelling. My bunion was so painful that I could not place any pressure on my foot or walk. It was not until I used a toe separator, took medication, and placed ice on the swelling did I start feeling relief to walk again. However, when I stop taking ibuprofen the swelling would come back and I would find myself unable to place pressure on my foot. I had to keep the toe separator on my foot for a few days before I no longer needed it, but you will definitely see the difference in your bunion. You may have a different level of pain then I did so it is ultimately up to you how you would like to handle the situation. I would only like to suggest that you definitely get a toe separator to align your toe to prevent the bunion from getting worse. I hope my review has been helpful and hope your bunion is resolved quicker then mine!

I bought this replacement handle, because it would have cost almost twice as much to buy an original Waterpik brand replacement. Although other reviewers said it was a problem, I didn't see how the water flow could be that much less.. Now I SEE!! It's like you've set your Waterpik pressure on 1 and that's as high as it will go.. It's a trickle and barely flows, and my Waterpik is set on 10. It takes twice as long (or longer) to empty the tank with this nozzle, because the flow is so low.

Additionally, the swivel action of the mouthpiece in the handle doesn't work right. You can turn the holder, but the pik itself doesn't turn when you spin the handle control. There's no point in having a spinning handle control, if it doesn't turn the mouthpiece itself.

I've definitely wasted my money by trying to save money with this replacement product, and am afraid the back pressure might actually ruin my machine. Only a refund could make this bad purchase better!

title: Amazing support for twin pregnancy!
text:
I am 21 weeks pregnant with twins. I have a support belt from Motherhood from my 1st (singleton) pregnancy that I found to be uncomfortable and really rather unhelpful. I only tried wearing it 3 times and just gave up. (I did not have back pain with my first pregnancy, and have not had it - yet- my problem is that my belly feels too heavy and I want support holding it up!) The Motherhood belt seems to be just for back support. This one, however, provides both!

I have the same complaints about it that other reviewers have noted - the shoulder straps show above the collar of most shirts (I solve this by safety pinning it to my bra straps - i'd like to attach something like lingere snaps directly to the shoulder straps, so I can just snap it around my bra straps). That helps for the collar problem with most shirts. It is still a problem with lower cut and v-neck shirts.

I do wish there were more eye hooks on the part that supports my belly. I was a size 6 before pregnancy, and at 21 weeks with twins I have a belly about the same size as mine was when I was full term with my singleton 1st baby. I've been switching between the middle and loosest hooks. An option to hook it between those two would probably work better. It does look like it would be easy to add an extra set of eye hooks (and I just might do that), but so far it has been more of a minor irritation. I start most days on the middle hooks, and if/when it starts to feel like it's digging in I just adjust it to the looser option and it's fine for the rest of the day. Slightly less support that way, but still leaps and bounds better than no support.

It is incredibly easy to make all of the adjustments while wearing this product. I can easily and quickly adjust it during one of my frequent trips to the bathroom at work. I wear the style of maternity pants that come up over my belly, so I do need to pull that down in order to adjust the belly support. It is not necessary to take it off or adjust it when going to the bathroom. (I remember the Maternity one being uncomfortable going to the bathroom while wearing). It is flexible enough to adjust well enough that it does not dig in anywhere while sitting.

Although I wasn't experiencing any back pain before wearing this, I'm really loving the excellent back support. It feels great, and I have noticed that it helps me keep better posture, which I'm sure will prevent future back pain.

Highly recommend this product, and also hope the manufacturer works on fixes for the two problems noted above (don't let those two things keep you from purchasing this product, though - they're minor and it's possible to work around them, which is worth it considering the incredible support it provides).

title: Difficult to set up, failed after just three years, replacement declined
text:
To set up the scale you need to take out the batteries, put them back in, open a special website, connect your device's wifi to the scale's wifi, finish using the website (which is slow and sometimes doesn't work at all), reconnect to your wifi and then you're *probably* done. I struggled to get this working after several attempts, but once I got it working it was good for a while.

After three years of use, my scale would say "sensing" "step off" and then I'd step off, but the scale would repeat "step off" until it went back to sleep. I googled this problem and it's a *very* widespread failure of this product. I tried all the troubleshooting steps recommended by FitBit and other users to no avail, short of actually taking it apart.

After taking all these steps I reached out to FitBit. They declined to replace the unit, despite how pervasive this issue is, because I was out of the warranty. And now I'm out $150.

Bad product, bad service. Avoid.

title: Too many jams which resulted in wasted test strips.
text:
As per our usual process, we search online retailers, EBay, big box stores and Amazon for a new type of glucose tester for my father. He wanted to try a different approach to loading the test strips so that he did not have load them individually each time he wanted to test his glucose levels. This seller had the Breeze 2 tester at what we considered a very reasonable price and promised quick deliver. Well, they kept their promise as the tester arrived when it was promised. Great seller to work with.

As I mentioned in my review of the test strips for this unit, after trying to use the 10 wheels of test strips that came in the box of test strips that we ordered separately, we decided to go back to the old unit that we have where we load each strip individually. The reason being that we were never able to use all of 10 strips on the wheel. Each wheel that we tried had at least one strip jam when it rotated into position. Several of the wheels had 2 or more jams. We can not say if the cause of the jams was with the testing unit or the wheel of strips. But after having 10 out of 10 wheel jam, we decided to change back to the old testing unit.

title: Fits the bill!
text:
We found these fairly easy to assemble with 2 sets of hands. Some parts didn't seem to fit together very well, so my husband held them in place while I tightened the nuts. Attaching them to our Aero Crossbars was much simpler, but I would have preferred the bottom bracket to be flat- bother vehicles have the flat aerodynamic crossbars.
We did install the with the longer part on the outsides of the vehicle, so they make a "W" on the roof of the car.
The problem for us, was the lack of instructions on how to tie down the kayaks. We have used the supplied straps for shorter trips, when our ratchet straps were not available, but I MUCH prefer our ratchet straps! We loop the strap around each kayak and cross under the crossbars. Essentially, the J carrier only holds the kayak on it's side, while the ratchet strap holds the kayak to the crossbars.
Overall, I think that if we looped the provided straps through the J carrier and over the kayak (just strapping to the J carrier), in combination with our aero bars, on a longer trip, these j carriers would be likely to fail. We will likely look at name-brand j-style carriers for something sturdier for the next season. I am still researching a better way to tie down our kayaks.

title: The greatest multi-tasking toothpaste ever
text: I was lucky to receive a full size tube of Crest Pro-Health Toothpaste- Fresh Clean Mint for free from Smiley 360. I wanted to share my opinion of the product to give insight into how effective it has been for me personally. I am a huge advocate for amazing dental hygiene and strive to always get a thumbs-up at each and every dentist appointment. This toothpaste is actually the multi-tasker of all toothpastes without a doubt. Many toothpastes will claim they can whiten teeth or help with sensitivity or help with tartar or keep your breath fresh and more. This toothpaste does all of these things and exceeded my expectations. I have sensitive teeth and this absolutely worked better than the brand I was using prior to this.  I had no problems eating anything that was too cold at all so it filled my need for sensitivity protection. In my profession I always need to make a great impression and because I smile a lot I value the ability to whiten my teeth with a toothpaste that covers my other needs too. I enjoy my two cups of coffee each day and Crest Pro-Health made it possible that I wouldn't have to worry about any lasting coffee stains on my teeth. The fact that Crest Pro-Health was inspired by dentists just adds another feather to its cap. Ooh and I don't want to forget to mention that it's Triclosan-free. Triclosan is being further reviewed by the FDA because it may actually help make bacterias resistant to antibiotics. It has also been shown to alter hormone regulation in animals. It is not proven to actually be a danger to people at this point but, the FDA is definitely looking into it further. I prefer to avoid products with Triclosan in them just to stay on the safe side. Thank you so much Crest for your awesome multi-tasking Crest Pro-Health. I received this product for free for the purpose of my review and all of my opinions are  100% my own.

title: Not a toothbrush replacement
text:
I really hate rating things down that do exactly what they say, even if what they’ve say is less than what I consider ideal. Luckily this product clearly claims that it's an equivalent to a normal toothbrush, and that it can clean better in some of the material.

That's just not true.....

The silicone bristles are much too large to penetrate between teeth. They're also just not rigid, not at all. The vibratory action seems fine, but I'm not sure if it's doing much due to the design of those bristles. The only way I could make my teeth feel clean is by manually manipulating this thing and brushing my teeth using my hand, like a classic manual brush. Even then, it just doesn't work as well as classic bristles.

So...... for making claims that this works as well as a brush it loses a star. For using a bristle that is obviously not designed by someone with knowledge on how to clean teeth it loses another star.

The following are just observations and are not providing weight to the 3 star review. Since I think all devices similar to this will probably work the same way. Mainly, you might need some special toothpaste. I've tried an Aquafresh and a Sensodine paste, and both of them are much too viscous to be properly frothed by the vibratory action this device provides. After 30 seconds, after a minute, after 2 minutes, there are still globs of paste that did not froth. So... in order to get tooth paste onto all surfaces of your teeth you'd have to literally brush your teeth before using this, again defeating the purpose. Or you can use 10x more paste than normal to coat the entire thing... that might work? Finally, those globs of tooth paste take forever to clean off of the spongy silicone.

The whole thing is a mess.... I'd be very skeptical of any glowing reviews. I just don't see it happening.

On the good side, the charger works, and the rubberized coating is nice.

text:
Purchased this, based on all of the reviews and youtube videos showing how to use. It does exactly as it claims. I've used St. Ives Apricot Scrub for years, and have also purchased Microdermabrasion Crystals, from Amazon.com Smile, to mix my own scrubs, however, wanted to try this.

The skin does roll off your body, and when using on your face, do not look for that same effect. I have only used it twice on my face, to space out the exfoliation and to let my skin heal, but, there is a definite difference.

One thing to note, is, if using on your face, scrub up and down and then sideways - do not rub in circles. Also, press firmly, but, not enough to break your skin. Your skin will get red, and you will feel like you have a sunburn, but, the aftereffects are so well worth it. My face is actually smoother and softer, after just using it twice. Do not use it everyday on your face, as it would be way too much exfoliation and your skin will never heal.

It truly does what it claims and in the end, is more cost effective, as scrubs, and professional treatments add up very quickly, and this is something that will last for at least 2 years. If you add it all up, you are getting a great deal here AND it actually does what it says.

One last thing, is that customer service/support is great and they will answer any questions you have and explain what to do, if you are experiencing any problems. That in itself shows they stand behind what they are selling and claiming this product can do - and it does.

Licorice Root (Glycyrrhiza Glabra)

Licorice Root Benefits

Licorice root contains many anti-depressant compounds and is an excellent alternative to St. John's Wort. As a herbal medicine it has an impressive list of well documented uses and is probably one of the most over-looked of all herbal wonders. Licorice is useful for many ailments including:

Health benefits
Healing substances

Hundreds of potentially healing substances have been identified in licorice as well, including compounds called flavonoids and various plant estrogens (phytoestrogens). The herb's key therapeutic compound, glycyrrhizin (which is 50 times sweeter than sugar) exerts numerous beneficial effects on the body, making licorice a valuable herb for treating a host of ailments. It seems to prevent the breakdown of adrenal hormones such as cortisol (the body's primary stress-fighting adrenal hormone), making these hormones more available to the body.

It has a well-documented reputation for healing ulcers. It can lower stomach acid levels, relieve heartburn and indigestion and acts as a mild laxative.

It can also be used for irritation, inflammation and spasm in the digestive tract. Through its beneficial action on the liver, it increases bile flow and lowers cholesterol levels.

Boosts immune system

Licorice also appears to enhance immunity by boosting levels of interferon, a key immune system chemical that fights off attacking viruses. It also contains powerful antioxidants as well as certain phytoestrogens that can perform some of the functions of the body's natural estrogens; very helpful during the menopause. Glycyrrhizinic acid also seems to stop the growth of many bacteria and of viruses such as influenza A.

Relieves pain and stress

It has an aspirin-like action and is helpful in relieving fevers and soothing pain such as headaches. Its anti-allergenic effect is very useful for hay fever, allergic rhinitis, conjunctivitis and bronchial asthma. Possibly by its action on the adrenal glands, licorice has the ability to improve resistance to stress. It should be thought of during times of both physical and emotional stress, after surgery or during convalescence, or when feeling tired and run down.

New research: Licorice hailed for its potential to fight tooth decay

Control respiratory problems and sore throat

Licorice eases congestion and coughing by helping to loosen and thin mucus in airways; this makes a cough more "productive," bringing up phlegm and other mucus bits. Licorice also helps to relax bronchial spasms. The herb also soothes soreness in the throat and fights viruses that cause respiratory illnesses and an overproduction of mucus, such as irritating coughs, asthma and chest infections.
Lessen symptoms of chronic fatigue syndrome and fibromyalgia

By enhancing cortisol activity, glycyrrhizin helps to increase energy, ease stress and reduce the symptoms of ailments sensitive to cortisol levels, such as chronic fatigue syndrome and fibromylagia.

Combat hepatitis

Licorice both protects the liver and promotes healing in this vital organ. The herb's anti-inflammatory properties help calm hepatitis-associated liver inflammation. Licorice also fights the virus commonly responsible for hepatitis and supplies valuable antioxidant compounds that help maintain the overall health of the liver.

Treat PMS and menstrual problems

The phytoestrogens in licorice have a mild estrogenic effect, making the herb potentially useful in easing certain symptoms of PMS (premenstrual syndrome), such as irritability, bloating and breast tenderness. Although the glycyrrhizin in licorice actually inhibits the effect of the body's own estrogens, the mild estrogenic effect produced by licorice's phytoestrogens manages to override this inhibiting action.

Prevent heart disease

Recent studies have found that by limiting the damage from LDL ("bad") cholesterol, licorice may discourage artery-clogging plaque formation and contribute to the healthy functioning of the heart.

title: Worked great to clean up old paste and prep the CPU and heatsink for new grease
text:
This two-part system works great and well work having. I used ArctiClean 1 to remove the 9-10 year old dried up paste in two of my old PCs, and it did a great job. All that was left after cleaning and removing the old paste was a little bit of black residue on the aluminum heat sink, and that was removed by using ArctiClean 2. I used some new carbon-based thermal paste and reassembled my PCs, and both are working good and the CPU in each machine is running cool.

If anyone is planning to do what I did and replace old paste on the CPU, and the CPU heatsink fins have any dirt or dust that can't be brushed or vacuumed away, I would highly recommend cleaning the heatsink fins with a cleaner safe for aluminum and a soft brush. I used a spray cleaner specifically made for A/C coil cleaning, as many household cleaners will cause aluminum to start to corrode after being exposed to them. I applied the cleaner to the heatsink, brushed the fins, then rinsed with water and let the heatsink dry before putting it back in the computer. I also wore an ESD control wrist strap and line clipped to the chassis when I worked on my PCs.

title: Beautifully designed and built - but heavy!
text:
Just got it in and unpacked. The good news, well, there's lots: the build really exceeds my expectations, as does the design. I think in terms of the thought that went into design and the care into the build, this table is a BARGAIN!. I just had a massage today and I WISH her table had an adjustable head cradle like this one! I feel quite uncomfortable unless I can tilt the cradle down a bit, and it's nothing to accomplish that on this one. The table is also quite attractive in a no-nonsense kind of way. The blue padded top is a might bit clinical, but that is offset by the very nice wooden legs.

This is a very strong table! I weight 260, and when I get on this thing it doesn't budge a bit! Solid as a rock!

The 'extras'? Well, I haven't listened to the music yet. The bolster is functional, covered by the same blue stuff as the cradle and the table. It's not PVC, but it's PVC-like, or Naugahyde-like. Stinks a bit - but I'm sure that'll dissipate after a few days of airing out. The carrying bag is very basic canvas, with outside pockets. Nothing special. However, the cradle can fit inside the table when it's folded. Not sure about the bolster.

The bad news? Heavy! This thing is a beast! They say 35 LBS. Well, maybe. I haven't weighed it, but it's heavy. So, if you work out of one or two offices, or out of your house, this table is a great bargain and seems built to give years and years and years of service (and comes with a lifetime warrantee). But if you travel to massage/therapy gigs, I wouldn't advise this table unless you want transporting it to be part of your workout regimen. Sure you can pack it in the bag and sling the strap over your shoulder - and your shoulder and neck will let you know after you've walked a block or two. You don't want to need a massage after giving one, so don't use this as your travel table.

But what intelligent design and kick-ass construction. It will last, and two elephants could probably mate on top of it without making a squeak (well, the elephants might, but not the table!)

text:
I really wanted this to work. We have horrific musty odors in our undersink areas, and I don't even expect any sort of product to help this. I've bleached, we've checked for mold, etc - to no avail. Regardless, after reading Ona reviews here and in other online forms, I thought it sounded miraculous.

How I used it: I put some of the crumbles in a small container under the sinks. These lasted at least a month, and were roughly about 4 ounces of crumble. There is a LOT of product in the quart container. In that sense, it does go a long way.

1. I believe this product to be effective and more tolerable to the nose in the non-scented form.
2. the Apple form is just not at all "apple" - it's so awful, to be honest. It has no similarity - whatsoever - to apple fragrance. It doesn't even smell fruity, lemony, etc. It honestly reminds me of lysol gone rotten.
3. cost: very value-appropriate for how much you receive and the fact that it will work to eliminate the *original* odor.

Bottom line: I thought this helped at masking the odor we had, but the odor of this product scent itself was worse or equally bad. I would like to try the basic one. My goal is to neutralize, and not out-stink, the original odor.

I do have some doubts these are USA made products only because the usual statement of origin is not idiomatic US/UK english. No native speaker says "Made by USA" or "Made by Espana" - Its always Made in USA or Made In France or wherever. Could a US factory have a packaging manager who wasn't a native English speaker? Of course, but wouldn't someone else in their "USA factory" have seen the non-standard country of origin statement on the label and pointed out the problem?
No one I've met in business would think of allowing a potentially negative labeling issue to place their product's quality in doubt. My doubts lead me to believe these are Chinese made capsules, despite the "Made by USA" labeling.

title: Best sploof you can buy
text:
I've tried pretty much all of the "personal air filters" on offer from reputable retailers on Amazon and Smoke Buddy's product is simply the best option. Like any filter, it only has a certain lifespan and that will be reduced if you're a heavy smoker. That being said Smoke Buddy's filter has the best longevity of those I've tried, not to mention performs among the best at actually neutralizing odors and reducing visible smoke exhaust.

The biggest complaint I've heard is that this product doesn't compare well to homemade alternatives produced much cheaper. I can't argue with those complaints from a value perspective, but I happily purchase the Smoke Buddy because it looks a little more subtle than a toilet paper roll and is exceptionally effective at eliminating odors.

If you want to maximize the life of your personal air filter, there is an empty chamber at the top of the filter that can easily be stuffed with a dryer sheet or even extra cheap surgical masks people may have lying around. You can essentially make a budget prefilter that in my experience multiplies the life of your Smoke Buddy by a factor of 3-4x.

title: I LOVE THESE!!!
text:
Five stars for these Konjac sponges. I love them and I know you are going to love them to. I have really sensitive skin, and have suffered with eczema for years. I have always had to be very careful about what I put on my skin, especially my face, because everything seems to irritate the eczema. These sponges came really fast in the mail I got them in about three days. They came in a with a cute little purple keepsake storage bag.
These konjac sponges provide a natural, effective, non-irritating, non- toxic, deep cleaning for your face. They are all natural, and vegan. That’s always a plus. When you first open up the sponge it is as hard as a brick (this is normal and to be expected of these sponges). Once you put the sponge in the water, let it sit there for a few seconds and it will get really soft and start growing bigger.
When I used my sponges, I use them without any product on them because this only irritates my sensitive skin even more. I use it moving in a circular motion going upward. I have to say, afterward I had no skin irritation at all, and my skin felt really soft and silky. This sponge will leave your skin feeling like you just had a deep cleanse too. I will be purchasing more of this not only for myself, but for friends and family. I recommend this Konjac sponges to anyone that has sensitive skin, even anyone that doesn’t.
I received this product at a discounted rate for my honest, unbiased, opinion. I take all of my reviews serious and I am always honest about them.

title: Really helped dry eyes, vision seems clearer

N-Acetylcysteine is a metabolite of cysteine, a non-essential amino acid that is both found in foods and synthesized by the body from the amino acid methionine. What it gets right - is perhaps the most important element, telling you your weight! I've tested the unit about 18 times on 3 different surfaces around the house. Be aware that the first time you weight yourself (even after moving the scale) the scale seems to calibrate itself. It's off by about 5 lbs the first attempt. Each subsequent attempt (5x on each surface) is within .4 lbs of the other attempts. This accuracy combined with the body measure tape will give you two solid measurements to track your progress. Speaking of the measuring tape, it works well and is a nice added bonus. I opted for the silver edition to match my satin nickel accessorized bathroom, and it goes quite well together. Overall the fit and finish is pretty solid, from afar the unit looks quite appealing.

What it starts to diminish with - is the finer details. My largest gripe is that the base does not sit even with the glass. On the left side the gap is 1/2", but on the right side it's 7/16". Again, this is me being anal. If you're looking at it from far it's hardly noticeable.

Where the glass meets the base the scale has pads that feature a nice chrome mirror finish with concentric circles reminiscent of a vinyl record. However the majority of the base itself is a bland silver-ish color indicative of its price tag. One thing that irks me is the one liner "Max=400lbs D=0.2lbs" below the digital display. I feel it ruins the more expensive vibe it tries to give off, this kind of tag could have just been inserted into an instruction manual or underneath the unit. Also, the box image (4 of 5) is most indicative of the product you will receive. It has a two liner etched into the bottom center of the glass "MOSISO Smart Step On Technology." Again, I feel like it cheapens the unit. It would have been nice if it were just a sticker and removable. Of course the body measure tape includes a MOSISO branding as well. For a freebie I'm not complaining though!

Overall I like the unit a lot, the body measure tape is a freebie I don't often see so it's nice to be able to track two different metrics. At the end of the day it's a scale, and as long as it's repeatably accurate that's all that matters.

title: Kinda OK
text:
I like the small size and that they are rechargeable. I wish they cut hair better.

I have a small poodle that needs grooming and in particular something I can use to get between the pads and toes of his feed. I wanted something small, maneuverable, and quiet as he does not like to be groomed. Probably because I have nicked the web skin between his toes using a regular clipper, or squeezed his foot trying to get the clipper between the pads.

His hair is very fine and can be quite thick, so this little groomer has trouble getting through. The fixed blade is metal, probably stainless steel, while the moving blade is some white substance, possibly plastic, more likely ceramic.

It does cut the hair, but not much at a time and not very aggressively. When you push the blades against a tuft of hair, the tuft is flexible and tends to just get pushed over rather that cut. When I used it on his feet it took a long time and a lot of maneuvering to get a little bit of hair. In particular the thick mat of hair on the bottom of his foot laughed at the little groomer, so I switched back to the regular clipper and dug out the mats of hair (and nicked the web skin, sigh). Once only the dregs of hair were left, the little groomer was able to make progress in cleaning up the last stray patches as long as I could put my finger behind them to keep them from being pushed over.

Bottom line: It works, kinda. It may be useful in the final cleanup on a show dog, but for everyday grooming it is inadequate.

title: Device with - ERR - Problem, Good Support with Long Wait Time
text:
I have enjoyed my Fitbit Charge so far in the past week, and decided to invest in Aria.

- Bad - The Device
I keep getting ERR message, with successful wifi connection, no matter how many times I tried it. With this error, the device is an expensive paper weight. I have not been able to weight myself for the last 2 days since I bought it.

- Good - The Setup and Service
The initial setup was relatively seamless. The device connected to my wifi with no issue. I called the Fitbit support number, and after attempting to reboot it, stepping on/off for several times, they concluded that the device is defective. They said they will ship a new one with ETA in 2 days.

- Conclusion So Far - Use Your Caution
Learning that so many people appear to be having this ERR issue (cause may be different, but users can't tell), I have a feeling that this device went into the market too soon. For a device at this price, with Fitbit tracker's success so far, it must perform better for most of the buyers. It appears that the defect rate is too high. Customer service is good, once you can get hold of them, but expect to wait 10+ minutes during the day, and 20+ minutes (22 minutes for me last night) during evening prime time. I will see how my second Aria will perform, and may raise a star if good result. Will write more once I receive the 2nd unit.

text: My 94 yr old father moved into my house from the hospital after a recent fall. Body wipes at that hospital were wonderful, and these that I found on Amazon seem to be the same quality. They are very thick like felt, soft, and hold a lot of cleaning fluid. I like to use them especially on his bald head, because their felt-like texture gently captures skin flakes on his head, without continuously wiping  for literally half an hour with the thin wipes. The wipes are very moist, which soaks into the dead skin flakes, allowing them to be wiped away much faster than with a thinner, drier wipe. As a result, the skin on his head (or anywhere else) looks healthy and smoother.  His head is a continual difficulty for me to maintain. He doesn't like lotions or creams to combat dryness, which can cause dead skin to "stick" into thick pads of dead skin. These wipes leave a moisturizing layer which seems to help the dryness. I hope that these wipes are always available!

title: Good travel combo
text:
Of the two items in this combo, I am happiest with the flosser- it’s very comparable to a name brand travel flosser I have, right down to the fiddly little rubber cover for the charging port- you don’t want to lose that! You will need an adapter to plug each of these items into an electric socket but those are easy to come by. The flosser has four tips and an orthotics tip (the one with the tiny brush on the end) plus two silicone tip ends -not sure what their purpose is.

The toothbrush on the other hand is not up to expectations. It charges through a port on the bottom of the handle, so it has to be laid on its side to charge. It isn’t very stable standing upright anyway, so will probably always be on its side or perhaps in a cup of some sort. But the biggest drawback I see is finding compatible brushes once you’ve used the four that come with the unit. They suggest changing the brush every three months and they are small and soft so it might need to be more often.

I still think this is a pretty good value and will make a good travel set. I know from years of using these devices that they will benefit your oral health and love seeing the prices come down so more people can afford them.

Each unit comes with operating instructions which are pretty easy to understand given they are written by someone for whom English is not their first language.

title: Adding my voice to the chorus!
text:
I bought this primarily for my son who has a constant post nasal drip, but since he's a little guy, I decided to experiment on myself first.

While I don't suffer from ongoing, painful sinusitis like some of the other reviewers, I had a really bad sinus infection several years ago that left me with a significantly reduced ability to smell. Sometimes it's worse, sometimes better, but overall I really have to stick my nose in deep to smell anything.

I'm currently on day 4 of L. Sakei and I'm kind of amazed... Starting today I can smell things, up close and from a distance. I was able to smell the Nasobiotex (Who knew it has a yeasty smell? Not me circa 3 days ago!). My very simple lunch has layers of flavor, too.

In case it helps, I'll share my exact method. (Also, I hate the word snort--writing it, saying it, hearing it--so I want you to know I'm doing this out of my affection for you as a fellow human.)

To deliver the L. Sakei as deep as into the nasal cavity as I can, I've been snorting it through a rolled up piece of paper.
- To make the straw, cut a clean sheet of paper.
- Roll it tightly around a pencil or pen.
- Tape it down, then slide off the pencil.
- I tried this with different pencil and pen widths and found that what works best is a wider straw that fits tightly in the nostril, almost no space around it.

For the snorting, I place a clean piece of paper on the counter (a post-it note will do - not the sticky side, of course).
- Place two scoops of L. Sakei on the paper, an inch apart.
- Place the paper straw in one nostril and hold the other one closed.
- Snort away.
- Repeat on the other side.

Next up, I give it to my son. I'll report back with an update soon.

Good luck!

title: Might not be good enough.
text:
I’ve now had this for 12 weeks. I use it for longer distances, while the I-walk is used for shorter moves around the house and office. It fails to deliver on most of its promise.

1) foldable: no. No it’s not. Once open and useable it would take a contortionist with super human strength to get this to fold. Try doing it on one foot with someone waiting for you, like a cab. I dare you. The moving parts don’t fit together with any tolerance to allow movement to fold when the retaining bolts are loose. Forget about this feature.

2) brakes: no. No it does not. The wheels have no grip, so IF the brakes stop them from rolling they just slide. The grip strength required to get the brakes to work would rival Thor, and the result of braking is really just wear on the wheel as it drags. I now have a flat spot from a prolonged application of the brakes on an incline. Use your foot. The brakes don’t work.

It needs rubber on the wheels.

Parts: The first one arrived with parts that didn’t fit right. I returned it. The second was the same. Whoever designed the quick release bolts at the front axle was high.

The front wheels attach with bolts that will listen over time. If you go any distance at all please check them before you’re wheels fall off.

The basket: the attachment to the scooter for this sack is downright laughable. It falls off regularly requiring unloading and reinstallation. It’s worse when you try and put it down in the trunk while loaded and it comes out half hanging on.

Keep in mind I bought this to maintain normal mobility while healing from ORIF of my calcaneus. 12 weeks plus time before surgery. I’ve walked dogs, gone to work every day as a physician, gone to museums and taken walks with my family. It’s probably fine for around the house or in a rehab center. But if you want a normalized life on one foot you probably want something else.

title: Heavy guy enjoys this cushion
text:
When the padding wore out on my pricey Steelcase Leap office chair - I scoured the internet for a butt cushion solution without needing to drop a lot of cash on a new chair which I figured out just wear out again. I am a bit on the heavy side, about 230 lbs and I have found that foam/memory foam cushions out there just get squashed flat and do not provide the support or comfort that I need. I thought long and hard before buying the Royal Purple Seat Cushion because I was extremely skeptical; I have never used a Purple product before, so I did not know what the material that they use on their products was all about. I figured that the material is not memory foam so it might just be the solution I am looking for.

Does the product work as advertised?
Yes, I have to say that the cushion is comfortable and has taken the pressure off my lower back. I no longer feel like I am sitting directly on my spine which is exactly why I purchased this product.

HOWEVER Please be aware that there is a 'break in' period for this cushion.
If you are on the heavier side, the edge of the cushion may press firmly against your legs causing them to go numb, which was a huge bummer as I thought this would not work out. My advice is to elevate your legs on some kind of foot stool/rest (about 4 to 5 inches) so that your legs do not press against the edge of the cushion too hard and you do not experience the numbness. After about 2 weeks of 'break in' time, the edges of the cushion have become softer and no longer dig into my legs causing the numbing effect. The Purple Butt Cushion at this point is now perfect - So do not get discouraged if you get the product and experience this - persist and you will be rewarded with a great cushion.

Even though I experienced the temporary 'break in' leg numbness, I still give this product 5 stars because I believe it is the best seat cushion solution out there. In fact my wife takes the cushion off my chair all the time and uses it on her chair (I Guess I may need to get another one).

title: Natural, not sensitive - skin friendly
text:
So bummed. I was really hoping that this was going to be a winner. -I recently ran out of my long - time perfect, natural CC cream because they've started to include dimethicone, so I have been searching for a new daily SPF for face. I was hoping to find something similar to my old cream which would mean naturally sun protective (zinc oxide/titanium dioxide), moisturizing, and having some sheer coverage. (I'm also allergic to salicylic acid/ witch hazel, which only complicates the search!) It has been sadly difficult to find something with minimal ingredients to fit the bill.

I first tried this company's foundation in their other line (Bella Mari), but it was sadly irritating, drying, and very itchy on my skin. That being the case, I thought, "well, a lot of reviews say Herbal Choice is more oily, and it has even fewer ingredients - maybe it will be better!" Unfortunately, that was just wishful thinking.

I really shook the bottle before applying per other user recommendations, so I found the product well-mixed when it came out. I liked the texture, and didn't feel it was too oily (I do the oil - cleanse method and moisturize with grapeseed oil when necessary, so oil doesn't bother me). The color was great for my fair skin (red hair, some freckles), but the scent was a bit unpleasant (whereas the BellaMari foundation had a nice herbal scent). The real problem, however, was that this was even more itchy than the Bella Mari foundation. I tried to make it through the day to give a fair assessment, but I had to wash my face and take it off after just a few hours! When I went to wash, I saw that the product settled around some skin flakes on my forehead which were not visible when I first applied (I mean, had i known I had a lizard skin forehead, I would have addressed it before leaving the house that morning!!)

So, sadly, this was not a winner. I felt it accentuated flaws and only irritated my skin with itching and redness. Not sure what ingredients in these products are the issue, but even though they are doing a great job of staying all - natural, they were not great for my sensitive skin.

text:
I've never taken the "peeling" stuff very seriously. Usually that just means the stuff beads up and gives you a mild scrub (like the facial peeling cleansers). So I used this expecting that sort of thing and was a tad disappointed nothing happened (don't judge me, the instructions/ packaging was all in Korean).
Anyway, life went on. I think it's been a week and a half and suddenly the entire bottom of my foot just started peeling. I seriously look like I have "Walking Dead" feet. I couldn't figure out what the heck I'd done. What did I step in? Battery acid? Did I somehow catch athletes foot or some other foot fungus!?!? Then I started thinking about that spiffy Korean foot mask I'd used and looked it up. Yep. Stuff works. After taking a pumice stone to my zombie feet in the shower, I now have super soft and bright feet! Seriously, they've never been this smooth. Even my heels are smooth and all my cracks are gone! I live in AZ and wear sandals all the time. This is a big deal!

title: Good Monitor
text:
The pads work as expected.

Kerr Medical shipped fully assembled. All I had to do was add three C batteries to the alarm and program the alarm to recognize the pads.

Programming was just pressing a pin into the back of the alarm until two LED lights lit up in the alarm, then sit on - and get off of the pads, then press the pin into the back one time to finish.

The plastic pads make a little stiff plastic "crinkle" noise if they are not under a mattress or couch cushion. This draws attention of my senior Mom and can lead to repetitive questions, or removal if I'm not watching.

The alarm is made for wall mounting or setting on something. My preference is slipping it into a front pants pocket. The alarm is larger and heavier than a wallet but it works ok for me and I wear loose fit jeans. If it goes off, I just reach into the pocket and reset the chime.

When Mom is on the couch I may be at the computer in front of her on the floor. When the couch (chair pad) alarm goes off, she is typically already on her feet and stepping away.

Left on her own she would go onto the porch in summer heat, so this is just adequate warning. With her fall risk I don't know if another product would alert me faster or physically impede her (which I really don't want to do).

The directions (mention) imply that this also works with "Cordless Floor Mat", "Cordless Nurse" call button and "Cordless motion sensor".

The "Low volume" is not disruptive, about as loud as a typical cell phone ring.

This may be like the [[ASIN:B0043RFKME Bed Alarm and Bed Pad (Cord Free)]] if it uses the 433-EC alarm, but this includes a chair pad (see their reviews for more feedback). One of those reviews mentions a power plug adapter - but I did not receive one for this product.

title: Good support for my Honda CR-V
text: After some lower back issues, I was in the market for seat and lumbar support cushions to help with longer car rides in my Gen 3 Honda CR-V. There are dozens on the market and I've tried most of them from cheap no-name brands to the expensive temperp**** and brooksto** brands. I found the cheaper ones were either too thin and non-supportive or way too firm and no give to them. I also found the more expensive ones comfy with good support, but a bit too thick and pushed me either too high up or too far forward in my seat. I turned to amazon and reviews from others which helped me settle on trying this Obus seat. Right away I found it fit almost perfectly in my CR-V's driver seat in both depth and width. After driving around for a few days, it provided the right amount of padding, and while I'm about an inch or so higher I'm nowhere near the head liner (I'm a bit under 6 feet tall). I did not experience feeling any wires or seams as others have mentioned. Finally I noticed that I no longer needed a separate lumbar cushion, the Obus seat raised me just enough to get more support from the standard seat. I also spoke with my physical therapist and she mentioned that Honda's bottom seat tends to be low and agreed just the seat cushion alone should do the trick. So if you are in the market to improve the comfort of your Honda's seat, give the Obus seat a try.

title: I'm actually quite disappointed with the product
text:
I'm actually quite disappointed with the product. I really hoped that it would work and IMO it does not do as promised. I think it's a great product that would work on straight hair or wavy hair but not on curly and thick hair. I don't know how it worked on ethnic hair because it didn't work on my curly hair. It's heavy and doesn't really straighten the roots or reduce the frizz, so I had to go back with my straightener and re-do my whole head.

Pro:
1. It's noiseless, so you can dry your hair noiselessly while your toddler sleeps right next to you.
2. Heats up quickly with a temperature setting option that will ensure you don't fry your hair and, it auto shuts off
3. Great for touch ups in between blow drys

Cons:
1. Did NOT reduce the overall time
2. Each section needs at least 4-5 passes to get the hair slightly smoother. Very time consuming and the end result is not worth it.. :(
3. Made my hair more frizzy and look like a lion's mane

Verdict: Not worth the effort. Will be returning it.. :(

I've only used this a few times so far, so I can't comment on how it compares to other brands I've purchased. It seems to be the same as other brands, and it's nice that it's in a glass jar instead of plastic like the previous brand I bought.

title: Beats the Competition.  Worked Great.
text:
Since removing the fin covers on a Goodman is a pain - I wanted to ensure I had a good brush for cleaning the fins, and so I bought two --- this one, and a blue one. This one, "Razita Slyire Air Conditioner Condenser Fins Cleaning Brush, Refrigerator Coil Whisk Brush" - worked great! The other one (the blue one) - worked terribly.

What was the difference? This one has thin soft bristles, that removes dust/dirt without damaging the fins. The other (blue) one - has thick/stiff bristles that damaged my fins and were too thick to remove the dust/dirt!

Buy this one. Very good purchase.

I used it to clean a Goodman outdoor AC unit, bought in 2017. It has very fine fins, very closely space. Perhaps other AC units have more spacing between the fins (where that stiffer blue brush might work better?). I'm not expert; but all I know is that this brown brush with fine bristles did the job excellent.

title: SO FRUSTRATED!!
text:
I am beyond frustrated with fitbit in general and this scale specifically. I received the Aria for Mother's Day and proceeded to spend two frustrating hours trying to get the scale connected to my network. I tried three different computers and my iphone. I rebooted everything twice and nothing worked. Finally, for no apparent reason it connected. I took a deep breath and thanked my lucky stars. By Tuesday evening - less than 48 hours later, the scale stopped syncing for no reason. It took me another hour to get it reconnected. I've taken the batteries out so many times that the contacts seem loose. It is only a matter of time before the thing breaks completely. The frustration doesn't seem worth the $100+ this scale cost. I can easily record my own weight and not take days off my life when by blood pressure skyrockets trying to get it to work. It is a great idea but the execution leaves something to be desired.

This is not even to mention the fact that my husband "gave" me the Fitbit Flex for my birthday in April thinking I would have it by mid-May. I can't find it anywhere, and now I'm wishing we hadn't invested in the Aria to go with it.

5. flood the surface with the product in a pressure sprayer that you're doing from the bottom up. Then scrub with brush or pad back and forth.
From the bottom up couple feet at a time until you get comfortable. Rinse and repeat until you get the results you want. Would be best to work with someone scubbing right behind the sprayer operator giving the product a few second head start. My toons were pretty bad and it cleaned it nice one time around. title: Excellent Scale but NOT ideal for a Medline Hoyer Lift
text:
I purchased this scale because I needed to track the weight of an invalid family member who cannot stand on a weighing scale. After reading many reviews of weighing scales on Amazon, I decided to purchase this scale because of its high customer ratings and mentions that some purchasers used it with a hoyer lift. Here's my experience...

The scale is EXCELLENT and accurate to within 1/2 pound validated by my various empirical tests using known weights.

However, the scale is NOT ideal for use with a Medline MDS88200D Hoyer Lift. Having studied engineering in college and having some mechanical aptitude, I connected the scale to the Hoyer Lift using the provided rubber spacers and an additional shim to stabilize the assembly. (see photos)

I then connected the 6-point cradle to the bottom of the scale using the provided U-bolt , which luckily happened to be the correct dimension to accept the hoyer's cradle pin. When attached this way, the scale added about 8-9 inches between the Hoyer boom arm and the top of the cradle.

Problem #1: In order to accept a patient in a sling, the boom arm needed to be raised almost to the top of its lifting range.

Problem #2: Another problem I encountered with the scale is that it did not swing freely when the boom arm was raised past a certain point. What happened is that the scale's orange case hit the side of the boom arm pivot and deflected to a non-perpendicular angle. The cradle remained perpendicular, however, the newly assumed angle put unnecessary stress on the scale's case and caused the scale to give inaccurate readings.

Bottom Line:

Would I buy this scale to use with a Medline MDS88200D Hoyer Lift - NO

Would I buy this scale to weigh something else that's heavy? - absolutely YES but only if the hanging points are unimpeded.

title: Great scale with slightly less than perfect accuracy
text:
I love the fact that it automatically syncs to my FitBit account. I also have a Fitbit Surge watch so it's nice to be able to log on to my account and see all my data easily without having to manually log anything. The scale has a very sleek appearance and feels sturdy. The display is easy to see and I like the fact that it turns on and off by itself without having to push a button. It also tells the difference between different users automatically so I don't have to push any buttons to get accurate calculations like I did on my old scale.

The reason for the 4 stars instead of 5 is that I think the accuracy of the weight and body fat measurements can be off at times. Sometimes it calculates the weight really fast and it seems off. I'll step off and on again right away and it will give my a 4-5 pound difference. This is not very reassuring. I don't think it's way off, but it still makes me question the accuracy. I know weight fluctuates quite a bit throughout the week, so it's not a big deal if it's off a little. Then there was a period of about 5 days that my weight was exactly the same all 5 days, to the decimal point. Perhaps that's just a crazy coincidence, but I find it a little hard to chew.

Pros:
Sleek design
Easy to read display
Auto on/off
Auto recognition of user
Auto sync with Fitbit through WiFi

Cons:
Questionable accuracy (though probably not way off)

Again, great scale and I'd give it 5 stars if I had more confidence in the accuracy of the readings. Hard to say anything about the body fat accuracy since I have no other way of measuring that. When compared to my old scale, it seems to be about 1-2% less, which I certainly won't complain about :)

text:
I ordered this while expecting my first baby. I really wanted to take a birth class, but finding a birth educator or advocates of personalizing your birth experience in Las Vegas can be a bit challenging.

I started with the Nutrtion audio cd while I was folding laundry one morning and was really impressed with how much new information I absorbed. It was like attending a nutrition bootcamp, but really easy to understand. I could identify why I was experiencing cravings and what to do about them. I can't even express how much some of Becky's tips helped me combat nausea and hunger.

The content was broken down nicely so it was easy to get through. I could listen to Common Concerns & Solutions while driving to work and keep Relaxation & Pain Management stored on my iPod so that I could induce deep state of relaxation in bed each night before I went to sleep. This was by far the most convenient and diversified product I found in its class.

The Prenatal Toning dvd wasn't something you watch every day--the author leads you through detailed instruction that explains the proper techniques and then recommends you plug them into various activities throughout your day. I found it very beneficial and I'm approaching labor and delivery with a lot more confidence. I feel like this set prepared me mentally and physically for childbirth

title: Could be better!
text:
I looked at a lot of scooters and decided on this one based on the features listed. I was a little disappointed. The scooter is not very compact and does not fold easily. The turn radius isn't that great, although it does provide more stability with the shortened radius. It's just not very convenient to get around on inside my house. You definitely have to be careful on even the slightest bumps as even a very small threshold can pitch the handlebars abruptly. If you aren't careful it could dump you over. It is definitely not an all terrain scooter. You need smooth even surfaces for a safe ride.
I would also highly recommend purchasing an additional cushion/pad for the leg rest as it is very hard. It caused me so much pain in my upper tibia the first two days that I almost returned it knowing crutches wouldn't not have been anymore painful. It is better with the additional padding. The one thing I know for sure is that I will be one happy camper when my Achilles tendon heals and I can ditch the aircast boot and scooter!

title: see results in 2 weeks!! this brush is so worth it!!!
text:
I love this product so much!!!

First of all, let me start off by saying the customer service is WONDERFUL! They get back with you promptly if you email them with any questions or concerns. Overall they are just super helpful and interested in giving you the best experience.

Now on to the product...

I have very sensitive combination skin. It's always either too oily, too dry, or oily and flaky at the same time, and always accompanied by blemishes. No matter how many hundreds of dollars I've spent on skin care in the last couple of years, over the counter or high end- nothing could help my condition. Recently, as I was looking on Amazon for a cleansing facial brush such as Clarisonic, feeling defeated and being overwhelmed with the price as well as numerous, negative reviews, I started looking elsewhere and accidently came upon Beaute La Royale and am so thankful I did... Here's why:

The small facial brush is perfect. It's bristles are soft to the touch but clean very well. I first tried it with my DermaDoctor face wash but seeing no results, I decided to try it with Aveeno active naturals clear complexion foaming cleanser because it's a bit more mild and gentle (and $40 cheaper) ;). In doing so, given about 2 weeks, I already saw GREAT results. I had barely any breakouts (if at all), and my skin over-all looked more smooth and vibrant. My pores notably shrunk and blackheads started to disappear! After 5 years of acne and hundreds of different products and countless hours of time trying out/applying, here I am $30 in and 2 weeks later, with my skin problems basically solved. I'm so happy! To prove the effectiveness of this brush even more, I went 2 weeks on vacation without using the brush (still using the Aveeno foaming cleanser but applying with just hands), and I haven't had this many blemishes at one time in a very long while after using my brush, and my pores have visibly expanded, leaving my skin looking tired and dull. With that being said, the positive results have definitely come from the brush!

I've seen reviews of people not quite happy with the one speed option, but with my experience I wouldn't want it any slower or faster. It deeply cleanses your pores thus removing bacteria and dirt, clearing up problem skin and blemishes, but doesn't leave your skin irritated and inflamed (and this is coming from a girl with EXTREMELY sensitive skin). So I would not worry about the speed. It's not designed as a power took. If anything it might be a tad too fast, so be sure not to use pressure when using the brush. Gently use circular motions on your face and let the brush do the work for you.

The other 3 features are also very helpful. I love the feeling of the sponge on my face- very gentle and soothing. I use it to put on my night face cream. The body brush is wonderful for removing cellulite, and I also have eczema so with further use I am excited to see if that helps me with the large "dots" and flaky/itchiness. I use the pumice for exfoliating my heels, etc. and it does a very good job. It is not so rough that it hurts, but gets the job done.

Again, the customer service is so good! You will not be disappointed with this product and the extensive results! You will fall in love - no matter your skin type!!!

Thank you Beaute La Royale!!!

title: Worked for a week... then severe side effects
text:
Alright, so I took full dosage and it took about a week and a half to notice that I wasn't retaining water from my food sensitivities anymore. This is an issue I've been having since 2013 so it's pretty significant!

However, shortly after I started to have side effects. Gastritis, chest pain, smell ammonia (not sweat, internally mostly through my left nostril), random dry cough, heartburn, stomach upset, gas and gurgling, what looks like eczema on my knees and legs.

Can't find anyone else who had this issue. I've stopped taking it two weeks ago and it's still a problem, so I don't plan on significantly lowering the dosage. There's just not a lot of info out there about this product.

Edit: So, most hose symptoms have gone now, except for the eczema and ammonia smell and heartburn. I stopped the Restore and now regret doing that and wish I just lowered the dose, after reading more about the product. I started taking it a couple days ago and am feeling better, improved sleep and energy but reworking on those food sensitivities again (it came back I'm assuming because I only took it for about 2 weeks and then stopped because of the aforementioned things going on). I'm back on it now, and I'll be sure to update this review as time goes on.

Edit 2: it's now the end of May (last edit was in Feb), and I can't say I recommend this anymore. I took and waited, but if you have gut dysbiosis, despite the creator's claims, this product could make it way way worse. The new symptoms are still around, and on top of that, it has affected my sleep negatively now: insomnia and hypnagogic hallucinations. Fun. Nothing handles these symptoms except for taking high dose probiotics (400bill to 1trill per day). I have to get dairy free gluten free corn free probiotics. Elixa, Custom Probiotics, and UP4 work for me (Elixa a little less bc of the potato starch).

The bottle has also changed. Ingredient name change and less instructions which I think is a huge mistake. For a lot of people, starting out at a TBSP per day is a giant mistake. Lots of users are taking DROPS.

Well, atleast I had a taste of what a properly working gut feels like.

text: I really liked this product but I couldn't be generous and give it five stars. I think you really get what you pay for and for the price, it's not bad at all. With an eye primer, the colors went on smoothly, evenly and blended well. I guess my main issue with it was that the instructions were a bit confusing and didn't really give me the look I was going for so I winged it,put my own twist on it and it turned out really well. The eyeliner it came with was alright. It went on smoothly and easily enough but it didn't quite blend the way it was supposed to since it says to put it on first. I was rather impressed with the mascara. Even though it's a bitty bottle and isn't exactly the most quality brand, it didn't clump hardly at all and it was thick with out having to do multiple layers. Also, the smallish brush makes it easier to get those bottom lashes done. All in all, I had no issues with not getting what I ordered, I got it when I was supposed to and enjoyed the product so much that I ordered another one for a friend and had it sent to her as a gift. My best piece of advice to give to someone who is purchasing or thinking of purchasing would be to not be afraid of experimenting with it. You don't have to do what the box says to get a sexy smokey eye look out of it. Find a technique you like and stick with it. It's very well worth the price though I wouldn't recommend it to some one who doesn't have much make up to begin with. You're probably going to want to use your own products with it.

title: Perfect replacements.
text:
These function perfectly as replacement nose pads. Both of the original nose pads broke on my current pair of glasses, and I had scavenged replacements from some older glasses. When those broke, I was forced to find some new ones and came across these. I suppose you could just go to an eyeglass shop to have them replaced for $5 to $10 each, but I had a hard time justifying that when this bag of replacements is so inexpensive.

If you don't have the snap-in style, you'll need a tiny screwdriver to remove the tiny screw from your glasses, but you probably have that from an old eyeglass repair kit. A word of advice, learned the hard way, is to remove the screw over a light colored towel or cloth. That way, if the screw falls, it won't bounce onto the floor. How a tiny piece of metal can bounce is beyond me but I know that it will.

Also, don't automatically assume that these will fit your glasses. Carefully compare yours to the picture. I have an older pair of glasses that these will not fit.

title: Does the job
text:
My old dial scale was not very easy to read, so I was looking for one that I thought would be better. I thought this one looked like it might be a little easier to read. It is a little better, but it is still hard to tell exactly which line it is on when fully standing and looking down. Size wise it is a small scale and while that is good because it fits where I need it to, it does make it a little hard to read. If you have big feet, this may not be the scale for you.

It seems accurate with my old scale. It does sometimes give a little different reading if you step on, off, and on again. However, I don't need it to be perfect, just confirm that I am loosing. I solved this problem by taking the advice of another reviewer. I get on and off three times. If I get the same reading twice, I take that one. If I get three different ones, I take the middle one. They are never more than 1 to 2 lbs different.

You do have to reset to zero most of the time, but from what I have learned about dial scales, that is actually considered a good thing. And really, how difficult is that to do? It takes 1 second.

All in all, I am pleased with this scale. If it had been expensive, I might expect more, but for no more than it cost, I think it is fine and does the job that I need it to do.

title: PhoneMax Amplified Telephone
text: I've used this phone for about a month now and I think it's going to be a great purchase.  I had an old GE amplified phone that was inadequate for my hearing.  I guess it amplified the volume by maybe x2.  Also, it had some features that I rarely used.  As my hearing got worse I decided to get a new phone.  I selected the PhoneMax because it had a standard ringer as an option - I learned by reading other reviews that the Clarity phones (the other option I was considering) only had an amplified ringer (i.e. loud).  The phone seemed to have the big feature I needed - more volume.  It does have a lot more volume.  One possible caution: I think the advertisements say it's got 40 dB amplification, open the users manual and it says 25 dB (as I recall).  I don't think the phone delivers 42 dB amplification, but it probably can deliver at least 10 dB and possibly 25 dB - it probably has more than enough for you unless you really, really, really have a hearing problem - I wear hearing aids when I have to, but most of the time I can get by without them, and the phone can supply very much more volume (x10) than I need if I turn the volume all the way up.  One other feature is that it amplifies the high frequencies more than the low, so voices sound different on the phone - but you'll likely still be able to recognize who you're talking to.  The ringer has 3 levels, off, lo, hi, and also 3 tones (I, II, & III).  The volume control is a simple analog rotary dial on the front of the phone - easy to access and easy to change.  The phone, and all comparable amplified phones, were kind of costly, in my opinion; on the other hand I think I'll get good use from it for at least 10 years - maybe longer.  I recommend it.  Not a lot of bells and whistles, just what you need.
