title: Mediocre cleaning/scraping combo
text: This combo pack consists of a razor scraper, along with some refill blades, and a spray bottle of cleaning solution. Neither is notably high-quality, and instead of the combination, I'd recommend buying superior products separately. The scraper is made entirely of plastic, and while it holds the blade securely, it feels fairly flimsy as a unit. The blade guard is hard to retract and extend, even right out of the box seeming to need some kind of lubrication; the blade doesn't retract itself, so an object or finger that's drawn right along the edge of the blade is still in danger of being cut. While it scrapes okay, it's not a well-made or well-designed tool, even compared to the low-end tools from big-box hardware stores. The cleaning spray, similarly, just doesn't seem to work that well. I tested it multiple times on a greasy glass cooktop, one of the applications it's sold for, and found it didn't even come close to removing the gunk as well as my usual Weiman glass cooktop cleaner. All in all, nothing in this package is special or works very well; it feels like a cheap collection of random second-rate items. It's okay, but there are better alternatives.

text: These are pretty average cotton masks. The material is soft, and the adjustable ear loops fit well though the straps are skinny enough that they might cause some discomfort for some wearers. The sizing is average, what I'd call a solid "medium" for US adults or larger kids. They're large enough for an average-sized person, but not anyone bigger than that. title: Excellent masks with a few disposable extras
text:
These are very well-made masks, though the cloth is quite impermeable. They come packaged with some disposable extras, a laundry bag and a storage bag, which are okay but not high-quality, and each mask is enclosed in a ziploc package printed with hilariously poorly-translated Engrish instructions about cleaning and use.

The fit is excellent, with a well-made curved form, adjustable ear loops, and an excellent, long, flexible nose wire that makes it easy to achieve a tight fit around the nose (though the fit in the chin is still a little tight so that a wide yawn can pull the mask out of position). The nose wire is the best I've used on any cloth mask so far, and actually gives me a better fit around the nose than many N95s — though the mask obviously doesn't seal nearly as well on the rest of the face, and your inhalation and exhalation goes around the sides of the fabric more than it actually goes through, the nose wire still prevents glasses fogging very well, directing exhaled air down and to the sides instead of up toward your eyes. The outer fabric is very dense and impermeable, so there is still some clamminess when wearing it for a long time, but I find these masks quite comfortable.

title: A Very Well Made Product, But to What End I'm Not Sure
text: This white noise machine works as one would want. The controls and accompanying instructions are intuitive and clear, the display screen showing time, temperature and humidity is crisp and easy to read, and the night light on the top of the device is easily adjustable with finger taps. This lighting is reminiscent of a candle's yellow glow and is rather soothing particularly at its lower settings. While there are indeed a broad range of sounds generated by this machine, many are not at all to my liking, some of them duplicating what seems to me like unpleasant bodily functions. Still, the variety of sounds to chose from make it likely that most people will find some that they will like. This also seems like a well-made device, sturdy with a good speaker -- not at all like the many cheap and flimsy small electronics manufactured in China that one comes across  so often these days. The retail price of under twenty dollars listed on Amazon at the time I ordered this white noise machine is more than reasonable. These characteristics make this machine a very good choice for those looking for a product of this type. I have to add, however, that I'm at a loss as to the utility of such an item. It comes across to me as one of those things that people spend money on for no particular reason other than to spend money on something. I certainly didn't find if especially relaxing nor perform any function like providing time, temperature, etc. that couldn't be done through my smart speaker or any number of other devices common in many homes these days. That said if others think such a sound generating machine can make a substantial difference to their sleep or relaxation he or she should definitely put this particular make and model at the top of their list.

title: High quality, you get what you pay for
text:
Ginseng is part of my testosterone maintenance plan, but it has numerous other benefits as well. I try not to run out of it, so that I can take it twice a day.

As with most herbal supplements, the quality and thus efficacy varies wildly. You may save a few bucks on a bottle, only to have the entire purchase be a waste of money due to poor quality and/or poor processing. It's hard to figure this out from a capsule label. You need to do some research on different brands. It starts with how the herb is grown. Is your ginseng grown in the traditional way, or is it grown using soil-destroying, nutrient-depriving chemical fertilizers? The Eco-Taste brand is grown organically and is free of GMOs, sugar, corn derivaties, and other toxins.

They also age their ginseng root, a step that is crucial to maximizing the potency. The dosage in each capsule is about right for ginseng (taking two capsules daily), though you may wish to take more capsules depending upon your circumstances. These are not large capsules, so they are easy to swallow.

I'm very satisfied with this product.

title: Great product, may cause gas and bloating in some individuals
text:
This protein powder is innovative, something you don't see in this product space very often.

I stopped using dairy-based protein powders many years ago. I normally use a vegan blend, because you need multiple plant sources to get a good amino profile. It so happens that oat figures fairly large in my diet. I use oat flour for baking and meal six of the day is usually based on raw oats.

So I thought I would try this oat protein powder, with the understanding I would need another plant derivation elsewhere in the day.

It has no junk in it. My primary concern was "the other white powder," that addictive, disease-causing drug commonly known as "sugar". It's organic and even has some vitamins and minerals added to it. Many people have never tasted organic, unprocessed oats so they associate the flavor of oats with "bland". This supplement not only gives you that organic oats flavor (albeit, processed into a powder), it also contains the sweetener erythritol, which is a sugar substitute. The FDA says erythritol is good for oral health.

One effect erythritol has in some people is it increases gas and bloating. That was the case for me. Such is my lot in life. So I will use it as a baking ingredient but I won't use it for shakes (thus reducing how much I consume at any given time).

We even use them for our older pets, both at night and when they have to travel in colder weather. Of course, they're also good for muscle pain and cramps too.
This one is TERRIFIC. Seals tight so no leakage. The cover is super soft and comes off so it can be washed and placed back on easily. (You probably don't want this without a cover or, at least wrapping it in a towel because it can get too hot and it's rubber). The cover is soft and cute and washed well.
Note: l've only used this for hot-never cold- so I don't know about putting it in the freezer. The mouth is too small to stuff ice cubes in it. I suppose it 'could' be used but IMHO there are better products for cold that stay cold longer.

title: An expensive toy that's good for the sole
text:
[[VIDEOID:1dc83ecd3872ce00d0a3b44c0afffc9]] DISCLOSURE: I received this product at a discount to test and review.

I spent way more for this than I typically do to review a product, but I had to have it. I love having my feet massaged. I've had Swedish massage, acupressure, deep tissue, reflexology, and I've even been Rolfed. I even had a friend once who would give me a foot massage in exchange for fresh pineapple. I made sure I always had one around when he visited. (This massager is better than he was.)

This is an odd machine. It resembles a bumper car and even has its own headlight. It provides the following functions from which to choose:

Self-Timer (10, 20, 30 minutes)
Shiatsu (On/Off)
Program mode (P1, P2)
Pressure (F1, F2, F3, F4, F5)
Heating (H1, H2)

There are really only two functions: 1) round knobs under your feet that move back and forth; 2) air bags similar to BP cuffs above your feet that inflate (and then deflate) and put pressure to the top of your feet which also serves to push your feet harder against the moving knobs. Most of the actions occurs to the front half of your feet with the heels getting little action. What's odd is that there appear to be six knobs around the heel (two rows of three knobs), but only the center knob of each row moves. It would have been much better if all six knobs moved.

The heating function doesn't work that well. I think that's where this massager really needs attention. And the program modes don't excite me much. They seem the same and aren't as good as turning on Shiatsu and air pressure.

The foot sockets have liners that can be unzipped and removed for cleaning. The bottom of the unit has two indents you can slide your fingers into to pick this up to move. The cord is somewhat thin and short.

Overall, the massage feels really good. I've been able to get the air pressure up to only F3, and that was after I used this for a few days. Too much air pressure pushing your feet against the knobs can be painful if you're not ready for it, but there is a button to release the air if you get uncomfortable. I've also found that I can slide my size 10 feet around a little inside for different effect. I also like to put them in at an angle so that knobs can massage the outer side of my foot. Yum. I wish the heater worked better, and I really wish there was a compartment built into this to hold the power cord/transformer so I didn't have to carry it around separate from the massager.

If you work on your feet, you're going to love coming home and slipping them into this unit. You don't have to beg anyone for relief. This is an expensive toy, but if you can afford it, go for it.

title: Not too bad

title: Improved her nails

title: More than just a protein
text: What I like about this particular brand of protein powder, is that it can operate as more than just a post workout recovery drink, and do double duty as a meal replacement as well. A couple of years back, I had some surgical procedures in my mouth as a result of some receding gum lines, that required gum grafts. That really is as unpleasant as it sounds. I mentioned that, because at the time it was difficult to eat solid foods for a while, so I was more or less on a liquid diet. I would very much like to have had this protein at that time, as a meal replacement because I feel it would have done a very good job of offering a good overall nutritional value. In this case, I have been using it as a post workout recovery drink. For that purpose, it works very well too. I do fairly high impact resistance training, so by the end of it I'm spent. My muscles certainly benefit from post workout recovery drinks that are protein rich, and will encourage muscle regeneration and synthesis. I found that this protein did nicely at helping me recover from my workouts. I have had the opportunity of trying the vanilla flavored one as well, and I think I actually prefer that one to the chocolate. My wife on the other hand, very much prefers the chocolate. So, I guess you can see that it's obviously going to be subjective. I personally found the chocolate to be a little sweet for my taste. So it's no surprise that my wife liked it, because she has quite the sweet tooth. I did find it to have just a touch of a grainy texture, but certainly nowhere near as bad as others that I have tried. I use a ninja blender that has a smoothie attachment, and that thing does a pretty incredible job of pulverizing the powder. I make my shakes very simply by just adding ice and water, with a couple scoops of this protein powder. As far as the ratios of how much water to powder I use, I usually experiment with that and don't pay much attention to the recommendations by the manufacturer. Personally, I prefer to dilute it a little bit in more water, as I find that makes for a more pleasant drink. All in all, I do like the fact that it has a good nutritional balance of fibers, vitamins, and minerals, as well as the protein content. Like I mentioned, when I had my surgery, it would have been nice to have had this as an option as well as the Ensure drinks that I was always having. I think it's a fine option, and I would recommend it.

title: Good healthy ingredients
text: I have to say that I was fairly impressed with the quality of this protein powder. I find the ingredients to be very impressive. I do like protein powders to be nicely flavored, but I'm always very skeptical of ones that are too tasty. If they taste more like Hershey shake for example, versus a chocolate protein shake, then you know they're heavily laden with sugar, and other additives that bring down the quality of the protein powder itself. This vanilla flavor one I found very nicely flavored. It wasn't too sweet at all. I'm not too sure that I like the recommendations on how much powder to add to how much water however. 10 to 12 ounces of water with two scoops of this protein powder, is in my opinion not enough water. I use a ninja blender, that has a smoothie attachment, and so I just measured water by eye, more or less, but I could tell you for sure I put probably closer to 16 to 20 ounces of water. I just like to water it down a bit, as I found for my personal taste, it was more pleasant that way and went down smoother. The taste is subtle and nice, especially when diluted, like I did. I use it as a post workout drink, to help my muscles recover from resistance training that I do five to six times a week. I found it very adequate as far as a post workout recovery drink, and on par with other whey proteins that I would routinely use. I mean, you have to take that with a bit of a grain of salt, because it's hard to anecdotally quantify the results in comparison, but I can say that I hardly notice the difference between this and your name brand whey proteins. I didn't try it for cooking or anything like that, but I know that these powders can be used in many different recipes for baking protein rich snacks. All in all, I found that it was a nice quality protein, that certainly fit the bill, and did the job for me and my needs. I found it very easy to take down, and light on my stomach. For all these reasons, I would certainly recommend it.

title: pretty decent

title: good quality
text: I am very impressed with the quality and performance of this ankle compression brace.  I found that the velcro hold up very well, and of course can be adjusted to apply the amount of compression that you will be comfortable with.  The brace offers a very decent amount of support, due to the fact that it is quite bulky, and in my opinion that is a good thing.  I'm sure some people may not see that as a positive, due to the fact that it will be more difficult to wear inside your shoes, and perhaps less comfortable that a thinner sock like material.  I however, would rather the brace do as it is intended, and that is apply compression, and restrict movement, which this one does very nicely. So for my needs, and for better and quicker healing, a restrictive brace like this one, is far more preferable.  I do recommend it, if you are dealing with an ankle injury that needs compression, and restriction of movement.

title: works great for sleep
text: Ever since I was a kid, and I am in my 40's now, I have been sleeping with ear plugs.  It started because of my father, who snored so loud that he could drown out a passing Harley Davidson.  Since then, I simply cannot sleep without them, as I like the area where I sleep to be quiet and dark.  I often reuse my earplugs night after night, as buying a fresh pair for every night can get expensive, and honestly most earplugs that I have used are good for a long while.  These are no exception, and I have gotten a few weeks out of them so far, and still going.  they do lose a little bit of effectiveness over time, but not that much at all.  They have a nice bounce back and do well to block out external noises. They are quite comfortable in the ear, and easy to sleep with.  If you are like me and need a quiet environment to catch some z's, then you'll need a pair of these for that good night sleep.

title: It works period
text: So I suffer from very dry and cracked feet, especially my heels which can get pretty rough.  I have found foot creams to be annoying to apply as they take forever to saturate, and leave my feet a little greasy for my liking.  I saw these sock like thingies and had to try them.  First I think that these work best of you use a foot scrubber first to remove some dead skin, and then proceed to wear them while you sleep.  Let me also say that I hate wearing socks to bed, but do not mind these in the least as they are open toed, and allow my feet to remain cool.  The interior is also a little cooling, as there is some kind of gel or cream like insert to do the moisturizing.  I wish I had taken a before picture, that is my bad, but believe me when I say that my feet were much much drier when I first started to wear them.  I have worn them for about a week every night, and I am always impressed with how smooth my feet feel in the morning.  It really does work, and is a much better idea and alternative to foot creams.  You simply slip them on, and go to sleep.  What could be easier than that.  If you scrub dead skin off of your heels before using them, they will work even better to maintain and improve the hydration of your heels.  I know that worked for me, and I am very pleased with the results.

title: Works well as intended
text: I have been a bit of a gym rat for most of my life, and have concentrated of muscular development.  Why do I mention this?  Well because, that also means I'm not as flexible as say a Yogi, or gymnast.  yes I struggle to wash my own back in the shower, because I simply can't reach all of it.  I wanted to try this silicone back scrubber for exactly that reason.  I have used others in the past, that are like that loofa or poof material (not exactly sure what you call it but I think you know what I mean), and they are fine, but eventually fall apart.  They also take longer to dry, so I was happy to find a silicone one.  It stretches well, and allows me to do as I intended to do with it, which is wash my whole back. The handles are a nice touch, and I always like the feel of silicone, as it gives a nice little back scratch too, if you add tension to it.  If you are like me, and not flexible, then this is right for you to get those problem areas that are out of reach.  Works well so far, I just hope it lasts long too.

text: I got the Medium version of this and it works pretty well from a resistance standpoint. It definitely provides some resistance and works well to exercise your hand or fingers. This putty works as well as the other resistance devices I have so I'm happy with it from that standpoint. It offers plenty of resistance so I don't know that I could handle the Firm version of this. It doesn't have a discernable odor but it is a bit oily feeling while you're using it. However, after I put it away I don't feel like I have to wipe anything off my hands so I guess whatever the oily feeling is absorbs well.

title: Feels Nice On The Neck
text:
This device gives you two forms of therapy for neck pain - heat and 630nm red light penetration. It warms up quite quickly and I can say that the heat feels very nice against my skin. With temps ranging from 101 to 113 degrees with an in-between 106 in the middle, you can find a heat setting that you like. You turn it on by short pressing the power button, which starts it in level 2 (106 degrees). Subsequent presses go to level 3 then back to 1 and so on. It turns off with a long press. The neck band consists of three sections that are hinged and the band fits comfortably on my neck (size 16) and there's still quite a bit of room left for larger necks. I like that the red light chips go all around the band, almost to the ends, so your neck is basically surrounded by the heat. I like that. On top of the band there is an indicator that glows with the heat level number so there's no guesswork as to the level you're at. It comes with decent instructions and a charging cord. Unfortunately, like most devices these days, no charging brick is supplied.

Overall, I like this neck heater pretty well. The heat relieves the pain I sometimes feel in long computer sessions and the lightweight band is easy to keep handy for those times.

title: Just So-So
text: I'll say this much for this shaver: it's very compact and thus works well for travel or keeping in the car for a quick touch-up. However, the motor is quite weak and on my face seemed to pull, leading to an uncomfortable feeling and some irritation. The pop-up trimmer works pretty well on my sideburns - no irritation there. Overall though, this shaver doesn't give an overall comfortable or very close shave for me on my whole face. Perhaps it's ok for a quick touch-up on small areas. It comes with a cleaning brush, a head cover, a travel bag, and a USB cord for charging. My overall rating - I don't think this underpowered shaver is worth the price charged.

title: Very Nice Lemon Oil
text:
I had never tried the US Organic brand before so I was anxious to try it. I love lemon oil and this is a very good one. Out of the bottle it has a wonderful strong pure lemon scent. I put a few drops in one of my diffusers and it filled the room with a nice lemon scent in short order. Since it's a very concentrated oil you don't need many drops in the diffuser.

This essential oil comes in a 1 ounce amber glass bottle (30ml), which is 3x larger than the typical 10ml bottles of essential oil. It has a Euro dropper top for easy dispensing. I particularly like that it is certified organic. It's on the pricy side compared to others but it's a very nice oil and you get quite a bit of it. I recommend this very nice lemon essential oil. Enjoy!

title: Works Well On Sore Neck
text: My neck often gets sore when I have long computer work sessions. But since I've been using this after these sessions I've gotten some good pain relief with it. I've found the middle height works best for me. I plan to keep using this regularly.

title: Truly Portable Red Light Therapy Lamp
text:
This portable red light therapy lamp is very thoughtfully designed. First of all, it's battery operated so it can truly be operated anywhere with no cord hassle. It uses one rechargeable 18650 battery and 2 are included, along with a charger for them, so you never run out of power. There are 3 LEDs - 630, 660, and 850 nanometers. The 630 and 660 ones are red lights for closer to the surface skin treatment and the 850 one is for deeper muscle treatment. The 850 near infrared one is invisible to our eyes. There is a 5 minute auto-shutoff. The base is magnetic and a wider metal base is included so the lamp is stable no matter how you adjust the gooseneck. Eye protection is included as well.

I use red lights to relieve the pain of occasional tendonitis in my thumb and this one is easy to use. It is very well thought out, works well, and I recommend it if you're in the market for a red light therapy device.

title: Decent Non-adjustable Red Light Therapy Lamp
text:
There are lot of red light therapy lamps on the market these days and this one is a good example of the genre. It is pretty low power and intended to be used either right on the target area or no more than a couple of inches away. The light consists of 3 wavelengths - 630nanometers, 660nm, and 850nm. The therapeutic value of each is superficial, medium depth, and muscle depth respectively. The 630 and 660 ones are visible as red light and 850 one near infrared) is invisible to our eyes. I use red light lamps to help with neck and lower back pain after a long computer session. This lamp has a pretty small targeting ability obviously so it should be used to target specific areas that are not very wide. There are no intensity or timing controls on this lamp. It does shut off automatically after 5 minutes.

The form factor of this lamp is a standalone gooseneck lamp. It is not particularly stable in all configurations and it is easy to adjust the gooseneck so it tips over. It has a simple on/off switch as its only control. All 3 LEDs come on at the same time. A big positive for this lamp is that it is rechargeable, which greatly increases its flexibility. Untethered to an outlet, it can be used anywhere. Eye protection and a charging cord are included.

This lamp does work but I find its low power, lack of adjustability, and instability of the physical platform combined with its pretty high price make it not very competitive with others on the market which are more intense and adjustable. A saving grace for you might be its rechargeability, which might raise it over others for you.

title: Cooling Topical Cream
text: This pain relief cream goes on very smoothly and a little goes a long way, so use sparingly. When I applied it to my aching wrist tendonitis flareup, I felt an immediate cooling sensation but not much else. After I few minutes, though, I noticed that the pain in my wrist had lessened some and the tendon seemed to ease up a bit. It's not magic but it seems to help some. The camphor and menthol smell appropriately medicinal, and the odor is helped along by peppermint, eucalyptus, and some other things. With the 2 for 1 deal and $5 off coupon that is currently available, it seems like a good value if you like camphor/menthol products.

title: Nice Specialty Bandages
text:
Often in sets of bandages you don't get the butterfly (knuckle) or fingertip ones, or only a couple of each. This set can make up for that shortfall by giving plenty of each. The packaging of these is really nice. In the box, you get two smaller boxes. Each one has 26 knuckle and 24 fingertip bandages.

Each fabric bandage does the job it's intended for. I like that they have adhesive on all 4 sides of the nonstick pads. The fingertip bandage fits nicely and securely on its intended location. The knuckle bandage has long legs to fit around the finger and hold the bandage on the knuckle. The photo shows the fit of both. Since these are fabric bandages, they're not waterproof.

This is a good set of bandages to add to your first aid kit around the house or car. You may not need this shape often, but when you do, you do!

title: Compact Panel Format Red Light Therapy Lamp
text:
There are quite a few red light therapy lamps on the market these days. Most are packaged in a lamp format with a screw-in red light bulb. This one is in a compact panel format that can be powered directly from a USB port. The panel has 18 LEDs: 3 630, 6 660 and 9 850nm wavelengths. When turned on, only half of the LEDs appear well-lit. That is because the 850nm light is nearly invisible. The compact size makes it ideal for travel.

The light from this lamp feels really great on my sore neck and lower back after hours sitting up working on my computer. It doesn't feel warm at first but when you train it on a body part, you feel the heat penetration pretty quickly. An adjustable stand is included that allows varying the angle. The angle is fairly adjustable over a range of almost vertical to about 45 degrees. Of course you can use it off the stand as well. The panel has an on/off switch on its body and the cord has a timer control switch. The control is on the cord is a bit odd. When you first turn it on it is on the 5 minute setting and it flashes 12 times before turning the lamp on. Pushing it a second and third time sets the timer to 15 or 30 minutes. The cord is fairly long for flexibility of placement. There are no different intensities, so this panel is pretty simple. A carrying case and power plug are included.

There are no instructions included aside from a few printed directions on the cardboard box it comes in. I think a product such as this should come with instructions that explain its use and any safety warnings/issues that may arise. Aside from that I find this a nice device. It seems built well, it works well, and the LEDs should last a long time.

title: Not Worth The Price
text: These insoles provide decent heel shock absorption due to the gel pad and deep heel cup. That's the best part of these. I have medium width feet and I didn't feel hardly any arch support at all. The raised arch was just alongside my foot and the insoles didn't hold my foot in place well. The cushioning on the forefoot is minimal. Honestly, I just can't justify the price of these given my experience with them.  I just didn't feel comfortable either running or walking with them, and that's the bottom line with insoles.

title: Very Nice Blend
text: This essential oil blend has a decidedly citrus note. Although the product description says one of the ingredients is lime, it isn't. The citrus scent comes from the sweet orange in it, which happens to be one of my favorites. It works great in my diffuser and fills the room with a wonderful orange scent that is buffered a bit by the cedarwood in it. Note that the bottle contains 5ml, half of what a usual essential oil bottle contains. Although a bit on the pricy side, this is a very nice blend indeed. I like it a lot. Enjoy!

title: OK Sound Machine - with some flaws
text:
Unlike a lot of sound machines, this one is rechargeable and can operate without a cord. That's a good thing because the charging port is located underneath the unit and the unit cannot stand up when the supplied USB-C charging cord is attached. The vendor really should have supplied a right-angle cable to fix this. At any rate, the sounds supplied with this unit are pretty good. There are 6 of them - forest, thunder, white noise, waves, wind, and campfire. Unfortunately, they're fairly repetitive on a pretty short cycle and you hear the pause as the cycle repeats. This is somewhat annoying. Other sound machines either blend the cycles or randomize them. There is a timer function that can be set in 20 minute increments up to 2 hours or you can run the unit continuously. There is a volume control but I couldn't tell how many volume levels it has. It goes from very soft to quite loud. The lights on the front can either be turned off or set to illuminate either 1,3,or 6 of them. When on, the lights "breathe" - go on or off. I don't want moving lights when I'm trying to sleep so I recommend turning them off.

So I rate this sound machine as just ok. The sounds are nice but the cycles are too short. The best features are the rechargeability and the very compact size, which makes it great for travel.

title: Really Strong Stuff...
text: ... but it works! It has a really strong smell that lingers. It smells of tea tree, eucalyptus, and peppermint predominantly. I happen to like those smells so this stuff works for me. It's far better than foot odor in my opinion and I like the fact that it lasts awhile. I use it on my feet after exercise and it works right away. After spraying it in my shoes and letting it dry, it completely replaced the bad odor with those of the oils. This stuff has earned a permanent place in my closet and I will spray my shoes regularly. I like it and recommend it.

title: Does The Job!
text: This trimmer does a good job on nose and ear hair. It works fast and I didn't feel any tugging or discomfort as I used it, although it did tickle a little as I used it in my nose. The heads come off with a twist and are easy to install. The hair trimmer has an adjustable guard so it can be used on multiple areas if you're so inclined.  Included are a USB charging cord and a cleaning brush. This is a good instrument at a good price. It works well and I recommend it.

title: Very Nice Heated Pad
text: This heating pad is a bit different than typical ones in a couple of ways. First, it's weighted a little bit, but not too much. That helps the heating elements stay a little closer to the area you're applying heat to and makes it more effective. Second, the cord, at over 7 feet, is longer than most and gives some extra flexibility. The pad is very generously sized at 1x2 feet so it can soothe relatively large areas. The outer cover is a very soft, plush material that feels great against the skin. It's simple to operate  - press the Power button to turn it on and then click the Heat button to cycle through the 6 heat settings. The instructions say it turns off automatically after 2 hours. I wish the instructions said what temperatures each of the heat settings is, but it goes from quite low to more heat than I can stand. I like the 4th setting best. The pad heats up quickly and feels very soothing. I like it a lot and I recommend it.

title: Terrific Massage Gun
text:
This is a very impressive massage gun. It comes in a very nice case that provides protection and storage for the massage gun itself, its 4 heads, and the power adapter. The instruction manual provided deserves particular kudos. It, of course, gives instructions on how to operate the gun, insert the different heads, and charge the unit. However, there is also a usage section that shows the uses of the various heads; has color illustrations of the different muscles that can be targeted in the arm, shoulder, waist, leg, and foot; and suggestions for massage durations for the different muscles pictured. In many devices that I look at the instruction manual is kind of an afterthought, but this one is very well done.

The design of the unit is excellent. The rubberized surface feels good in the hand and provides for a good grip while it is operating. It is very solidly built as are the individual heads. The slanted handle is easier on the wrist while operating it, giving a more natural position for the wrist without stressing it as much as with other massage guns that have straight handles. There is just one control button - long press to turn it on and off, short presses to select one of the 5 speeds. There are indicator lights showing the battery charge state and speed selected. It always starts with the slowest speeds. I find the 5 speeds plenty adequate for my needs. There are 4 heads provided with the unit, each with different target uses. They're easy to swap in and out and stay securely in while the unit is operating. My favorite heads are the ball and flat ones. Mine came fully charged and battery life is stated in the manual as 4 hours, but I imagine it varies depending on the speed used.

The bottom line for a device like this, of course, is how does it feel while using it. I can report it feels very good and provides great massaging action, ranging from light to deep stimulation. I've been using it on my neck after long computer sessions and my wife does the same. We both like this massage gun a lot. An additional quality is how quiet the motor is. It is so quiet you don't disturb others while using it in close proximity.

This is a very well-built, high quality, quiet massage gun and I highly recommend it.

text:
I really wanted to love these earplugs. I have chronic migraine with sound sensitivity, so I wear earplugs almost every day. I have been wearing the soft foam plugs, but when I saw these, I was eager to give them a try. They looked perfect!
However, I was disappointed at their sound blocking abilities. The foam plugs do a much better job of blocking noise. Even with these earplugs in, I still had to plug my ears with my fingers to block out loud sounds.

Though they don’t do a good job of blocking sound, they are fairly comfortable and they stay in my ears much better than the foam plugs. They’re also waterproof and come in a handy carrying case (though they get stuck in the case, making it hard to open or close).

However, my main reason for wearing earplugs all the time is to block sound, and these fail at that, so I can’t give them more than three stars. It seems like I just cannot get a good seal with them inside my ear canal. If I could, perhaps they’d do a better job of blocking sound.
Also, they’re very OBVIOUS. They’re not very low profile and the bright colors make them quite noticeable. I’m sure that if you dropped one, the bright color would aid in finding it, but I was hoping for an earplugs that was a bit more discrete and low profile.

title: Soothing, effective pain relief. NO use or care instructions.
text:
I've knocked a star, only because instructions are lacking for this headache relief cap. I mean, true -- what do you need to know? You put it on like a hat... you can tell which side is the front and back (a little cutout area for the nose and the gel is located in the front of the hat). So, what's to know, right??

Well... how long do I cool this mask? Can I warm it up for heat relief? How do I keep the mask clean? Is it washable?

Hm. The box doesn't say, and no written use or care instructions are included in the box.

I got this particular headache cap because I saw that the online description included HEAT relief, not just COLD. It says so in the product description, but is not disclosed anywhere on or with the actual cap when you receive it.

***TWO hours in the fridge for cold therapy

***TEN to 30 seconds in the 'heater' for hot therapy (a toaster oven is pictured...and I would highly recommend NOT heating the mask this way. I surely hope they meant a microwave! This would be the safest [and correct, imo] to heat this mask, or you will end up with a ruined cap and a true headache! ;-)

Currently, I've only used this cap for COLD therapy and I have NOT had to place it in the fridge. The gel is cool to begin with and has been plenty cold enough at 'room temperature.'

The light compression and cool gel is very soothing. It has relieved headache pain as well as helped sleep come quicker.

I really like this headache cap and will be using it often. I just wish the instructions were a little clearer and included!

title: Velcro catches on linens
text:
This is a contoured sleep mask with an adjustable strap. The mask appears to be constructed of two layers of polyester sealed at the seams with padding added around the edges of the eyes. An elastic strap is sewn on each side by the temples. This strap is in 2 separate pieces that are joined by a 3.5” long strip of Velcro in the middle that meets behind your head. Included in the package is a single pair of foam earplugs in a non-resealable plastic bag. The product was made in China.

I’m on the fence about this sleep mask. It fits my face well and successfully blocks out all light when I am sitting up. But when I try to sleep with it on, the mask sometimes turns on my head so no light is blocked. And then when I adjust the Velcro strap to fit my face, the pieces of Velcro strips don’t line up perfectly—it’s shorter on one end and longer on the other, and the exposed Velcro catches on my pajamas, hair, and pillow case. The included earplugs are just a gesture—these are single use earplugs with no carrying case. All in all, this is a very basic sleep set that will do in a pinch or for a short hospital stay, but it is not a workhorse sleep mask set that I would want to wear every day for months on end.

title: Tasty little chocolates
text:
This is a bag of chocolate sweets, each containing a bit of BC30 probiotics. BC30 is short for GanedenBC30® (Bacillus coagulans GBI-30, 6086), a patented strain of Bacillus bacteria. The bacteria forms endospores, giving the spores a tough outer shell that can survive extreme conditions. This is the basis for the claim that the probiotics in this product survive stomach acids better than many other forms of probiotics. Other ingredients in the product are: dark chocolate (chocolate liquor, sugar, cocoa butter, soy lecithin, vanilla), maltodextrin, soybean oil, confectioner's glaze (shellac, coconut and canola oil), acacia gum, and corn syrup; thus, this product should not be consumed by people with soy allergies or gum sensitivities. According to the package, one nugget constitutes one serving, and contains 30 calories, with 1.5 g fat, 2 g sugar, and 0.36 mg iron. The package is a foil bag that includes a plastic zip for reclosure (the plastic zip on my bag malfunctioned from the start).

I was quite impressed with the taste of these little chocolate nuggets. If you let them melt in your mouth, they compare to middle-of-the-road chocolate truffles, such as Lindt. There is certainly no indication from the flavor that this is supposed to be a nutraceutical. I tried taking one a day for a month. I didn't notice any differences in my digestive tract or immune system during the month. But then, I also eat a bowl of natto (fermented soy) every day, which contains additional probiotics. What I did notice when I first started taking these chocolate nuggets was chocolate-indigestion after each dose. I'm sensitive to dark chocolate, which tends to give me gastroparesis if the chocolate is strong enough. So yes, there is plenty of actual chocolate in these nuggets. Fortunately, after about a week, my belly adjusted to the daily dose of dark chocolate, and I was able to eat the rest of the nuggets without problems. In any case, if chocolate tends to give you indigestion, gastric reflux, or gastroparesis, this is not the right probiotic product for you. Also, if you have control issues--if you open a bag of chocolates or cookies and can't stop eating until the bag is empty, this product is not for you. What's going to happen if you eat the whole bag? Nothing-- GanedenBC30® has been thoroughly tested for safety, but at $0.52 and 30 calories per nugget, you're going to wish you hadn't brought them into the house. Better to stick to another probiotic formulation that is easier to take just one of.

Overall, this is an easy way to incorporate probiotics into your daily routine. Just be aware that these nuggets contain real dark chocolate, and may be habit forming.

title: Excellent Pair of Cleaners for Laundry & Dishes, Very Fine with No Lumps
text:
I have made my own laundry soap for years and two of the chief ingredients are Borax and Washing Soda (Soda Ash).

This is two 5 lb bags--one of Borax and one of Washing Soda. Each is finely ground and no lumps which makes them easy to dissolve when making my laundry soap.

I have a liquid version and a powdered version. I am currently using my liquid version.

For the liquid version I use
3/4 cup super washing soda
3/4 cup borax
Shake well to dissolve in a 1 gallon jug about 1/4 full of warm water then add water to fill the jug leaving room for the
3/4 cup Original Blue Dawn
This makes 1 gallon of laundry soap which uses 1-2 TBL for front loader or 1/4 c for top loader for fresh, clean clothes.

The powdered version uses
1 bar (5 oz.) Fels-Naptha laundry bar, grated or run through the food processor
2 cups (14 oz.) borax
1 3/4 cups (14 oz.) washing soda
Instructions
Grate the entire bar Fels Naptha (or other laundry bar soap using the fine side of a cheese grater or food processor.
Pour grated soap, borax, and washing soda into a large mixing bowl.
Stir to mix well then transfer mixture to quart-size or larger container. (I like to run it all through a food processor to make it all very finely chopped)
To Use: Add 1 tablespoon powdered laundry detergent to the wash load. You may need to adjust depending on your conditions and washer size. You will not need much to produce excellent results.

I go back and forth on which I use depending on whether I can get some fels or not.

As you can see, these bags of Borax and Washing Soda will last me a very long time for my laundry needs which makes these a good value. And they come right to my door!

I tried it on my lips and then on my real problem spots ... my elbows.

I have really dry cracked elbows with pieces of dry cracked skin sticking up. That's from me using my elbows to prop myself up in bed and read at night. My elbows really hurt when my bedsheets or any other cloth rubs against them. They are in bad shape or they were until I started applying this product.

This petroleum jelly has a thinner consistency then the name brand but I really think it works better then the name brand. I tried the name brand product on my elbows but it didn't help like I expected it too. I think this products thinner consistency helps it to be absorbed into the skin better.

After applying this product to my elbows for 3 nights, the rough hard pieces of skin on my elbows soften up and layed down.

Plus this petroleum jelly is less greasy then the name brand. It doesn't leave greasy stained spots on my bedding or clothes.

The only issue is the jars blue lid comes off way to easily. I wish it fit better.

I would definitely recommend this product.
