title: Helpful Product!
text: A few years ago I had cataract surgery that has actually made my night driving worse than better. I've not been able to drive at night and if it rains or snows, I ac't see a thing. So when I saw the ad for these night vision glasses I felt they would be worth trying and knew I could probably find these on Amazon. The product quality is quite good and comes in a sturdy case. I gave the glasses a try one night and felt they were helpful. I'm not certain if they would help me in rain or snow but for driving at night they did seem to settle down all the light trails and stars. I haven't tried these yet in city driving where there are more lights and so I am uncertain whether these will help. I have a feeling that with all the added car lights, traffic lights, lights from stores and restaurants that these probably would not help. My gut tells me this because on country roads I still had stars and trailing lights from on-coming cars, but the glasses did turn down the intensity. I would recommend these for others with similar issues.

title: Safety vigilance is all you need for this great product.
text:
I am a diabetic and my feet are in terrible shape. Dry, cracked and calloused. Before I begin, I would be remiss if I failed to mention that electric devices such as this are typically NOT recommended for diabetics. This is because if you are not super vigilant with caution, you can very easily cause yourself an abrasion. Cuts, abrasions or any type of injuries to a diabetic (especially in the feet or legs) are nightmares to heal and quite serious. So, if you are a diabetic and plan to use this product, you should be absolutely certain that you (or whoever is going to be using it on you) will not be in a hurry, take your time and don't rush. Basically, touch it to a spot once or twice and then FEEL with your finger or hand to make sure that you're not going too deep or causing any type of injury. Do this every time and every spot. If you're like me, you'll eventually want to go a little faster and cover more ground. However, I didn't because I know from past experiences what this can cause.

With all that being said, I have used my Emjoi Micro-Pedi Callus Remover twice so far and I love it. I've used battery operated devices in the past and they just wasn't powerful enough. My rough, hard skin would stop the rotating action of the device. That is the safer way, of course but I could never really get anything accomplished. That is why I decided to go to an electric callus remover. Rough, hard skin is NOT going to stop the rotating action of this callus remover. That means it will eat right through the hard, callused skin and start into the fresh, alive skin and that will HURT. And, if you are a diabetic, it will cause you an abrasion that could take forever to heal. So, be vigilant!

Provided my Emjoi continues to work well and last a decent amount of time (which time will tell), I am glad I bought this product and would definitely purchase it again.

title: Works if you have this specific intolerance
text:
This will only work if you have troubles digesting certain foods --- bacon, pork, lunch meats, aged cheeses, and some select fruits and veggies like eggplant. Also, you have to take it within 15 minutes of eating your food.

My husband complained he had food intolerances, but he was not sure which foods were the problem. After leaving a party early because he was not feeling well, I was determined to figure out what is hurting him. He said bacon and cheddar cheese gave him problems, but not chicken nor mozzarella cheese. I thought this was very odd, so I did some research. Eventually, I learned about histamine intolerance and decided this was worth a shot buying to see if it helps. It does help! He has to take two with bacon or pork, but with milder histamine foods, one is good.

It's still better to just avoid histamine rich foods, but this is good for times when it is hard to avoid those foods.

title: By far the best “functional” gait belt I have used for my disabled ...
text:
By far the best “functional” gait belt I have used for my disabled elderly mother. It’s broad width, easily accessible slots for your hands and the relative ease of wrapping and adjusting the belt around the trunk of an individual makes this product unique and much more functional than several other transfer belts I have used for my mother. However, the design and construction of the belt is terrible, which causes it to easily rip at the outer edge of the slots were you place your hands and could lead to the sudden and catastrophic failure of this device and result in the falling of a disabled individual.

I actually have bought two of these belts on two different occasions. The first belt lasted about three months before the first major rip, which made further use of the belt too risky because of my fear the belt would completely tear and result in my mother falling suddenly. Note my mother weighs only 128 pounds. However, because I really liked the “functionality” of the belt, I ordered a second one and hoped the failure of the first belt was due to a fluke production issue. However, the second belt miserably failed again in the same way and within the second week of its use. On closer inspection, I found the belt to be oddly constructed from multiple sections not initially appreciated and stitched together with only a single line of thread, which is not apparent until two pieces rip apart. Furthermore, the fabric itself tears much more easily than expected. Both of these design and construction issues can cause sudden and unexpected failure of this belt and lead to the sudden fall of a disabled individual, especially if they are much heavier than my mother.

I suggest the manufacturer of this belt to re-design it with much stronger fabric and reinforced stitching and to switch to a single unit construction, which would negate the need to stitch smaller units together.

I would judge this current product to be potentially dangerous because of its tendency to suddenly and unexpectantly fail without warning, thereby placing disabled patients at a risk for falling in spite of the assistance of a care giver.

title: There's a bit of a learning curve with this product ...
text:
There's a bit of a learning curve with this product. I've had a few lash lifts in the past and this product does basically the same job minus the tint step. I watched a couple of videos and then hastily/impatiently started my lash lift. Tips:

1) Don't apply the perm solution all the way up your lashes. This will cause your lashes to curl in on themselves and look ridiculous. It also takes quite a while to grow out (I'm currently living this one out).

2) Glue your lashes straight up onto the curler. If you fan them in any way, they will bend awkwardly toward the edges of our face (also living this out).

3) Make sure you glue the rod on really well (I used the silicone one). If the rod lifts at all during the process the shape of your lift will me affected. Also if the solution seeps behind the rod onto your lid it kind of burns. I had minimal redness, puffiness, and sensitivity for about a day due to this.

4) You don't need that much product when it comes to steps one and two. You also do not need to process for longer than about five-seven minutes. The solution is quite potent. I've had lash lifts before and my optimum processing time is around seven minutes. I suggest starting out on the lower and and building up.

title: A good UV lamp you can trust!
text: In light of the coronavirus outbreak, we purchased this bulb to disinfect things. After three weeks of moderate use, our first bulb broke. Considering the disruptions to the supply chain, the vendor did a very good job in supplying us a replacement. We have been using this bulb for about 6 weeks and it seems to be working well. We use it to clean PPE masks and food products that can’t be cooked or disinfected in other manners. However, this light is highly aggravating if exposed to living objects (which is why it’s good at killing virus and bacteria). Precautions must be taken, which for us was putting the bulb in a closet and using an extension cord with on off button so we could make sure the light was off before we enter. For us, this light has provided peace of mind that our used PPE and food products are likely safe for use.

title: KUDOS for Dry Eye Relief
text: My 91 year old father has dry eyes.  He is a voracious reader and this condition has significantly curtailed his enjoyment of life.  We've been to five ophthalmologists and tried about every OTC dry eye product on the market.  No real answers or solutions.  We found that the best remedy was for him to put simple saline solution into his eyes.  The relief is significant but short-lived.  Unfortunately, at his age, applying the saline solution is cumbersome enough that he does not do it as frequently as he needs to provide continuous relief.  Eye droppers and eye cups were simply too difficult for him to self-administer saline solution from the bottles they came in.  I decided that there must be an easier way.  I purchased this product along with some 10ml glass portable mini refillable atomizer spray bottles.  Both products have made it much easier for my father to frequently apply the saline solution to his eyes.  The Nano Mister provides a much finer mist (almost like a fog) and does not provoke hardly any reflexive eyelid shutting.  And it works!  I will ensure that the liquid compartment remains clean and disinfected for the Nano Mister and the atomizer spray bottles.  But it looks like we found a way for my father to gain significant relief in a way that makes him compliant in its administration.

title: Purchased and already sent back
text:
I've had the [[ASIN:B002JE2PSA Withings WiFi Body Scale, Black]] for several years and wanted to try the Aria scale because I'd used the Fitbit tracker for some time.

THE SETUP
I was able to setup the scale for myself fairly easily, but there's another in my house and inviting his email always failed. We just got an error message that said he couldn't be added. I contacted support and they literally didn't have clue. I've developed enough Web sites in my time to know that it's fairly easy to set up error and exception logging, so I'm not sure why they were so slow to help. Finally, after a week of weighing myself, support suggested I delete my account (the primary) and try to add my friend as the primary and then reinvite myself since it seemed my address had already gone through once. I immediately questioned if they were sure about this advice, because I'd lose my data and a weeks worth of measurements. I heard back 24 hours later from someone else saying that was the wrong advice, and I never should been told to do that. Thankfully, I was smart enough to know and hadn't. Another week went by and the invite just started working magically.

USE
Compared to the Withings scale, the measurement and display seems clunky. I can never quite tell what it's doing and if you're not careful about moving around, you'll get duplicate measures. It does vary a lot. You can step on it a minute later get entirely different readings. To be fair, the same is true of the Withings scale, and I think digital scales in general. The Aria though, weighed me consistently 2 pounds heavier than the Withing scale. My body fat percentage was always about 2 - 3 points less though.

DATA
The Withings Website beats Fitbit's far and away when it comes to tracking and visualizing weight and body fat data. Afterall, weight and BMI are pretty much meaningless numbers if lean mass aren't taken into account. But I could never figure out how to get the Fitbit website to actually tell me how many pounds of body fat it registered, as opposed to just the percentage. Withings does that quite nicely and it also has a beautiful mobile app that I like even more than the Web site. I could've sworn hovering over the measures showed actual pounds of body fat, not just percents, but that seemed to stop a few days in. Withings will also show you lean mass, which the Aria doesn't seem to do.

I might've kept the scale had it not been for the technical problems inviting other users, the clunky display and the poor use of data on their web site.

title: A Miracle - I wish I knew about this years ago!
text: My son was 9 years old and I had been trying for years to stop the bed wetting at night.  I had tried everything but nothing worked.  I limited his beverages after dinner, I woke him up at midnight, I made him change the sheets, and I did not allow any sleepovers.  He was not fighting me; he wanted to stop wetting the bed but once he went to sleep he never woke up until morning.  As a last straw, I purchased this alarm.  I was skeptical and felt I was wasting my money but to my surprise, my son stopped within a month or so.  The alarm would go off every night at about four in the morning and he would jump up and go to the bathroom.  After one month, I felt he had finally won the battle but I still made him wear the alarm as a backup.  He started to wake up on his own and I have not had a problem since.  He is 10 years old now and the alarm is history.  It was a long and difficult battle for us but it is in the past now and I give full credit to this system.  Good luck to everyone who reads this and know there is a light at the end of the tunnel for you too!

title: Excellent Tutorial
text:
I purchased this bundle to quickly come up to speed on Rhino 5. While Rhino has a very simple and useful help system, the documentation appears to be slim-to-none. Considering this, these videos are well worth the price. I have had some minimal experience with Autocad and 3D-Studio Max, so the concepts presented about surface normals, commandline usage, export formats, etc were not entirely foreign to me. The manner of instruction and the information presented would be beneficial to a total beginner as well.

The instructor focuses on critical features of Rhino early. The topics presented allowed me to be productive quickly. Within a couple of days I was able to create accurate 2d and 3d parts, export them in dxf and stl formats, run them through my cam software, and cnc them on my mini-mill. If I had a 3d printer, I would have had these parts even quicker.

The instructor focuses a lot on product design. He doesn't spend as much time focusing on using Rhino's capabilities to achieve absolute cad accuracy as he does drawing freeform curves. But he does demonstrate enough of the methods of how to achieve accurate angles, lengths, tangency, using the commandline, etc that you can go from there to achieve whatever level of accuracy you require.

I highly recommend these tutorials if you would like to quickly learn Rhino 5 to design your own parts for CNC for 3D printing, product design, or computer modeling projects.

title: Good brand but poor QC control
text:
The package came with 2 attachments missing. When I switched it on, I noticed a loud humming sound. Being a curious person I decided to open it up to explore. This is my findings:
1. The casing is pretty thin and I am sure will not be able to withstand any impact like dropping.
2. The shaft for attaching the attachment heads was not aligned centrally which means it is slanted to one side very near to the casing. As a result when the power is on the vibration will cause the shaft to hit the casing causing loud vibration sound as some reviewers complained. I suggest 4 screws should be used instead of the existing 2 screws to secure the transformer. It will provide better alignment and support. Currently my solution is to use some hard leather piece to brace the transformer that is attached to the shaft to centralise it before using epoxy glue to strengthen the flimsy plastic screw holes before tightening the screws.
3. The flat pin standard US plug was badly made as one side of the pin is bigger than the other thus making it difficult to plug into the socket.

In conclusion I would suggest Wahl should pay more attention to their China factory in quality control before marketing their products. It is a matter of time when words of mouth could kill a brand due to poor quality control.

However, after only a single evening, I saw that the toy was already being torn up. My dog was biting pieces off the end, and we could see little bits of the toy on our rug. A couple days later, one of the rope cords was basically done for. Because of how much my dog loves this, I can see it lasting another week in its current form, and then potentially longer as a husk of its former self.

I can't speak to its efficacy for teeth cleaning. It likely doesn't hurt, but at the rate it's lasting, I don't think it'll make too much of an impact.

title: New and Improved Isn't Always Better
text:
I have used Magic Clean bidets for about the last 15 years and been quite pleased with them. There are a couple of things about this latest version that leave me dissatisfied. First is the new and improved mounting method. The previous model I bought four and a half years ago was pretty straightforward: two plastic bolts firmly attached to the bidet unit that would slip through the toilet seat bolt holes on the toilet. Simple, sturdy, idiot proof. The new method has us affixing a mounting flange that goes between the toilet and the bidet which is both flimsy and unnecessarily complicated, the result being that the bidet is not nearly as secure as in the past. The intent seems to have been to make it easier to remove the bidet by simply sliding it off the mounting flange. Why is this needed? In the four and half years I had the previous model I removed it from the toilet exactly zero times.

Second in my gripes is the annoying "ding" that haunts the user. (Remember those seat belt reminders on cars?) Sit down: ding. Stand up: ding. Turn unit on: ding. Turn unit off: ding. There is no way that I can find in the manual to silence this utterly unnecessary audio signal. The only purpose I can discern is so that those waiting to use the bathroom at a party will be able to know exactly when someone's backside hits the seat, and then track the progress of the user's bodily function by paying attention to the musical chimes.

Having said all that, the bidet thus far does its job just fine. Will it last as long as the last one? Time will tell.

title: Much better than emery boards!
text:
I keep my natural nails long, and do all my styling myself. I usually use three or four different emery boards, each one having one or two different levels of styling. It's a big pain in the butt, and I have always had the issue of my nails cutting into the boards and wearing them down rather quickly.

I found out about these glass/crystal nail files through reviews on normal nail files, and I thought it wouldn't hurt to give it a try. A nail file that doesn't wear down sounds amazing! I only just received them and have yet to see if that holds true, but I have tested them already. They feel great on my nails, and I don't have to worry about them catching and destroying my nails the way some boards do when the paper begins to rip. They definitely shape and buff well, but I do think they file a little slow compared to normal emery boards. I do apply pressure, too, so that isn't the issue--they just aren't as rough.

I may not be able to make this my solo nail filing tool, but overall I am pleased with the product. It's great for fixing broken edges or fixing any big of your nails that snag, and it's amazing for shaping and buffing smoothly. I also like that there are five of these for just a few dollars more than what I've found a single one for, since you can keep one handy in multiple places.

title: try all three
text:
I have been using serums for a little over 3 months now but I have not used a Vitamin C serum. I really like the idea of the serums and I do I feel that my skin has looked younger and it has defiantly cleared up a lot of my adult acne. I was looking for other options so I don’t have to constantly put on the serum wait for it to dry, then put on a moisturizer or another serum wait for that to dry and then a primer. It was taking way too much time in the morning. When I saw that Dewdrop had a series of three serums, that all had multiple ingredients I thought this would be good. The serum is made with vitamin E, vitamin C, Hyaluronic acid, and aloe leave juice. Therefore making this a must buy. I actually bought there hyaluronic acid, retinol, and vitamin C serums. They all have great ingredients and will help with moisturizing and time. I am glad this one does not have retinol I it because if you use retinol you have to stay out of the sun because it can cause skin irritation.
I received this product on time and as described by seller. Item was properly packaged and item was intact. No leaking was noted. The serum came in a brown glass bottle. Vitamin serums should come in a darker glass container so the light does not break down the chemicals. It should be a liquid that is almost like a watery lotion. It is white in color, some are clear based on what vitamins used. This serum is exactly how it should be. I am very pleased with the product so far. I feel it is a good product and good for the price. I also will be reviewing the other two products as well.
I received this product at a discounted price or for free in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. The change in price did not change my opinion in any way.

title: Received Used Set
text:
This is a perfect little kit to remove blackheads and whatnot. It is small and easy to throw in a makeup pouch to take on vacation. It comes with many different loops in different sizes to fit the size of whatever it is you need removed. It even comes with the needle to pop pimples and stuff.

Now the reason for my 2 stars. IT CAME USED. GROSS!!! How did I know it was used??? One of the tools is a spoon looking thing with a hole in it. and...there was GROSS STUFF IN THERE. like old gross dried up pus and old blackhead gunk. I put it right back and ordered a new one. but the same one just because I liked the size and the tools.

The new one that came was clean. But I still sanitized the tools like a million trillion times....and then I sanitized it again. Better safe than sorry.
I tried using the one on the opposite end of the needle. I used it right after I showered and those blackheads popped out like magic. The tool also didn't leave any of those horrid red marks on my skin. I highly recommend using it after you shower. Haven't tried the other tools yet but have high hopes for them. Just..check your set for yucky stuff!

title: I decided to purchase the Fitbit Aria WiFi Smart Scale and see if the negative reviews held up ...
text: I was a bit put-off by some of the Fitbit WiFi scale posted on here - but after wearing a Fitbit Alta-HR for 3 weeks and being particularly impressed by its sleep cycle option, I decided to purchase the Fitbit Aria WiFi Smart Scale and see if the negative reviews held up in my personal experience.  Unlike the wrist band Fitbit Alta-HR, the scale setup is a bit more complicated.  So its probably a good idea to download / PRINT OFF THE USER MANUAL (as the shipping box info in less than minimal).  The Aria Smart Scale requires one knowing their Wifi router's password - as the scale's connection is via the local (residential) WiFi network. The Fitbit Alta-HR arm band uses Blue Tooth to connect to your smart phone; one can then access the phone data via its WiFi access to your computer, if you want to see the phone's Bluetooth data on a larger screen or print it off.  As the Aria scale relies on WiFi to transmit data - I used my computer to setup the scale, once the WiFi connection to / from the computer was established.  This also allows one to easily add up to 8 different user of the scale.  One's weight and BMI are displayed on the scale's LCD window, as well as transmitted to the app and Fitbit computer program.  I personally had no problems with the scale setup and it's integration into the Fitbit phone app as well as the Fitbit computer program.  I don't have any long-term experience with battery life or durability of the scale - so I gave it a 4 star rating.

Use everyday, at home and on vacation. Used in the in-laws guest bedroom, not a single vapor escaped.

I use this product to capture exhaled vapors from a vaporizer. The smell is already really mellow, but this Buddy takes the odor down to under 5%. A single incense stick in your home of spray Febreze from time to time and your neighbors, family and friends never have to know you use a medicated inhalant or be disturbed by the pungent odors.

This will last a long time depending on your use. NEVER pour water on the inside, it will cake the build-up and make it heavy. Use rubbing alcohol, pour it in, let it dry in an airy dry place, only do this every few months when the Buddy becomes hard to exhale through.

title: HORRIBLE Product, Even WORSE Customer Service!!! Do yourself a favor and either buy dailies or use Oxysept!!
text:
For those not interested in my story, please scroll down and just read the 'solution' part.

MY STORY & THOUGHTS ON CLEAR CARE:
Before I started using Clear Care, I was using Alcon's Opti-Free Replenish. I was one of those people who wanted to take the minimum amount of steps/time to clean my contacts (aka laziness). So naturally, when I first bought and used this product, I thought I was taking a big step in taking better care of my eyes. Watching the hydrogen peroxide bubble from the neutralizing disc made me think "ooh yeah!! Now I get to experience CLEAN contacts that won't irritate my eyes after only a few hours of use!" However, in reality, I still had to remove my contacts after 4-5 hours or have people think I smoke a lot of cannabis. Eventually, this made me think that perhaps I just have ultra sensitive eyes. After several visits to my optometrist, I've switched from monthlies to biweeklies to weekly contacts. However, still, same results with Clear Care. I thought oh well, I guess I'll just have to wear my glasses more often.

About a month and a half ago, I ran out of Clear Care. No worries... just buy a new bottle right? Well, this time my experience was much different. I used the new bottle & case EXACTLY TWICE before I threw it in the trash. Those two times, the hydrogen peroxide did not fully neutralize and burned my right eye both times (of course I did not even attempt to put on my left contact after burning my right). Both times, I let the disc neutralize for at least 12.5 hours (to be exact, 12.5 hours the first time, and 28 hours the second).... well above the recommended 6 hours. I flushed my right eye for at least 20 minutes but I still felt the burn for hours.

I immediately tried to contact Alcon to try to get a replacement neutralizing case/disc. I called them three times just to get put on hold for 30-40 minutes each time before I hung up. Then I contacted them through their website by filling out their complaint form, explaining everything that had happened. To be honest, I didn't expect an immediate response... I thought maybe a week later to respond was reasonable.... two weeks would be borderline acceptable. After the second week passed, I threw out the almost full bottle of Clear Care and new case/disc.

Two days ago (which would be over a month and a half after I filed a complaint), I received an email from Alcon saying that they received my complaint and that I should not hesitate to contact them by phone/email with my concerns. LOL wow that's hilarious!!! I replied that the very least they should have done is send me a new neutralizing disc and that they need to check their quality control with their products. Yesterday I received their reply explaining different factors that would prohibit the hydrogen peroxide from neutralizing properly along with ~20 questions about my past incident (which were pretty much answered when I filled out the complaint form on their site... all they had to do was read). On top of that, they "may request return of the solution with the cup & disc for evaluation." Again, this is over a month and a half after I filed a complaint and they have the nerve to assume that I would keep their POS product. Naturally, I politely told them to piss off. Ironically, it is because of their idiotic emails that encouraged me to write this review.

SOLUTION:
During this whole ordeal, I put in a lot of research on cleaning contacts and eye care. The best solution obviously is to just get daily lenses, but that is a very expensive way to go.... especially if you wear your contacts every day. I know some people who wear their glasses most days and contacts only when they go out, so for them dailies are a viable option. For someone like me, who wears contacts at least 5 out of 7 days of the week, I highly recommend Oxysept. This is a product similar to Clear Care in that it uses a neutralizing hydrogen peroxide system to clean your contacts. The difference is the speed of neutralization. Clear Care neutralizes most of the peroxide in about 20 minutes. In other words, the peroxide will only effectively clean your contacts for about 20 minutes. You can witness this for yourself by seeing how it bubbles intensely right away and after 20 minutes the bubbles subsides. With Oxysept, peroxide neutralization is a much slower process, thus making it more efficient at disinfecting your lenses. However, there are a few things to keep in mind. Oxysept is not a one step process. You need to clean your contacts with a daily cleaner (Lobob SOF/PRO2 or Walgreens Extra Strength Daily Cleaner) and rinse with saline prior to disinfecting with Oxysept for at least 6 hours. And before your put on your contacts, you need to rinse them again with saline. Also, once a week you need to add a tablet of Ultrazyme to remove protein buildup from your lenses. This may sound like a lot of steps and a PITA (and it is at first), but trust me, it's VERY simple and the results are light years ahead of Clear Care.

Like I said before, I used to only be able to wear my contacts for about 4-5 hours before my eyes become dry, irritated and red. Now after switching to Oxysept, I am able to wear them all day and even through the night when needed and I can truly feel the difference in the health of my eyes. I have yet to experience any irritation and on top of that, I am also able to extend the life of my contacts (I've been using the same weekly lenses for about 4 weeks now and they STILL feel like new).

One more thing to keep in mind though... Because there are more products being used along with Oxysept (daily cleaner, saline and Ultrazyme), it is more expensive to use than Clear Care. However, because you only need 2 drops of daily cleaner per lens, and only use Ultrazyme once a week, they will last you for a long time.

Bottom line... If you care about your eyes, STAY AWAY FROM ALCON PRODUCTS

title: One of the best purchases I’ve made this year!
text:
I bought this product for use at home. I sleep with noise, my husband does not. I was using my AirPods at night but they, 1) Didn’t last all night, 2) would fall out of my ear, and 3) hurt my ear if I laid on them. I saw this and for the price, decided to give it try. I am not disappointed! The eye mask is soft and comfortable. It’s adjustable and keeps light out. The speakers are easily moveable to fit where your ears are and the sound is excellent. The speakers are flat so I can lay on the side of my head and I don’t feel them. I don’t wake up with my ears hurting from the pressure. The best part is that the charge lasts 12 hours. My husband gets up for work before me and I haven’t heard him get up since I started using this mask. This would be excellent for travel as well!

The only potential cons are: 1) I think the sound can be heard by someone in close proximity, even if the volume isn’t turned up that loud. Thankfully it doesn’t bother my husband or wake him up. He said it wasn’t any different than when I used my AirPods, and 2) the small cable used to connect it to the charger just has to hang out of the side somewhere. So far I haven’t found it to be annoying or noticed it when I am laying on that side.

Overall, I love this product!

title: Great Watch !!!
text:
I have had this watch for 2 years and it is still running strong. I love the big face with the large numbers that are easy to read. I do alot of rough outdoor work and this watch is pretty tough. I recently had to replace the band and the paint is worn off the buttons and the ring around the dial, but it keeps time great and gives you alot of info at a glance. The temp. is affected by your body heat which is understandable, but you can take it off and get a more accurate reading in just a few minutes. My favorite thing is that you can submerge the watch for 5 to 10 minutes and get an accurate water temperature reading. It also tells the tide level for where you set it to and gives you a UV reading and moon phase. The UV sensor usually reads 0, but it will pick up if left in direct sunlight for a few minutes. It does more than most watches, and I will probably buy another one someday if this one ever dies.

This watch is Yoda approved.

I grab some wine and settle in to watch some sinful TV or a good book. I would recommend using a rubber band or hair tie around the ankles to keep this from sliding around.

You put on the booties, pour the liquid in, and sit back and relax.

At first I thought this was just a waste of my time because nothing happened... after a few days my feet were peeling like snake skin! It was oddly satisfying that all the dead skin was just falling off my feet. It took a few more days for it to fully finish, and I had to wear closed shoes for those days but it was sooo worth it. My feet looked renewed and healthy.

After using these a few times I do recommend the days after using this to use some foot cream or balm and wear socks and it speeds up the process.

Happy Peeling!

title: Easy, No Fuss Lens Cleaning
text:
I was introduced to this cleaner by my eye doctor and I have to applaud the easy, no fuss way that the Clear Care solution helps me keep my contact lenses clean. Fill up the case that is supplied with the solution, put the lenses in the special holder with the disc at the bottom, drop the holder in the case and leave for at least 6 hours for the solution to neutralize.

In the morning I have clean, ready to use lenses that look as clear as the first day I took them out of their original package.

WARNING: This solution cannot be used to rinse off the lenses and then have the lenses placed directly on the eye. You must leave the solution in contact with the special disc, which will cause the solution to neutralize. For rinsing, I leave the overnight solution in the cup, just in case I drop the lens and need to quickly rinse off. Just use the neutralized solution and you are ready to go.

title: Does contain carbohydrates.
text: The roadside lemonade flavor tastes great, however I think the nutritional information is misleading. The numbers are for 1/4 scoop, while the recommend taking a full scoop. This is usually only done to hide an undesirable nutrient that is less than 1g in a serving because the FDA does not require you to show nutrients that are less than a gram per serving (like how smarties are 'sugar free' even though they're entirely made of sugar, bc the serving size is less than a gram). Since the serving size is a quarter of a scoop, and the nutrient marked as 0g could actually be up to .9 grams, in a full scoop there could be 3.6 grams. Considering the ingredient list shows sucralose we can assume they're hiding the carbohydrates. There are .89 grams of carbs in 1 gram of sucralose. Therefore, each scoop of powder actually contains 3.56 grams of carbohydrates.

title: Best Ever & Price is Right
text: This refill for the Quickie wand is far superior to the original just-sponge head.  The scrubbie material behind the heavier sponge allows the sponge to last longer. In the past, the just-sponge head would detach from the plastic base sometimes. I'm a guy, and I use more force when washing dishes, have destroyed many sponges.  This newer model holds up to my heavy-handed dishwashing.  Plus, the heavier sponge holds up better for washing sharp kitchen knives. The cellulose sponges become shredded by the knives, while the heavier sponge holds up much better. Also, we also found that this head does not provide soap as easily but I just hold the head upside down so soap can fill to it, squeeze the sponge head at the center (behind the filling hole in the wand head) and the soap flows into the sponge head. Or, hold it upside down so soap can fill, squeeze the sponge head into the side of the sink a couple of times, which helps it to fill.  I keep my kitchen wand in an upright position, too. My wife has a wine bottle coaster (to fit the large bottles) on the counter next to a sink, with a tall drinking glass on it. Her dish brush and the kitchen wand store heads up in the glass to dry between uses and the drips, if any, are caught by the wine bottle coaster. A saucer would work as well as the wine bottle coaster, and both are washable.

title: It saved my 2015 Honda Accord (and my lower back)
text:
I have a 2015 Honda Accord and I like the car but the driver's seat is hard. There is no give and because the car suspension is a little stiff, going over bumps caused me to eventually develop lower back pains. Side note: Out of 8 cars I've owned, I never had an issue with seat comfort until I bought the 2015 Accord.
I tried several car seat cushions from Amazon but could not find one that helped. I initially bought the purple double seat cushion and it would've been perfect if the LxW dimensions were a little bigger. I returned it and ordered the ultimate purple seat cushion as a last resort.
I've been using it for a couple of weeks now and I think it's going to work out. It is a little firm but does provide good support and it "gives"when going over bumps without bottoming out. I weigh just over 200lbs. I'm not sure how well it'll work for someone who weighs less.
In conclusion, this cushion saved my car (and my lower back). It took me 6 cushions to find the right one. 2 weeks ago, I woke up hating my car and was ready to take a loss by selling it and purchasing something else. I can honestly say that the people ultimate seat cushion helped.

title: This is our second.
text:
We originally owned the 2 speed motor version of this same sound machine. We since worn it out and ordered this model.

What we like:
* It is a "loud" sound machine.
* The top and side can slide to change the pitch and volume.
* We use this for our children to sleep better while we watch TV at night, and they enjoy turning it on themselves.

12 Months of real experience:
* If you run it all night, every night. After about a year the motor lost it's lubrication and struggle to turn on. I removed the screws from the bottom, added some light oil and it improved instantly. This is likely just the result of how we use it.
* We dropped it once, and it didn't fair well. This is why we now own a new one. The edges are not kid friendly if they pick it up and then drop it from about 2 feet.

Recommendation:
We obviously liked it well enough to purchase it twice. We wish the top better held up to dropping. We love the results it has on our children's ability to sleep despite loud noises outside their room.

title: Unbiased review:  Not worth the effort or money
text:
After reading the reviews I figured most of them were people who were given free stuff or paid to review. There were just too many positive reviews and disclaimers saying they had gotten "discounted" product. I ordered anyways with hope in my little heart. I have thick, wavy hair and my hopes were something that would cut my straightening time down. I knew it would never get my hair as straight as my high heat professional iron, but if it could smooth frizz and make it somewhat straight I would be happy. My flat iron works great but takes a long time and is damaging.
Soooo....no bueno. This brush has potential and I hope a company gets the technology right soon but it's not there yet. It's like using a crappy low heat flat iron. In order to get my hair slightly smoother I needed to take small sections and push it all the way through the brush, hold it tight and then slowly pull it through. Each section needs at least 4-5 passes to get the hair slightly smoother. Very time consuming and the end result is not worth it. All parts seemed to work appropriately; turned on quickly, display was easy to read. It did seem to take a very long time to hear up to 450 degrees. Twice I walked away it was taking so long and when I came back the unit had auto shut off so I had to wait all over again.

title: I always thought that was no way a brush like this would be able to straighten hair
text:
This is really a fascinating product. I did receive this at a discount for my honest and unbiased review.

First of all, I always thought that was no way a brush like this would be able to straighten hair. I was wrong. This brush, firstly, is very well made. It’s made of a hard plastic and the bristles are stiff and have a rubbery texture at the tips. This makes detangling and brushing easy and smooth.
The brush temperature gets quite high. The brush itself can get quite hot, so I suggest being careful with that, but rightfully. The handle does stay cool so that’s safe. The brush also comes with a heat resistant glove which also works great.
I’ve always been a bit leery of products like this because with my experiences, I have thick wavy hair that really hates to cooperate with hair appliances. Using a traditional flat-iron, and even with shoulder length hair, takes 30+ minutes. It took me less than 10 minutes with this brush. I absolutely love it.

Quality seems to be very good considering the price. These aren't super high quality leather straps, but that should be self-evident. They do look to be real leather, evenly cut into thin strips. I much prefer leather over silver or gold chains and so far these have fit the bill and held up well. I also like the variation in colors. Adjustment holds (although I don't use it) and the part that holds the glasses tightens and stays well.

Time will tell if they hold up to the rigors of me playing around in my shop, working on cars, and generally doing things that break stuff. I'll update the review if I have any issues with them, but so far, so good!

title: Pretty Good So Far!
text: I've recently received this "Posture Corrector".  I've only had a short time wearing it, but so far its pretty good and I  like it very much.  Just note, like with any corrector your body will have to adjust to wearing it over time.  A few years ago, I had a single back strap style bought it from a brick and mortar store.  After putting it on over a hoodie twice while trying it out to keep it very clean, I felt nothing different, and I wasn't sure what it was trying to do so I returned it. However, for this style I have now, I do feel my shoulders being pulled back, nothing else though.  Truthfully..., I really don't know what exactly you are suppose to feel straightening up, since I only feel my shoulders being squeezed together.  I guess, it's doing something!  LOL! But time will tell when if my neck is able to hold my head up higher without constantly dropping it back down.  Hopefully! After time it won't say, "Nope! I still can't do it, now go find something else😄!"  Well, I ordered the full upper back covering style pictured. Here are my photos, so check them out because one thing for sure this corrector is made, and stitched extremely well.  Look at the nice zip lock storage packaging, along with the colorful detailed instructions card to hang up on the frig.  Well... that's where I put it as a reminder to don't take another snack, and put it on.  Also, the comfort wraps, those square things are nice and thick, plus also made very well. The weather is hot, so I do think after many hand washing cycles, all three items will hold up for a very long time. LOL! Of course I can't forget to mention the disappointing cons, well its only one. The wrap around pull straps are too short.  Yet, on Amazon they appear much longer, but they are little wee bit difficult to grap to pull, and if someone with a much wider upper back, the straps may end up fastening slightly under their armpits instead of closer to their shoulders as pictured.  But if it does, I guess you could try giving the comfort wraps a go under the armpits.  So would I recommend this style of "Posture Corrector" to friends.  ABSOLUTELY☺!!!  It's made very well.  It is a short time wearing it, so once I start to see changes within my posture, I will give a final update.

This is a torture device

The back support portion kept riding up no matter what I did so I was always pulling it back down as it made the sides gape out all the time. I have heard women rave maternity bands help alleviate back pressure/pain, I actually felt the same if not worse with this on in that area.

I ended up with gouges on my stomach and groin from where this cut in after only a few hours of trying to wear it.

The straps did absolutely nothing but cause serious pain. I believe the intention is that they help hold the weight up of the pregnant belly but they do not. I tried tightening the straps as much as possible. All this did was cause the straps to cut in under my breasts more and more and apply extreme pressure to the sternum which made it very difficult to breath. I could still pull the straps up and feel how it would feel if they actually helped lift any weight of the pregnant belly up but they did nothing. Also, if they did anything how do you hide them? Even a running tank with a very high neck line didn't cover the straps the only thing that would cover these is a turtle neck as they do not sit over on the shoulder where your bra strap normally sits they actually sit up higher toward the neck so are visible when you wear anything but a turtle neck.

title: Sleek Hair Every Time!
text: Straightening my hair can be such a hassle. I have the thinnest, finest, yet curliest hair ever. I use all kinds of conditioning creams, sprays and heat resistant protectants on my hair to keep it from being fried. I blow dry a lot, and I use my flat iron on my bangs. It takes too much time to tame the frizz of what I call hair to straighten the whole deal. I recently tried out the Cellto Brush Hair Straightener and honestly can't say anything negative about it! All I have to do is blow dry my hair, like I already do and brush it out with the Cellto Brush. No more yanking a flat iron through this mane! The Cellto Brush has an awesome digital screen that is clear to read and also easily adjusted by the push of button. Adjustments to temperature can be made as well as turning power to the brush on and off. Full heat up time takes under 1 minute and the brush is ready to use. I work the morning shift at my office, so I have to be ready fast. I plugged in the brush before showering and let it sit on the counter-which was safe because only the bristles actually heat up. The insides of the bristles run through my hair with such ease I didn't have to use my detangling spray for once! The tips of the brush are soft and massage the scalp while using. I loved that! I also didn't have to worry about the tips burning my scalp or the sides of my head which was a big relief because I've burned myself numerous times with a typical flat iron. This is NOT your typical flat iron, expect to see smooth, healthy straight hair while brushing and throughout the day after using. The cord of the brush can be folded together and wrapped up in the attached velcro strap. Easy set up and easy clean up! I would suggest using smaller pieces of hair in the brush than your normal brush so you get the maximum results. Also make sure your settings are higher or lower on temperature depending on how thick or coarse your hair is. I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

title: Accuracy is terrible
text:
Just taking some time to complain about the accuracy and reliability of your Aria scale. It is horrible.

After a couple of weeks of thinking i was really making great progress, it turns out something must have been broken in the scale. I was down about 10 lbs more than i had expected, and those measurements went on for about a week. i thought i was really doing well. Then out of the blue, all my weights are now up 10 pounds from where they were. i thought i was down in the 180s now i am back in the 190s. During the time everything was down, my body fat % numbers were down as well. and then one day. everything is back up.

I find it hard to believe that in one day i all of a sudden gained 10 pounds. unless, now the scale is broken the other way. I have not changed any eating habits. I keep the same amount of calories. The scale has not moved from it's position. So i have deleted all the old "false" measurements and am back up 10 pounds.

So now i am a bit angry and depressed that i was not making as much progress as i had hoped, progress I was relying on your devices to help me track ACCURATELY. I was really excited in thinking i was making great strides towards my fitness goal.

I have the Fitbit ZIP as well, i had the Ultra but it's bad design did not stay clipped to shorts and was lost (who knows where) and while i wanted to keep common technology so i only had to look in one place for tracking steps, etc., I feel I am going to have to dump your scale and most likely your tracker as well. Seriously, how can i trust any of your equipment when your equipment can show such huge swings as +/- 10 lbs.? You sell a product that is supposed to be accurate. Hell, i can lean too far back on my heals and change the weight by a good pound or so. The weight shouldn't change just because i have bad balance. I would not call that very accurate. as for the 10 pound swing, i can't even imagine what would have caused that.

And so begins the search for new tools to help me towards my fitness goals.

Thank You fitbit for a lot of wasted time, money and helping to screw up my confidence.

title: Life changing
text:
This is lengthy but I feel worth sharing in case anyone is wondering if it’s worth the cost or how it may help:
I first was exposed to these products while in a short term rehab for depression, as well as recovering from way too many years off prescription opiate use that led to the inevitable abuse as your brain chemistry is genuinely altered~90% of the pain that began the journey had been healed thru yoga until the opiates overtook my ability to continue practicing regularly & simply spiraled the situation~I was fortunate to find a phenomenal facility that focused on healing the brain as well as spirit & discovered that I was definitely NOT imagining my decline the last 5 years as my alpha waves were dramatically lower than delta & beta, the only 3 part of that treatment. I KNEW I didn’t feel like myself anymore, after a series of years of incredibly emotional &/or traumatic experiences in addition to the opioid affects, but it’s hard to know if it’s just reality now or something is truly off.

Aside from having read about how the opioids alter brain chemistry, I had read about & discussed w my dr how a brain can get stuck after a series of these types of situations where emotions trigger such different than norm neurochemistry & I was hopeful yet desperate! The first thing I was 100% sure of during my first days there was that after my normally scheduled twice weekly 20 min session on the CES, I felt better than I could recently remember. I began signing up for an extra session every evening right after group meetings, during snack time & before bed. The days my depression nudged me to blow it off or it was already full, I had more trouble sleeping & was less motivated to do anything the next day. When I learned the nursing station had a couple of machines we could use in our room at night, it was a life saver! I watched friends who came in struggling in MUCH more dramatic ways than myself start to really turn around & thrive when their psychiatrist assigned one the carried around & could access 24/7, esp 1 who never removed the headphones from his neck & only gave his ears breaks from the clips occasionally (though I m guessing so much use led to the clips not feeling so tight after 30-40 min!! So lengthier use was easier….for this reason, I sometimes leave mine clipped to something a bit thicker than my ear when not in use)

I was thrilled when my psychiatrist wrote me a script for one during our last meeting before I left! (I had been talked into using MAT, medication assisted treatment, for the opiod situation vs going home clean after learning how the brain begins to heal & the 12-18 mth time frame~which my husband & others falsely previously convinced me was trading 1 for another bcuz when done correctly it’s got to be 1000x more likely for long term success…it’s 2 years since leaving & I’ve not remotely struggled while down to only 20% of daily med taking when left & like clockwork roughly a year ago began having moments of feeling like my true self again, which have now increased to almost full time! 2 yrs of healing vs 10 years of opioids & 7+ at amounts that should’ve easily killed me~if you know someone….MAT immediately & learn addiction science!!! We get it all wrong )@: ) Despite having great insurance, I paid $3k for the facility where many w/o ins were paying $60k, only 45 days!, of course it wasn’t covered~neither they nor the pharmacy had any clue what I was even looking for!?!? After hours of online research, I found the ones identical to what we used~obviously I wasn’t chancing something else! I got it for a bit less, but after a couple of weeks debating the expense, I decided it was NONnegotiable!!!! I could tell how much I needed it, especially back to emptying my folks’ home due to both unexpectedly passing 6 mths apart just before I checked in, & very shortly followed by covid, which I’m pretty certain spread there early feb just before I left…2 days after 1st “flu,” dozens were sick, 2 went to hospital & 1 came back w oxygen, & by week’s end staff was wiped out too!

I don’t see using the Deluxe feature of creating my own, but absolutely LOVE the variety of sessions included & wish we knew there vs the standard they gave us. I didn’t use the glasses often there because there weren’t many, but knew it was worth including. I still don’t use them as often as the other, but definitely prefer the option & is a noticeable difference at times! I most often use an Alpha heavy 42 min session, & simply go about doing housework or whatever, esp when doing multiple sessions back to back, but when I’m REALLY feeling stuck, anxious, or just off, a good 20-30 min session sitting & just soaking it in or while reading is something VITAL to my day.

If you struggle w ANY of the recommended uses, I simply cannot recommend enough!!!! Take the time to read the manual online & understand what your seeking & how best to achieve results. The science supports it if you research, but I’ve witnessed & experienced first hand. It’s criminal that insurance pays for dangerous medications & procedures that treat symptoms but not something that can actually HEAL the issues! Even therapy & yoga are only as good as the person leading you…this is something YOU can control & depend on. It’s worth every penny & more. Go for it~

title: I have been using it every day for a week and sometimes more and really like it. YES it is noisy but just put ...
text:
I plan to fully experience this spa tub, I have been using it every day for a week and sometimes more and really like it.

YES it is noisy but just put some music on and listen with some earbuds. It's not unbearable, the noise is mostly due to the vibration option. When vibration is off there is a humming noise, I believe from the motor that tries to filter the water through the heating mechanism.
YES the heat really does work, instructions say to fill with warm water and wait 15 minutes. I put my feet in immediately to feel the change, and boy does this thing really give the water some heat.

Now, my tub does not bubble but it's not really a big deal, sure I'd like it to bubble but my feet will feel the same either way. I will look into this and try to fix it. If your tub does bubble I'd suggest not adding a soap, this should be common sense. But I do add bath soaks, salts, melts and bath bombs to my little foot tub to add the little extra touch. Just make sure to fully rinse it out, especially when using salts.

I love the textured bottom, it doesn't hurt my feet. It feels like your rubbing your feet on little pebbles on the beach. I did take out the rollers and will probably only put either the back set in or front set in at once, not both. The rollers do seem a bit awkward and hard, maybe if they were a slight jelly texture it would feel really good.

I do not plan on returning it because I truly do love the product and some bubbles aren't a deal breaker for me. The heat is definitely a +++. Overall I'm satisfied.

title: Great vitamin - don't overdose
text: GREAT vitamin. Really. I work long shifts as a CNA and this really helps give you the extra oomph. However, be careful to only take the recommended dose - 2. I love my vitamins, and I sometimes would take 3 at once in the morning whenever I knew I was about to work 16 hours and then had school or whatever. I did that every once in awhile and I was fine. Then I started regularly being unable to get enough sleep in, (I worked 3 jobs for a short while) and I started taking 3 a day for about 2 weeks. On the second week I got sick from it. Very sick. Constant nausea and diahrrea. Felt horrible, thought I might be pregnant but it was just this vitamin. Day one of not taking it I felt better. However I found that once I tried to go back to taking the recommended dose, I got sick again. I tried even just taking one a day. Can't take it anymore. So be wary, don't overdo it and always always take with food. Space out the doses if you can. But it is very helpful.

title: Good earplugs, but no decibel rating on box
text:
In an effort to be as transparent as possible, I was provided these earplugs for free. With that out of the way, I still like them. I have trouble with most earplugs because I have small ears and cartilage piercings. The blue and gray earplugs are soft enough to keep my ears from hurting. They don’t interfere with my jewelry. I might trim some of the tabs off the gray pair and just leave one tab for removal. The tabs are a little long for my ears for sleeping. The orange ones are a bit firmer, but the instructions say they’re only meant to be worn for a few hours anyway. The silicone earplugs are great for keeping water out and they can be formed to any ear shape.

The individual boxes are a nice touch. The instructions on the back of the box have some typos though. As with any earplugs, the best way to insert them is to take your opposite hand over your head and pull the top of your ear back. This is the best way to be sure the earplug is deep enough. Be sure to do the same thing when removing otherwise the vacuum you created will hurt as you pull the earplugs out. I didn’t see that in the instructions, but I feel that’s important to include. There’s also no decibel rating anywhere in the packaging so that’s concerning. In the product title, it says 32db so I’m assuming that’s for the orange pair. I wouldn’t use these for hearing protection from loud noises because of that not being explicitly stated, but for keeping water out and for sleeping would be fine.

title: Works for my daughter and she likes the Camo design
text: They Work! We take at least one often more 8+ hour drives to see family each year. My daughter gets car sick on car trips over 45 minutes, and we were having to stop for long periods of time making our already long trips excessively long and miserable. So we tried these out, and now they are a must have for long drives. As long as we remember to put them on before we leave, and place them correctly she doesn't get sick. We do have to take them off when we stop for meals etc. because the small plastic bump that pushes on the pressure point can press hard enough to indent and irritate her skin after wearing for many hours. (Like falling asleep in your jeans and waking up with an imprint of them on your skin!) But if it doesn't put pressure it wont work, so we just take breaks from it and adjust the positioning slightly and it works out fine. Also my daughter just loves the Camo design. They worked so well I bought an adult pair for myself when I was experiencing morning sickness during pregnancy and it made a difference. (Although mine weren't these cool camo bands, they were plain blue) It seems to me the first time we put them on they were way too tight, so I had to give them a good stretching (Like before you blow up a balloon) so they were loose enough not to be restricting circulation, but tight enough to put pressure in the right spot.

title: These are my favorites so far
text:
UPDATE 12/23/15:
After using these for a while, I've decided that they almost tie for my favorite pair of ear plugs. Definitely worth the reasonable price! The only reason they aren't my "most favorite" pair is that I bought the Alpine MusicSafe ear plugs after writing the original review. The Alpines are probably my favorite overall plugs, because they have different filters that you can change out to fine tune the volume reduction. But the DownBeats are VERY similar to the Alpines, so if you don't want to spend as much, get the DownBeats. You won't be disappointed.

*************
ORIGINAL REVIEW:

I have these, as well as Etymotic ER20 ear plugs, Erasers Musicians plugs, and I've also used standard foam ear plugs. These are my favorite of all. Here are the details...

FIT: These are made of a soft plastic, much like the material of the Etys. They have 2 flanges compared to the Etys 3, and they seem to seal in the ear well without going too deeply into the ear canal. They are by far the easiest ear plugs to insert that I have ever owned. They're also easy to remove, even though the stem doesn't stick out very far from your ear. In comparison, my #1 complaint with the Etys is fit/comfort. The Etys are extremely uncomfortable; they feel like they're poking too far into my ear canal and my ears get sore after wearing them for only a few minutes. The stems stick out too far and make them easy to bump and dislodge from my ears. The Earasers fall somewhere in between DownBeats and Etys for comfort. They don't hurt like the Etys, but they're made of a harder material, so they don't seem to seal as well. I've tried both the small and medium sized Earasers, with similar results from both.

SOUND QUALITY:
The DownBeats sound pretty good to my ear. They lower the sound enough to make it comfortable to listen. They do muffle the sound somewhat, but not as badly as standard foam ear plugs. To my ears, the Etys also muffle the sound, and at the same time they don't lower the volume enough for me. The Earasers seem to have the most clear sound of the three, but the volume is not lowered enough...I just don't feel that they are protecting my hearing. Some of my problems with the Earasers and Etys not lowering the volume enough may be my own fault. Maybe I'm not getting them inserted properly, but if it's that much trouble to get them inserted properly, they're not the solution for me.

So far DownBeats are my favorite plugs. The slightly muffled sound is really the only thing that I'm not 100% happy with on the DownBeats. I plan to try Alpine MusicSafe plugs at some point, just to see if they sound clearer, so I'll update my review with comparison to those as well.
